2nd carpenter Stillebroer punished with 3 times 24 hours short in irons, while keeping watches and required duty, for again arbitrarily removing himself from the watch. A CONTINUAR LA PROPIA COMISIÓN POR LAS C: To continue the same commission along the coasts of Spain in the Ocean. (...) Clock no. 13 by Berthoud was set going, which is the only one of any reliability among the eight we have (...) (continues on the first day of navigation for lack of space). "(...) We also began to determine the rate of no. 79, Arnold's pocket watch, which Captain D. Benito de Lira has just received and has lent (...) because of his assurance of the excellence of the machine, built with all the new refinements of the craftsman (...) but the gloom and bad weather have not permitted a formal examination of its movement as I wished (...). A LA 1 1/2 (TARDE) ENTRÓ LA VENTOLINA DE: At 1:30 (afternoon) a light breeze came in from the N (...) Night fell with the sky overcast and the horizons hazy, wind moderate and heavy sea from the SW and WNW.

A LA 1 1/4 FALLECIÓ EL MARINERO ANTONIO: At 1:15 the sailor Antonio Gallego died.
A LA 1 SE ECLIPSÓ EL SOL POR CUYO MOTIVO: At 1 the sun was eclipsed, for which reason we observed its end to find the longitude.
A LA 10 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA: At 10 arrive at the port of La Coruña
A LA 1:00 SE HAYAN EN UNA MAR MUY BONANC: At 1:00 they found themselves in a very calm sea with the colour of the bottom, and had sounded without finding it. At 2:30 they see land to starboard to the WSW. It seemed very high to them, with the mountain tops covered in clouds. No forests or trees could be made out. They sounded 80 fathoms, bottom of shell grit, coral and very fine brown sand. They set course SW and SW by S to get away from the coast, with the [?] going ahead to reconnoitre the land, and at 5:40 they saw other land to port, which made them believe they were in some archipelago or in a large bay of some small continent. He describes the coasts of the islands and the waters. He says that by the noon observation the northern island, at its middle, lies in latitude 46º 44' and in longitude 36º 01' east of Paris. They gave these islands the name Australes.
A LA 1ª HORA DEL DIA CORTAN EL TROPICO: At the 1st hour of the day they cross the tropic.
A LA CAZA DE UNA EMBARCACIÓN CON BANDERA: Chasing a vessel flying the Portuguese flag.
A LA LLAMADA LAVETE AL NO DIST. 87 LEGUA: To the place called Lavete, to the NW, distance 87 leagues.
A LA TARDE CALCULA LAS VARIACIONES DE LA: In the afternoon he calculates the variations of the compass.
A LA VISTA DE SAN BARTOLOME Y SAN MARTIN: In sight of San Bartolome and San Martin.

At 10:00 in the day the wind dropped, leaving a heavy swell. They cannot take observations because of the fog. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 00:00 MUERE EL SOLDADO DE LA GUARN: At 00:00 the soldier of the ship's garrison Julian Ponce de Asma dies. "I had his mattress, sheets and pillows thrown into the water."
A LAS 09 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVID: At 09 hours arrives at the port of Montevideo.

A LAS 10 AVISTAMOS UNOS PÁJAROS CHIQUITO: At 10 we sighted some small birds, all white.
A LAS 10 DE LA MAÑANA ECHAMOS LOS DOS DI: At 10 in the morning we threw the two dead into the water.
A LAS 10 DE LA MAÑANA HIZO EL COMTE. SEÑ: At 10 in the morning the commander made the signal to anchor.
A LAS 10 DE LA MAÑANA MURIÓ UN GUARDIÁN: At 10 in the morning a guard who was travelling as a passenger, named Antonio Andrade, died.
A LAS 10 DE LA NOCHE ENTRÓ EL VTO: At 10 at night the wind came in.
A LAS 10 HORAS SONDAN CON 100 BRAZAS Y N: At 10 hours they sound with 100 fathoms and find no bottom.

A LAS 10 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MON: At 10 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 10 HS DIERON FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 10 hours they anchored in the port of Montevideo.

A LAS 10 SE HALLÓ POR EL AZIMUT 8º 18' D: At 10 a variation of 8º 18' NW was found by azimuth.
A LAS 10:00 DAN A LA VELA CON DESTINO A: At 10:00 they set sail bound for San Blas. The merchant frigate La Pandora left just afterwards bound for Guayaquil. He discusses the characteristics of the navigation from Acapulco to San Blas.
A LAS 10:00 DIVISAN TIERRA. VAN EN DEMAN: At 10:00 they sight land. They head for Puerto Deseado, where they anchor at 15:20. Data generally from dawn and noon bearing.
A LAS 10:00 ENTRAN EN LOS MARES DE LA PA: At 10:00 they enter the seas of the southern part of New Zealand. Many fish and [?] were seen.
A LAS 10:00 FONDEA EN MONTECRISTO Y A LA: At 10:00 anchors at Montecristo and at 15:00 sets sail. Measurement from noon or from the day's run, although there are many days without data.
A LAS 10:00 SE RECONOCIO ESTAR ALGO SENT: At 10:00 the upper part of the mainmast was found to be somewhat weakened and a reinforcement was added to it.
A LAS 10:00 SONDAN Y HALLAN FONDO EN 55: At 10:00 they sound and find bottom at 55 fathoms, loose whitish mud. From 20:00 they have calm. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 10:15 PRETENDEN ATRACAR EN ISLA AS: At 10:15 they intend to land at Ascension Island but the rough sea in the anchorage prevents it and they decide to continue the voyage. There are 4 folios describing Ascension Island, the catching of turtles and how they use them to cure scurvy. He relates the death of the sailor Francisco de Lagos from that disease.
A LAS 10:30 SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 10:30 anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 11 DE LA MAÑANA SE PONEN A LA VELA: At 11 in the morning they set sail (before this there are interesting sheets with data on the ship, equipment, orders, etc.). Measurement and data from noon, the descriptors are usually from dusk. Journal of ship's captain Antonio de Córdoba Lazo de la Vega, commander of the packet boats Sta. Casilda and Sta. Eulalia, to the Strait of Magellan and Staten Island. French chart.
A LAS 11 HS DA FONDO EN EL AMARRADERO DE: At 11 hours anchors at the mooring of the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 11 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 11 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 11 HS DAN FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 11 hours they anchor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 11 HS. SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 11 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.

A LAS 11 SE AVISTARON 5 PÁJAROS GRANDES: At 11 5 large birds were sighted, with the flight of a duck, tobacco-coloured.
A LAS 11:00 FONDEA EN MONTECRISTO Y SE H: At 11:00 anchors at Montecristo and sets sail at 17:30.
A LAS 11:00 FONDEAN EN PUERTO RICO: At 11:00 they anchor at Puerto Rico.
At 11:00 land was sighted at 4 leagues. At 12:00 recognises the island of San Martin.
A LAS 11:00 SE HACE A LA VELA. DATOS DEL: At 11:00 sets sail. Data from noon or from the day's run, although almost all the descriptors are from dusk.
A LAS 11:30 AVISTA LA ISLA DE LA ASCENCI: At 11:30 sights Ascension Island at 12 leagues.
A LAS 11:30 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 11:30 hours arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 11:30 LLEGA A PUERTO RICO Y SALE A: At 11:30 arrives at Puerto Rico and leaves at 12:30 without having anchored.
A LAS 11:45 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO. CARTA: At 11:45 anchors at Puerto Rico. Dutch chart.
A LAS 12 1/2 VIMOS UN CHUBASCO (...) DE: At 12 1/2 we saw a squall ahead that looked like wind but passed without harm. (...) Evening came with clear sky, the horizon with some cloud. Little wind and sea from the SW. (...) Dawn: clear sky, fresh breeze.
A LAS 12 DE LA NOCHE DEL DÍA 16 EL BUQUE: At 12 at night on the 16th the ship weighed anchor and departed from Havana. There are no weather references for this day. Course: noon reference; remaining variables: general references or near noon. This is another navigation journal of the same vessel on the same route, kept by another person. Position: observed latitude taken and longitude by dead reckoning.
A LAS 12 DEL MEDIO DÍA DA FONFO EN EL PU: At 12 noon anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 12 DIMOS FONDO EN (...) FANGO SUEL: At 12 we anchored in (...) loose mud (end of the voyage to Montevideo. We change the heading for the voyage Montevideo-Cádiz).
A LAS 12 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑ: At 12 hours arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 12 HS SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 12 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 12 HS. DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 12 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 12 SE AVISTÓ EL CERRO DE MONTEVIDE: At 12 the hill of Montevideo was sighted to the W by N, NW (...) At 2 the city of S. Phelipe and its port were sighted (...) after we crossed the entrance we headed for its inner part and anchored in 17 feet.
A LAS 12 SE VIÓ LA AURORA BOREAL: At 12 the aurora borealis was seen.
A LAS 12:00 HALLAN 55 BRAZAS DE FONDO AR: At 12:00 they find 55 fathoms of bottom, very fine sand. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 12:00 SONDAN Y HALLAN 42 BRAZAS DE: At 12:00 they sound and find 42 fathoms of bottom, fine brown sand. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 12:15 VIMOS AL O UN NAVIO, ME PARE: At 12:15 we saw to the W a ship, I think of about 40 guns, steering ENE toward the strait, and at 12:30 she hoisted a Dutch flag, and I believe it was hers, judging by her sails.
A LAS 12:30 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 12:30 hours arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 12:30 HS LLEGA AL FONDEADERO DEL P: At 12:30 hours reaches the anchorage of the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 12:30 SONDAN Y HALLAN 52 BRAZAS DE: At 12:30 they sound and find 52 fathoms of bottom, fine brown sand. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 13 HS ARRIBA AL FERROL DEL PUERTO: At 13 hours arrives at Ferrol, of the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 13: 30 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 13:30 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 13:00 FONDEAN AL N DE LA ISLA DE S: At 13:00 they anchor to the north of the island of San Lorenzo.
A LAS 13:00 SONDA EN EL PLACER DEL N: At 13:00 sounds on the northern shoal.
A LAS 13:30 AVISTA TIERRA. A LAS 14:30 R: At 13:30 sights land. At 14:30 recognises San Bartolome.
A LAS 13:30 CALMO EL VIENTO. A LAS 17:00: At 13:30 the wind dropped. At 17:00 it blew from the NNE. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
At 13:30 the wind dropped. At 17:00 it blew from the NNE. During the night the wind freshened and raised a heavy swell.
A LAS 13:30 CONSIGUE FONDEAR, EN EL PUER: At 13:30 manages to anchor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 13:30 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO. MEDIC: At 13:30 anchors at Puerto Rico. Measurement from dusk or from the day's run.
A LAS 14 H S DAN FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE L: At 14 hours they anchor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 14 HS 30' LOGRA AMARRARSE EN EL PU: At 14 hours 30' manages to moor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 14 HS AMARRA EN EL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 14 hours moors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 14 HS FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 14 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 14 HS SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 14 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 14 HS VE UNA SAETIA QUE VA AL ESE: At 14 hours sees a saetia (small coastal sailing vessel) heading ESE.
A LAS 14: 30 HS SE AVISTA LA ISLA DE PAL: At 14:30 hours the island of Palma is sighted.
A LAS 14:00 AVISTAN UNA EMBARCACION INGL: At 14:00 they sight an English vessel which said it came from Corrque and was going to Jamaica, that it had been 40 days at sea and reckoned itself at 33º45' longitude by the meridian of London.
A LAS 14:00 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. DATOS D: At 14:00 anchors at La Coruña. Data from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from dusk. French chart.
A LAS 14:00 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. MEDICIO: At 14:00 anchors at La Coruña. Measurement from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from dusk.
A LAS 14:00 MARCA EL CABO DE SANTA CRUZ: At 14:00 takes a bearing on Cape Santa Cruz and steers toward the Caimans.
A LAS 14:00 SE HACE A LA VELA. DATOS DEL: At 14:00 sets sail. Data from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from dusk. Madeira meridian and Dutch chart.
A LAS 14:00 SE HACE A LA VELA. MEDICION: At 14:00 sets sail. Measurement from noon or from the day's run, although the descriptors are from dusk.
A LAS 14:00 VIMOS UNA MANCHA EN EL AGUA: At 14:00 we saw a patch in the water, not very big, passing like [?], of a greenish colour as if it had bottom, and we happened to pass immediately outside it.
A LAS 14:30 EL SAN PEDRO LE HACE SEÑAL D: At 14:30 the San Pedro signals damage to him; they repair the lead of the pump tube on the starboard side of the water chest.
A LAS 14:30 FONDEA EN SAN JUAN DE PUERTO: At 14:30 anchors at San Juan de Puerto Rico. Descriptors from noon or the day's run.
A LAS 14:30 MARCAN EL CABO SAN JORGE AL: At 14:30 they take a bearing on Cape San Jorge to the SW at 6 leagues. At 00:00 they anchor on the north side of that cape, 2 leagues from the coast.
A LAS 14:30 MURIO EL SOLDADO JOSEPH SEQU: At 14:30 the soldier Joseph Sequeiro died of scurvy and was put into the water at 19:00. "Black birds like thrushes have been seen, only the wing is more pointed, and at 11:30 a small whale or whale calf close alongside."
A LAS 15 HS DA FONDO EN LA BOCA DEL PUER: At 15 hours anchors at the mouth of the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 15 HS FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE MONTE: At 15 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 15.30 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 15.30 hours arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 15:00 AVISTAN TORTUGAS, TAMBIEN VE: At 15:00 they sight turtles; they also see some of the birds of these days, though fewer.
A LAS 15:00 ESTABAN A 1/2 LEGUAS DE LA I: At 15:00 they were 1/2 league from the island of Sisarga and the violence of the wind and sea was great. Anchors at 17:00 at La Coruña.
A LAS 15:00 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO. MEDIC: At 15:00 anchors at Puerto Rico. Measurement from noon or from the day's run, although there are many days without data.
A LAS 15:00 MUERE EL SOLDADO DE MARINA D: At 15:00 the marine soldier dies of typhus.
A LAS 15:00 SE HACE A LA VELA. DATOS DEL: At 15:00 sets sail. Data from dusk or from the day's run.
A LAS 15:00 UN RAYO CAUSA MUCHOS DESTROZ: At 15:00 lightning causes much damage to the ship. Data from noon except the descriptors, which are from dusk. Spanish quarteron.
A LAS 15:30 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO. MEDIC: At 15:30 anchors at Puerto Rico. Measurement from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from dusk. French chart.
A LAS 15:30 FONDEA EN SAN JUAN DE PUERTO: At 15:30 anchors at San Juan de Puerto Rico.
A LAS 16 HS ARRIBÓ AL PUERTO DE MONTEVID: At 16 hours arrived at the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 16 HS EL VIENTO REFRESCA Y HORIZON: At 16 hours the wind freshens and the horizons close in.
A LAS 16 HS FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 16 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 16 HS SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 16 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 16: 30 DIO FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE L: At 16:30 anchored in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 16:00 EL SAN PEDRO LE AVISA DE AVE: At 16:00 the San Pedro informs him of damage to the topsail yard, which was broken. At 7:30 the commander told him that she had an irremediable defect in the hull and was making one inch of water per hour.
A LAS 16:00 MARCA CAYO CONFITES. CARTA F: At 16:00 takes a bearing on Cayo Confites. French chart.
A LAS 16:00 MARCA LA PUNTA MAS AL O DE L: At 16:00 takes a bearing on the westernmost point of Lanzarote at 5 or 6 leagues. French chart.
A LAS 16:00 SE ARROJO AL DIFUNTO AL AGUA: At 16:00 the dead man was thrown into the water.
A LAS 16:00 SE VIO 1 HILERO DE CORRIENTE: At 16:00 a line of currents was seen from SE by E to NW by W.
A LAS 16:25 CON CORTA DIFERENCIA MUERE E: At 16:25, give or take a little, the guard soldier Joseph de Moya dies, consumptive according to the surgeon Lacombe, and after the Ave Maria, at 18:15, he was put into the water in the customary manner.
A LAS 16:30 EL SAN PEDRO LE MANIFIESTA T: At 16:30 the San Pedro reports to him that she has considerable damage and both lie hove to.
A LAS 16:30 ENTREGA LOS PLIEGOS A LA VEL: At 16:30 hands over the dispatches under sail and afterwards moves away. Data from noon (from 18 Dec the descriptors are from dusk).
A LAS 16:30 FONDEA EN EL PLACER DE CAYO: At 16:30 anchors on the shoal of Cayo Güinchos. Data from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from dusk. Madeira meridian and Dutch chart.
A LAS 16:30 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 16:30 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 17 1/2 SE HA VISTO LA TRINIDAD (RE: At 17 1/2 Trinidad has been seen (recognised by the Rosalía and Ascension according to Bellen) (...) Notes: 1st - From the Canaries to the parallel of 7º N the winds, though not very fresh, were constant (...) 2nd: From that parallel of 7º N calms and light airs began for us, as if it were the limit of the variables, together with strange and large differences to the N (and to the S very few).
A LAS 17 HS SE DEMARCA LA ISLA DE LOBOS: At 17 hours the island of Lobos is sighted.
A LAS 17 HS. DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 17 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 17.30 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 17.30 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 17:00 FALLECIO EL ARTILLERO DE MAR: At 17:00 the sea gunner Juan de la Luz died. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn.
A LAS 17:00 SONDAN Y HALLAN FONDO EN 60: At 17:00 they sound and find bottom at 60 fathoms, loose whitish mud. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 17:00 SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO EN: At 17:00 they sound and find no bottom at 60 fathoms. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 17:15 FONDEA EN MONTECRISTO. DESCR: At 17:15 anchors at Montecristo. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. The journal begins on 31 Jan 1766 but he does not leave until 3 Feb because of the violence of the clouds and the wind that came from the W and [?]. He had trouble passing the strait of the channel.
A LAS 17:25 VEN POR ESTRIBOR TIERRA Y MA: At 17:25 they see land to starboard and take a bearing on a large mountain at ESE 2º S, so they spent the night tacking with much wind, heavy sea and thick fog.
A LAS 17:30 AVISTA LA ISLA DEL SOMBRERO: At 17:30 sights the island of Sombrero.
A LAS 17:30 FONDEA EN LA HABANA. DATOS D: At 17:30 anchors at Havana. Data from dusk or from the day's run.
A LAS 17:30 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CO: At 17:30 hours arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 17:30 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 17:30 hours anchors in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 17:30 VEN PASAR UN ARBOL SECO. TIE: At 17:30 they see a dry tree pass. Hazy weather, skies and horizons overcast. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
A LAS 18 HORAS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 18 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 18 HS SE DEMARCA LA ISLA DE NOROÑO: At 18 hours the island of Noroño is sighted.
A LAS 18 HS. ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVI: At 18 hours arrives at the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 18:00 AVISTA TIERRA. A LAS 4:00 RE: At 18:00 land sighted. At 4:00 recognizes Cape Finisterre. Data from noon or from the day's run.
A LAS 18:00 AVISTAN LA ASCENCION. MEDICI: At 18:00 they sight Ascension. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn.
A LAS 18:00 ENTRA EN PUERTO RICO PARA EN: At 18:00 enters Puerto Rico to deliver the dispatches under sail and puts out again, as she intends to spend the night tacking.
A LAS 18:00 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. DATOS D: At 18:00 anchors at La Coruña. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. French chart.
A LAS 18:00 MARCA LA VIRGEN GORDA: At 18:00 takes a bearing on Virgin Gorda.
A LAS 18:00 MARCA PUNTA MAISI. CARTA FRA: At 18:00 takes a bearing on Punta Maisi. French chart.
A LAS 18:00 SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO EN: At 18:00 they sound and find no bottom at 60 fathoms. Current running with great force to the SE. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 18:30 DEMARCA LA PUNTA DE PUERTO P: At 18:30 takes a bearing on the point of Puerto Plata at 3 leagues. At 6:00 Montecristo is sighted at 4 or 6 leagues. At 11:00 anchors.
A LAS 18:30 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. CARTA F: At 18:30 anchors at La Coruña. French chart.
A LAS 18:30 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. CUARTER: At 18:30 anchors at La Coruña. Spanish quarter-sheet [?].
A LAS 18:30 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 18:30 hours drops anchor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 18:30 MARCA PUNTA MULAS A 3 LEGUAS: At 18:30 takes a bearing on Punta Mulas at 3 leagues. French chart.
A LAS 18:30 SE ECLIPSO UNA TERCERA PARTE: At 18:30 a third of the moon was eclipsed and at 20:30 the eclipse ended.
A LAS 19 HS SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 19 hours anchor is dropped in the port of La Coruña.
At 19 hours anchor is dropped in the port of Montevideo.
At 19:00 sights the island of Salvaje. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter-sheet [?].
A LAS 19:00 HABIENDO TIRADO UN CAÑONAZO: At 19:00, having fired a cannon shot and hoisted the Spanish flag and pennant, she hove to and flew the Portuguese flag. They came within hailing distance and told us it had been 9 days since she left Janeiro, that she was sailing to Benguela on the coast of Africa, and that she was 110 leagues from Cabo Frio, E 1/4 SE of it.
A LAS 19:00 SONDAN PERO NO SACAN NADA CO: At 19:00 they sound but bring up nothing with the lead. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 19:30 EMPEZO A ECLIPSAR LA LUNA: At 19:30 the moon began to be eclipsed.
A LAS 19:30 LES FALTA LA VELA MAYOR DESD: At 19:30 they are missing the mainsail from the clew to the luff [?].
A LAS 20 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVID: At 20 hours arrives at the port of Montevideo.
At 20:00 recognizes the island of Sesarga. Noon data, although some days are from dawn. From 9-2-1767 they are from dawn. The journal begins 17-Dec-1766 because she sailed that day but had to return after being forced back. On 23-Dec she sails definitively.
A LAS 20:00 SONDAN Y HALLAN FONDO DE ARE: At 20:00 they sound and find a bottom of fine sand at 44 fathoms. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 20:00 SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO. LO: At 20:00 they sound and find no bottom. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 20:30 AMENZABA TANTO LA TEMPESTAD: At 20:30 the storm was so threatening that they offer the mainsail, or its value, to Our Lady of Carmen.
A LAS 20:30 FONDEA EN MONTECRISTO. DESCR: At 20:30 anchors at Montecristo. Descriptors from noon or the day's run.
A LAS 21 HS OBSERVAN UNA FIGURA FORMADA: At 21 hours they observe a figure formed by a great glow and a multitude of stars; they make a sketch.
A LAS 21:00 EMPIEZAN A \"ENCONTRAR UNA E: At 21:00 they begin to "find a kind of sargasso different from that of our seas: thick reeds with leaves coming out on both sides, which are round at the tip and wider than at their base, both they and the reeds yellow, and then we saw a white tropicbird that chirped a good deal around the ship. Although whales different from those noted in the journal have been seen, this morning from 8:00 there have been so many that we continually saw 3, 4 and more at a time, some frolicking, others sleeping; we passed near many, but particularly one that did not wake until we had it at a distance of 8 to 12 varas from the gangway, which it did with a great snort and, with great agility, making its turn. They are larger than our whale calves but not the size of those of the northern hemisphere." They find much bottom color and flocks of birds.
A LAS 21:00 ENTRAN EN EL ESTRECHO DE BAN: At 21:00 they enter the Strait of Banca.
A LAS 21:30 FONDEA EN LA BAHIA DE MONTEC: At 21:30 anchors in the Bay of Montecristo.
A LAS 23 HS CONSIGUE DAR FONDO EN EL PUE: At 23 hours manages to anchor in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 23:45 HS DIMOS FONDO EN EL PUERTO: At 23:45 hours we anchored in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 2:00 MURIO 1 INDIO TAPE Y A LAS 10: At 2:00 1 Tape Indian died and at 10:00 they throw him into the water. At 20:00 the wind calmed. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 3,5 DE LA MAÑANA SE VE LA FIGURA D: At 3,5 in the morning the described figure is seen.
A LAS 4 1/2 DE LA TARDE PASÓ 4 MILLAS AL: At 4 1/2 in the afternoon passed 4 miles W of White Roch (White Rock, the journal clarifies).
A LAS 4 DE LA MAÑANA FALTO LA USTAGA DE: At 4 in the morning the topsail halyard [?] parted.
A LAS 4 DE LA MAÑANA SE VIÓ TIERRA AL PA: At 4 in the morning land was seen, apparently Flores, which bore SE, and Corvo somewhat confusedly at ESE by the compass, distance from Flores 8 to 10 leagues.
A LAS 4:30 DE LA MAÑANA AVISTAN TIERRA Y: At 4:30 in the morning they sight land and it was Corvo, bearing S 65º E at about 5 or 6 leagues.
A LAS 5 1/2 ENTRÓ UNA TURBONADA DEL SE D: At 5 1/2 a squall came in from the SE with wind and drizzle.
A LAS 5 1/2 FALLECIÓ EL ARTILLERO DE MAR: At 5 1/2 the sea gunner Gregorio Perez died.
A LAS 5 CHUBASCO Y RODÓ EL VIENTO AL NO,: At 5 a squall, and the wind veered to the NW; nightfall with a bad look, fresh wind, with a light swell from the N and NW; dawn broke mottled with cloud, fresh NE wind, sea from the WNW.
A LAS 5 DE LA MAÑANA ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE: At 5 in the morning arrives at the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 5 DE LA MAÑANA VEN UNA GOLETA EN V: At 5 in the morning they see a schooner to the S. They wanted to come alongside her to get news from Europe, but the wind shifted and the continual squalls prevented it. At noon they lose sight of her. They see a turtle, birds like charruas [?], and a plank about 3 varas long and one wide, full of barnacles.
A LAS 5 FALLECIÓ EL GRUMETE AGUSTIN ROSE: At 5 the ship's boy Agustin Rosete died.
A LAS 5 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA C: At 5 hours anchors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 5 HS VE UNA EMBARCACIÓN QUE PASA P: At 5 hours sees a vessel passing to leeward of the frigate and cannot make her out.
A LAS 5:00 DESCUBREN UNA FUENTE DE TIERR: At 5:00 they discover a [?] of low land and, as day came on, approached the coast. They are heading for the entrance of the Bay of San Julian. At 19:30 they anchor N of a shoal.
A LAS 5:00 LEVAN. A LAS 15:30 CALMO EL V: At 5:00 they weigh anchor. At 15:30 the wind dropped and they anchor. At 17:30 they weigh with a land breeze that dropped at 19:00.
A LAS 5:00 LEVAN. CON LA CALMA DAN FONDO: At 5:00 they weigh anchor. With the calm they anchor.
A LAS 5:00 LEVAN. DESCRIBE LA COSTA. A L: At 5:00 they weigh anchor. Describes the coast. At 20:30 they anchor 4 leagues from land.
A LAS 5:00 LEVAN. TODO EL DIA NAVEGAN CE: At 5:00 they weigh anchor. All day they sail near land. The squall makes them move somewhat away from land without recognizing the Bay of San Julian.
A LAS 5:00 SE HACE A LA VELA DE LA BARRA: At 5:00 sets sail from the bar of Manila.
A LAS 5:30 ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA: At 5:30 arrives at the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 5:30 LEVAN. A LAS 18:00 FONDEAN: At 5:30 they weigh anchor. At 18:00 they anchor.
A LAS 5:30 VEN TIERRAS AL SE QUE PARECIA: At 5:30 they see lands to the SE that looked like islets, having in view those of the previous day at 4 or 5 leagues. They take bearings of them. Corrected longitude 161º 37'.
A LAS 5:30 VEN UNOS ISLOTES Y A LAS 8:30: At 5:30 they see some islets and at 8:30 the land to the ESE, which looked less barren, as they made out 2 or 3 trees and some bonfires that showed it was inhabited. At noon they are 2 leagues from the coast.
A LAS 6 DE LA MAÑANA PARTE DE REGRESO A: At 6 in the morning departs on the return to La Coruña.
A LAS 6 SONDAMOS Y CON 150 BRAZAS NO SE: At 6 we sounded and with 150 fathoms found no bottom, although all the signs were of soundings.
A LAS 6 Y MEDIA DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE: At 6 and a half anchors in the port of Havana.
A LAS 6:00 AVISTAN 1 BERGANTIN EN EL 2º: At 6:00 they sight 1 brigantine in the 2nd quadrant at a distance of 3 leagues, which apparently was sailing to America. The repairs continue.
A LAS 6:00 AVISTAN TIERRA Y RECONOCEN EL: At 6:00 they sight land and recognize the easternmost of the islets of Martin Bazo and Ascension Island at about 11 or 12 leagues.
A LAS 6:00 DESCUBREN UNA ENSENADA. A LAS: At 6:00 they discover an inlet. At 8:30 the wind dropped and they anchored. They discover in the water some swarms of red prawns or shrimp. They called the inlet San Pedro. They anchor at 19:00 when the wind dropped.
A LAS 6:00 FENECIO DE ESCORBUTO JOSE SAM: At 6:00 José Sam, the crew's bloodletter, died of scurvy. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn.
A LAS 6:00 SE HACEN A LA VELA. NO SE PUD: At 6:00 they set sail. No observation could be made. Measurement and data from nightfall or from the day's run; some days it is described at dawn.
A LAS 6:00, HABIENDO ACLARADO ALGO EL TI: At 6:00, the weather having cleared somewhat, they thought they saw land to the N and came upon a very large patch of birds.
A LAS 6:30 LLEGA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO: At 6:30 arrives at the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 7 (DE LA NOCHE) UNA GRANDE TURBONA: At 7 (at night) a great squall to the SW (...) a good deal of rain.
A LAS 7 DE LA MAÑANA SE DA FONDO EN EL A: At 7 in the morning anchor is dropped at the moorage of the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 7 DIMOS VISTA A LA TIERRA QUE ERA: At 7 we sighted land, which was the coast of the Río de la Plata.
A LAS 7 ENTRÓ LA VENTOLINA DEL N: At 7 the light breeze came in from the N.
A LAS 7 HS. PARTE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑ: At 7 hours departs from the port of La Coruña, heading for Montevideo.
A LAS 7:00 SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO EN 1: At 7:00 they sound and find no bottom at 100 fathoms. They see some sea lions and some dead crabs coming from Cabo de San Antonio with the waters running to the SW. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 8 1/2 SE AVISTÓ LA TIERRA. OTRO PU: At 8 1/2 land was sighted. Another reference point: Isla Alboredo at NW 1/4 N, distance 6 leagues.
A LAS 8 3/4 FALLECIÓ EL ARTILLERO DE MAR: At 8 3/4 the sea gunner Fernando Cano died.
A LAS 8 DE LA MAÑANA SE DIO EL SACROSANT: At 8 in the morning the most holy viaticum was given to 6 sailors afflicted with scurvy. In the morning gulls and little white doves have been seen.
A LAS 8 ENTRÓ LA VENTOL. POR EL SO: At 8 the light breeze came in from the SW.
A LAS 8 HS DAN FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MON: At 8 hours they anchor in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 8 HS, ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑ: At 8 hours, arrives at the port of La Coruña.
At 8 a flock of dolphins was seen.
A LAS 8 SONDAN 63 BRAZAS DE AGUA, FONDO: At 8 they sound 63 fathoms of water, bottom of oozy sand. They are heading for Cabo Deseado.
A LAS 8:00 DESCUBREN POR LA PROA UN CASC: At 8:00 they discover ahead the hull of a vessel, which they took for a reef. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 8:00 DESEMBOCAN EL CANAL DE BAHAMA: At 8:00 they come out of the Bahama Channel. Dutch chart.
A LAS 8:00 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO. MEDICI: At 8:00 anchors at Puerto Rico. Measurement from noon or from the day's run except the descriptors, which are from nightfall.
A LAS 8:00 LEVAN. FONDEAN A LAS 15:00 PO: At 8:00 they weigh anchor. They anchor at 15:00 because of the calm and a contrary current, at 18:00 they weigh and at 20:00 anchor again 2 1/2 leagues from the coast.
A LAS 8:30 FONDEAN AL CALMAR EL VIENTO E: At 8:30, the wind having dropped, they anchor in an inlet. They see some swarms of red prawns or shrimp. They weigh at 9:00 but anchor again to explore the numerous sandbanks. They call the inlet San Pedro. They sail very close to land until 19:00, when the wind dropped, and anchor. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 9 (DE LA NOCHE) POR ESTAR BIEN FRE: At 9 (at night), the breeze being very fresh with a bad look (...) following the swell from the NE.
A LAS 9 (NOCHE) SE VIERON RELÁMPAGOS Y C: At 9 (night) lightning was seen and continued to increase (...) weather with a bad look, some thunder. (...) The wind was very variable the rest of the night, with gusts and lulls (...) horrible look of the lightning (...) at 2 1/4 (...) the wind was very fresh and a lot of rain fell before and after. The sea was not disturbed and dawn broke thus with a bad look, thunder and lightning, which dissipated with the north wind that settled in at 6 (early morning).
A LAS 9 HS ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDE: At 9 hours arrives at the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 9 HS PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO A LA CORU: At 9 hours departs from Montevideo for La Coruña.
A LAS 9 HS SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE L: At 9 hours anchor is dropped in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 9 HS. DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 9 hours drops anchor in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS 9:00 AMAINO EL VIENTO Y CAMBIO AL: At 9:00 the wind eased and shifted to the NW. At 20:00 a furious SW wind assailed them, which put them in obvious danger of being wrecked.
A LAS 9:00 CALMO EL VIENTO Y FONDEAN. PO: At 9:00 the wind dropped and they anchor. Shortly after they weigh, heading for the port of San Julian, coasting. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A LAS 9:00 FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA. MEDICION: At 9:00 anchors at La Coruña. Measurement from noon or from the day's run, although there are many days without data.
A LAS 9:00 FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO Y A LAS: At 9:00 anchors at Puerto Rico and at 12:00 sets sail.
A LAS 9:00 FONDEARON CERCA DE LA COSTA,: At 9:00 they anchored near the coast, then weighed and coasted, heading for the port of San Julian.
A LAS 9:00 HS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE M: At 9:00 hours drops anchor in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 9:00 VEN 1 PAJARO DE TIERRA SEMEJA: At 9:00 they see 1 land bird similar to the thrush, and during the day's run martinplacas [?], shearwaters and carneros [?].
A LAS 9:30 DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MONT: At 9:30 drops anchor in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS 9:30 HS AMARRA EN EL PUERTO DE LA: At 9:30 hours moors in the port of La Coruña.
A LAS DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDE: At [?] drops anchor in the port of Montevideo.
A LAS SIETE EMPRENDIMOS LA CAZA A UNA EM: At seven we gave chase to a vessel sighted in the 3rd quadrant, which when we were near her flew the Dutch flag, and we recognized her as a storeship [?], which was not hailed because the wind had slackened. Log-line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms [?]. Half-minute glass of 30 sec. First point of departure on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4 ed. 66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
A LO LEJOS SE AVISTA UNA EMBARCACIÓN: In the distance a vessel is sighted.
A MEDIANOCHE CORTARON EL ECUADOR ANDANDO: At midnight they crossed the equator, making 5 miles.
A MEDIO DÍA SE DEMARCÓ LA SIERRA DE TARQ: At noon the Sierra de Tarquino (Turquino?) was sighted bearing NW 4º N, distance from the coast facing north, 8 leagues
A MEDIODIA DEMARCA BARACOA Y LA PUNTA DE: At noon takes bearings of Baracoa and the Punta del Guaico. At sunset a bearing was taken of Punta de Moa.
A MEDIODIA MONTAN EL BAJO DE LAS HORMIGA: At noon they round the shoal of Las Hormigas.
A MEDIODIA PASAN POR 1 BAJO A 6 LEGUAS D: At noon they pass over 1 shoal 6 leagues from the coast, which the Prince de la Feville had already described in his voyage of the South Sea. They anchor at 19:00 when the wind dropped and the current was carrying them, having the Isla de los Reyes to the NW at a distance of 3 leagues. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
A MEDIODIA REBASAN EL CABO CORRIENTES EN: At noon they pass Cabo Corrientes, heading for La Tortuga.
A MEDIODIA RECALAN SOBRE EL PARALELO DE: At noon they make landfall on the parallel of the island of Santa Elena. Makes some observations about the island and its position. Describes it.
A MEDIODÍA (...) TPO CLARO, VTO FRESQUIT: At noon (...) clear weather, freshish wind, horizon and sky streaked with cloud (...) nightfall with the horizons and sky streaked with cloud. Scattered [?], the sea from the wind and a freshish easterly. Dawn as at nightfall.
A MEDIODÍA (...) TPO. CALIMOSO, CIELOS Y: At noon (...) hazy weather, skies and horizons streaked with cloud, the sea from the wind and E calm. (...) Nightfall and dawn in the same terms as at noon.
A MEDIODÍA (...) TPO. CALIMOSO, CIELOY H: At noon (...) hazy weather, sky and horizons heavy, the sea from the SE. Nightfall in the same manner. Dawn as at nightfall, with fresh wind from the SE 1/4 S.
A MEDIODÍA (...) VTO FRESQUITO, LA MAR D: At noon (...) freshish wind, the sea from the [?], sky and horizon streaked with cloud. Nightfall and dawn in equal terms.
A MEDIODÍA CIELOS Y HORIZ. OFUSCOS, MAR: At noon sky and horizons dark, sea from the NW and freshish wind (...) nightfall, sky and horizon, sea and wind as at noon (...) dawn, sky and horizon as stated, the sea from the W and fresh wind.
A MEDIODÍA HICE CORRECIÓN CON EL MERIDIA: At noon I made a correction with the meridian.
A MEDIODÍA QUEDAMOS CON (...) CIELO ACEL: At noon we were left with (...) sky streaked with cloud, horizons dark, the sea heavy from the [?] and a fresh easterly. Nightfall and dawn as at noon.
A MEDIODÍA SE DEMARCÓ LA BOCA DEL PUERTO: At noon the mouth of the port of Guantánamo was marked bearing N 1/4 NE, distance 4 leagues.
A MEDIODÍA TUVE 7' DE DIFERENCIA MÁS AL: At noon I had a difference of 7' more to the S from the observation. I corrected with the fantasy meridian.
A MIDI, LA TERRE LA PLUS À VUE AU N., RE: At noon, the land most in view to the N bore N29E, and the one furthest west bore N65W. At 5 leagues.
A MIDI, LE 6, LE VOLCAN RESTAIT AU N38O: At noon, on the 6th, the volcano bore N38W.
A MIDY MOUILLÉ A LA RADE DU PORT AU PRIN: At noon anchored in the roads of Port au Prince.
A PARTIR DE AQUÍ PARECEN HABER LLEGADO A: From here they seem to have arrived at their destination, and next there are narratives about Indians, about the history of San Lorenzo, and a vocabulary of the language of the Nuca Indians.
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA COMIENZA A USAR LA: From this day the longitude of Banguey is used
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA DEJA DE DARSE LA LO: From this day the longitude of Tenerife is no longer given and only the longitude of San Bernardino is used
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA DEJA DE DARSE LAS P: From this day positions are no longer given and there are even no tables, until 13 February
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA DEJA DE DARSE POSIC: From this day positions are no longer given and there are no tables, until 15 May.
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA DEJA DE HABER TABLA: From this day there are no tables and no position data given, until 31 March 1777.
From this day there are no tables and no position data, until 8 August, when Montevideo is reached and this log ends
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA EMPIEZA A HACERSE E: From this day the survey of the Strait of Magellan begins, and there are no tables or position data until 18 March 1786.
A PARTIR DE ESTE DÍA NO HAY TABLAS HASTA: From this day there are no tables until 3 April. It seems that on these days they are anchored and provisioning the ship.
A PRTIR DE ESTE DÍA ENTRAN EN UN ARCHIPI: From this day they enter an archipelago of islands and there are no tables, although position data are given in the description of the weather, and sometimes the course.
A QUATRE HEURES DU MATIN APPAREILLÉ POUR: At four in the morning weighed anchor to get out to the open from the port. At eight in the morning anchored in 46 fathoms
A QUATRE HEURES DU MATIN APPAREILLÉ. ET: At four in the morning weighed anchor. And at ten o'clock anchored, waiting for the tide, in 15 fathoms, muddy bottom.
A SIX HEURES 1/2 DU SOIR, LE 19, MOUILLÉ: At half past six in the evening, on the 19th, anchored in 25 fathoms, sandy bottom. At 6 o'clock, weighed anchor
A UNE HEURE DE L'APRÈS-MIDI, MOUILLÉ PAR: At one in the afternoon, anchored in 5 and a half fathoms, muddy bottom
A UNE HEURE ET DEMIE DU MATIN, VU DES BR: At half past one in the morning, saw breakers very close to us, which we took bearings of from the N. to the S.W. by 1'O. [?]
A VECES REPETIDAS Y CRECIDAS NEVADAS: At times repeated and heavy snowfalls
AAN DE HAND VAN BEREKENING VAN DE AFSTAN: By calculation of the distance between the sun and the moon it is concluded that one was 1°3' too far east.
AANGEHOUDEN DOOR ENGELS OORLOGSSCHIP. WA: Stopped by an English warship. They were looking for two Dutch (?) ships
AANGESTELD LUITENANT FRANS VAN VLAANDERE: Lieutenant Frans van Vlaanderen appointed captain-lieutenant. Captain-lieutenant Cornelis Clement deceased, and the second lieutenant Willem Skoerman [appointed] lieutenant.
AANGEZIEN HET SCHIP DREIGT TE ZINKEN WOR: Since the ship is in danger of sinking, part of the cargo is thrown overboard. The barometer and thermometer were destroyed by the storm
AANHOUDEND STORMWEER MET DIKKE LUCHT EN: Continuous stormy weather with thick sky and high, wild sea
AANKOMST AFRIKAANSE KUST, BEGIN INHANDEL: Arrival at the African coast, start of the trading period.
AANKOMST OP DE GREINKUST. BEGIN INHANDEL: Arrival at the Grain Coast. Start of the trading period.
AANLEGGENDE STORM, ONWEER IN DE EW. BIJ: Setting-in storm, thunder in the EW [?]. As the high water ebbs, the current decreases.
AANMERKINGEN OVER HET BESTEK EN DE STROO: Remarks on the dead reckoning and the current in the Florida Channel
AANNEMEND TOT DICHTGEREEFDE MZK, AFNEMEN: Increasing to close-reefed topsail breeze, decreasing to single-reefed topsail breeze
AANNEMENDE HARDE WIND TOT DUBBELD GEREEF: Increasing strong wind to double-reefed topsail breeze
AANNEMENDE HARDE WIND TOT STORM, DAARNA: Increasing strong wind to storm, then shift to the SW, decreasing wind
AANNEMENDE TOT STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILS: Increasing to stiff reefed topsail breeze
AANTAL MILITAIREN STAPT OVER OP ANDERE S: A number of soldiers transfer to other ships.
AANTAL ZIEKEN NEEMT NOG STEEDS TOE. NU 6: The number of sick continues to rise. Now 60, mostly high fevers and severe pain in the joints.
The number of sick is increasing.
The number of sick is decreasing somewhat.
AANVULLING OP DE VORM BEWOLKING: BEND ZO: Addition to the form of cloud cover: [?] SE.
AANVULLING OP DE VORM BEWOLKING:\"AFWL\": Addition to the form of cloud cover: "AFWL"
AANZICHTSKAARTJE AMSTERDAM, MET BESCHRIJ: Picture postcard of Amsterdam, with a description of how it lies on the French and English charts
ABUNDANCIA DE PAJAROS DE TODAS CLASES Y: Abundance of birds of all kinds and some patches of sargassum. Skies and horizons dark, snowing. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
ABUNDANCIA DE PAJAROS DE TODAS CLASES. C: Abundance of birds of all kinds. Skies and horizons closed in by thick drizzle. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
ABUNDANCIA DE PAJAROS GABIOTONES CORBAS: Abundance of birds, gulls, cormorants, [?] and 1 seal. Skies and horizons with broken cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
ACABAN DE PASAR LIBRES DE CORRIENTES CON: They have just passed clear of currents, with very dirty yellow water
ACHTER LANDKENMERK KAAP FRIO STAAT TUSSE: After longitude, the landmark Cape Frio is in parentheses (follow no. 55 as the average). Saw at 2 o'clock land between WSW and NWbW. At 5:15 had Cape Frio due north, the observations taken an hour before for those chronometers reduced to this time [?]
ACHTERGEBLEVEN MATROOS, FRANS VAN HEYNIN: Sailor Frans van Heyningen, who had stayed behind, put in irons. 1 cup [of drink] run out.
ACHTERIN JOURNAAL VANGLIJST, 182,5 VATE: Behind in the log: harpoon list, 182.5 barrels of blubber, 15 small pipes, 42 [?]
Squally, sky and horizon with heavy swell.
ACLARADO EL HORIZ. (...) ANOCHEC. CIELKO: The horizon cleared (...) at nightfall. Sky clear but with the appearance of wind, sea from the N and W heavy (...) at dawn with the sky clear and a freshening wind.
ADELBORST 1E KLAS J. EYMER IN ARREST WEG: Midshipman 1st class J. Eymer under arrest for sleeping on watch.
ADELBORST CHARLES LOUIS CONSTANTIJN VAN: Midshipman Charles Louis Constantijn van Schuler becomes titular lieutenant
ADM_177_1230_0239 T/M _0248 ZIJN PLAATJE: ADM_177_1230_0239 to _0248 are pictures of islands. Many soundings of the depth.
ADVIERTEN QUE HACEN MEDIA PULGADA DE AGU: They note that they are making half an inch of water by the sternpost on the starboard side
AFGESTRAFT MATROOS SEIJMONDS EN KNAMP WG: Sailors Seijmonds and Knamp punished for sleeping on lookout
AFGESTRAFT MET 12 SLAGEN MET HET HANDDEG: Light sailor Tippens and the boys Thepen and Drencke punished with 12 blows with the hand cutlass for immorality
AFGESTRAFT MET 12 SLAGEN VH HANDDEGEN MA: Sailor Tieman punished with 12 blows with the hand cutlass for not following orders and improper tone
AFGESTRAFT MET 24 HANDSLAGEN (?) MATROZE: Sailors Stronkhorst, Schuttig, Kniep, Fijke, [and] De Ligter punished with 24 blows (?) for immorality and theft from the … The marine A. Collet, for lack of canes, with 30 blows (?)
AFGESTRAFT MET 24 SLAGEN MET HANDVLAGE (: Sailors Fijke, Stronkhorst, Van Wijck, De Ligter and Komper punished with 24 blows with the [?] for repeated immorality
AFGESTRAFT MET 60 SLAGEB MET HANDAGEN DD: Sailor 2nd class J Kenis punished with 60 blows with the hand cutlass for having robbed his comrades.
AFGESTRAFT MET SLAGEN DE JONGEN J. FELCH: The boy J. Felchzer (?) punished with blows for wantonness and malice, committed by deliberately destroying and damaging the belongings of one of the other boys
AFGESTRAFT WEGENS DIEFSTAL DE SCHEPSJONG: The ship's boy Bruska punished with 64 blows for theft.
AFGESTRAFT WEGENS LIEDERLIJKHEID DE MARI: Marine 1st class J. Koogwinkel punished for debauchery.
AFGEVAREN PLAATS VOLGENS VERBETERD BESTE: Sailed position according to corrected dead reckoning: south latitude 8 degrees 1 minute and longitude 2 degrees 10 minutes
AFGEVAREN ZUIDERBREEDTE 40°14'. AFGEVARE: Sailed south latitude 40°14'. Sailed longitude west of Greenwich 9°56'
AFHOUDENDE NAAR PLYMOUTH. ANKERDEN OP 9: Standing off toward Plymouth. Anchored in 9 fathoms. Sailed again from Plymouth to sea. (It is not clear on which date exactly; the logbook continues on 1 Aug.)
AFNEMEND TOT STIL IN DE VOORMIDDAG EEN S: Decreasing to calm, in the forenoon a ship in the NW.
AFNEMENDE KOELTE TOT LABBER EN STIL: Decreasing breeze to slack and calm
AFSCHOONEND SOMS LIGT BUIJIG MET REGEN: Clearing, sometimes light, squally with rain

AFSTAND TUSSEN ZON EN MAAN. LENGTE BEPAL: Distance between sun and moon. Longitude determination

AGREGADO A LA MULTITUD DE PAJAROS AVISTA: Added to the multitude of birds sighted
AJUSTA EL RELOJ. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL ME: Adjusts the clock. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn
AJUSTAN EL RELOJ POR LA MAÑANA. MEDICION: They adjust the clock in the morning. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn
AJUSTAN EL RELOJ. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL M: They adjust the clock. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn
AJUSTAN Y ARREGLAN EL RELOJ. REFLEXION A: They adjust and repair the clock. Reflection on the methods of measuring longitude and other parameters. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn
AJUSTE DEL RELOJ. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL M: Adjustment of the clock. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run; often the descriptors are from dawn
AL 9 MAN IN DE KOOI MET KWADE DIKKE BENE: All 9 men in the bunk with bad swollen legs because of the heavy weather
AL AMANECER AVISTA LA ISLA DE TIERRA DE: At dawn sights the island of Tierra de Juan Fernandez. "Error in the chronometer's longitude at E 12º48'39''
AL AMANECER AVISTAN 1 BERGANTIN AL NE QU: At dawn they sight 1 brigantine to the NE that was following about SSW. At 14:00 weed passed and at dawn land birds were caught. Cape San Vicente bears 95 miles at N 81º E
AL AMANECER AVISTAN CABO SAN VICENTE Y 3: At dawn they sight Cape San Vicente and 3 vessels. They take a bearing on the Sierra de Monchique
At dawn they sight the island of La Palma. Measurement and data from noon, with fewer descriptors, which are usually from nightfall. They follow the Dutch chart
AL AMANECER ESTABAN TOLDADOS CIELO Y HOR: At dawn sky and horizon were overcast and the sea smooth
AL AMANECER ESTAN A 7 LEGUAS DE TIERRA: At dawn they are 7 leagues from land
AL AMANECER SE DEDUCE LA VARIACIÓN DE LA: At dawn the compass variation is deduced as 6º NW. Sun's meridian: 86º 28´
AL AMANECER SE ECHO AL AGUA EL CADAVER D: At dawn the body of the dead squad corporal was thrown into the water
AL AMANECER SE HACEN A LA VELA EN VUELTA: At dawn they set sail back to the port of La Coruña
AL AMANECER SE REGISTRAN 2 VELAS DE LA V: At dawn 2 sails are sighted on the opposite course, one bearing S and the other E. Cape San Vicente bears 154 miles at S 86,5º E
AL AMANECER SONDAN EN 46 BRAZAS DE FONDO: At dawn they sound in 46 fathoms, brown sand. They sail near the coast looking for the entrance to San Julian Bay. Describes the inlet that the coast makes. At 19:30 the wind dropped and they anchor in 20 fathoms. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
AL AMANECER TIENEN UNA FRAGATA A LA VIST: At dawn they have a frigate in sight to the WSW "which, although we recognized her as a Portuguese merchantman, at 8 hoisted French colours and we replied with the English". At sunset the frigate was about to be lost from sight
AL AMANECER, LA ESCUADRA SIN VERSE, EXCE: At dawn, the squadron out of sight, except the S. Julián.
AL ANOCHECER FUE CAYENDO EL VTO Y A LAS: At nightfall the wind fell and at 10 it was almost calm, various light breezes came (...) the wind having steadied from the WSW (...) at dawn hazy horizons with some harmless squalls that brought only snow, the wind was fresh-ish.
AL ANOCHECER SE CARGARON LOS HORIZ. Y TU: At nightfall the horizons became heavy and we had some small squalls with some rain; wind more or less light and variable and at 9 1/2 everything cleared and the wind freshened. Dawn the same
AL ANOCHECER SE EMPEZÓ A LLAMAR EL VTO A: At nightfall the wind began to call to the W (...) it kept freshening (...) some squalls came with gusts of wind. At dawn cloudy sky, squally horizon, fresh wind and sea from the NW and SW.
AL ANOCHECER SONDAN EN 48 BRAZAS. LOS DA: At nightfall they sound in 48 fathoms. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
AL E DE LA ISLA BUENAVISTA (EN LAS DE CA: To the east of the island of Buenavista (in the Cape Verde Islands), corrected to the west, distance 37 leagues. Measurement and data from noon, with fewer descriptors, which are usually from nightfall. They follow the Dutch chart
AL MARGEN \"BERIL DE LA SONDA EN EL CABO: In the margin "Beril of the sounding at the Cape of Good Hope". They had many birds in view, especially the velvet sleeves, a sure sign of being in soundings, but the colour of the sea also indicated it.
AL MEDIO DÌA ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORU: At noon arrives at the port of La Coruña
AL MEDIO DÍA ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVI: At noon arrives at the port of Montevideo
AL MEDIO DÍA FONDEA EN CANARIAS PARA DEJ: At noon anchors in the Canaries to leave mail, remains on the island until 23 July.

It has been taken into consideration and found good, in case the breeze, which is at present calm, comes again from the NE, to set sail now in God's name.
