ANOCHECIO CON CIELOS Y HORIZONTES CON CE: Nightfall with skies and horizons with brown cloud patches
Nightfall with skies and horizons with scattered cloud patches
ANOCHECIO CON CIELOS Y HORIZONTES NUBULO: Nightfall with skies and horizons cloudy
ANOCHECIÓ ACHUBASCADO, CON EL VIENTO O F: Nightfall squally, with the wind W fresh; at 5 we began to experience squalls; at 8 wind SSE fresh; some lightning in the 2nd quadrant; dawn looked bad, wind S fresh, heavy sea
ANOCHECIÓ ACHUBASCADO, VIENTO ENE FRESCO: Nightfall squally, wind ENE fresh; during the night I had some squalls; dawn squally, wind NE fresh and heavy sea
ANOCHECIÓ ATURBONADO CON CELAJERÍA DOBLE: Nightfall threatening squalls with double cloud patches and sea from the NW (...) dawn sky and horizons laden, fresh wind and sea from the WSW.
ANOCHECIÓ AZELAJADO AMANECIÓ ACHUBASCADO: Nightfall with cloud patches, dawn squally.
ANOCHECIÓ AZELAJADO AMANECIÓ CLARO: Nightfall with cloud patches, dawn clear
ANOCHECIÓ AZELAJADO, VIENTO DICHO Y MAR: Nightfall with cloud patches, aforesaid wind and choppy sea from the same, dawn squally and fresh breeze, which throughout the day's run has stayed from the NE to the ENE
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO HORIZONTES CON ARR: Nightfall clear sky, horizons with cloud banks and thick cloud patches, wind almost calm and [?] sea from the SW and W (...) dawn with horizons squally from the SSW to the NW and the rest with scattered cloud patches, dull and heavy seas from the W and S and the wind calm.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO Y HORIZONTES AZELA: Nightfall clear sky and horizons with cloud patches, fresh breeze from the N and small swell from the N, dawn sky and horizons with cloud patches, fresh breeze, small swell from the N
Nightfall clear sky and horizons with cloud patches, little wind and small swell from the N, and in the night the wind freshened somewhat, dawn misty, moderate wind, small swell from the N
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO, HORIZ. ATURBONADO: Nightfall clear sky, horizon threatening squalls, choppy sea from the SE and from the wind and fresh easterly (...) dawn clear sky, horizon with scattered cloud patches, sea from the wind and easterly moderate.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO, HORIZ. CON CELAJ,: Nightfall clear sky, horizon with thick cloud patches, swell from the SW and fresh breeze (...) dawn as at nightfall.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO, HORIZONTES CON ZE: Nightfall clear sky, horizons with clear cloud patches.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO, LOS HORIZONTES CA: Nightfall clear sky, the horizons laden.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CLARO, Y HORIZONTES FOSC: Nightfall clear sky, and dim horizons, this night several squalls were experienced, dawn squally, aforesaid wind and sea from the same, the squalls continued, the winds have stayed from the E to the ESE
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO CON CELAJ. SUELTA, HORIZ: Nightfall sky with scattered cloud patches, horizon threatening squalls, sea from the wind and fresh easterly. At 11 a strong flash of lightning was seen to the NE.(...) dawn clear sky, horizon of dark cloud patches, sea from the wind and fresh easterly.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO TOLDADO , HORIZ. OFUSCOS: Nightfall sky overcast, horizon obscured, heavy sea from the SW and the wind moderate (...) dawn sky and horizon obscured, sea from the SW and the wind moderate.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZ. CERRADOS DE NIE: Nightfall sky and horizon closed in with snow, fresh wind and heavy sea from the SE (...) dawn sky and horizon laden with dark cloud patches, sea from the SE and S and fresh wind.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZ. CON CELAJ OSCUR: Nightfall sky and horizon with dark cloud patches, choppy sea from the SW and NW and fresh breeze (...) dawn sky and horizon with dark cloud patches, heavy sea from the NW and SW and fresh breeze.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZ. CON CELAJ. OSCU: Nightfall sky and horizon with dark cloud patches, choppy sea from the SW and NW and fresh breeze (...) dawn sky and horizon with dark cloud patches, heavy sea from the NW and SW and fresh breeze.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZ. CON GARÚA, VTO: Nightfall sky and horizon with drizzle, wind from the SW fresh in gusts (...) dawn clear sky, horizon with cloud patches, heavy sea from the SW and the wind from the SW fresh.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZ. TOLDADOS, VTO B: Nightfall sky and horizon overcast, moderate wind and sea from the wind (...) dawn sky and horizon overcast, and snow falling, heavy sea from the SW and SE, fresh breeze.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELO Y HORIZONTES ATRUVONADOS: Nightfall sky and horizons threatening squalls, dawn sky and horizons laden.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELOS Y HORIZ. TOLDADOS, LA M: Nightfall skies and horizon overcast, sea from the wind and fresh easterly. At 7 3/4 a squall (...) dawn sky and horizon closed in with drizzle, fresh wind, sea from the SW.
ANOCHECIÓ CIELOS Y ORIZONTES CON ZELAJER: Nightfall skies and horizons with clear cloud patches
Nightfall skies and horizons with clear cloud patches.
Nightfall skies and horizons with scattered cloud patches
Nightfall skies and horizons with scattered cloud patches.
ANOCHECIÓ CLARO, VIENTO BONANCIBLE, LA M: Nightfall clear, moderate wind, swell from the W, at 2 it fell calm, and at 2 1/2 the moderate wind came in from the NE, dawn clear except for the S part, where there were cloud patches, wind NE moderate, smooth sea
ANOCHECIÓ CON EL CIELO AZELAJADO Y LOS H: Nightfall with the sky cloudy and horizons laden, aforesaid wind, dawn in the same terms, throughout the day's run the wind has stayed from the ESE to the SE
ANOCHECIÓ CON EL CIELO Y HORIZONTES TOLD: Nightfall with sky and horizons overcast, smooth sea, fresh breeze (...) at 12 1/2 the wind freshened (...) dawn with horizons and sky covered in thick drizzle, the wind less fresh and some sea from it. The wind kept dropping. Note: during this and other logs there is talk of "closed in with garúa", "thick garúa", "garúa falling", etc. I have taken it as drizzle, according to the American meaning, but perhaps it should be taken as fog, as the RAE dictionary defines it
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS CIELOS ACELAJADOS, LOS: Nightfall with skies cloudy, horizons from the S to the W threatening squalls, sea from the SW and fresh wind (...) dawn sky overcast, horizons squally, sea from the SW and NW and fresh wind.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS CIELOS Y ORIZONTES BRI: Nightfall with skies and horizons breezy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS CIELOS Y ORIZONTES CAL: Nightfall with skies and horizons hazy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS CIELOS Y ORIZONTES CLA: Nightfall with skies and horizons clear
Nightfall with skies and horizons clear.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS CIELOS Y ORIZONTES OFU: Nightfall with skies and horizons obscured.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS HORIZONTES ACELAJADOS: Nightfall with horizons cloudy toward the 4th quarter, moderate wind. Smooth sea. Dawn in calm, horizons threatening squalls with some sea from the NW. At 5 1/2 in the morning, wind SSW, which freshened, with squalls. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms. Half-minute glass of 30 sec. First point of departure on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4th ed. 66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS HORIZONTES AZELAJADOS,: Nightfall with horizons with cloud patches, wind N moderate, at 5 wind NE, dawn clear sky and horizons with cloud patches, moderate wind and small swell from the N
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS HORIZONTES CARGADOS EN: Nightfall with horizons laden in calm with heavy sea from the ENE, at 8 the wind veered to the WNW, dawn the sky clear and the horizon with cloud patches, the wind NW fresh
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS HORIZONTES OBSCUROS, V: Nightfall with dark horizons, aforesaid wind and sea from the NE, dawn in the same terms, throughout the day's run the wind has stayed from the E to the ESE
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ACELAJADOS A: Nightfall with the horizons cloudy, dawn with the horizons clouded over
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ACHUBASCADOS: Nightfall with the horizons squally, dawn with the horizons cloudy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ALGO ACELAJA: Evening came with the horizons somewhat cloudy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ASELAJADOS: Evening came with the horizons cloudy
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ATURBONADOS: Evening came with the horizons squally
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES AZELAJADOS: Evening came with the horizons cloudy
Evening came with the horizons cloudy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES CALIMOSOS: Evening came with the horizons hazy
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES CALIMOSOS AM: Evening came with the horizons hazy; morning came with the horizons dark
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES CARGADOS: Evening came with the horizons heavy
Evening came with the horizons heavy.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES CLAROS: Evening came with the horizons clear
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES NUBLADOS: Evening came with the horizons clouded
Evening came with the horizons clouded.
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES OBSCUROS: Evening came with the horizons dark
ANOCHECIÓ CON LOS ORIZONTES ZERRADOS: Evening came with the horizons closed in
ANOCHECIÓ CON NINGUNA APARIENCIA DE VIEN: Evening came with no sign of wind; at 2 with a squall a light breeze set in from the S; morning came cloudy, the light breeze and the sea from the WNW continuing; at 7 a weak squall
ANOCHECIÓ DE MAR CARIZ, CON MAR DEL S Y: Evening came with a threatening look [?], with sea from the S and wind from the same quarter; at 10 heavy sea and gusty wind with squalls; morning came in the same state as the evening
ANOCHECIÓ ESTANDO EL CIELO CON CELAGERÍA: Evening came with the sky having scattered cloud streaks, the horizons squally, the sea from the wind heavy and the wind very fresh (...) morning came with sky and horizons having thick, dark cloud streaks, wind very fresh and considerable sea.
ANOCHECIÓ ESTANDO LOS HORIZONTES Y EL CI: Evening came with the horizons and the sky heavy, wind moderate and little sea from it.(...) Morning came with the same look as the evening and the wind fresh.
ANOCHECIÓ FRESCO EL VTO, CIELO CLARO, HO: Evening came with the wind fresh, sky clear, horizons with cloud banks and brown cloud streaks, and little sea. Morning came the same.(...) In the morning the wind has been fresher with some sea and the horizons have been very smoky.
ANOCHECIÓ TOLDADO, VIENTO SO FRESQUITO,: Evening came overcast, wind SW lightly fresh, and small sea from the NW; at 3 lightning began in that quarter; morning came squally; at 7 a squall came in from the NW
ANOCHECIÓ TOLDADO, VIENTO Y MAR DICHA, A: Evening came overcast, wind and sea as stated; at 1 wind WSW; morning came cloudy, said wind fresh with small sea; at 7 a squall came in from that quarter
Evening and morning came the same.
ANOTA EL AVISTAMIENTO DE NUMEROSAS AVES: Notes the sighting of numerous birds (gannets, pelicans, etc.), talks about them
ANOTA LA POSICION DE LA ISLA SEGÚN LA OB: Notes the position of the island according to the observation taken on the afternoon of the 10th, the noon of the 12th and the afternoon of the 13th
ANOTA LA RECALADA A PUERTO ZAPATA A LAS: Notes the landfall at Puerto Zapata at 16:30 and makes an examination of the position of this island in relation to Manila
ANOTACIONES DE RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VIE: Notes of course and wind direction of the afternoon. Course and wind direction of noon / other general references
ANTES DE AMANECER ENTRA VIENTO FRESCO DE: Before dawn a fresh wind from the SSW comes in, raising a lot of sea
APAREILLAGE DE SAINT PIERRE: Getting under way from Saint Pierre
APAREILLER DE PORT LEONIDE: To get under way from Port Leonide
APAREILLÉ DE L'ISLE D'AIX: Got under way from L'Isle d'Aix
Got under way from L'Isle d'Aix.
APAREILLÉ DE LA RADE DE BREST: Got under way from the roadstead of Brest
APAREILLÉ DE LA RADE DE LA LEOGANE A 4 H: Got under way from the roadstead of La Leogane at 4 in the morning. Anchored in the roadstead of Port au Prince at 4.
APAREILLÉ DE LA RADE DU CAP A 5 HS DU MA: Got under way from the roadstead of the Cap at 5 in the morning
APAREILLÉ DE PORT DESBARQUE POUR LA MART: Got under way from Port Desbarque for Martinique
APAREILLÉ DE SAINT PIERRE: Got under way from Saint Pierre
APAREILLÉ DE TOBAGO. MOUILLÉ DANS LA BAY: Got under way from Tobago. Anchored in the bay of Fort Royal of Martinique
APAREILLÉ DE VERGEROU. MOUILLÉ DANS LA R: Got under way from Vergerou. Anchored in the roadstead of Ile d'Aix. Got under way
APAREILLÉ DU FORT ROYAL. MOUILLÉ DANS CU: Got under way from Fort Royal. Anchored in Cul de Sac du Fort Royal
APAREILLÉ DU PORT DAUPHIN: Got under way from Port Dauphin
APAREILLÉ EN L'ISLE D'AIX: Got under way at L'Isle d'Aix
APAREILLÉ ET DÉPART DU LA BARRE DE CAYON: Got under way and departure from the bar of Cayonere
APAREILLÉ POUR L'ISLE DE RÉ: Got under way for L'Isle de Ré
APAREILLÉ. MOUILLÉ AU FORT ROYAL DE LA M: Got under way. Anchored at Fort Royal of Martinique
APAREILLÉ. MOUILLÉ AU PORT LOUIS: Got under way. Anchored at Port Louis
APAREILLÉ. MOUILLÉ DANS CUL DE SAC DU FO: Got under way. Anchored in Cul de Sac du Fort Royal
APAREILLÉ. MOUILLÉ DANS LA GRAND RADE DE: Got under way. Anchored in the great roadstead of Fort Royal
APAREILLÉDE LA RADE DE LOUISBOURG POUR R: Got under way from the roadstead of Louisbourg for Rochefort
APPAREILLÉ (05:00), SONDÉ PAR 30. BRASSE: Got under way (05:00), sounded in 30 fathoms, 38, 35, 30 and 29, sand bottom (16:00)
APPAREILLÉ (14:00), PROLONGEANT LA TERRE: Got under way (14:00), coasting along the land. The sounding gave 19 fathoms, sand bottom (19:30)
APPAREILLÉ DE L'ÎLE DE PÂQUE (20:00): Got under way from Île de Pâque (20:00)
APPAREILLÉ DE MADÈRE (09:00). PRIS POUR: Got under way from Madère (09:00). Took as the point of departure the latitude and longitude opposite.
APPAREILLÉ DE TALCAGUANA (13:00), À LA C: Got under way from Talcaguana (13:00), on the coast of Chili.
APPAREILLÉ À 5 HEURES DU MATIN. MOUILLÉ: Got under way at 5 in the morning. Anchored 2 leagues N. of the first anchorage. At 2 hours in the afternoon,. The longitude is that given by watch No. 19.
APPAREILLÉ, ET MOUILLÉ AU FOND DU PORT P: Got under way, and anchored at the bottom of the harbour in 13 fathoms, mud bottom: the middle of the Île du Cénotaphe bore S.E. at half a cable's length
APPAREILLÉ, ET MOUILLÉ PLUS AVANT DANS L: Got under way, and anchored farther into the bay, in 6 fathoms 4, bottom of muddy sand.
APROVECHA LAS CONDICIONES PARA REALIZAR: Takes advantage of the conditions to carry out series of variation and correction. Notes the tables. Measurement and data of noon or of the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AQUÍ TERMINA EL DIARIO. VIENTO DE LA MAÑ: The diary ends here. Wind of the morning or afternoon / general weather
ARRESTANT JOSEPH GHIELMAN UIT DE BOEIEN: Prisoner Joseph Ghielman out of the irons
ARRIBA A LA RÍA DEL FERROL: Arrives at the estuary of Ferrol
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA: Arrives at the port of La Coruña
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA A LAS 7 HS: Arrives at the port of La Coruña at 7 hours, without major incidents
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA EN LA PRES: Arrives at the port of La Coruña in the present day's run
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA SIN MAYORE: Arrives at the port of La Coruña without major incidents
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA, SIN MAYOR: Arrives at the port of La Coruña, without major incidents
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MALDONADO POR PROBLE: Arrives at the port of Maldonado due to problems in navigation
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO: Arrives at the port of Montevideo
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO A LAS 9:: Arrives at the port of Montevideo at 9:30 hours.
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO EN LA PRE: Arrives at the port of Montevideo in the present day's run
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO SIN MAYOR: Arrives at the port of Montevideo without major incidents
ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO, ENTREGAN: Arrives at the port of Montevideo, delivering the dispatches
ARRIBAN A CAMARIÑAS DONDE SE MANTIENEN H: They arrive at Camariñas where they remain until 24 January. Descriptors, sea and wind from dawn, the rest from noon
ARRIVEERDEN DES S'NAMIDDAGS TEN 2 URE TE: Arrived in the afternoon at 2 o'clock at the roadstead of Batavia
ARRIVEERT IN STRAAT SUNDA. ARRIVEERT 12: Arrives in Strait Sunda. Arrived 12 February at Batavia. Sails in March for Sourbaija.
ARROJAN EL CADAVER AL MAR: They throw the corpse into the sea
ARTICULBRIEF GELEZEN EN DAGELIJKS DE VEN: Articles of war read and the ventilator pulled daily.
Articles of war read aloud by the clerk.
ARTIKELBRIEF GELEZEN. BOTTELIERSMAAT, JA: Articles of war read. Steward's mate, Jan Ouwenanse, died.
ATIENDEN A 9 MARINEROS, LOS PICADOS DE E: They attend to 9 sailors, those stricken with scurvy
AU MOUILLAGE D'AVATSCHA, DEPUIS LE 8 SEP: At anchor at Avatscha, from 8 Sept. 1787 until the 30th. At 7 in the evening, on the 7th, anchored in the bay of Avatscha, in 7 fathoms, mud bottom
AU MOUILLAGE, DANS LA BAIE DE MONTEREY,: At anchor in the bay of Monterey, since the 15th, at one in the afternoon. At 1 in the afternoon, anchored in 12 fathoms, fine sand bottom: the landing place on shore bore S10W
The water increases to 3.5 inches per hour. Frigatebirds, swallows, bonitos and flying fish
AUMENTA EL AGUA QUE HACIA EL NAVIO HASTA: The water the ship was making increases to 9 inches every 24 hours. "Note: this leak is singular, for on the day we lost sight of Tenerife it reached 14 inches in 24 hours and afterwards decreased to 5, then increasing again to 9 inches...". They are employed in its repair
AUMENTA EL NUMERO DE PAJAROS AVISTADOS: The number of birds sighted increases
AUNQUE EN LA LONGITUD APARECE 36º 49´DEB: Although the longitude appears as 36º 49´ it must be 6º.
AUNQUE EN LA LONGITUD PONE 190,9 DEBE SE: Although the longitude says 190,9 it must be 290,9. Noon or general data of the day's run
AUNQUE EN LAS ANOTACIONES DEL DIARIO HAC: Although the diary notes refer to the table, it does not exist, hence the wind references are from nightfall. The longitude is not exact (the minutes cannot be seen in the document)
AUNQUE PONTE LONGITUD 339 CREEMOS QUE SE: Although it puts longitude 339 we believe it is 329 and have corrected it.
AUNQUE REFIERE QUE LA LONGITUD DE LLEGAD: Although it states that the longitude of arrival is 391 degrees, we imagine there is an error and that it meant to put 291 degrees. Course and wind at noon / sea at nightfall
AUNQUE SE OBSERVO, NO FUE DE NINGUNA SAT: Although it was observed, it was not at all satisfactory because of how clouded the sun was in its image, and therefore I do not make use of it
AVISTA A LAS 10:00 LOS JARDINES DE LA RE: Sights the Jardines de la Reina at 10:00. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarteron
AVISTA A LAS 13:00 LA ISLA DE PINOS. DAT: Sights the Isla de Pinos at 13:00. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarteron
AVISTA A LAS 16:00 LA TIERRA FIRME DE LA: Sights the mainland of the island of La Habana at 16:00. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarteron
AVISTA A LAS 5:00 LA ISLA DE SANTA CRUZ: Sighted at 5:00 the island of Santa Cruz de Tenerife, and the Canary mail ship Magallanes remains behind. Noon data, except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter
AVISTA A LAS 8:30 LAS ISLAS DE TRINIDAD: Sighted at 8:30 the islands of Trinidad and Tobago. The currents have been quite strong to the N. Noon data, except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter
AVISTA EL CABO SAN ANTONIO. DATOS DEL ME: Sighted Cape San Antonio. Noon data, except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter
AVISTA SAN BARTOLOME Y SAN MARTIN: Sighted San Bartolome and San Martin
AVISTA TIERRA A LAS 16:00 PERO NO LA PUE: Sighted land at 16:00 but cannot identify it because the fog is completely closed in. Noon data or from the day's run
AVISTA UNA EMBARCACION PERO NO CONTESTO: Sighted a vessel but it did not answer the recognition signal
AVISTA VARIAS ISLAS QUE NOMBRO DE LA PAS: Sighted several islands which he named of the Passion, it being the 1st week of it, steering to approach the one furthest N and look for anchorage and replenish the water. They observe all of them to be full of coconut palms; having coasted them and finding no bottom, he headed for the one furthest W and saw several armed islanders, being unable to anchor for lack of a place to moor. He named this island of the Brave
AVISTAN 1 BALLENA MUERTA QUE FLOTA EN EL: They sighted 1 dead whale floating in the water, which at a distance looked like a crag
AVISTAN A LAS 6:30 UNA FRAGATA FRANCESA: They sighted at 6:30 a French frigate at great distance astern. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AVISTAN EMBARCACION DE RIO DE JANEIRO QU: They sighted a vessel from Rio de Janeiro that was going to Macao, had 9 days of sailing and considered itself 100 leagues from land and at 341º 30' longitude counted east of the meridian of Ferro. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AVISTAN LA CABEZA DEL CABO DE SAN VICENT: They sighted the head of Cape St Vincent 11 miles to the NW. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AVISTAN LA ISLA DE LOBOS A 5 O 6 LEGUAS: They sighted the island of Lobos 5 or 6 leagues to the NW 2º N. It seems the voyage ends there. Measurement and data from noon, except descriptors which are usually from nightfall. They follow the Dutch chart
AVISTAN LAS ISLAS DE LAS TRES MARIAS A L: They sighted the islands of Las Tres Marias at 13:30 ahead and to windward. He describes them
AVISTAN TIERRA A LAS 11:00 QUE SOSPECHAN: They sighted land at 11:00 which they suspect to be Cape of the Virgins, afterwards Cape Espiritu Santo. Data generally from dawn and bearing from noon
AVISTAN TIERRA TEMPRANO. A MEDIO DIA MAR: They sighted land early. At noon they took the bearing of Punta Naga N 51º 30' E (uncorrected) at 15 miles. New reflection on the differences found between dead-reckoning and observed bearings, calculations and formulas for correcting the bearings and measuring instruments. At noon they are near Tenerife. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AVISTAN TIERRA. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL MED: They sighted land. Measurement and data from noon, except descriptors which are usually from nightfall. They follow the Dutch chart
AVISTAN UN BERGANTIN FRANCES PROCEDENTE: They sighted a French brigantine coming from the coast of Guinea bound for Bengal
AVISTAN UNA EMBARCACION DE 2 PALOS. MEDI: They sighted a 2-masted vessel. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
AVISTAN UNA EMBARCACION DE 3 PALOS A LAR: They sighted a 3-masted vessel at long distance
AVISTAN UNA VELA AL SSE QUE IBA DE VUELT: They sighted a sail to the SSE that was returning from the NW; they made contact and it turned out to be a French frigate that came from Angola on the coast of Guinea and was going to Guarico with 606 Negroes, large and small and women, that 2 days earlier it had spoken with an English vessel and considered itself at 2º47' lat N and 352º37' long
AVOND: PEILEN DRIE GEBROEDERS OZO EN KAA: Evening: took bearings of three brothers ESE and Cape St. Marie NNE and Table Mountain NE. Remarks on the chronometer and the clocks
AVOND: PIEK ZWTW 1/4 W. DE HOEK VAN LANS: Evening: the peak SWW 1/4 W. The corner of Lanzarote SWW. And the outermost [?] of the NE corner WNW 1/2 W. At 12 o'clock the peak bore NW.
AVOND: SCHIP IS 11' 46'' OOSTELIJKER DAN: Evening: ship is 11' 46'' further east than the dead reckoning indicates
Afternoon watch and evening watch: waiting for the merchantmen.
AW: DE RUYTER GAF ONS VOOR ZIJN LENGTE 3: Afternoon watch: De Ruyter gave us his longitude as 344,33'
AW: MAKEN LOOS ALARM: Afternoon watch: made a false alarm
AW: MEN DENKT HET EILAND AMSTERDAM TE ZI: Afternoon watch: they think they see the island of Amsterdam, but not with certainty because the weather is very tempestuous and the sky thick.
AW: WENDEN OM DE N: Afternoon watch: tacked around the N
AW? GLAZEN: HALSDEN OM DE OOST. DW? GLAZ: Afternoon watch glasses: tacked around the east. Forenoon watch glasses: tacked around the west
AWV: HET IS DOODSTIL, TEN ANKER, 11-12-1: Afternoon and first watch: it is dead calm, at anchor, 11-12-13 forenoon
AWV: UIT DE AFSTAND VAN ZON EN MAAN (6 G: Afternoon and first watch: from the distance of sun and moon (6 observations taken) it appears that we were at 64° 56' 10'' and according to the chronometer 65°42' E of Greenwich.
AWV: ZIEN SOLA IN HET Z EN EEN GEDEELTE: Afternoon and first watch: see Sola to the S and part of Margarita in WSW. Later see the easternmost of the Trairos and the westernmost S
AWV: ZWARE STORM, DREVEN OM DE WEST. IN: Afternoon and first watch: heavy storm, drifted around the west. In the evening watch the weather calmed. West of meridian 91 miles. Changed around the east 3,75 miles. Obtained 87,25 miles.
AYER TARDE SE VIÓ UN PÁJARO: Yesterday afternoon a bird was seen
AYER TODA LA TARDE SE VIERON INFINIDAD D: Yesterday all afternoon countless prawns were seen
B(E)RAMEN EEN VERSAAMELPLAATS VOORDEN 1: B(E)RAMEN a rendezvous before 1 August in Magdalena Bay, after that date in Konings Bay, for the ships from the Maas
B.B. KWARTIER 1 OORLAM VOOR HET NATTE WE: B.B. quarter 1 hour-glass for the wet weather
BAAS TIMMERMAN J. C. GROSMAN OVERLEDEN: Master carpenter J. C. Grosman died
BAKKER C.H.T. HORNEN OVERBOORD GESPRONGE: Baker C.H.T. Hornen jumped overboard and drowned.
BAKKER P. DE NIES OVERLEDEN, OVERBOORD G: Baker P. de Nies died, put overboard.
BANCAS DE NIEVE VISTAS AL NE Y MAS PAJAR: Banks of snow seen to the NE and more birds than other days
BANCAS DE NIEVE VISTAS AL SE: Banks of snow seen to the SE
BAREND HUGDWAGTER OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN: Barend Hugdwagter fell overboard and drowned.
BAROMETER TE WILD OM TE OBSERVEREN DOCH: Barometer too wild to observe but falling.
BAROMETER VAN WENKBACH DOOR HET STAMPEN: Barometer of Wenkbach, because of the pitching, 1/10 above or below the aneroid
BAROMETER:DUIMEN-LINIEN-TIENDEN: 29-8-4,: Barometer: inches-lines-tenths: 29-8-4,25; weighed anchor, steered SSE and SE out of the bay
BAROMETERSTAND IS EIGENLIJK WEERGEGEVEN: Barometer reading is actually given as 30.2; in those cases where only 3 digits are given I have added a 0 to it
BAROMETERSTAND WAS 270300, MAAR DIT PAST: Barometer reading was 270300, but this does not fit in the series.
BAROMETERSTANDEN WORDEN OP 2 MANIEREN AF: Barometer readings are read off in 2 ways: take the one from the forenoon watch
BARON V.D. CAPELLE , CAPITEIN LUITENANT: Baron V.D. Capelle, captain lieutenant of the OIC, F 133? Adam Essing, F 125 Hendrik Kuyper died
BATAVIA, MET H. BRUHN, VAN BATAVIA NAAR: Batavia, with H. Bruhn, from Batavia to Rotterdam 1835, extract B, folio 286-289
BEGIN DER ZO PASSAAT: Start of the SE trade wind
BEGIN INHANDELINGSPERIODE AFRIKAANSE KUS: Start of the trading period on the African coast.
Began with the whole leaguers of water.
BEGONNEN MET RANTSOEN WATER TE GEVEN: Began giving out a ration of water
Kept course since the dog watch.
BEK. LENGTE OP DE OVERSEIJLDER 1° 18', V: Longitude known by the overseiler 1° 18', according to which the east corner of Madeira WSW 8 miles
BEK. LENGTE OP DE OVERSEIJLDER 2° 0', VO: Longitude known by the overseiler 2° 0', according to which still 16 miles west of the east corner of Madeira
BEK. LENGTE OP DE OVERSEIJLDER 2° 18' EN: Longitude known by the overseiler 2° 18' and from Porto Santo W 17 miles.
BEK. LENGTE OP DE OVERSEIJLDER 3° 4', VA: Longitude known by the overseiler 3° 4', from Porto Santo SWW 27 miles.
Obtained longitude by distance of sun and moon.
BEKOMEN LENGTE EENMALIG VAN TIJDMETER 9: Obtained longitude once, taken over from chronometer 9.
BEKOMEN LENGTE GEOBSERVEERD DOOR ZON EN: Obtained longitude observed by sun and moon
Obtained longitude is the chronometer's longitude.
BEKOMEN LENGTE VAN DEN OVERSEIJLDER 7° 5: Obtained longitude from the overseiler 7° 55'. Switch here to the first voyage, which seems to have somewhat better weather data; take observations from the officers
BEKOMEN LENGTE VAN GREENWICH. WARE BEKOM: Obtained longitude from Greenwich. True obtained longitude according to chronometer. Observe the latitude of Sierra Leone 8° 29' and longitude of Tenerife 3° 45'. Remarks on the Dutch pass chart
Obtained longitude via the other chronometer.
BEKWAAMER PW 1½ GM WATER BIJ DE POMP MET: Abler [?] PW 1½ GM water at the pump with coal. The compasses vary 20° = 17° 30' N/W
BEKWAMEN THEN 9 UUR EEN TRAVAAT VAN DOND: At 9 o'clock got a squall of thunder, lightning and rain. From fresh to moderate breeze, lightning accompanied by squalls (short violent gust of wind with heavy rain)
BELDEN DE UITKIJKEN OMDAT ZE DEZE NACHT: Called the lookouts because tonight they think they will pass the latitude of the island P. (C?) VARIRA?
BELEGGEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER HET AAN DOEN V: Held a ship's council about calling at a harbour on Madeira or 1 of the Canary Islands
BELEGGEN SCHEEPSRAAD. SCHEEPSVOLK IS NOG: Held a ship's council. The ship's crew are still fresh and healthy.
BELEGGEN SCHEEPSRAAD. VERHOREN DE TROMPE: Held a ship's council. Questioned the trumpeter. He says he did not use a knife, but his hands. He is put back in irons at S.E.COMP. The provost and a soldier are also punished for theft. Appointed the quartermaster Pieter Marteel of Sluis in Flanders as steward.
BELEIJDEN EXTRA RAAD WEGENS HET AANDOEN: Held an extra council about calling at St. Jago. By unanimous vote it was resolved to continue the voyage. More in the minutes, as can be seen. The sailmaker was released from the irons again.
BELLÍSIMO (...) LA BRISA (...) DE DÍA EM: Very fine (...) the breeze (...) by day it began to calm.
BELOVEN DE BOTTELIER GENOEGDOENING IN SU: Promised the steward satisfaction in Suriname (?)
BEMANNING KREEG EXTRA OORLAM WEGENS DOOR: Crew received an extra ration of rum because it rained through and through
BEMERKEN VERANDERINGEN IN DE KLEUR VAN H: Noticed changes in the color of the water outboard. See several birds of various kinds.
BEMERKTEN DAT WIJ BUITEN GISSING OM DE N: Noticed that we had been set to the north beyond our reckoning
BEMERKTEN VERANDERING VAN DE KLEUR VAN ': Noticed a change in the color of the water
BENOORDEN MADURA 3° N/O EN ZICHT 1° N/O: North of Madura 3° N/E and sighting 1° N/E as on the chart; this was also found on the previous voyage. Compass at 3° N/E
Deliberations about the course to Java.
BERGEN ENIGE CARGAZOENEN IN DE KAJUIT VO: Stowed some cargo in the cabin for the upper coast and put five bread casks in the aftermost cargo hold
BESCHERMER KRIJGT OPDRACHT OP TE HOUDEN: Protector is ordered to stop the chase.
BESCHERMER KRIJGT OPDRACHT TE GAAN JAGEN: Protector is ordered to go chasing to the east. Stops at sunset.
BESCHRIJVING TRINIDAD EN MARTIN VAZ, HEE: Description of Trinidad and Martin Vaz; has with him a treatise on navigation by M. d'Après de Mannevillette, and a Spanish chart from 1800
BESCHRIJVING VAN DE GESCHIEDENIS VAN DEZ: Description of the history of this local current
BESCHRIJVING VAN DE LIGGING VAN DE EILAN: Description of the position of the islets. Other names for these (probable) Bermudas.
BESCHRIJVING VAN HET LAND. HIELDEN HET V: Description of the land. Took it to be the coast between Rio Wanuarij and Rio Aperwague
BESLOTEN OM 40 MANSCHAPPEN TE BEWAPENEN: Resolved to arm 40 men with muskets
BESLOTEN ST JAGO NIET AAN TE DOEN, OMDAT: Resolved not to call at St. Jago, because they still had enough water
BESLOTEN WATER TE KOKEN OM DE WATERVOORR: Resolved to boil water to replenish the water supply.
BESLOTEN WERD OM KAAP DE GOEDE HOOP NIET: Resolved not to call at the Cape of Good Hope
BESLUITEN CABO AAN TE DOEN IVM TOESTAND: Resolve to call at Cabo because of the condition of the ship
BESPEURD VERANDERING VAN KLEUREN VAN 'T: Perceived a change in the color of the water
BESPEURDEN VERANDERING IN 'T WATER. VANG: Perceived a change in the water. Caught porpoises
BESPEURDEN VERANDERING IN DE KLEUR VAN ': Perceived a change in the color of the water
BESPEURDEN VERANDERING VAN WATER. ONZE C: Perceived a change in the water. Our companion had the same latitude as us. In the text a longitude of 10 degrees 26 minutes is given, in the margin a longitude of 10 degrees 40 minutes. Anchored on the bank
BESPEUREN EEN MERKELIJKE VERANDERING IN: Perceive a marked change in the water.
BESPEUREN NA DE MIDDAG VERANDERINGEN IN: Perceive changes in the water after noon
BESPEURING VERANDERING IN HET WATER: Perception of a change in the water
BESTEK 3°38' TE OOSTELIJK SINDS ASCENCIO: Reckoning 3°38' too far east since Ascension
BESTEK AFGEZET OP DE KAART VAN J. HAEIJT: Reckoning plotted on the chart of J. Haeijter
Reckoning plotted on the chart of J. Haeijter.
BESTEK COMMANDANT WAS 16:17, 63:19, VAN: Commander's reckoning was 16:17, 63:19; the Jager's was 12:23, 63:16
BESTEK DER SCHEPEN DOORGESEIND: GOES: 42: Reckonings of the ships signaled: GOES: 42°37'', 38°0. PRINCES LOUISA: 42° 0, 37°58'. MONNIKKENDAM: 42°40', 38°5'. WASSENAAR: 42°38', 38°0'. JUNO could not be made out correctly because of the great distance.
BESTEK GECONTROLEERD MET ZON-MAAN LENGTE: Reckoning checked with sun-moon longitude: 1°30'30" too far east
Reckoning checked with sun-moon longitude: 1°40'45" too far east
BESTEK I.V.M. GIS VAN GOUSTAARD VERMOEDE: Reckoning in connection with the presumed estimate of Goustaard [?]. Set our reckoning on the waxing-degree chart. By 'at night' is meant the night of the following day
Reckoning is the same as the previous day.
BESTEK KWAM GOED UIT. EILANDEN ZIJN BIJ: Reckoning came out well. The islands appear to me, as seen while sailing along, to be dreary barren rocks
BESTEK KWAM ZUIDELIJK UIT. WILLEN ANKERE: Reckoning came out southerly. Wanted to anchor at St. Cruz on Tenerife, got a pilot, but because of variable winds and calms this did not succeed
Reckoning after estimate of the previous day 3 o'clock.
BESTEK NEEMT AANVANG OP DE POSITIE VAN 6: Reckoning begins at the position of 6° 12' and longitude 119° 45'. Change of longitude 0° 12'.
BESTEK NEEMT ZIJN AANVANG. TIJDMETER GER: Reckoning begins. Chronometer reckoned from Onrust: 104°39'0''
BESTEK OM 1 UUR WAS VAN DE NEPTUNUS: 30: Reckoning at 1 o'clock was, of the Neptunus: 30 degrees 31 minutes north latitude and 360 degrees longitude, of the Joan de Witt: 30 degrees 28 minutes north latitude and 360 (or 0) degrees 39 minutes longitude, of the Ajax: 30 degrees 32 minutes north latitude and 360 (or 0) degrees 17 minutes longitude. Observed longitude of the Joan de Witt was 2 degrees 7 minutes and of the Ajax 3 degrees 7 minutes. Calculated from our observations the latitude of Salvago at 30 degrees 6 minutes, and thus 12 minutes more southerly than the chart of the Atlantic Ocean shows.
BESTEK OM HALF 1 VAN DE NEPTUNUS: 37 GRA: Reckoning at half past 12 of the Neptunus: 37 degrees 43 minutes latitude and 2 degrees 31 minutes longitude, of the Joan de Witt: 37 degrees 37 minutes latitude and 2 degrees 59 minutes longitude, of the Ajax: 37 degrees 47 minutes latitude and 3 degrees 7 minutes longitude.
BESTEK SCHIPPER POT: 22° 25' NB, 357° 15: Reckoning of Skipper Pot: 22° 25' N, 357° 15' E.
Reckoning of Skipper Pot: 6° 42' N, 3° 4' E.
BESTEK SCHIPPER POT: 9° 20' NB, 359° 0': Reckoning of Skipper Pot: 9° 20' N, 359° 0' E. Reckoning of Weazle: 9° 26' N, 16° 53' E according to the meridian of London, comes to 358° 48''.
Reckoning since 11 o'clock in the EW [?].
BESTEK VAN DE 'MAAT' WAS GISTERMIDDAG: L: Reckoning of the 'Maat' yesterday noon: longitude 0° 24'. He had 30 sick in the bunks. 'We' hailed him to steer SWbS until about the latitude of Porto Santo at Madeira, then south. 52 miles south in a day?.
BESTEK VAN DE ANDERE SCHEPEN: POLLUX: NO: Reckoning of the other ships: POLLUX: north latitude 10 degrees 33 minutes, longitude 320 degrees 54 minutes. VLIEGENDE VIS: north latitude 10 degrees 33 minutes, longitude 320 degrees 13 minutes

Ship of Silvester N lat 37°36' longitude 325°19'. Ship of Van Woenzel N lat 37°38' longitude 325°18'. Ship of Boot 37°39' longitude 326°12'

BESTEK VAN DE COMMANDANT: BREEDTE HETZEL: Reckoning of the commander: latitude the same as 'we', their longitude 358° 18'. 'We' had 3° 9'.
BESTEK VAN DE FRANSMAN WAS 45°0' NB EN 3: Reckoning of the Frenchman was 45°0' N and 339° E
BESTEK VAN DE KAPITEIN GR. V. RECHTEREN:: Reckoning of the captain Gr. v. Rechteren: SbyW 19.75 miles. (Estimated) N 8°45'. L 357°51'. (Observed) N 8°56'. Reckoning of Captain Oosterhuijs: SbyW 17 miles. 8°56'. 358°39'. 8°55'.
BESTEK VAN DE KOOPVAARDER. (GEEN EIGEN B: Reckoning of the merchantman. (No reckoning of his own mentioned). Urge the merchantman to carry as much sail as his ship can bear, because the Boreas has to carry so little sail to stay with him that the ship rolls dreadfully and takes in much water through the gunports and the seams of the hull.
BESTEK VAN DE NEPTUNUS: 46 GRADEN 37 MIN: Reckoning of the Neptunus: 46 degrees 37 minutes latitude and 7 degrees 49 minutes longitude, of the Joan de Witt: 46 degrees 35 minutes latitude and 8 degrees 8 minutes longitude, of the Ajax: 46 degrees 35 minutes latitude and 8 degrees 21 minutes longitude. This was the reckoning at half past 1.
BESTEK VAN DE PIET HEIN WAS OM 3 UUR: NO: Reckoning of the Piet Hein at 3 o'clock was: north latitude 44 degrees 16 minutes, longitude 336 degrees 44 minutes. Difference of longitude 0 degrees 38 minutes east. Longitude of the Vliegende Vis was 42 degrees 30 minutes west of Greenwich. Fleet came from the Cape of Good Hope, had a 3-month voyage bound for Portsmouth
BESTEK VAN DE SCHEPEN OM HALF 1: DE NEPT: Reckoning of the ships at half past 12: the Neptunus 43 degrees 14 minutes latitude and 4 degrees longitude, the Joan de Witt 43 degrees 7 minutes latitude and 4 degrees 21 minutes longitude, the Ajax 43 degrees 12 minutes latitude and 4 degrees 29 minutes longitude.
BESTEK VAN DE SUSSANNA: LENGTE 48° 47' E: Reckoning of the Sussanna: longitude 48° 47' and variation 26° 30'. Sick 12 and dead: 1. Reckoning of the Johanna: longitude 45° 11' and variation 24° 52'. Sick 12 and dead: 2. Reckoning of the Drie Gebroeders: longitude 46° 23' and variation 26° 32'. ? dead. Reckoning of the Fortuijn: longitude 46° 14' and variation 28° 10'. Averaged longitude by these? longitudes: 46° 44'. Corrected course and distance? 2/3 N. 22.5 miles. Sounded, no bottom.
BESTEK VAN DE WASSENAAR GEVRAAGD, DE WAS: Reckoning of the Wassenaar requested; the Wassenaar had Cape Aiguillas this morning at 8 o'clock at 30 miles WNW, the latitude found yesterday was 34:55'
BESTEK VAN DE WASSENAAR. ZB 27: 39 LENGT: Reckoning of the Wassenaar. S lat 27: 39 longitude 27: 29
BESTEK VAN DE: POLLUX: NOORDERBREEDTE 20: Reckoning of the: POLLUX: north latitude 20 degrees 48 minutes, longitude 319 degrees 22 minutes. JAGER: north latitude 20 degrees 46 minutes, longitude 320 degrees 6 minutes. PIET HEIN: north latitude 20 degrees 44 minutes, longitude 319 degrees 13 minutes. VLIEGENDE VIS: north latitude 20 degrees 51 minutes, longitude 319 degrees 29 minutes
BESTEK VAN HET FRANSE SCHIP (VAN GISTERE: Reckoning of the French ship (from yesterday): 9° 45' N. As for his longitude, the report was very confused and nothing could be made of it. He is said to have had the longitude of 346° from 'our' meridian. Remarks on the reckoning, among others calculations by means of meridia[?]
BESTEK VAN KAPITEIN GRAVE VAN RECHTEREN,: Reckoning of Captain Grave van Rechteren, from noon: East. 47. 33°58'. 29°20'. 33°57. According to that, the Cape of Good Hope: E 1/4 S, 78 miles from him. Reckoning of Captain Oosthuijzen: East. 37.5. 33°53'. 27°36'. 33°53'. According to that, the Cape of Good Hope: E 1/3 S: 99.5 miles from him.
BESTEK VAN KAPITEIN OOSTHUIJSE: ZTW 1/2: Reckoning of Captain Oosthuijse: SW 1/2 W, 38.5 miles, 19°19', 354°56', 19° 47'. According to that (estimated) Ile de Sal SW 1/2 W 36 miles.
BESTEK VAN KAPITEIN OOSTHUIJSE: ZZW 1/2: Reckoning of Captain Oosthuijse: SSW 1/2 W. 23.5 miles. 16°3'. 353°40'. 16°4'. (Estimated) point of St. Jago SW. 12 miles.
BESTEK VAN KAPITEIN PRUIJS VERSCHILT ZEE: Reckoning of Captain Pruijs differs very little from ours. Meridian west of Madeira, 362.25 miles.
BESTEK VAN SCHIPPER POT: 26° 34' NB, 358: Reckoning of Skipper Pot: 26° 34' N, 358° 16' E.
BESTEK VOLGENS DE KAART VAN STEEL: Reckoning according to the chart of Steel
BESTEK WAS 24 MINUTEN TE WESTELIJK BEREK: Reckoning was calculated 24 minutes too far west.
BESTEK WORDT VERGELEKEN MET ANDERE GEGEV: Reckoning is compared with other data. The conclusion is that the chronometer shows 28' too far east. Reckoning is adjusted
BESTEK WORDT VERGELEKEN MET DE ANDERE KA: Reckoning is compared with the other captains

BESTEKKEN VAN DE SCHEPEN: GOES: 83° 20',: Reckonings of the ships: GOES: 83° 20', 39°9'. PRINCES LOUISA: 83°0', 39°3'. MONNIKKENDAM: 84°1', 39°10'. JUNO 85°17', 39°30'. WASSENAAR: 82° 53', 39°9'.
BETROKKEN BUIIGE LUCHT WEERLIGT GOED WEE: Overcast, hazy sky, lightning, good weather
BEVINDEN ZICH DAGELIJKS ZUIDELIJKER TE Z: Find themselves daily more southerly than the reckoning, probably because of the current
BEVINDEN ZICH NU IN HET GEZICHT VAN DE S: Are now in sight of Saldanha Bay.
BEVOND BIJ HET OPENEN DER ZUURKOOL VATEN: On opening the sauerkraut casks found everything to be sea coral [?]. Therefore issue some of it to the crew
BEVONDE LAASTE OBSERVATIE 10 MINUTEN LEN: Found at the last observation that the longitude had been set 10 minutes to the north
BEVONDEN 10 MINUTEN OM DE NOORD GEZET TE: Found that we had been set 10 minutes to the north
BEVONDEN 10° 32' 11° 14' EN BEVONDEN NB: Found 10° 32' 11° 14' and found N lat 14°51'. AW/EW: weigh anchor.
BEVONDEN 15° 26' N WESTERING. VERANDERDE: Found 15° 26' N westerly variation. Changed meridian to the W by 3.25 miles
BEVONDEN 2 CONSTAPELS EN 1 MATROOS NIET: Found 2 gunners and 1 sailor not at their posts. Both gunners were put in irons on water and bread, the sailor was punished.
BEVONDEN 27 MINUTEN OM DE OOST GEZET TE: Found that we had been set 27 minutes to the east
BEVONDEN BIJ HET OPMANNEN VAN 'T WATER E: Found, when manning the water [pumps?], a leaguer at 4.5 [?] after being emptied
BEVONDEN BIJ OBSERVATIE DAT DE CHRONOMET: Found by observation that the chronometer was 1'2'30 slow of Greenwich mean time, upon which we set the same rate and the westerly longitude readings at 15 sec gain per day.
BEVONDEN BREEDTE STAAT: 58°38'. PAST NIE: Latitude found to be 58°38'. Does not fit at all.
BEVONDEN BREEDTE VOLGENS OCTANT. NOG EEN: Latitude found by octant. Another found: N 44° 54'.
BEVONDEN DAT DE CHRON. 4' A 6' TE OOSTEL: Found that the chronometer was 4' to 6' too far east.
BEVONDEN DAT DE CHRONOMETER EEN REEKS VA: Found that the chronometer, from a series of distances, was 54'40 [?] Greenwich mean time, upon which we set the same anew, reckoning 23 seconds per [?] per day.
BEVONDEN DAT WE 11 MIJL OOSTELIJKER WARE: Found that we were 11 miles farther east than our dead reckoning had put us. Off the coast of Africa.
BEVONDEN DAT WE DOOR DE STROOM NOORDWAAR: Found that we had been set northward by the current. Sounded depths of 55 fathoms: gray and black fine sand.
BEVONDEN DAT WE MET ONS BESTEK 2 1/2 ° T: Found that by our dead reckoning we were 2 1/2° too far east.
BEVONDEN DAT WIJ OM DE ZUID GEZET WERDEN: Found that we had been set to the south, steered NE.
BEVONDEN DE 6 VATEN MEEGEGEVEN ZEEKORAAL: Found the 6 casks of sea coral issued to us completely stinking and rotten, so that they were not edible. Therefore threw them overboard.
BEVONDEN DE GEOBSERVEERDE LENGTE VOLGENS: Found the observed longitude by chronometer to be 16°15', that of the most accurate reckonings by various different observations 16°16'.
BEVONDEN DE LENGTE 120°33' TE ZIJN. ZEIL: Found the longitude to be 120°33'. Sailed into Sunda Strait the following day.
BEVONDEN DE MISWIJZING VOOR DE ZONS AZIM: Found the compass variation from the sun's azimuth to be 324 ! northwesterly.
BEVONDEN DE TIJDM EEN DAGELIJKS VERLOOP: Found the chronometer to have a daily rate of 29'' for St. Java Head.
BEVONDEN DE TIJDM. LENGTE ANDERMAAL DAT: Found by the chronometer longitude again that it corrected the same 20'18" to the east, as a result of its rate.
BEVONDEN DE TIJDMETER 13´45´´ TE OOSTELI: Found the chronometer 13´45´´ too far east.
BEVONDEN DE ZEIL EN BROODKAMER NOG DROOG: Found the sail room and bread room still dry, etc.
BEVONDEN DOOR AFSTAND VAN ZON EN MAAN DE: Found by distance of sun and moon the calculated longitude 30 degrees 4 minutes.
Found by distance of sun and moon the longitude of 28 degrees 57 minutes.
BEVONDEN DOOR AZIMUTEN EN AMPLITUDE DAT: Found by azimuths and amplitude that the ship's head was SE 17 to 21° N/W, with which the [?] to the east agrees. Because of the imperfect arrangement of the azimuth compass repair we could not obtain accurate bearings.
BEVONDEN DOOR DEZE BREEDTE DAT DE NOORDW: Found by this latitude that the northwest point of Majaguana was placed 5 miles too far north on the chart of the West Indian islands.
BEVONDEN DOOR EEN HOOGTE AAN DE MAAN DE: Found by a altitude of the moon the latitude of 35 degrees 36 minutes 49 seconds.
BEVONDEN DOOR HOOGMETING DAT WIJ DOOR DE: Found by altitude measurement that we had been set to the north by the current, markedly beyond our reckoning.
BEVONDEN DOOR OBSERVATIE AAN DE STERREN: Found by observation of the stars that the chronometer longitude is 1°10' too far east (dead reckoning is being adjusted).
BEVONDEN HIER DOOR DAT ONS BESTEK 3GR56M: Found hereby that our dead reckoning was 3 deg 56 min too far east, corrected the same and set the reckoning at 45 deg 50 min.
BEVONDEN HIER DOOR DAT ONS BESTEK 4 GRAD: Found hereby that our dead reckoning was 4 degrees too far east, set it 4 degrees 9 minutes farther west, coming to the longitude of 345 deg, according to which the island of Flores was NNW, 11 miles from us.
BEVONDEN IN DE LAATST 2 ETMALEN EEN STRO: Found that in the last 2 days we had had a current SSW 2/3 W.
BEVONDEN LENGTE DOOR AFSTANDMETING 11° 4: Found longitude by distance measurement 11° 42'. Thus the last 2 longitudes differ by 1° 30', the chronometer being too far east. The journal keeper places his trust in the observation of sun and moon over the chronometer. Gives 3 reasons.
BEVONDEN LENGTE NIET DUIDELIJK IN ORIGIN: Found longitude not clear in the original.
Found longitude by the French chart. (Estimated longitude per Tenerife: 60°40'E)
BEVONDEN LENGTE ZEPHYR 48°47'. (GISLENGT: Found longitude Zephyr 48°47'. (Estimated longitude per Tenerife: 46°14'E)
BEVONDEN LENGTE ZEPHYR 49°50'. (GISLENGT: Found longitude Zephyr 49°50'. (Estimated longitude per Tenerife: 47°47'E)
BEVONDEN LENGTE ZEPHYR 52°31'. (GISLENGT: Found longitude Zephyr 52°31'. (Estimated longitude per Tenerife: 51°00'E)
BEVONDEN MEEDE VERSCHEIJDE ABSENT EN MIN: Also found several absent and fewer than the crew book stated. Latitudes according to the declaration made of them at sea [?].
BEVONDEN MERKELIJK BUITEN ONS GISSING NO: Found that we had been set northward, markedly beyond our reckoning.
BEVONDEN MISWIJZING DOOR HET AZIMUTH 2°1: Found compass variation by the azimuth 2°14' northeasterly.
BEVONDEN MISWIJZING VOOR DE ZONS AZIMUTH: Found the compass variation from the sun's azimuths to be 2 to 27 NW.
BEVONDEN OM DE 3 ETMIJLEN EEN STROOM GEH: Found that every 3 nautical miles we had had a current of 1 degree to the east.

BIJ DE WINDRICHTINGEN STAAN WEDEROM DE O: Among the wind directions the unknown symbols appear again, as earlier at the LOOPUIJT_1845.

BIJ GENERALE KOERS STAAN 2 WAARDEN DE EE: At the general course two values are given. The first is stated above, the second is SSE 1/3 S, 19 miles.
BIJ GENERALE KOERS STONDEN 2 WAARDEN DE: At the general course two values were given. The first is mentioned above, the second is SE 1/4 S 17.25 miles.
BIJ HET AANBREKEN VAN DE DAG KONDEN ZE G: At daybreak they could not see any of their ships. Saw three ships to windward, but they could not tell whether those ships belonged to the convoy.
BIJ HET AANSLAAN VAN EEN NIEUWE BEZAAN B: While bending on a new mizzen sail a strap broke, causing the gaff to fall onto the half deck. Two sailors also fell down with it. Jacob Louwrens fell onto the stern counter and then overboard. The other sailor fell onto the half deck and was badly injured.
BIJ HET ANKER LEGGEN OP DE RHEDE VAN DUY: On anchoring in the roads of Duyns, [?] gunpowder and cartridges.
BIJ HET GENOEMDE LANDKENMERK STAAT VERME: Next to the said landmark it says: "Discovered 21 Aug. 1769".
BIJ HET LANDKENMERK STAAT DE OPMERKING:: Next to the landmark is the remark: (Government chart of the Indian Ocean)
BIJ HET OEFENEN MET DE GEWEREN GING EEN: During musket practice a musket went off by accident and hit the soldier I. Tasserom in the head, whereupon he died.
Sounding with the lead, no bottom.
When reading the air pressure I note the symp. meter.

BIJ WINDRICHTING STAAT OOK: O TE OOSTEN?: Under wind direction it also says: E to the east?
BIJ ZEETOESTAND WORDT A GEGEVEN. ONDUIDE: Under sea state an A is given. It is unclear whether increasing or abating is meant.
BIJ ZONSOPGAN HET EILAND FARULHO N 1/2 O: At sunrise the island Farulho N 1/2 E, by estimate 7 miles.
BLEEF TEN ANKER LIGGEN. VOLGEN 2 DAGEN Z: Remained at anchor. Two days without a position fix follow, at St. Anna.
BLEVEN BIJ ONS BESTEK, WE VERONDERSTELDE: Stayed with our reckoning; we supposed there was little error.
BLEVEN GEANKERD LEGGEN. KREGEN ORDERS HI: Remained at anchor. Received orders for this.
BLEVEN GEANKERT MET DEN LICHTE ANKER EN: Remained anchored with the light anchor and go under sail, come to anchor again at the last-mentioned depth/bottom because of calm. The Platvoet weighs anchor and goes under sail.
BLIXEM SLOEG NET NIET IN: The lightning just failed to strike.
BODEM OP 40 VOET, MODDER ZAND EN KLEINE: Bottom at 40 feet, mud, sand and small stones (limestones).
BODEM OP 44 VOET. GEBROKEN SCHELPEN MET: Bottom at 44 feet. Broken shells with black and brown pebbles mixed with a little grey sand.
BODEM OP 50 VOET. WIT ZAND MET STENEN EN: Bottom at 50 feet. White sand with stones and shells.
BOEGDEN DE KOERS ZO OM OP DE BREEDTE VEN: Steered the course SE in order to come back to the latitude of the Cape. Kept a good lookout.
BOEK: MR. VALMONT DE BOMARE, DICTIONAIRE: Book: Mr. Valmont de Bomare, Dictionaire d'histoire naturelle.
BOLIVAR HAD ALLES VEROVERD, DAAROM HADDE: Bolivar had conquered everything, so many ships had had to withdraw from the roads of Lima; the Spaniards held only Callao on this coast.
Bombardier Jan van Hall of Dieren.
BOOTSCOMMANDANT UIT DE BOEIEN, GEDEGRADE: Boat commander taken out of irons, demoted because of repeated drunkenness. Also, for theft of wine, two sailors taken out of irons with a severe punishment.
BOOTSMAAT DE KEIJZER ONTSLAGEN. KROM IN: Boatswain's mate de Keijzer dismissed. Krom locked in irons on water and bread; the 2nd mate J. Hanssen for appearing late on watch and, after being called to account, insulting the officer of the watch.
BOOTSMAAT VAN ERP IN DE BOEIEN: Boatswain's mate van Erp in irons.
BOOTSMAN J.B. WINCKELMAN IN DE BOEIEN GE: Boatswain J.B. Winckelman locked in irons for neglect of duty and repeated brutality.
Boatswain Jan Koort of Lubeck died. The number of sick rose to 80.
BOOTSMAN OVERLEDEN, BOUDEWIJN ANDRIES MO: Boatswain Boudewijn Andries Morel died, put the body overboard, sell his belongings.
BOOTSMANSMAAT JAN BOUWMAN OVERLEDEN AAN: Boatswain's mate Jan Bouwman died of dysentery.
BOOTSMANSMAAT JAN PHILIP VNA DOBBEROC VA: Boatswain's mate Jan Philip VNA Dobberoc of Hamburg and sailor Franciscus Pinte of Middelkerke died.
BORSSELE NEEMT AFSCHEID, HIJ VAART VEEL: Borssele takes leave; it sails much faster than we do.
BOSKOPPEN SPRINGEN UIT HET WATER MET GRO: [?] leap out of the water with great force.
BOTELIERSMAAT EN JONGEN WORDEN BESTRAFT: Steward's mate and boys punished for theft.
BOTTELIER P. VAN HET HOF ONTSLAGEN, DE W: Steward P. van het Hof dismissed. The acting sick attendant, the sailor 3rd class Bergmeijer, had given sick bread to the sick without orders to do so, so P. van het Hof was innocent. Punished Bergmeijer with blows and sentenced him to bear the costs of the irons.
BOTTELIER PIETER DE ROO VAN AMSTERDAM OV: Steward Pieter de Roo of Amsterdam died.
BOTTELIER RINGELS WEGENS PLICHTSVERZUIM: Steward Ringels in irons for neglect of duty.
BOTTELIERSMAAT AREND HOESTIJN UIT LEIDEN: Steward's mate Arend Hoestijn of Leiden and ship's boy G.J. van Thienen of Middelburg died.
BOUWDE EEN ZIEKENTENTJE OP HET DEK. (BES: Built a sick tent on the deck. (Description of sailor's burial ceremony.)
BOVEN DEZE GEGEVENS STAAT NA DE DE PIJLI: Above this data, after the, stands the bearing.

BRACHTEN 1 ZIEKE NAAR HET HOSPITAAL: Brought 1 sick man to the hospital.
BRACHTEN DE KISTEN MET HANDGRANATEN IN D: Brought the chests of hand grenades into the tops.
Brought a sick man to the hospital.
BRACHTEN EEN ZIEKE NAAR HET HOSPITAAL. L: Brought a sick man to the hospital. Let 11 men go ashore.

BUIJIGE LUCHT MET DONDER EN WEERLICHT: Squally sky with thunder and lightning

CADA VEZ MENOS AGUA: Less and less water each time

At daybreak sky and horizon with a bank of cloud and brown clouds, fresh WSW wind with sea from the wind and from the NW.

CELAJERIA NEBLINOSA, HORIZONTES CARGADOS: Misty cloudiness, loaded horizons and some drizzle.
CERCA DE LA UNA HUBO UN BUEN CHUBASCO DE: Near one o'clock there was a good shower of rain and lighter wind (...) Afterwards it continued calming (...) until it fell entirely calm.
