COMANDANTE DE LA PRIMERA FRAGATAS SUECA:: Commander of the first Swedish frigate: Gustavo Baezfeldi(?). The captain of the second: D. Federico Norberg. The Danish frigate was called Wodfort and its captain Jens Daverhagen.) Latitude "by the land".
COMMANDANT DEED EERSTE VERKENNING SEIN: Commander made the first reconnaissance signal.
COMMANDANT DEED IEDER UUR EEN SCHOT OM T: Commander fired a shot every hour to let it be heard where he was. West meridian 100,5 miles. Changed 15,75 miles W. Obtained 116,5 miles.
COMMANDANT DEED ZEIN VOOR DE CAPTN EN DE: Commander made signal for the captains and Count van Rechteren to come aboard him.
COMMANDANT DOET SEIN OM KONVOOI TE SEPAR: Commander signals to separate the convoy. List of ships.
COMMANDANT HAD 0°14' NB EN 3°17' GEG EN: Commander had 0°14' NB and 3°17' estimated and 0°41' observed longitude.
COMMANDANT HAD 34°46' ZB EN 34°56' LENGT: Commander had 34°46' ZB and 34°56' longitude, east of Lezard 298,75.
COMMANDANT HAD 56°NB, 356°24' WL, PIED H: Commander had 56°NB, 356°24' WL, Pied Heyn 56:23, 353:14, De Jager 56:27, 357:7.
COMMANDANT SIEN DEED VOOR ONS! EN GOES O: Commander made signal for us! and Goes to sail to sea.
COMMANDANT VAN DE SOLDATEN ADRIAAN DE RI: Commander of the soldiers Adriaan de Ring died.
COMMANDANT VD SOLDATEN IN ARREST WGNS BR: Commander of the soldiers under arrest for brutalities.
COMMANDANT WIL MISWIJZING WETEN. MISWIJZ: Commander wants to know the compass variation. Variation commander: 16° 36'. Variation De Beschermer: 16° 19'. Changed longitude 2° 42'.
COMMANDANT: NB IS 4° 20' EN LENGTE 332°: Commander: NB is 4° 20' and longitude 332° 19'. Going to do some hunting.
COMMISSARIS ROELANDUS KOMT AAN BOORD OM: Commissioner Roelandus comes aboard to discharge the remaining crew from service.
COMMISSIE VOOR HET EXAMEN VAN DE CONSTAB: Commission for the examination of gunner's mate Steltenkamp for gunner held a session.
COMO EL TIEMPO ERA CLARO Y PSAN INMEDIAT: As the weather was clear and [?] immediate, they can observe it well, bearing in mind that the same objects seen at night or in dark weather would have given cause to fill the charts with reported shoals.
COMO EL VTO FUE DE TURBONADA CALMÓ BREVE: As the wind came in squalls it calmed briefly (... at 1 1/4 wind came in from the N (...) at 2 lightning was seen in the 1st quarter, very continuous (...) dawn came looking better than yesterday although squally.
COMO EN LOS DÍAS ANTERIORES, LOS DATOS E: As on previous days, the data are taken from the "events", since the table appears empty.
COMO LOS DÍAS ANTERIORES, SIN AGUAS: As on previous days, without water.
COMP SCHIP JAGTRUST PASSEERDE HET EILAND: Company ship JAGTRUST passed the island. The second division under Mr. [?] J Wierts sailed from Texel on the [?] May 1786, and that the country's brig De Pijl, Capt May, had arrived at the Cape.
CON ALGUNA CELAJ. (...) ANOCHEC. CIELOS: With some cloud patches (...) At nightfall skies and horizons with clear cloud patches, sea smooth (...) At dawn the same.
With cloud patches and sea from the SW and W.
CON EL FIN DE AVISTAR CUANTO ANTES LA CO: In order to sight the coast of Chile as soon as possible (...)
CON EL FIN DE AVISTAR LA COSTA ENTRE VAL: In order to sight the coast between Valdivia and Concepción of Chile.
CON EL FIN DE HACER EL CORSO SOBRE LOS C: In order to cruise off Capes Finisterre and Ortegal.
CON EL VTO FLOJO DEL NE (...) ESTANDO CL: With a light wind from the NE (...) the weather being clear and the sea from the SW somewhat heavy. It continued so until after sunset, when it calmed, and at 10 1/2 (...) a light squall shifted to the WNW (...) The wind was veering to the W, with a threatening look.
CON EL VTO. BONANCIBLE POR EL SUR (...): With the wind moderate from the south (...) sea smooth and weather serene until 9 at night, when due to the calm (...) it continued so all night and dawn came with clear cloudiness and some sea from the SE.
CON LA BRISA FRESCA SIN MAR (...) AL ANO: With a fresh breeze without sea (...) at nightfall the breeze was fresher.
CON MAR DE PROA Y POCO VTO (...) ANOCHEC: With head sea and little wind (...) night fell with the sky and horizons streaked with cloud, the wind almost calm with sea from the N (...) at 5 1/2 (...) calm.
With sea from the direction of the wind.
CON MAR GRUESA DEL SO Y SE Y NEVANDO MUC: With heavy sea from the SW and SE and snowing a great deal. So night fell; before 12 the wind began to calm (...) Dawn came with everything closed in with snow, and so much of it fell on deck that it was necessary to throw it off with shovels, as it snowed incessantly; the wind was moderate, but not the seas from the SW and SE, which made us roll a great deal, and these together with the melted snow made the deck impassable, and so there were many falls.
CON MUCHA MAR DE ÉL Y ALGUNA DEL SO Y DE: With much sea from the [?] and some from the SW and S (...) Night fell with sea and wind as at noon, sky streaked with cloud and horizons of bad appearance (...) At 8 1/2 lightning began in the SW and NE (...) a squall from the south of ugly appearance, and the lightning continued, lasting all night. Dawn came with the sky thick with cloudiness, squally horizons, heavy seas from the W and SW and a fresh wind. At this hour a heavy hail fell.
CONDEN JAN HANTHEUNESSEN NIET MEER ZIEN: Conden Jan Hantheunessen not seen any more.
CONSIDERAN EN JUNTA LA POSIBILIDAD DE AR: In council they consider the possibility of putting in at the island of Santa Catalina but in the end decide to continue, given the more favorable change of the wind.
CONSTABELSMAAT FRANSEN OVERLEDEN AAN EEN: Gunner's mate Fransen died of a chest ailment.
CONSTABLE J.J. GROOTE IN DE BOEIEN WGNS: Gunner J.J. Groote in irons for not locking the gunroom. Likewise 3rd sailmaker Koelte. Wahl, for nonchalance.
CONSTAPEL JAN KIEVIT VAN TER VEER OVERLE: Gunner Jan Kievit of Ter Veer died, put overboard in a coffin.
CONSTAPEL SAMUEL CORBET VAN BELVAST OVER: Gunner Samuel Corbet of Belfast died.
CONTINU KAAPSE DUIVEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Continual Cape pigeons near the ship.
CONTINUA EL SARGAZO. ENRUMBA EN DEMANDA: The sargassum continues. Heads for the island of Santa Maria.
CONTINUA EL SARGAZO. NO PUDO OBSERVAR: The sargassum continues. Could not observe.
CONTINUA LA MISMA AGUA. VEN MUCHOS BONIT: The same water continues. They see many bonitos and flying fish, at 16:00 1 tropicbird and at 8:00 some large birds like gannets whose head and breast are white and wings brown, which they call rams, and some swallows. Crosses the line at 21:45.
CONTINUAMOS A GRANGEAR EL RÍO DE LA PLAT: We continue to work our way in the Río de la Plata.
CONTINUAMOS CON LOS HORIZ. Y CIELOS CARG: We continue with the horizons and skies loaded.
CONTINUAMOS EN DEMANDA DE LA TIERRA, QUE: We continue seeking land, which we now eagerly desire (...) an abundance of sea lions, jellyfish, sargassum and some birds such as tropicbirds gave us to understand that we were not far from the coast.
CONTINUAMOS EN DEMANDA DEL CABO SAN LUCA: We continue heading for Cabo San Lucas.
CONTINUAMOS FONDEADOS (...) A LAS 10 1/2: We continue at anchor (...) at 10 1/2 we were clear of [?] and we began to steer SW 5º S.
We continue with heavy overcast weather.
CONTINUAN LAS MARTINPLACAS Y A LAS 11:00: The martinplacas [?] continue and at 11:00 they see many flocks of shearwaters over the water. "The sea we have from the south is without doubt from the pamperos that are blowing and in this season are formidable." They are already making 5 inches of water per hour.
CONTINUARON NAVEGANDO POR ENTRE BANCAS D: They continued sailing among banks of snow, following their course with all vigilance to get clear of them.
CONTINUEEL VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP, WAAROND: Continual birds near the ship, among them large grey gulls.
CONTINUEERDEN NOG DAAGELIJKS OM OLIJ TE: Still continued daily to pour oil.
CONTINUOS AGUACEROS Y FUGADAS DE VIENTO: Continuous downpours and gusts of wind, not sustained.
CONTINUOS CHUBASCOS Y MUCHA CERRAZON: Continuous squalls and much dark overcast.
CONTINUÓ LA BRISA BONANCIBLE (...) LUEGO: The moderate breeze continued (...) after the moon rose the night cleared and the wind eased.
CONTINUÓ LA BRISA FRESCA (...) EL CIELO: The fresh breeze continued (...) the sky and horizons were somewhat dark and the sea less heavy.
CONVOOI KREEG SEIN DAT IEDER KON WERKEN: Convoy got signal that everyone could work as he saw fit; we left it, believing the reason to be that daily it tacked with loss, that the masts were not much to be trusted, that the sick increased from day to day, that the brig De Comeet no longer had any bread, and that it could not well be calculated when with such a convoy the Cape would be approached.
COOMEN SRIEMINEN, EEN VREEMD MATROOS AAN: Coomen Sriemin, a foreign sailor aboard.
COORIENTES A 3 MILLAS/HORA. QUEDA A LA C: Currents at 3 miles/hour. Lies hove to. Noon data (since 18-DIC the descriptors are from nightfall).
CORPERAAL VAN DE SOLDAATEN JOHANNES SOLS: Corporal of the soldiers Johannes Solsberg of Utrecht fell overboard.
CORPOR. CHRISTIAAN GROTH AAN SCHEURBUIJK: Corporal Christiaan Groth died of scurvy.
CORPORAAL VAN DE KOLONIALE TROEPEN T. BR: Corporal of the colonial troops T. Bruno died.
CORRECCIÓN DEL ÚLTIMO RUMBO. LATITUD DE: Correction of the last course. Latitude of arrival 42º 11', (...) mean parallel 41º 53', departure from meridian 21 to the E. The difference in longitude 28' E. The longitude of arrival 6º 56', the direct course 30º 30' 1st quarter, and the distance 41 miles.
CORRECTIE OP DE TIJDMETERS WORDT UITGEVO: Correction of the chronometers is carried out.
CORREDERA DE NUDO A NUDO 46 PIES INGL. L: Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms. 30-second sandglass. First point of departure on the French chart of '53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4th ed. '66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a set square.
Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms. 30-second sandglass. First point of departure on the French chart of '53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4th ed. '66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a set square.
CORREN DE LA MISMA MANERA HASTA LAS 10:0: They run the same way until 10:00. They decide to return directly to Buenos Aires given the lack of water and because they cannot "suffer any longer on that coast the harsh gales that are experienced since the month of February".
CORREN PARALELOS A LAS ISLAS DEL CUERVO: They run parallel to the islands of Cuervo and Flores. Measurement and data from noon, minus the descriptors, which are usually from nightfall.
CORREN SOLO CON TRINQUETE. \"NO PUDIENDO: They run with only the foresail. "Being unable to suffer any longer on this coast the harsh gales that are experienced since the month of February, and also finding ourselves obliged to take the route straight for the Río de la Plata for lack of water." The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
CORRIENDO SIEMPRE CERCA DE LA COSTA. A L: Running always near the coast. At 15:00 they raised to the SW a hill that is S of the Santa Cruz river.
CORRIENTE DEL N. A LAS 20:00 FONDEAN A 3: Current from the N. At 20:00 they anchor 3 leagues from the coast. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
CORRIENTES AL N COMO ES NATURAL EN ESTE: Currents to the N, as is natural in this area. Noon data although some days are from dawn. Since 9-2-1767 they are from dawn. The diary begins on 17-DIC-1766 since it sailed that day but had to return. On 23-DIC it sails definitively.
CORRIENTES AL O FURIOSAS Y POR ELLAS NO: Furious currents to the W and because of them it was not possible to put in at Cumaná, so he decides to take the route of La Guaira. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarteron [?].
CORRIENTES AL SE 1/4 E EN ALGUNOS HILERO: Currents to the SE 1/4 E in some rows of [?]. Noon data although some days are from dawn. Since 9-2-1767 they are from dawn. The diary begins on 17-DIC-1766 since it sailed that day but had to return. On 23-DIC it sails definitively.
CORRIENTES AL SE CON MUCHO RUIDO Y ALBOR: Currents to the SE with much noise and commotion in the water. Noon or day's-run measurement although there are many days without data.
CORRIENTES AL SE CON VIOLENCIA. A LAS 7:: Currents to the SE with violence. At 7:00 the Isle of Pines is recognized.
CORRIENTES AL SE. A LAS 18:30 SONDAN Y H: Currents to the SE. At 18:30 they sounded and found 54 fathoms depth, fine brown sand. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
CORRIENTES AL SSO. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL: Currents to the SSW. Measurement and data from noon, minus descriptors that are usually from nightfall. French chart.
CORRIENTES FUERTES AL O. DATOS DEL MEDIO: Strong currents to the W. Noon data minus the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter [?].
CORRIENTES HASTA LA BERMUDA. MEDICION DE: Currents as far as Bermuda. Noon or day's run measurement, although there are many days without data.
CORRIENTES QUE CORREN POR EL BERIL Y EL: Currents running past the [?] and the Newfoundland Bank.
CORRIENTES QUE LE HAN TIRADO 50 MILLAS C: Currents that have set them 50 miles off the course, because of the lie of the channel, to N 1/4 NE. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. Spanish quarter [?].
CORRIENTES SUMAMENTE CRECIDAS AL N CON F: Extremely swollen currents to the N with strong eddies.
CORRIERON CON EL MISMO TEMPORAL A PALO S: They ran under bare poles in the same gale until 12:00, when it eased somewhat.
CORRIGEERDEN DE POSITIE NIET IN HET JOUR: They did not correct the position in the journal.
CORTA LA LÍNEA EQUINOCIAL POR LOS 355º 5: Crosses the equinoctial line at 355º 52' according to the Tenerife meridian.
CORTAMOS POR LA LINEA AQUINOCIAL POR LOS: We crossed the equinoctial line at 16º 38' W of Cádiz.
CORTE DE LA LÍNEA LAT. S 0º 10': Crossing of the line, lat. S 0º 10'.
CORTE DE LÍNEA, A LAS 5 DE LA MAÑANA: Crossing of the line, at 5 in the morning.
COSTEA EL BAJO A 2 MILLAS Y POR SU HORRO: Coasts along the shoal at 2 miles and, because of its dreadful appearance, gave it the name Bajo Triste (Sad Shoal). Describes it. Here the extract ends.
COSTEANDO CON EL TERRAL. DATOS DEL MEDIO: Coasting with the land breeze. Data from noon or the day's run minus the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Madeira meridian and Dutch chart.
CREE ESTAR A 45 LEGUAS DE TIERRA: Believes to be 45 leagues from land.
CREO QUE POCAS VECES SE LOGRA VER DE TAN: I believe it is rarely possible to see from so far away.
CRUZA EL TROPICO DE CANCER. DATOS DEL ME: Crosses the Tropic of Cancer. Noon data minus the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarter [?].
CRUZAN LA LINEA EN LONGITUD DE 8º 0': They cross the line at longitude 8º 0'.
CUANDO PASO POR EL MERIDIANO LA ESTRELLA: When the star of 1st magnitude called the Foot of the Cross passed the meridian, the latitude by it was found to be 1º 28' 24'' N.
CUYA DEMARCACIÓN Y LATITUD DE LLEGADA HA: Whose bearing and latitude of arrival up to this hour place me at 6º 47' longitude, which differs from the dead-reckoning position by 52' further east of the bearing, leaving the cape at a distance of 3 1/4 leagues.
CÁDIZ AL LNE 5º N DIST. DE 23 2/3 LEGUAS: Cádiz at ENE 5º N, distance 23 2/3 leagues.
DA FONDO DEBIDO A LA FUERZA DEL VIENTO: Anchors because of the force of the wind.
DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO: Anchors in the port of Montevideo.
Anchors at Trinidad but weighs anchor and continues. Irregular data, some from dawn, others from the whole day.
DAAR DE OBSERVATIES GEDURENDE DEZE DAGEN: Because the observations during these days (6/10) were very poor due to the thick, misty air, and because of the large error in latitude in the chronometer observation of the 8th, it is probable that the longitude found so much further east is less
DAARNA VAART HET SCHIP DOOR NAAR ST. MAA: Afterwards the ship sails on to St. Maarten.
DACHTEN 1 ROB BIJ HET SCHIP TE HEBBEN: Thought they had 1 seal near the ship.
DACHTEN LAND IN Z TE ZIEN: Thought they saw land to the S.
DADO EL PENOSO ESTADO DEL NAVIO HACEN JU: Given the pitiful state of the ship, they hold a council and decide to put in at Rio de Janeiro for fear of the pamperos and for lack of a pilot to enter the Río de la Plata.
DAGDEEL 1: ONGESTADIGE KOELTE, DIKKE LUC: Part of day 1: unsteady breeze, thick sky with continuous rain, difficult sea. Part of day 2: suddenly calm, the barometer fell to 29,10. Calm and high sea. At 9.00 o'clock a hard storm. Part of day 3: abating storm.
DAGDEEL 2: HOOGE ZEE UIT HET ZW: Part of day 2: high sea from the SW.
DAGDEEL 2: HOOGE ZEE UIT ZW: Part of day 2: high sea from the SW.
DAGDEEL 2: ZWARE BUIJEN VAN WIND EN ZEE: Part of day 2: heavy squalls of wind and sea.
DAGDEEL 2: ZWARE BUIJEN, HAGEL, REGEN, E: Part of day 2: heavy squalls, hail, rain and lightning in the SW. High sea.
DAGDEL 2: ZWARE BLIKSEM, DONDER EN HOOGE: Part of day 2: heavy lightning, thunder and high sea.
DAGELIJKS VEEL ZIEKEN: KO IN DE KOOI EN: Many sick daily: [?] in the bunk and another 30 or so outside who kept going and standing. Most with high fevers, severe headache and dizziness in the head.
DAGELIJKS WERDEN ER ENIGE VAN DE EQUIPAG: Daily some of the crew who were too full-blooded were bled. Had 9 sick, but of little importance, some with spoiled stomachs and others with venereal complaints. The rest were fresh and healthy, extremely lively and cheerful, and ate with appetite. Continued giving them each morning a small dram of genever drawn on quinine and other ingredients.
DAN ALQUITRAN A ALGUNOS LADOS DEL COSTAD: They apply tar to some parts of the side of the hull. Measurement and data from noon or the day's run, often the descriptors are from dawn.
DAN FONDO EN MONTEVIDEO. RUMBO Y DIRECCI: They anchor at Montevideo. Course and wind direction from noon / the rest of the references the ones closest to noon.
DAN FONDO EN SANTA CATALINA HASTA EL 30: They anchor at Santa Catalina until 30 March.
DANDO CAZA A UNA EMBARCAICÓN DISTANTE AL: Chasing a distant vessel, somewhat ahead.
DANS LA JOURNÉE, CHANGÉ DE MOUILLAGE, ET: During the day, changed anchorage and anchored in 4 fathoms, muddy bottom. The Fort de Cavité bore N16E.
DANS LE JOUR, CHANGÉ DE MOUILLAGE: L'ÎLE: During the day, changed anchorage: the Île du Cénotaphe bore E27N. The entrance of the port, S20E.
DANS LES SUSDITS JOURS, NOUS AVONS NAVIG: In the aforesaid days, we sailed over a bank where the lead gave 22 to 12 fathoms, sand and rock bottom.
DE 'FUNKER' VAN HET 5DE REGIMENT, W ZIEP: The 'funker' of the 5th Regiment, W. Ziep, had died.
DE 21STE VERTREKT DE JOURNAALHOUDER NAAR: On the 21st the journal keeper leaves for Portsmouth, from there overland to London, to sail from London by steamboat in 26 hours to Rotterdam. The journal keeper stays in the Netherlands until 1 October 1829, then sails again to the Indies (on the ship Henrietta Klassina). The journal keeper also reports on this voyage. The data, however, are not usable.
DE 2E SCHRIJVER J.P. LIGTVOORT IN DE BOE: The 2nd clerk J.P. Ligtvoort put in irons for drunkenness and extreme brutality.
DE 2E SCHRIJVER LIGTVOORT UIT DE BOEIEN: The 2nd clerk Ligtvoort released from irons.
DE 3E STUURMAN D. UBERG (?) UIT DE BOEIE: The 3rd mate D. Uberg (?) taken out of irons.
DE 8 KLIPPEN IN DE ENG KAART W. HEATHER: The 8 rocks in the English chart W. Heather 1815 lie SW by S of us at the longitude of Peak [?], at the latitude of 34° 20' to 34° 45".
DE AANVAL WAS HEVIG, DUURDE 3,5 UUR, VUU: The attack was fierce, lasted 3.5 hours, 705 shots were fired; an attack was also made from Malacca; 5000 pounds of powder were used.
DE ADJUNCT SCHRIJVER DE HEER IN ARREST W: The assistant clerk, Mr [?], under arrest for the unauthorized imposition of punishment.
DE AFGEZEILDE MIJLEN BEDRAGEN: 2321. OP: The miles sailed amount to: 2321. On image AAN_1229_1831_0023 is a list of ships lying here in the roads.
DE AJAX HAD EEN GOEDE VERKENNING VAN POR: The Ajax had had a good reconnaissance of Porto Rico and had Cape Sanama WNW, 26 miles from them.
DE AJAX PRAAIDE EEN PRUISISCHE KOFF, KWA: The Ajax hailed a Prussian koff, which came from Lisbon bound for Amsterdam, had been 3 weeks at sea and had had a NW wind all that time. The ship was [?], 38 miles from Hijsant. At quarter past 12 the position of the Neptunus was: 47 degrees 19 minutes latitude and 6 degrees 55 minutes longitude.
DE AJAX PRAAIDE EEN SCHIP, EEN HAMBURGER: The Ajax hailed a ship, a Hamburger, going from Charleston to Nantes; its longitude was 356 degrees 4 minutes and the position of the Ajax was: 43 degrees 11 minutes latitude and 359 degrees 42 minutes longitude.
DE AJAX PRAAIDE EEN SPAANS SCHIP, DAT 18: The Ajax hailed a Spanish ship that had sailed from Havana on 18 June bound for Cadiz. The longitude of this ship was 339 degrees, that of the Ajax 335 degrees.
DE ARRESTANT J. ELIAS UIT DE BOEIEN ONTS: The prisoner J. Elias released from irons.
DE ARRESTANTEN OP DEN 6E TE VOREN VERMEL: The prisoners mentioned earlier on the 6th released from irons.
DE BARKAS VAN DE COMMANDANT KWAM LANGSZI: The commandant's barge came alongside, but when they wanted to row back, they drifted out to sea because of the stiff breeze from the SW, while the rope of their drogue was too short. Our captain immediately came aboard with a pilot from shore, took two reefs in the topsails and set the staysails, at 5 in the evening let our anchor cable slip and by 6 o'clock had got hold of the barge. Shortly afterwards at anchor again.
DE BAROMETER IS VAN KLEMAN IN FRANSCHE D: The barometer is by Kleman, in French inches and divided into 12 parts.
DE BAROMETER NOG ZEER WILD EN MOEILIJK T: The barometer still very wild and difficult to observe.
DE BAROMETER SCHEEN ZEDERT ENIGE TIJD AA: The barometer has seemed for some time not subject to any change, probably defective.
DE BAROMETER ZAKKENDE TOT 29,00. BIJ DE: The barometer falling to 29,00. At the barometer reading stand two values, namely 29,40 and 29,20; I have noted the highest.
DE BAROMETER ZAKTE INEENS VAN 29.95 NAAR: The barometer suddenly fell from 29.95 to 29.50 inches.
DE BESCHERMER GAAT JAGEN IN HET OOSTEN T: The protector goes hunting in the east until the afternoon.
DE BOEDEL VAN DE MATROOS PIETER BANG VER: The estate of the sailor Pieter Bang sold and the remainder noted in the VMW.
DE BOOTSMAN IS OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN OVE: The boatswain fell overboard and dies.
DE BOOTSMANSMAAT AANGESTELD ALS SCHIEMAN: The boatswain's mate appointed as schieman, the schieman's mate appointed as boatswain's mate, the sailor Ernst as schieman's mate.
DE BOTTELIER JAN BOXTERMOLLER OVERLEDEN,: The steward Jan Boxtermoller died, body put overboard.
DE BOTTELIER MULLER SCHULDIG GEMAAKT AAN: The steward Muller, found guilty of misappropriating provisions meant for distribution, I suspended, to do sailors' duty.
DE BRUIN KRIJGT ZIJN COMMISSIE OVERHANDI: De Bruin is handed the commission by the SBN.
DE CAAPSCHE DUIVEN DIE HET SCHIP HADDEN: The Cape pigeons that had accompanied the ship in a great multitude began to disappear.
DE CAPTEEM M. DE VRIES OVERLEED 'S OCHTE: The captain M. de Vries died in the morning.
DE CHIRURGIJN 3E KLASSE D.P. LAER IN ARR: The surgeon 3rd class D.P. Laer under arrest while continuing to perform duty. The sick attendant Ternate punished with three dozen blows with the flat of the hand for carelessness and brutality.
The surgeon Laer released from arrest.
DE COMANDEUR MATTIJS DE VOS OVERLEDEN: The commander Mattijs de Vos died.
DE COMMANDANT \"VAN BRAAM\" EN ONZE KAPI: The commandant "Van Braam" and our captain leave overland for Colombo.
DE COMMANDANT BESLUIT MET AARTHUIJSEN VO: The commandant decides to sail ahead with Aarthuijsen. The three remaining ships, which sail less well, stay together.
DE COMMANDANT BEZOEKT DE ANDERE SCHEPEN: The commandant visits the other ships of the squadron.
DE COMMANDANT DEED SEIN OM HEM DE BREEDT: The commandant signalled to have the latitudes signalled to him: Utrecht: 66° 38'. Wassenaar: 62° 2'. Goes: 64° 2'. Princes Louisa: 68°2'. Frigate Munnikkendam: 66° 38. Juno: 67° 54'. Note: the latitude was asked to be given and these are the degrees of longitude.
DE COMMANDANT DEED SEIN VAN 'T BESTEK OP: The commandant signalled to give the position: the island of Saona, according to the Dordin chart NE 37.5 miles. According to the new chart NE by E 31.5 miles.
DE COMMANDANT HAD 2°20' NB EN 359°17' AA: The commandant had 2°20' N and 359°17' by chronometers.
DE COMMANDANT KOMT MET EEN JACHT VAN BAT: The commandant comes with a yacht from Batavia and visits the Goes, the Princes and the Juno.
DE COMMANDANT SEINT DAT ONZE KAPITEIN BI: The commandant signals that our captain must come aboard to the commandant. The longboat is lowered for this and later taken back aboard.
DE COMMANDANT SEINT: 34° 25' ZB, 41° 8': The commandant signals: 34° 25' S, 41° 8' E. The mean ex-meridian latitude taken before and after noon was 35° 7' and [?] … (missing). Put our position on the chart at the ex-meridian latitude, because no signs of land could be seen at all and, to all appearances, we had been set strongly to the south.
DE COMMANDANT ZIJN BESTEK STOND OP BREED: The commandant's position was at latitude 34°42'' and longitude 326°20''.
DE COMMANDEUR LIET DE SCHIEMAN UIT DE BO: The commander had the schieman released from irons with a good reprimand. 7 sick.
DE COMMANDEUR VAN DE SOLDATEN WERD IN DE: The commander of the soldiers was put in irons. This one is accused of indecent things: he is said to have played with the private parts of a boy (and wanted the same from that boy).
DE CORPORAAL DER MILITAIREN AF GESTRAFT: The corporal of the military punished with some flat blows [?] for drunkenness and brutalities.
DE DAG HIERVOOR UIT HAVANA RICHTING CURA: Had left Havana the day before, heading for Curaçao.
DE DERDE KOK, JAN FREDERIK LOUWZANTS AAN: The third cook, Jan Frederik Louwzants, died of the diarrhoea which he had contracted at Elmina.
DE DERDE TIMMERMAN GEDESERTEERD. SLOEP N: The third carpenter deserted. Sloop to shore to fetch water and look for the carpenter. Sailor Daniel Tesko died.
DE DRIE GEBROEDERS WAREN GISTERMIDDAG OP: The three brothers had been yesterday afternoon at 1° 3' S and 97°7'.
DE EERSTE SCHIPPER IS AAN DE GEVOLGEN VA: The first skipper died of the effects of a rupture.
DE EKTHROM HAD OOK HET EILAND FERO GEZIE: The Ekthrom had also sighted the island Fero.
DE EQUIPAGE EEN EXTRA OORLAM: An extra dram of spirits for the crew.
DE EQUIPAGE ONTVING EEN EXTRA OORLAM TER: The crew received an extra dram of spirits on the occasion of the birthday of a member of the royal house.
DE EQUIPAGE WAS FRIS EN GEZOND, KREGEN E: The crew was fresh and healthy; every morning at 7 o'clock they received a bitter little drink of 'gin with quinine'. The bunks and bedding are aired on deck daily.
DE FONTUIJN WAS GISTEREN OP DE NB VAN 4°: The Fontuijn had been yesterday at north latitude 4° 25' and longitude 95° 50'.
DE FRANSE KAPER VERTROK. WIJ SCHOTEN 4 X: The French privateer left. We fired 4 times at him with live shot (…). But he continued on his course.
DE FUSELIER M. BERTOG AAN DISENTERIE OVE: The fusilier M. Bertog died of dysentery.
DE GEBETERDE KOERS 31 MINDER BEWESTEN 'T: The corrected course is 31 less westerly than southwest.
DE GEGEVEN LENGTE IS DE HOLLANDSE LENGTE: The longitude given is the Dutch longitude. According to the French chart it is: 304° and 56'.
DE GEIT GING DOOD, JAMMER VAN DE MELK: The goat died, a pity about the milk.
DE GEMIDDELDE LENGTE VAN ALLE 19 SCHEPEN: The average longitude of all 19 ships was on the 20th of this month 337° 33', from which our dead reckoning takes its progress.
DE GEMIDDELDE TIJDM. LENGTE GEEFT DUS EE: The average chronometer longitude therefore gives a difference of 22'48" too far east.
DE GEREFORMEERDE KERK ZWTW 1/2 W: The Reformed Church southwest by west 1/2 west
DE GIS VAN PENEDO DE ST. PAULO KAN QUA A: The estimate of Penedo de St. Paulo cannot be right as to distance; probably another digit must follow the 5.
DE GISTEREN GEBOEIDE SOLDAAT AFGESTRAFT: The soldier put in irons yesterday punished with a [?]
DE GOEDEREN VAN DE OVERLEDEN WOUTER VAN: The goods of the deceased Wouter van Simmeren sold.
DE GOUVERNEUR VAN BATAVIA KOMT MET EEN S: The Governor of Batavia comes with a sloop. Parade in the rigging, the commander fires 15 salute shots. Captain ashore. Lieutenant Faber held command.
DE HARDLOPER, SCHIPPER JOHANNES SELIEN,: The Hardloper, skipper Johannes Selien, has been abandoned by the crew; my skipper wonders whether they did enough to save the ship.
DE HEER DE LIEL OVERLEDEN (ZIE 9/6, IMAG: Mr De Liel deceased (see 9/6, image 49, (38)). 5 shots with 18 pounders when putting him overboard.
DE HEER LUITENANT LELI OVERLEDEN (38) (D: Lieutenant Mr Leli deceased (38) (struck through). Fired 5 shots with 18 pounders when putting him overboard. (See 12-6, image 50)
DE HOLLANDSE SLOEP GING MET 2 PASSAGIERS: The Dutch sloop went ashore with 2 passengers and Van Beek.
DE HOLLANSCHE BEZITTING BATTICALO IN HET: The Dutch possession Batticalo in the southwest 1/2? of us.
DE INVALIDE KORPORAAL J.W. BLONDEL OVERL: The invalid corporal J.W. Blondel died.
DE JAREN HIERNA VAART HET SCHIP ROND IN: In the years after this the ship sails around in the Indian waters. The journal ends in 1856 when the ship is still in the Indonesian archipelago.
DE JONGE J. FUGE OVERLEDEN: The ship's boy J. Fuge died.
DE JONGEN JACOBUS OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN: The boy Jacobus fell overboard and was killed.
DE JONGMATROOS CHRISTIAN FRIEDRICH LIEBE: The ordinary seaman Christian Friedrich Lieber of Osnabrug died, no. 15.
DE JONGMATROOS CORNELIS VAN DER LELY VAN: The ordinary seaman Cornelis van der Lely of Beverwijk died.
DE JONGMATROOS JAN GERRITSE VAN MAASTRIC: The ordinary seaman Jan Gerritse of Maastricht died, no. 13.
DE KAAPSCHE WOLKEN WERDEN NU DOOR ONS OO: The Cape clouds were now also discovered by us. This is a phenomenon seen south of the Tropic of Capricorn, by which one can tell that one is approaching the Cape of Good Hope. It consists of two small white clouds and one black one, which rise and set.
The cabin cook and baker in irons for drunkenness.
DE KAPITEIN IS VAN COLOMBO GEKOMEN, NADA: The captain has come from Colombo, after having been ill there.
DE KAPITEIN KREEG DOOR HET SLECHTE WEER: Because of the bad weather the captain had an accident; he fell from the stairs of the half deck into the hold. He instructed 1st Lieutenant Verweer to take over command.
DE KAPITEIN KWAM VAN DE KUST TERUG MET H: The captain returned from the coast with a headache. Later he was speechless and had convulsions.
DE KAPITEIN WIL AFWACHTEN AF ER GEEN OOR: The captain wants to wait and see whether there are no warships waiting in the bay of Hitland or lying in wait beyond the island. The crew is beginning to die, and after a heated exchange of words (in the afternoon) with the warrant officer it is decided to sail on.
DE KLIP VAN CALESFONIER DIE OPHALENDE LU: The rock of Calesfonier, which, as the sky clears, the chart of W. Heather places at 12° 25' N and 54° 45' west of Greenwich, bears by chronometer longitude from the Panter west 1/3 south, 92 miles.
DE KOERS IS NNO EN KUNNEN TUSSEN PORTO R: The course is north-northeast and we can pass between Porto Rico and the island Mona.
DE KOERS STAAT ALS VOLGT GENOTEERD: Z61°: The course is noted as follows: S61°11'W. I note that as S61:11W.
DE KOLONIALE SOLDAAT A. SCHEER OVERLEDEN: The colonial soldier A. Scheer died.
DE KORPORAAL VAN HET 25E REGIMENT J. SIM: The corporal of the 25th Regiment J. Simons died.
DE KRIJGSARTIKELEN VOORGELEZEN EN EEN PR: The articles of war were read out and a promotion held for the officers whose positions were vacant.
DE KRUISPEILING VOLGENS DE KUSTKAART NOR: The cross bearing according to the coast chart Norue and that of Horsburgh gives the longitude 103°32'. There are still some remarks about observed differences between the chronometers. Up to image 0033 lying in the roads and sailing in the East Indian archipelago, report with tables of chronometer readings.
DE KUIPER BEZIG AAN EEN BADKUIP VOOR ZIE: The cooper is busy with a bathtub for the sick.
DE KUIPER IS ZIEK, WILLEN DE KUIPER VAN: The cooper is ill; they want to borrow the cooper of Skipper Riems, but he is ill too.
DE KWARTIERMEESTER F. OUDENANSE IS TOEN: The quartermaster F. Oudenanse was found in his bunk when he had the watch; he was put in irons by hands and feet.
DE KWEEKELING J. VAN BEKKER OVERLEED EN: The apprentice J. van Bekker died and was committed to the sea.
DE LA ESCUADRA AL AMANECER SÓLO SE VIÓ U: Of the squadron at dawn only one ship was seen.
DE LENGTE DOOR DE TIJDMETER, (T/M 31 MEI: The longitude by chronometer (up to and including 31 May this is given at the first part of the day).
DE LENGTE DOOR ZON EN MAAN: The longitude by sun and moon.
DE LENGTE DOOR ZON EN MAAN AFSTAND: The longitude by sun and moon distance.
DE LENGTE DOOR ZON/MAAN (1E DD): The longitude by sun/moon (1st part of the day)
DE LENGTE IS AANGEPAST NAAR AANLEIDING V: The longitude was adjusted following an observation of the distance between sun and moon.
DE LENGTE TIJDMETER HERLEID VOLGENS EEN: The chronometer longitude reduced according to an observation to 1° 51'0" east of Greenwich.
DE LENGTE VAN DE DRIE SCHEPEN IS: DUIJFI: The longitude of the three ships is: Duijfie 0° 8', Zeepard 359° 40', Vreedenburg 359° 16'. The average longitude is 359° 41'
DE LENGTE VAN DE MENTOR VERSCHILT 2° MET: The longitude of the Mentor differs by 2° from that of the commander.
DE LENGTE VAN DE POLLUX (SCHIP VAN HET Z: The longitude of the Pollux (ship of the same convoy as the Iris) was 348 degrees 37 minutes. The longitude of the Iris was 354 degrees 57 minutes. So the difference by which we were too far east was 6 degrees 20 minutes.
DE LENGTE VAN DIT WELGELEGEN IS 31°51: The longitude of this Welgelegen is 31°51
DE LENGTE VAN HET SCHIP DE LIEFDE GISTER: The longitude of the ship De Liefde yesterday: 122° 49'.
DE LENGTE VAN HET SCHIP RECHT DOOR ZEE I: The longitude of the ship Recht door Zee is: 1°46'
The longitude of the ship Recht door Zee is: 359°14'
DE LETTERS \"LS\" IN DE KOLOM BREEDTE/LE: The letters "LS" in the latitude/longitude column.
DE LETTERS \"LS\"IN DE KOLOM BREEDTE/LEN: The letters "LS" in the latitude/longitude column.
DE LETTERS \"LS\"IN KOLOM BREEDTE/LENGTE: The letters "LS" in the latitude/longitude column.
DE LICHTMATROOS B. GURLING VIEL VAN DE K: The light seaman B. Gurling fell overboard from the crossjack yard, but kept swimming long enough to be rescued with a boat.
DE LINIE EQUINOCTIAAL GEPASSEERD. IN BRE: Crossed the equinoctial line. In the latitude column under 0° 6' it says: 9' south.
DE LINIE EQUINOCTIAAL OP 18 GR. 32' LENG: Crossed the equinoctial line at longitude 18° 32'.
DE LUCHT VERDEKT, DOOR DE ROOK VEROORZAA: The sky darkened by the smoke caused by the bursting and burning of the mountain Pamalang, on the southeast coast of Java; several bangs were heard.
DE LUITENANT 1E KLAS PIETER VAN GELDROP: The lieutenant 1st class Pieter van Geldrop died.
DE MADRUGADA CORTAN LA LINEA EQUINOCCIAL: At dawn they cross the equinoctial line. Measurement and noon data, minus descriptors that are usually from nightfall. They follow the Dutch chart.
DE MADRUGADA FONDEA EN EL PLACER DEL CAY: At dawn anchors on the shoal of Cayo de Sal because of the strong west-northwest wind with squalls.
DE MALLY HAD NB 37G52M, LENGTE VAN LONDE: The Mally had north latitude 37° 52', longitude from London 21
DE MARINIER G. DE ROOIJ UIT HOOFDE VAN H: The marine G. de Rooij, on account of repeated neglect of duty, being sickly in constitution and improper in conduct, was discharged from all duties as a marine.
DE MARINIER HALFWAS OVERLEDEN EN DE MATR: The marine Halfwas died and the sailor J. Venero died.
DE MATROOS 1 KL. C. H. BERG EN MATROOS 2: The seaman 1st class C. H. Berg and seaman 2nd class Van der Stel demoted to seamen 3rd class for poor and careless work when setting up the topgallant masts.
DE MATROOS 3K S. HAARINS VAN DE RAA GESL: The seaman 3rd class S. Haarins was knocked off the yard into the fore shrouds and fell from there onto the deck, whereby his right leg is broken.
DE MATROOS BARTEL HAMSKENS OVERLEDEN, NO: The sailor Bartel Hamskens died, no. 3.
DE MATROOS C.F. BLOEM UIT DE BOEIEN ONTS: The sailor C.F. Bloem released from the irons.
DE MATROOS DANIËL HOUTHUYZEN VAN AMSTERD: The sailor Daniël Houthuyzen of Amsterdam died.
DE MATROOS DAVIED SPITTER VAN GORIDA OVE: The sailor Davied Spitter of Gorida died.
The sailor Doris Eijge in irons.
DE MATROOS H. KINTER VAN HASELUNNE EN DE: The sailor H. Kinter of Haselunne and the soldier Karel Woycke of Thoren died, no. 11-12.
DE MATROOS HUYBERT VAN DER LEEUW VAN GOU: The sailor Huybert van der Leeuw of Gouda fell overboard and drowned.
The sailor J.T. de Junge died.
DE MATROOS JOHANNES BORN VAN DANTZIG OVE: The sailor Johannes Born of Dantzig died, no. 18.
DE MATROOS JOHANNES VRUND VAN AMSTERDAM: The sailor Johannes Vrund of Amsterdam drowned.
DE MATROOS JOSEPH PALMA VAN CORSICA OVER: The sailor Joseph Palma of Corsica died.
DE MATROOS MARCUS MADSON VAN CHRISTINA O: The sailor Marcus Madson of Christina died, no. 14.
DE MATROOS PIETER DE ROO AANGESTELD ALS: The sailor Pieter de Roo appointed as chaplain
DE MATROOS THOMAS MULDER VAN AMSTERDAM O: The sailor Thomas Mulder of Amsterdam died, no. 5.
DE MATROZEN VAN STAVEREN EN MULDER IN DE: The seamen Van Staveren and Mulder in irons in the day watch, and out of irons in the forenoon watch.
DE MEESTER ZETTE DE MATROOS JACOBUS BRED: The surgeon amputated the right leg of the sailor Jacobus Bredenbot.
DE MISWIJZING BEHOORT EVENALS DE VORIGE: The magnetic variation should be, as on the previous voyage, 34° NW
DE OFFICIERS KOK VEHAGEN WEGENS DRONKENS: The officers' cook Vehagen, for drunkenness and the resulting breaking of a considerable part of the [?] goods of the officers, and further for being improper in his language when spoken to about it, saying 'go to the lightning', was shut in irons by the second officer of the watch.
The officers' cook J.M. Kremeger died.
DE ONDERTIMMERMAN GERRIT JOOSTEN DE BOK: The under-carpenter Gerrit Joosten de Bok of Oude Wetering died.
DE OPPER TIMMERMAN EN DE SMID IN DE BOEI: The chief carpenter and the smith in irons
DE OPPERMEESTERS OVERLEGDEN OVER HET AFZ: The chief surgeons deliberated about amputating a leg
DE PASSAGIER PHILIP MEYER VAN DANTZIG OV: The passenger Philip Meyer of Dantzig died.
DE PEILINGEN KOMEN IN DE KAART VAN STRAA: The bearings fall on Horsburgh's chart of the Sunda Strait at south latitude 6°7'30'' and longitude 105°30', being only a difference of 9' in longitude.
DE PREDIKANT OBERLEIN HEEFT PREDIKATEN G: The preacher Oberlein gave sermons. Corrected course southwest 1/4? 14.5 miles.
DE PRIJS DE NAAM HAD FRIENDS OF LEMMERIC: The prize had the name Friends of Lemmerick. Maximum longitude 5G8M from the Cerene.
DE PROVISIONEEL STUURMAN FAAK HENDRIKS V: The provisional mate Faak Hendriks of Von Kriel died.
DE PROVOOST IN DE BOEIEN GESLAGEN WEGENS: The provost put in irons for drunkenness.
DE PROVOOST IS ONDER BELOFTE VAN BETERSC: The provost was released again on promise of improvement.
DE PROVOOST VOND DUCATEN, MAAR WIST NIET: The provost found ducats, but did not know who had put them in his bunk.
DE REIS VAN EUROPA NAAR AFRIKA ONTBREEKT: The voyage from Europe to Africa is missing, only summarized by the person who copied the journal. The journal begins at Castle Elmina. Important: the days end with the day watch and forenoon watch. I again always take over from the forenoon watch of the day before!
DE REST VAN HET JOURNAAL BLIJFT HET SCHI: For the rest of the journal the ship remains in the archipelago.
DE RIVIER WAS VOL IJS. BLEVEN TOT 31 MAA: The river was full of ice. Stayed lying at Helvoet until 31 March, being prevented by the ice from sailing to Dordrecht.
DE SAL, EEN DER KAAPVERDISCHE OF ZOUTE E: The Sal, one of the Cape Verde or salt islands.
DE SBN BUIJSKES HUURT DE CADMUS VOOR 385: Rear admiral Buijskes charters the Cadmus for 38500 guilders. '215 on our roll and extra messing for 7 heads. Heard that His Majesty's ship Prins Frederik lay badly leaking at the Cape of Good Hope.
DE SCHEEPSKOK SCHLENKE WEGENS VECHTERIJ: The ship's cook Schlenke, for fighting and slander, and the steward's mate Wilkins shut in irons. The first-named on water and bread.
DE SCHEEPSKORPORAAL, JAN SCHENNELT, OVER: The ship's corporal, Jan Schennelt, died.
DE SCHEPEN VAREN IN KONVOOI, MAAR DE LEN: The ships sail in convoy, but the longitude now deviates by about 2°
DE SCHILDWACHT DIE EERDER IN DE BOEIEN W: The sentry who had earlier been put in irons was released from the irons without the approval of the vice-admiral, whereupon he had to go back in, because according to the vice-admiral he deserved more punishment.
DE SCHIPPER ERASMUS SMIT MELDE DAT ZIJN: Skipper Erasmus Smit reported that his mate had broken his arm
DE SCHIPPER REUL EN HET VOLK WILDE HET S: Skipper Reul and the crew wanted to abandon the ship because they saw no chance of keeping it above water any longer.
DE SCHIPPER VAN DE AMERONGEN IS NIET WEL: The skipper of the Amerongen is not well. The chief surgeon goes over there.
DE SLOEP AAN BOORD (VAN DE BOVENKERKERPO: The sloop alongside (of the Bovenkerkerpolder) with some gunners' goods that had been left on board the Juno.
The smith W. Aders and the boatswain's mate E. Aalders put in irons because of a quarrel between the two
DE SNELSTE VAART IS? 3/4 MIJL GEWEEST. G: The fastest speed was? 3/4 mile. Corrected course and distance southwest by west 1/8 west, 45 miles. Change of longitude 0° 47'

DE SOLDAAT ADRIAAN VAN GENNIP VAN HAARLE: The soldier Adriaan van Gennip of Haarlem died, no. 17.
DE SOLDAAT CHRISTIAAN KLEMKE VAN BERLIJN: The soldier Christiaan Klemke of Berlijn died.
The soldier J. van de Bos died, no. 4.
The soldier Jan Benet Freman died.
DE SOLDAAT JOHAN ANDREAS PETERSEN VAN GR: The soldier Johan Andreas Petersen of Gravendaal died, no. 6.
DE SOLDAAT JOHAN GEORG GRAAL OVERLEDEN,: The soldier Johan Georg Graal died, no. 9.
DE SOLDAAT JOHAN HERNZICH SEITS OVERLEDE: The soldier Johan Hernzich Seits died, no. 3.
DE SOLDAAT MAURITS SCHWARTZ VAN HALLEROP: The soldier Maurits Schwartz of Hallerop died, no. 16.
DE STROOM GEDURENDE DIT ETMAAL N.O. O. G: The current during this day's run having been NE by E, a difference in latitude of 33 minutes was thereby produced, which gives 15 miles of distance and 1 degree 2 minutes change in longitude to the east, the corrected longitude thus being 303 degrees 49 minutes. At 1 o'clock the reckoned position of the Neptunus: 35 degrees 55 minutes latitude and 302 degrees 48 minutes longitude; of the Joan de Witt: 35 degrees 58 minutes latitude and 302 degrees 10 minutes longitude; of the Ajax: 36 degrees 2 minutes latitude and 302 degrees 22 minutes longitude.
The current sets strongly to the north.
DE STUURMAN EN NOG 2 MAN ZIEK: The mate and 2 more men sick.
DE STUURMAN MET NOG 2 MAN ZEER SLECHT: The mate with 2 more men very ill.
DE STUURMAN MET NOG 2 MAN ZIEK: The mate with 2 more men sick.
DE SUSSANNA ZIET LAND. PRAAIDEN HEM. ZIJ: The Sussanna sights land. Hailed him. His longitude: 65° 0'. Sussanna has seen a ship. The fluyt proved to be the Drie Gebroeders. Corrected course and distance WSW 22.5 miles.
DE TEMPERATUUR EN DRUK WORDT VANAF HIER: The temperature and pressure are recorded from here on in the AMW.
The thermometer stood at 84 to 85 degrees.
DE TIJDMETER KWAM NIET UIT OP SINT HELEN: The chronometer did not come out right at Sint Helena, which island we did not see; steered WNW for 12 hours.
DE TIJDMETER LENGTE MET DIE DER PIJLING: The chronometer longitude agreeing with that of the bearing, took it as the position sailed.
DE TIMMERMAN BEGINT DE TENT TE MAKEN. ZI: The carpenter begins to make the awning. See much filth floating.
DE TWEEDE SCHRIJVER H. ELDERS IN DE BOEI: The second clerk H. Elders in irons, as is the sailor J. Pieters.
DE UITKIJK ZAG GROENTE DRIJVEN, ZIEN OOK: The lookout saw greenery floating; also see 3 shore gulls and several kinds of birds.
DE VERHEID IS 177 MIJL OMDAT IN HET EXTR: The distance is 177 miles because in the extract the days 3 to 8 March are combined. Hence these days also have the same values.
DE VERJAARDAG VAN DE PRINS VAN ORANJE, E: The birthday of the Prince of Orange; extra wine for the crew.
DE VERSCHILLENDE WACHTEN WORDEN WEER AFZ: The various watches are again recorded separately. The weather data from here on are indeed from the forenoon watch.
DE VREEDENBURG VAART IN FEBRUARI 1790 EN: The Vreedenburg sails several times back and forth in February 1790 from Punte Gale to Colombo.
DE VROUW VAN DE SERGEANT GERLACH VAN DE: The wife of the sergeant Gerlach of the troops gave birth to a daughter.
DE VROUW VAN SERGEANT-MAJOOR J. GORDON B: The wife of sergeant-major J. Gordon gave birth to a daughter.
DE VROUW VAN VAN DE EERSTE TIMMERMAN IS: The wife of the first carpenter gave birth to a little daughter.
DE WAARNEMINGEN VAN DEZE DAG STAAN OPNIE: The observations of this day are entered again under Wednesday 28 September. After this day counting simply continues with Thursday 29 etc.
DE WARE BEKOMEN LENGTE IS HIER DE BEVOND: The true longitude obtained here is the chronometer longitude found.

The true longitude obtained here is the chronometer longitude found. The islands Paulus and Amsterdam lie, according to logbooks and the best chart, at 75 degrees 5 minutes longitude east of Paris, and according to the chart in use by the French, 3 degrees further west.
The true longitude obtained here is the chronometer longitude found. The current had set us about 45 minutes to the west since we left New Holland.
DE WARE BEKOMEN LENGTE IS VOLGENS BRUNEL: The true longitude obtained is according to Brunelli.
DE WASSENAAR HEEFT STEEDS MOEITE OM DE S: The Wassenaar constantly has trouble keeping up with the speed of the Utrecht.
DE WEERSGESTELDHEID STAAT ALLEEN VERMELD: The weather is only recorded for the dog watch. I have noted this. Thereafter nothing about the weather is recorded for the forenoon watch, but the course, longitude and latitude are recorded there.
The wind veered S-SSW-SSE-S by W.
The wind is too stiff to beat to windward.
DE WIND ZICH STEEDS VERHEFFENDE, LUCHT E: The wind constantly rising, air and water could no longer be told apart, and hail and rain without ceasing. The sea resembled a desert of sand full of hills, with driving snow. At 3 o'clock the barometer seemed to stand [still], and the weather also seemed to have reached its height then, as the hail stopped and changed to fine rain. At 4 o'clock the mercury, which had fallen 10 lines, had risen 1½ lines, and since six o'clock one could clearly perceive the lessening of the wind; at 8 o'clock the mercury had risen 4 lines and the weather had truly calmed, which gradually diminished along with the sea. Afternoon watch: dry and manageable weather; bent on a jib, mainsail and mizzen. The wind had gradually veered round to the SW. Forenoon: tacked about to the NW and set course. Wind decreasing to light airs. Noon position 28-35 South 57-08 East.
DE WIND- EN WEERGEGEVENS HEBBEN DOORGAAN: The wind and weather data generally relate to the HW, DW and VMW.
DE WINDKRACHT LIGT BESLOTEN IN DE WEERSG: The wind force is included in the weather description.
DE ZEE ALS IN VUUR (PRACHTIG GEZICHT): The sea as if on fire (magnificent sight).
DE ZEE BEDEKT MET EEN DONKER ROOD, KAPIT: The sea covered with a dark red; the captain, after investigation, thinks it an eruption of an undersea volcano.
The sea a dirty green colour.
DE ZEE WAS DOOR DE HEVIGE WIND EEN VUUR: The sea was a fire because of the violent wind.
DE ZEE WAS ZO HOOG DAT MET STAANDE OP DE: The sea was so high that, standing on the poop, the sea appeared above the fore yard.
DE ZEE WERD AFGAANDE WEG HOGER WAARDOOR: As the ship made way off, the sea grew higher, so that the ship began to roll heavily and water came aboard; the weather worsening, at half past nine hove to under the reefed mizzen, on the starboard tack, after first having made signal.
DE ZEE ZOO AFGRIJSLIJK VERBOLGEN DAT MIJ: The sea so dreadfully swollen that my 31 years' experience of it offered not the least precedent here. (Some? pieces overboard.)
DE ZEILMAKERSLEERLING A. DIJKSMA VIEL OV: The sailmaker's apprentice A. Dijksma fell overboard and drowned because he could not swim.
DE ZIEKE LUITENANT MESTERIKEN VRAAGT OM: The sick lieutenant Mesteriken asks for the surgeon of the Zuijlevelt. This is granted.
DE ZIEKEN ONDER HET SCHEEPSVOLK NEEMT ST: The sick among the crew are decreasing strongly, now only 32 sick. Gave the people 1.5 can of drinking water.
DE ZIEKEN VERMEERDERDE ZICH AAN BOORD. M: The sick increased aboard. Sailor C. Bohm and first boatswain's mate H. Hopman died and were buried at sea.
The sick increased from day to day. The brig De Comeet already had no bread left.
The sick did not yet recover.
DE ZOUTVLEES VATEN ZIJN BEDORVEN EN WORD: The salt meat casks are spoiled and are thrown overboard as unusable.
DE ZUURKOOL IS BEDORVEN EN WORDT OVER BO: The sauerkraut is spoiled and is thrown overboard.
DE ZWARTE LANDVOGEL IS AFGEMAT VAN HET V: The black land bird is exhausted from flying and lets itself be caught easily. It is put in a basket in the gallery.
DEDEN 13 KANONSCHOTEN EN WERDEN DOOR 'T: Fired 13 gun shots and were thanked by the flagship. God be thanked for a safe voyage, amen. Of 5 months and 22 days, not counting the days in port.
DEDEN 2 KLOPGANGEN OM OP ONZE POST TE KO: Beat to quarters twice to get to our stations.
DEDEN ALLES WAT MOGELIJK WAS OM BOVEN GA: Did everything possible to get up to windward.
DEDEN EEN LOSE MONSTERING, ER WAREN 3 AB: Held a loose muster; there were 3 absentees.
DEDEN EEN SCHOT EN LIETEN DE PASSJAER VL: Fired a shot and let the passenger flag fly.
DEDEN EEN SCHOT MET SCHERP OP EEN SCHIP: Fired a shot with live ammunition at a ship that sailed astern and showed no flag.
DEDEN POGINGEN DE VRESELIJKE SUIKERSTANK: Made attempts to drive out the dreadful sugar stench. Cook's mate Munniks released from irons, but punished again in the same way for 2 nights for insubordination in his duty.
DEED DEN WIMPELVOERDER SEIJN VAN PISVAAR: The pennant-bearer made signal [?] of Pisvaaren. The Gouverneur-Generaal had 336:44, the Casteel van Tilburg 335:46 and the Nieuwvijvervreugd 335:34.
DELEN 25 EXEMPLAREN VAN 'T ZENDELINGEN G: Handed out 25 copies of the Missionary Society's [publication] to the crew, also a tub of gherkins.
DELEN DE REST VAN HET PRIJSGELD UIT, NOG: Shared out the rest of the prize money, still from Malakka and Slanghoon.
DELEN KAAS UIT AAN 'T VOLK: Handed out cheese to the people.
Handed out cheese to the people.
DELEN MEEL EN MOSTERD ZAAD: Handed out flour and mustard seed.
DELEN MEEL EN MOSTERD. DAGELIJKS DE PATR: Handed out flour and mustard. Daily the portholes open.
DELEN UIEN AAN 'T VOLK: Handed out onions to the people.
DEMARCA LA ISLA DE ANNOBON: Bearing of the island of Annobon.
DEMORA CABO S. VICENTE AL ONO DIST. 56 M: Cape S. Vicente bears ENE, distance 56 miles.
DEMORA EL CABO ESPARTEL AL (NO PONE NADA: Cape Espartel bears (nothing stated), distance 39 miles.
DEMORA EL CABO SAN VICENTE AL SSE 7º L,: Cape San Vicente bears SSE 7° L, distance 38 1/2 leagues.
DEMORA LA MEDIANÍA DE LA ENSENADA DEL CA: The middle of the inlet of Cape Gracias a Dios bears N 6° W, distance 6 leagues.
DEMORÁNDOME CÁDIZA AL ESE 8º E DIST. DE: Cádiz bearing from me ESE 8° E, distance 12 leagues.
On the 2nd the second mate Johan Vogler fo. 10 died.
DEN 3DE CHIRURGIJN FREDERIK WEEBER KWAM: On the 3rd the surgeon Frederik Weeber died.
DEN ADELBORST 1E KLASSE KIETSMA IN ARRES: The midshipman 1st class Kietsma under arrest.
DEN COMMMANDEUR DELVOS HAD SCHIEMAN INDE: The commander Delvos had Schieman put in irons for brutality towards the boatswain the previous night.
DEN DERDEWAAK JG. SELLIUS OP BELOFTEN BE: The third watch officer Jg. Sellius released from his arrest on promise of improvement.
DEN EERSTEN OFFICIER VAN DEN COM VAN BRA: The first officer of the Com van Braam brought ashore and buried.
DEN HEERE ZIJ GELOOFT VOOR SIJNEN WELDAD: The Lord be praised for His benefits shown to us unworthy, for a safe voyage. Amen.
DEN JONGMATROOS JAN SNOEK VAN DELFT WIER: The ship's boy Jan Snoek of Delft, as he was sitting in the fore chains to relieve himself, was knocked out of the chains into the sea by a dreadful sea.
DEN LUITENANT BOONDERS, DEN SCHIEMANSMAA: The lieutenant Boonders, the mate's assistant H. Holmers and the second cooper Louwerentuur discharged.
DEN WINT OZO EN LIEP WEL TWEE STREEKEN H: The wind ESE and ran well two points back and forth.
DENKEN DAT ST. MARIA NIET OP DE JUISTE B: Think that St. Maria is not placed at the right latitude on the passage chart, because they see no (signs of) land.
DENKEN DE KIEKENSBAAI EN DE OOSTHOEK VAN: Think they see Kiekensbaai and the east point of Java. Take bearings of the east point of the island Noesa Baron at NNW 1/2 W, and the easternmost land that could be seen at ENE [?], 5 miles. Sunset: the westernmost land that could be seen NW by W W/S W, and a high mountain, probably the mountain Cadijri, NW by W, and the island Noesa Baron ENE, 6 miles. See land at NNE. Description of this land. Sounded all watches, no bottom.
DENKEN DE PASSAATWIND GEVONDEN TE HEBBEN: Think they have found the trade wind.

DEPART DE LA BASSE TERRE POUR FRANCE: Departure from Basse Terre for France.
DEPART DE LA BAYE DE CHESAPEEK: Departure from the Bay of Chesapeek.
DEPART DE LA RADE DE BREST: Departure from the roads of Brest.

DEPART DE LA RADE DE LOUISBOURG: Departure from the roads of Louisbourg.

DEPART DE PORT LOUIS POUR LA MARTINIQUE: Departure from Port Louis for Martinique.

DEPART DU CAP POUR FRANCE: Departure from the Cap for France.
DERDEWAAK JAN GOODRIED SELLIUS IS MEERMA: Third watch officer Jan Goodried Sellius was found drunk several times and was placed under arrest.

DES 'S MORGENS TEN 1/2 10 URE BEHOUDEN O: In the morning at half past nine o'clock stopped at the roads of Batavia, at anchor
DES MIDDAGS 4 U TEN ANKER. TEN 7 UREN ON: In the afternoon at 4 o'clock at anchor. At 7 o'clock under sail, towing. Anchored in 7 fathoms, muddy bottom.
DES MORGENS MET DEN DAG PASSEERDEN ONLON: In the morning at daybreak passed along Java and Imit and Mida. At 10 o'clock at anchor near Hoorn island; a sea breeze coming through, steered for the roads of Batavia and came to anchor at 2 o'clock in 5 fathoms..
DESCRIBE EL PASO DE LOS BAJOS Y DICE QUE: Describes the passage of the shoals and says it is very dangerous and narrow, "where all year the atmosphere is dark and rains, squalls and strong winds are frequent, in both monsoons"
DESCRIBE LA COSTA DE SAN BLAS: Describes the coast of San Blas
DESCRIBE LA ISLA ROQUETA A LA ENTRADA DE: Describes Roqueta island at the entrance of the port and the islet of Obispo. They anchor with a hawser, unable to enter the port because of the calm.

Dusk or day's run descriptors. At 15:30 it seemed to him he recognized Lanzarote and Fuerteventura
Dusk or day's run descriptors. At 18:00 bears Punta Guarico at 4 leagues
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Since 10:00 they have been sighting land but cannot recognize it because of the heavy cloud and do not believe it is Tenerife
Dusk or day's run descriptors. They carry the largest tear along a seam
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Sets sail at 10:00
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Sets sail at 5:00. Has been trying to leave since 1-7-1796 but cannot because of contrary winds
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Sets sail at 9:00
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Their foresail breaks
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Is running along the coast of Santo Domingo
Dusk or day's run descriptors. Is heading for Punta Naga

DESCRIPTORES DEL ANOCHECER. FONDEA EN PU: Dusk descriptors. Anchors at Puerto Rico at 14:00
DESCRIPTORES DEL ANOCHECER. QUEDAN A LA: Dusk descriptors. They lie hove to. At dawn sights Barbuda
DESCRIPTORES DEL ANOCHECER. SE HACE A LA: Dusk descriptors. Sets sail at La Coruña at 8:00. French chart. Since 7-Mar-87 has been trying to leave but the strong wind and continual downpours prevented it until the 12th.

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. At 18:00 bears Cabo Cabrón at a long distance. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Sights Virgen Gorda and Isla Baja. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Decides to lie hove to all night, considering themselves close to land. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Anchors at 0:00 west of the islet they call Cabras. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Until this day the wind has been from the NE to NW, fresh, the atmosphere squally, with rain, and the sea so heavy that no one could be embarked or disembarked. Sets sail after midday. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. The longitude is west of Ferrol. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. The latitude and longitude data are from 23:00. At 5:00 sights Punta Naga. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Much noise of currents in the waters. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Considers themselves to be in the middle of the channel. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Sets sail at 12:00. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. English chart
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Sets sail at 13:30. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.
Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Sets sail at 15:30. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.

Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. They are coasting along the island of Santo Domingo. Descriptors of the state of the atmosphere during the day's run. Several English charts.

Noon or day's run descriptors. The log begins on 31-Jan-1766 but he does not leave until 3-Feb because of the violence of the clouds and the wind coming from the W and NW. Had trouble passing the Strait of the Canal.
Noon or day's run descriptors. Cannot leave earlier because of the calms and the strong winds.

Descriptors, sea and wind at dawn, the rest at noon. This voyage appears as the return of the outward voyage of the Pizarro, which arrived badly damaged at Havana on 9-4-1765.

Descriptors, wind and sea for the whole day, the rest at noon
Descriptors, wind and sea for the whole day, rest at noon

Descriptors, wind and sea at dawn, rest at noon
Descriptors, wind and sea at dawn. The rest at noon
Descriptors, wind and sea at dawn. Meridian of Paris and French chart.
DESCUBREN 2 ESCOLLOS. SE ACERCAN A LA CO: They discover 2 reefs. They approach the coast. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
DESCUBREN EL SITIO POR DONDE ENTRA EL AG: They discover the place where the water enters but think it is impossible to examine and repair
DESCUBREN QUE EL BARCO HACE AGUA: They discover that the ship is leaking
DESDE ANTES NOTAN EL AGUA CON ALGUN COLO: For some time before they have noticed the water with a somewhat greenish colour but today it is very much so. A turtle passes
DESDE AYER EMPEZAMOS A PERCIBIR EN EL CO: Since yesterday we began to perceive in the colour of the sea a resemblance to that of Sonda
DESDE EL AMANECER HEMOS VISTO ESTE DIA M: Since dawn we have seen this day a greater number of large birds than usual and some whales, and in the afternoon common martinplacas [?], announcing that the wind must freshen. These we have seen in all seas, but another similar species of which we have already spoken, white and ash-grey, very slightly larger, we have had only since the vicinity of Tristan de Acuña, like the black birds that seem foolish
DESDE EL AMANECER TENEMOS MARTINPLACAS P: Since dawn we have had martinplacas [?] astern (I believe they are dolphins)
DESDE EL DIA DEL TEMPORAL HAN IDO ENFERM: Since the day of the storm up to 8 sailors have fallen ill, who today are in bed with pains in their bones and head, without strength and with a high fever, all of the same illness
DESDE ESTA MARCACIÓN (ISLA DE LOBOS) EMP: From this bearing (Isla de Lobos) my dead reckoning began.
DESDE HOY INCLUSIVE SE HA SUSPENDIDO DE: From today inclusive the giving of wine has been suspended
DESDE LA SALIDA DEL CALLAO DE LIMA HASTA: Since leaving Callao de Lima until today, when I lay on the meridian of Cape Horn, the ship has covered by the log 1088 leagues, with a mile of 20 leagues to the degree. Clear sky and heavy horizons. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
DESDE LAS 12 (DE LA NOCHE) ABONANZÓ EL V: From 12 (at night) the wind moderated and a strong swell from the SW remained
DESDE QUE DIMOS LA VELA (...) EL VTO. FU: Since we set sail (...) the wind was gentle and the sea from the SSW somewhat heavy.
They come out of the Bahama Channel.
DESPUES DE MEDIODIA EL SAN PEDRO TENIA S: After noon the San Pedro had her topsail [?]
DESPUÉS DE MEDIODÍA QUEDÉ EN CALMA, A LA: After noon I remained in calm, at 5 1/4 the wind came in on a squall, and so night fell, dawn came in the same conditions and the rain continued with more force
DESPUÉS DEL MEDIODÍA SE VIÓ SE VIÓ CON E: After noon a shearwater was seen with the bird that had been sighted, resting on the water.
DETERMINA ENRUMBAR DIRECTAMENTE AL PUERT: Decides to steer directly for the port of Acapulco. Some of their barrels fall apart
DEWIJL MEN DE LENGTE VAN BOSENHOVEN VERN: Since the longitude of Bosenhoven had been learned, as the previous day's entry alongside shows, from the drifting of the weed of Sint Poulo and Amsterdam, and furthermore an evening bearing of 13 degrees 26 minutes, all the old journals also indicate this to us.
DEZE KLIPPEN ZIJN ZEER WEL IN HET TWEEDE: These cliffs are very well depicted in the second part of the Lighted Sea-Torch. Our reckoning [?] degrees and 15 min improved eastward
DEZE MAAND ARTIKELBRIEF GELEZEN: This month the articles of war were read
DEZE MAAND DE ARTIKELBRIEF GELEZEN. TROK: This month the articles of war were read. Worked the ventilator daily.
DEZE MIDDAG DOOPTE VOOR DE BARLES EN TEV: This afternoon baptism took place for the barles [?] and also for those who had not crossed the Tropic or the Line. 1381 guilders baptism money.
DEZE MORGEN WERD DE CORPORAAL JOHAN ERRH: This morning the corporal Johan Errhard was missed, who, as far as could be traced, must have fallen overboard. The number of sick among my crew was 22 and among the troops 55 men, largely with scurvy.
DIARIO DE LA NAVEGACIÓN QUE VA A HACER E: Journal of the voyage to be made by the lieutenant of frigate of the Royal Navy, Don Juan Ruiz de Apodaca, from the port of El Callo to the Bay of Cádiz, embarked in the ship of H.M. El Astuto, year 1778
DIARIO DE NAVEGACIÓN PUERTAS DESDE 1776: Navigation journal Puertas from 1776 to 1778" (squadron of the Marqués de Casa Tilly)
