DICE QUE EN LOS DIAS ANTERIORES PERDIERO: Says that in the previous days they lost several sails and parts of the ship as a result of working hard against a head sea, which for the most part was because its pitching was very frequent and violent
DICE QUE LA OBSERVACION FUE CONFUSA: Says that the observation was confused
DICE QUE NO TIENE ESPERANZA DE VOLVER A: Says he has no hope of sighting the ships of the convoy again
DICE QUE SEGURAMENTE TENDRAN QUE GANAR L: Says that they will surely have to gain the distance to San Blas by beating close-hauled, because the wind does not favour them
DICE: \"A MEDIODÍA QUE ESTAMOS TAN AVANT: Says: "At noon we are abreast of the green mangroves" Isla de Santa Ana (Santana, on the coast of Brazil)
DICHT GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN ONDERZ: Close-reefed topsail and lower sail breeze
DICHT GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE MET STORM: Close-reefed topsail breeze with storm squalls
DICHTGEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN ONDERZE: Close-reefed topsail and lower sail breeze
DIEPTE 26 TOT 28 VAAM ZANDGROND. AW-EW:: Depth 26 to 28 fathoms, sandy bottom. AW-EW: see [?] houses at east by north and [?] a large house at east by south. Hoist flag and pennant. See the flag of Cobulang [?] flying.
DIEPTE 30 VAAM, ZWARTACHTIG ZAND, DE STR: Depth 30 fathoms, blackish sand, the current has set them again 20 or so around the N so that they could not hold W.
DIEPTE 35 VADEM, GRAUW ZAND. STUREN ZO E: Depth 35 fathoms, grey sand. Steer S and SSE along the coast of Galle. Ask for a pilot. Meridian 15.5 miles to the east.
DIEPTE 44 VAAM FIJN ZAND. OBSERVATIELENG: Depth 44 fathoms, fine sand. Observed longitude 11° 37'
DIEPTE 50 VAAM KLIIPIG VUILE GROND. NA D: Depth 50 fathoms, rocky dirty bottom. After noon bear the middle of Fulo at northeast by north, 5 miles. End EW bear the high land of the south point of Hitland east and the island Fayeril (Fagherhil?) SSE 1/2 E. HW bear the south point of Hitland northeast by north and the lowest land in the east at the south point and
DIEPTE 56 VAAM, VUIL ZWARTACHTIG WAZIG Z: Depth 56 fathoms, dirty blackish muddy sand with a single small shell. PW: depths 30 to 6 fathoms, soft sticky bottom. By our reckoning stand between Moco Moco and Rio Sebarimen, south, a good 45 miles off the coast of Guiana
DIEPTE 93 VAAM, GROF ZAND MET SINGEL STE: Depth 93 fathoms, coarse sand with some small stones [?].
DIEPTE VAN 14 VAAM. KREGEN EEN LOODS AAN: Depth of 14 fathoms. Got a pilot on board. West meridian 616.25 miles. Changed 8 miles W. Obtain 624.25 miles.
DIEPTE VAN 35 TOT 10 VAAM STEKGROND. OPM: Depth of 35 to 10 fathoms, sticky bottom. Remarks on reckoning and position. See very low land. Because of the hazy air cannot see 3 miles from the deck. According to the reckoning are 16 miles too far west. Remarks on various charts, that of Joh. Loots (published by Mooy at Amsterdam) and that of Van Keu
DIEPTE VAN 60 VAAM, FIJN ZAND. (ZONSONDE: Depth of 60 fathoms, fine sand. (Sunset) the middle of the corner lying between the Mouwerijties bay and Dirk de Vries bay bears northeast 1/2 N: 5 miles. And the island (in?) the Dirk de Vries bay N 1/2 W
Depth of 73 fathoms, grey sand with [?].
DIEPTE VOOR EN ACHTER OPGENOMEN: ACHTER:: Depth taken forward and aft: aft: 16 fathoms, forward: 13 = 3 fathoms of stern trim.
DIEPTE. 26 VOET EN FIJN ZAND MET STEENTJ: Depth. 26 feet and fine sand with small stones
DIEPTEN VAN 14 TOT 13 VAAM. OM 9 UUR KWA: Depths of 14 to 13 fathoms. At 9 o'clock the pilot, David Staalman, came on board. D'Orangezaal, after a few days at Hellevoetsluis, goes cruising in the Channel and at anchor at Plymouth and back again to Hellevoetsluis.
DIEPTEN VAN 15 TOT 10 VAAM. KOERSEN OP D: Depths of 15 to 10 fathoms. Courses toward the Constapels. Sail along the land between the North Cape and the rivers Marapoca, Maayporoc and Carepura. Description of this coast
DIEPTEN VAN 8 TOT 10 VADEM STEKGROND. IN: Depths of 8 to 10 fathoms, sticky bottom. In the margin it says: see the Duottre…guei Jana (?) from E to W (?)
DIKKE BETROKKEN BUIIGE OVERDRIJVENDE, SO: Thick, overcast, squally sky, drifting and at times clearing.
DIKKE BUIIGE BETROKKEN, OVERDRIJVENDE LU: Thick, squally, overcast, drifting sky, afterwards clearing.
DIKKE VERSTOPTE LUCHT TOT AFSCHONENDE EN: Thick, closed-in sky until the sky cleared and drifted off.
DIKKE VERSTOPTE OPHALENDE OFSCHOON EN DE: Thick, closed-in, clearing sky, although followed again by a thick, closed-in sky.
DINGSDAG DEN 31E DES SNADEMIDDAGS QUAMEN: Tuesday the 31st in the afternoon came to anchor before Helvoet. The journal stops here. A number of pages further on, the author gives an account of a short journey from Meerkerk to Maastrigt and Luijk, 5.5 pages long.
DIRECCIÓN : LNE. SUPONGO QUE SERÁ LESTE: Direction: LNE. I suppose it will be east-northeast.
DISTANCIA A LA BOCA DEL ESTRECHO DE MAGA: Distance to the mouth of the Strait of Magallanes, 140 leagues.
DISTANCIA: LAS LEGUAS HAN DADO POR CORRE: Distance: the leagues given by the log line are 17. From 1 to 5 miles.
DISTANCIA: LAS LEGUAS LANZADAS POR CORRE: Distance: the leagues run by the log line were 24. From 1 to 6 miles per hour.
DIT ETMAAL 32 DUIM WATER LENS GEPOMPT: This day and night 32 inches of water pumped from the bilge.
DIT ETMAAL 36 DUIM LENS GEPOMPT: This day and night 36 inches pumped from the bilge.
DIT ETMAAL 48 DUIM LENS GEPOMPT: This day and night 48 inches pumped from the bilge.
DIT ETMAAL 48 DUIM WATER GEPOMPT. BEKOME: This day and night 48 inches of water pumped. Obtained longitude 9° !!! (It is written there.)
DIT ETMAAL 50 DUIM WATER: This day and night 50 inches of water.
DIT ETMAAL 58,5 DUIM LENS GEPOMPT: This day and night 58.5 inches pumped from the bilge.
DIT ETMAAL 60 DUIM LENS GEPOMPT: This day and night 60 inches pumped from the bilge.
DIT KOMT OP EEN LENGTE VAN 20G56M: This comes to a longitude of 20G56M.
DIVERSE SCHEPEN VAN EEN CONVOOI ONTMOET: Met several ships of a convoy and sailed along with them.
DIVERSE SCHEPEN VAN VERSCHILLENDE NATIES: Various ships of different nations were present. Saluted and thanked with several shots.
DIVERSE VLAGGEN EN WIMPELS GEHESEN VOOR: Various flags and pennants hoisted for the birthday of the Portuguese queen. Received a promise from the navy to be helped as soon as possible.
DOCTER VAN BOORD MET EEN CADET EN DRIE A: Doctor on board with a cadet and three other sick men.
DOEN 4 SCHOTEN IN DE MIST. DE KLOK WORDT: Fire 4 shots in the fog. The bell is rung. Near collision with the Amstelveen. She had sounded the bottom at 110 fathoms.
DOEN EEN DANKZEGGING VOOR (HET PASSEREN: Give thanks for (the passing of) the Ambrollos.
DOEN EEN KANONSCHOT IN MIST: Fire a cannon shot in fog.
DOEN EEN KANONSCHOT IN MIST. WORDT DOOR: Fire a cannon shot in fog. It is answered by our consort.
Fire a shot in the fog.
DOEN SCHOT VOOR DE KOOPVAARDER, 'S MIDDA: Fire a shot for the merchant ship; at noon the skipper comes aboard to show his papers.
Sometimes fire 2 shots in the fog.
DOEN SOMS 2 SCHOTEN IN DE MIST. BESCHRIJ: Sometimes fire 2 shots in the fog. Description of Fulo (with a drooping lip).
DOEN TWEE SCHOTEN OP WAARVAN ÉÉN MET SCH: Fire two shots, one of which with live ammunition.
DOG GEEN LAND TE ZIEN. ZETTEN MEN 'T BES: Yet no land to be seen. Put the dead reckoning 30 miles further west on the [?] chart, and according to that the nearest land is Caap St Martin OTZ 30 miles.
The doctor of the Johanna comes for a consultation.
DOLFIJNENE EN VLIEGENDE VIS. VANGEN EXTR: Dolphins and flying fish. Catch an extra large dolphin.
Thunder, lightning and rain. Northeast clearing.
DONDER EN WEERLICHT IN HET ROND, REGEN.M: Thunder and lightning all around, rain. Cleaned the deck. Caught 2 half-casks of water. Saw [?].
DONDER EN WEERLICHT OOK DROOG WEER: Thunder and lightning, also dry weather.
DONDERDAG 2 FEBRUARY KWAMEN OM 4 URE NA: Thursday 2 February at 4 o'clock in the afternoon came to anchor in 5 fathoms in the Goerre harbour (towed by steamboat Currnean).
DONNÉ LE NOM DE CAP FLEURIEU À CELLE LE: Gave the name Cap Fleurieu to the one furthest to the west.
DOODSTIL DUS NIETS VERANDERD IN NB EN LE: Dead calm, so nothing changed in NB and longitude.
DOOR DE DONDER GETROFFEN EN DOOD NEERGEV: Struck by the thunder and fell dead: sailor Baarend Rasmuss, soldier Jan de Pesteen of Assene.
DOOR DE HOGE DRAAIZEE KREEG HET SCHIP VE: Because of the high rolling sea the ship had to endure much water.
DOOR DE NABIJHEID VAN DE ZON GEEN VERTRO: Because of the nearness of the sun, no reliable latitude.
DOOR DE NEVELAGTIEGE LUCHT KONDEN WE NAU: Because of the hazy sky we could hardly get the horizon with the octant.
DOOR DE ZW WIND IS HET AL ENIGE DAGEN ZE: Because of the SW wind it has been very cool for some days, like autumn in the fatherland.
DOOR DEN SCHEEPS RAAT GERESOLVEERT OM HE: The ship's council resolved not to call at the island S'Jago.
DOOR HET STILLE WEER KONDEN WE TOT 25 VA: Because of the calm weather we could see 25 fathoms into the water, so clear it was. Sea water temperature at 8 fathoms depth.
DOOR HOGE DEINING SLINGERDEN MEN ZEER ZW: Because of the high swell they rolled very heavily. This was bad for the sails.
DOOR HOOGTENS HEDEN MORGEN BEVONDEN DOOR: By altitudes this morning the chronometers found the longitude west of Amsterdam, so that they did not suffice at all.
DOOR KOMPAS BEVONDEN 13°32'!. DEED SEIN: By compass found 13°32'!. Made signal for the Comeet to give her longitude, and her found longitude was 2°36'.
DOOR NAAR DE REDE VAN BATAVIA: Continued on to the roads of Batavia.
DOOR OBSERVATIE AAN ZON EN MAAN DE WARE: By observation of sun and moon the true longitude at 9.20 in the morning 27 degrees 0 minutes 0 seconds.
DOOR ONVOORZICHTIG LOSLATEN DER REEP VAN: Through careless letting go of the rope of the fore topgallant yard, it fell onto the chest of the soldier Van Eeren, who died of it immediately; in the evening committed the body to the sea.
DOOR STILTE GEEN STUUR IN 'T SCHIP. BEWE: Because of calm no steering in the ship. West of the meridian of the Peak 50.25 miles.
DOOR STROMING 23 MINUTEN OM DE NOORD GER: Through the current got 23 minutes to the north.
DOOR ZWAAR WEER ZIJN ZE HET KOOPVAARDIJS: Because of heavy weather they lost the merchant ship.
DOORDAT MEN AFGELOPEN NACHT VEEL WATER M: Because much water had to be pumped last night, 39 inches altogether, the carpenters made an extra inspection. This indicated a leak in the ship. To make the leak easier to reach, all 30 pound shot were taken out of the 'hell' and put in the shot lockers, so as to lighten the ship forward.
DOORGEHAALD: (NOGMAALS) MATROOS JOOST BR: Struck out: (again) sailor Joost Bruins deceased. (See 6 July)
DOS EMBARCACIONES LES PERSIGUEN TIRANDO: Two vessels chase them, firing cannon shots. Clear weather with brown clouds. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
DRAAIDE BIJ VOOR EEN PAS IJS: Hove to for a [?] of ice.
DRAAIDEN BIJ EN LOODEN, DOCH MET 120 VAD: Hove to and sounded, but with 120 fathoms no bottom.
DRAAIDEN MET 7 GLAZEN IN DE WIND TOTDAT: Lay to with 7 glasses in the wind until the ship Princes had been with the commander.
DRAAIDEN OM DE WIND, MET DE KOP OM DE WE: Hove to, with the head to the west. AM: saw the coast of Africa.
DRAAIDEN ONDER DE WIND OM DE DAG AF TE W: Hove to to leeward to wait for daylight. At sunrise could make out nothing from the top. Noon: could no longer see (the other ship) because of thick sky.
DRAAIDEN ONDER DE WIND. TIJDENS PV ZEILE: Hove to to leeward. During PV sailed with small sails. With the stem to the NOTO.
DRAAIDEN TEN 12.00 OM DE ZO BIJ VOOR TOP: At 12.00 hove to to the SE for top and tackle.
DRAAIEN BIJ MET DE ANDERE SCHEPEN. KAPIT: Hove to with the other ships. Captain goes with the longboat to the commander. It is decided to steer for Mauritius, because Mr Stavorinus (captain of ship Goes?) did not consider himself able to continue the voyage to the Cape with the damaged rigging.
DRAAIEN BIJ VOOR EEN KLIP LEGGENDE ZOTO: Hove to for a rock lying ZOTO 33 miles from Cape Finisterre.
DRAAIJDE BIJ TOT HET REDDDEN VAN DEN MAT: Hove to to rescue the sailor Staller, who had fallen overboard.
DRAIJDE TEGEN EEN PAKIJS OP DAT ALLE BON: Ran against pack ice so that all were [?].
DREEVEN MEEST SONDER STUUR, HADDEN VERSC: Drifted mostly without steerage, had several half [?] by the ship. Steered, as permitted, SSE. In the late afternoon very hot.
DREVEN DOOR DE HOGE DEINING OM DE NOORD: Drifted to the north because of the high swell.
DREVEN IN DOODSTILTE. THERMOMETER 88 A 9: Drifted in dead calm. Thermometer 88 to 90 degrees outside in the sun. Dead reckoning of skipper Pot: 6° 53' NB, 2° 15' OL.
DREVEN MEEST ZONDER STUU. ZODAT STERK OM: Drifted mostly without steerage, so that we were strongly pressed to the north.
DREVEN MEEST ZONDER STUUR.DREVEN MET DE: Drifted mostly without steerage. Drifted with the head to the west. Kept good lookouts.
DREVEN MEEST ZONDER STUUR.PRUSCOMEERDEN: Drifted mostly without steerage. [?] because of calm and current that we were being set to the west. At times strong rippling of the current.
DREVEN MEEST ZONDER STUUR.ZIEN IN DE PVW: Drifted mostly without steerage. Saw in the PVW a great fireball pass from east to west, the size of the full moon, close by.
DREVEN MEEST ZONDER STUUR; MET SONSRIJSI: Drifted mostly without steerage; at sunrise nothing but the aforementioned ship.
DREVEN WEGENS STILTE IN HET ROND: Drifted around because of a calm
DREVEN ZONDER STUUR.KONDEN NIET OM DE ZU: Drifted without steering. Could not get round the south
DRIE KIPPEN BESTEMD VOOR ZIEKEN OVERLIJD: Three hens meant for the sick died.
Busy catching the rainwater from the squall.
DURANTE LA NOCHE UN CONTÍNUO AGUACERO Y: During the night continuous downpour and short gusts; we woke to the same.
DURANTE LAS 24 HORAS SE HA MANTENIDO EL: During the 24 hours the wind stayed moderate, the sea smooth, and the sky and horizon with clear cloud patterns typical of a breeze.
DUS 36 MIN OF 9 MIJL AGTER HET SCHIP SET: So 36 min or 9 miles astern of the ship; set my dead reckoning NNW onward
DUS DIT ETMAAL 1GR5MIN OM DE WEST GEZET: So this day's run was 1°5 min made to the west
DUS WAREN 16 MIJL WESTELIJKER ALS GISSIN: So we were 16 miles further west than estimated
DW AANNEMENDE TOT STIJVE OZK MET VLIEGEN: Wind increasing to a stiff breeze from the E-S-E with a flying storm
DW: 'HET WEERLIGT ZONDER EENIG VOORBEELD: Morning watch: 'Lightning without any precedent'. Forenoon: the storm increasing more and more from the SW, the ship lying under the sea so that a considerable amount of water came on deck. With the [?] gale and a hurricane blowing, the ship, however much the topgallant mast and lower yard had been lowered, lay with her starboard side under water; this, together with two heavy seas that broke over to windward and filled the whole hold with water, took away all my hope that she would right herself again. I therefore resolved promptly (in this extremity) to throw the guns overboard on the lee side, which had the desired result: after we were rid of [?] pieces of 8 lb and [?] ditto of 6 lb, the ship righted. I therefore also gave orders not to throw any more away. At midday the weather was somewhat better, though the sea had grown so dreadfully that it was without precedent in my experience; the hatches all being battened down, the sick suffered considerably and it made for the healthy a very unpleasant and unhealthy stench between decks
DW: GEBRUIKEN TWEE ZWARE TOUWEN ALS DRIJ: Morning watch: used two heavy ropes as a sea anchor; must pump constantly with the two double-action pumps. The ship rolls heavily and creaks. Suppose there is a strong current around the [?] or the SW.
DW: GIJDEN ONZE ZEILEN DICHT VOOR TRAVAT: Morning watch: our sails are hauled up tight because of squalls. Forenoon: no headway because of thunder
Morning watch: sailor Cornelis Beeger died.
DW: MATROOS JAN BROG OVERLEDEN: Morning watch: sailor Jan Brog died
DW: MET 5 GLAZEN ZAGEN HET EILAND PALMA: Morning watch: at 5 glasses saw the island Palma to the E-S-E, by estimate 10 miles.
DW: MET 6 GLAZEN UIT KREGEN WIJ EEN TRAV: Morning watch: at 6 glasses we got a squall from the NE and E; we hauled up our topsails and made them fast.
DW: MIST EN REGEN, DIKKE VERSTOPTE LUCHT: Morning watch: mist and rain, thick clouded sky. Changed meridian 2.5 miles to the east.
DW: POMPTEN? DUIM LENS. AMW: TAPTEN? DUI: Morning watch: pumped [?] inches in the hold. Afternoon watch: tapped [?] inches
DW: POMPTEN? DUIM LENS. VMW: TAPTEN WEER: Morning watch: pumped [?] inches in the hold. Forenoon: tapped again [?] inches in the ship. Afternoon: pumped 10.5 in the hold. First dog watch: tapped again [?] inches.
DW: SCHIEMANSMAAT JURGEN BAKKER OVERLEDE: Morning watch: boatswain's mate Jurgen Bakker died.
Morning watch: the storm abates somewhat.
DW: VOLGENS ZON-MAAN AFSTAND 98° 5' OF 5: Morning watch: by sun-moon distance 98° 5' or 54' (unclear in the original) E longitude. Forenoon: found E longitude by sun-moon distance 99° 14'.
DW: WACHTEN OP KOOPVAARDERS. SCHIPPER MO: Morning watch: waiting for merchant ships. Captain Mobek was told to set more sail (because he always fell far behind). Dog watch: they bore away toward the leewardmost ship.
DW: WEINIG VOORTGANG DOOR HOGE DEINING: Morning watch: little headway because of high swell
DW: WIJ DREVEN VOOR ONDERZEIL MET REGEN,: Morning watch: we drifted under staysail with rain, thunder and lightning; towards 8 o'clock we set our topsail again.
DW: ZIEN STERKE RAFELINGEN VAN STROOM. D: Morning watch: see strong ripples of current. Da Garca: [?] of the Azores or Flemish islands. Take [?] a quarter point NW
DÉPART DE LISLE DEX: Departure from the Île de Ré
DÉPART DU DÉTROIT DE LE MAIRE. ZB 54°57': Departure from the Strait of Le Maire. S latitude 54°57'00'' W longitude 67°57'00''
DÍA BIEN CERRADO CON LA CONTINUA CELAJER: Day well closed in, with continuous cloud patterns
DÍA DE SALIDA DE CÁDIZ. NO HAY DATO DE R: Day of departure from Cádiz. There is no data on course. The state of the sea was taken at midday, and failing that at dusk or dawn
DÍA DE SALIDA DE CÁDIZ. SE HAN TOMADO LO: Day of departure from Cádiz. The data were taken as follows: state of the sea at midday, and failing that at dusk or dawn; latitude observed, and failing that on arrival. The ship commanding the convoy is the Miño.
DÍA DE SALIDA DE CÁDIZ; SE HAN TOMADO LO: Day of departure from Cádiz; the data were taken as follows: state of the sea at midday, and failing that at dusk or dawn; latitude observed, and failing that on arrival
DÍA DE SALIDA DE LA BAHÍA DE TABLA. NO H: Day of departure from Table Bay. No data on course and wind until 5 in the afternoon
DÍA EN QUE SE INICIA LA VUELTA DEL ESTRE: Day on which the return from the Strait of Magellan to Cádiz begins
DÍA HERMOSO CON EL CIELO Y HORIZ. MUY DE: Beautiful day with the sky and horizon very clear, a little sea from the wind and mild climate.
DÍA HERMOSO SOLO CON LA ALTERACIÓN DE AL: Beautiful day, only with the disturbance of some drizzle coming from a few squalls of wind.
ED VERSCHILLENDE LENGTE EN BREEDTE BEVIN: Several longitude and latitude determinations of recent days (taken at 8:00, 9:00 and 10:00) are compared with each other and the dead reckoning is adjusted
EEN 1-MAST CHALOUP MET RONDHOUT OP SLEEP: A single-masted sloop with a yard in tow arrived in the roads.
EEN 2/3 MAN (IK DENK QUA LENGTE OF LEEFT: A 2/3 man (I think by size or age) dead
EEN AAM VLEES BEDORVEN, LIETEN HET DOOR: A cask of meat spoiled, had the slaves eat it
EEN ADELBORST SCHOOT EEN ALBATROS DIE 10: A cadet shot an albatross that measured 10 feet 2 Amsterdam inches in wingspan and weighed 7 Dutch pounds.
EEN ANDER CONVOOISCHIP, DE ZUIDPOOL ZAG: Another convoy ship, the Zuidpool, sighted land; we ourselves could not see it
EEN CRAAMKIND OVERLEDEN: A woman's child in the lying-in ward died
EEN DER WATERVATEN WAARBIJ EEN FRANSE SC: One of the water casks, beside which a French sentry had been posted, having been broken open, he was put in irons on my orders.
EEN ENKELE KOKSHEN, HOPEN ZUIDVOGELS EN: A few cock-hens, heaps of southern birds and gannets.
EEN GROEP KLEINE EILANDEN. ZAGEN OP WELK: A group of small islands. Saw at which places along the coast of Palo Nyas the land was high and sloping down to the sea. Green fields.
EEN IJSBERG GEPASSEERD. IJSBERG IN HET N: Passed an iceberg. Iceberg to the NE
EEN JONGEN VAN ONS OVERLEDEN, GENAAMD JO: One of our boys died, named Johannes Heijnsbergen of Middelburg
EEN LUITENANT (?) EN EEN CORPORAAL (?) K: A lieutenant (?) and a corporal (?) quarrel over the division of the bacon ration; one cuts a piece off the other's nose
EEN MAN EN EEN MEISJE SLAAF OVERLEDEN: A man and a girl slave died
EEN MAN EN EEN VROUW SLAAF OVERLEDEN: A man and a woman slave died
EEN MAN SLAAF EN EEN VROUW SLAAF OVERLED: A man slave and a woman slave died
EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLEDEN AAN EEN ZERE KEE: A man slave died of a sore throat
EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLEDEN EN EEN MAN SLAAF: A man slave died and a man slave who had been sick jumped overboard and drowned
EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLEDEN, NOG 251 IN LEVE: A man slave died, 251 still alive
EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLEDEN, NOG 252 SLAVEN: A man slave died, 252 slaves still alive
EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLEDEN. VAT VLEES BEDOR: A man slave died. Cask of meat spoiled, the best for the slaves, the rest overboard
EEN MAN SLAAF ZEER ZIEK EN OVERLEDEN, EE: A man slave very sick and died, so a Spanish fly [blister plaster] no longer needed to be applied
EEN MAN, BEJAMIN VAN DER PUT, OVERLEDEN: A man, Bejamin van der Put, died (31)
EEN MANSLAAF EN EEN VROUWSLAAF OVERLEDEN: A man slave and a woman slave died, nos. 19-20.
A man slave and a woman slave died, nos. 21-22.
EEN MANSLAAF OVERLEDEN, NA OVERLEG SCHEE: A man slave died; after consultation of the ship's council [?] was appointed as skipper in place of the deceased.
EEN MARINIER IN ARREST WEGENS INSUBORDIN: A marine under arrest for insubordination.
EEN MATROOS EN DE SCHIEMAN VALLEN VAN DE: A sailor and the mate fall from the fore yard. The sailor stays hanging in the bight of the yardarm tackle and is unhurt, but the mate falls into the water and "drowned miserably, although he was very capable and could swim well, because he could not be saved owing to the ship's fast speed."
EEN MATROOS OVERLEDEN, GENAAMD JAKOB JAN: A sailor died, named Jakob Jansen of Norway
EEN MATROOS OVERLEDEN, NAAM SIEMON DIRKS: A sailor died, named Siemon Dirks.
A sailor fell overboard and drowned.
EEN MATROOS WEGENS ONATTENTIE AAN HET RO: A sailor under arrest for inattention at the helm and sailor Huysen for insubordination. Sailor Huysen punished later in the day and released
EEN MATROOS, ANTHONIE MEIJER, IN DE BOEI: A sailor, Anthonie Meijer, in irons for stealing a buffalo...?
EEN MATROOS, GENAAMD DINGENUS LAMBREGSEN: A sailor, named Dingenus Lambregsen of Tergoes, died. He was sick and had committed suicide. Was put overboard
EEN MATROOS, GENAAMD JACOB JELLES WIELT: A sailor, named Jacob Jelles, fell from a mast, no help possible.
EEN MATROOS, STOFFEL VAN MEESERS (?), HA: A sailor, Stoffel van Meesers (?), had contracted the falling sickness, noticed for the first time this voyage
EEN MENIGT ALBATROSSEN BIJ HET SCHIP: A multitude of albatrosses near the ship
EEN MENIGTE VLIEGENDE VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: A multitude of flying fish near the ship
EEN MENIGTE ZEEVOGELS WAREN ER BIJ HET S: A multitude of seabirds were around the ship, of which some of the black and white kind were caught
EEN NEGER MATROOS VANGT EEN SCHILDPAD: A Black sailor catches a turtle
EEN NEGERIN IN DE KORIAM (KRAAM?): A Black woman in the lying-in ward
EEN NOORDKAPER (WALVIS) DICHT BIJ HET SC: A right whale close to the ship.
EEN OPSTAND DOOR DE SLAVEN WERD DOOR ENK: An uprising by the slaves was reported by some female slaves, so that it could be stopped in time.
EEN OS GESLACHT VOOR HET VOLK: An ox slaughtered for the crew
EEN POON MET BEHOEFTENS AAN BOORD GENOME: A pound of necessaries taken on board [?]
EEN SCHAAP GESTORVEN EN OVERBOORD GEWORP: A sheep died and was thrown overboard
EEN SCHAAP GESTORVEN EN OVERBOORD GEZET: A sheep died and was put overboard
EEN SCHIP VAN DE VLOOT HEEFT STENG EN TU: A ship of the fleet has lost her topmast and rigging, and 3 men with them
EEN SCHOT MET EEN KOGEL OP SCHIPPER BOUF: A shot with a cannonball at Captain Boufet.
EEN SCHOT MET SCHERP OP EEN ENGELS FREGA: A shot with live ammunition at an English frigate that did not show her flag.
EEN SCHOT MET SCHERP OP EEN ENGELSE SNAU: A shot with live ammunition at an English snow to come up astern.
EEN SCHUIT MET WATER GELOST, 11 KOPPEN A: Unloaded a barge with water, 11 heads came aboard. The water proves brackish and is pumped overboard
EEN SERGEANT VAN DE KOLONIALE TROEPEN OV: A sergeant of the colonial troops died.
EEN SERGEANT-MAJOOR VAN DE GEEMBARQUEERD: A sergeant-major of the embarked troops and a sailor of the crew died. Put the bodies overboard
EEN SOLDAAT VAN DE KOLONIALE TROEPEN OVE: A soldier of the colonial troops died.
EEN SOLDAAT, JOHAN PETER WILL VAN KINCHE: A soldier, Johan Peter Will of Kincheym, Poland, died.
A barrel of groats eaten empty by rats.
A woman and a male slave died, no. 28.
EEN VROUW SLAAF EN EEN JONGEN SLAAF OVER: A female slave and a male slave boy died
EEN VROUW SLAAF EN EEN MAN SLAAF OVERLED: A female slave and a male slave died
EEN VROUW SLAAF IN DE CRAAM GEKOMEN: A female slave went into childbed
EEN VROUW SLAAF OVERLEDEN. MATROOS MATHE: A female slave died. Sailor Matheijs Compe died
A woman gave birth to a daughter.
EEN VROUWELIJKE PASSAGIER BEVIEL VOORSPO: A female passenger gave birth successfully to a son. The child was named Hendricus Vasco Caron.
A female slave gave birth to a boy.
EEN VROUWSLAAF IN DE KRAAM VE JONGEN: A female slave in childbed with a boy
EEN VROUWSLAAF IS VAN EEN MEISJE BEVALLE: A female slave gave birth to a girl.
EEN VROUWSLAAF OVERLEDEN, NR. 58. IDEM,: A female slave died, no. 58. Likewise, no. 59
EEN VUURSCHIP OP DE PUNT VAN PILAT RIDGE: A fire ship on the point of Pilat Ridge / light on the hour a blue light and on the half hour a red torch off
EEN WEINIG VUURRING IN HET WATER. ZIEN E: A little phosphorescence in the water. Saw a right whale

"Moderately clear weather, so that many leagues could be seen all around without noticing any ice island at that time, but at 4 in the afternoon, as they continued south, they observed the sea entirely covered in every direction from the SE through the S to the W and continuing ahead to the S. At 6 3/4 (18:45), being at latitude 67º15' S, they could not go any further because the ice had increased so much and was so closely joined to the S over the whole extent from the E to the WSW that there was not the slightest appearance of an opening through which they could pass, and in this situation, not judging it prudent to persevere southward, they made the resolution to go in search of the land recently discovered by the French."

ESTA SINGLADURA SE HAN VISTO UN ATIÑORA,: This day's run a [?], sargassum and jellyfish were seen.
ESTA SINTGL EL VTO HA SIDO MÁS Y MENOS F: This day's run the wind has been more or less fresh in gusts from the NW to the W, sky overcast, horizon with drizzle, sea from the SW and NW.
ESTABA LA MAR AUN MAS CRECIDA: The sea was still more swollen.
ESTADO DE LA MAR AL MEDIODÍA Y EN SU DEF: State of the sea at midday, or failing that at dusk or dawn.
ESTAN 3º AL E DEL MERIDIANO DE MAURICIO,: They are 3º east of the meridian of Mauritius, the hopes of finding land to the E now faded.
ESTAN A 2' DE LONGITUD O DEL CABO: They are 2' of longitude west of the cape.
ESTAN A 5 O 6 LEGUAS DE LA TIERRA: They are 5 or 6 leagues from the land.
ESTAN A 6 LEGUAS DE TIERRA. BORDEAN LA C: They are 6 leagues from land. They tack along the coast. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from midday.
ESTAN A 7 LEGUAS DE LA COSTA. POR LA TAR: They are 7 leagues from the coast. In the afternoon the wind dropped. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from midday.
ESTAN A LA ENTRADA DEL PUERTO: They are at the entrance of the port.
ESTAN A LA VISTA DE LA ISLA ARBOLEDO AL: They are in sight of Isla Arboledo to the SW at 8 leagues. Measurement and data from midday except descriptors, which are usually from dusk. French chart.
ESTAN A LA VISTA DE LA ISLA DE LOBOS: They are in sight of the Isla de Lobos.
ESTAN A POCAS MILLAS DE LA COSTA. A LAS: They are a few miles from the coast. At 15:00 the wind dropped and then blew N. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from midday.
ESTAN CERCA DEL BANCO DE TERRANOVA: They are near the Newfoundland Bank.
ESTAN COMO A 2 LEGUAS DE LA PUNTA DE UNA: They are about 2 leagues from the point of an inlet bearing S 39º E.
ESTAN EN LAS CERCANIAS DEL MERIDIANO DE: They are in the vicinity of the meridian of Isla Mauricio, and finding no sign of the land said to have been discovered by the French, they took the course to the E.
ESTANDO A LA VISTA DE LA ISLA DE LA ASCE: While in sight of the island of Ascension they sight a packet boat that was heading SSE.
ESTANDO EL VTO BONANCIBLE POR EL SUR CON: With the wind moderate from the south, some light swell from the SE, and weather with scattered cloud: in the afternoon it freshened, a big downpour falling at one, and it kept shifting more toward the E, so that in the morning it is already ESE with the look of a trade breeze, which though not unusual in this area will be very welcome to us, especially having entered without the usual preludes of calms.
ESTAS 24 HORAS (...) LA BRISA FRESQUITA: These 24 hours (...) the breeze freshish though somewhat scant, little sea and weather overcast and not at all hot.
ESTAS CARACUADRANTERÍSTICAS DEL TIEMPO \: These [?] of the weather "make it understood that in these latitudes the general winds come to an end, and these being weak because of the season or monsoon we are in, these variations will be more lasting..."
This day the anchors are bent to their cables. Skies and horizons with scattered cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from midday.
ESTE DIA SALEN DEL ESTRECHO DE SONDA Y P: This day they leave the Sunda Strait and begin the course toward the Cape of Good Hope. He makes some warnings about the care to be taken on leaving the strait.
ESTE DÍA (...) NOS SEPARAMOS DE LAS 2 ES: This day (...) we separated from the 2 squadrons, French and Spanish, and began to make course for our destination.
ESTE DÍA 6 SE HICIERON VARIAS OBSERVACIO: This day, the 6th, several longitude observations were made at 10h 12' 12'': longitude west of Paris 18º 28' (...) that of my dead reckoning at the same time was 358º 32', more westerly than the observed one by 1º 52'.
ESTE DÍA A LAS 9 DE LA NOCHE PASAMOS LA: This day at 9 at night we crossed the equinoctial line, and at this point I passed 60 leagues east of Penedo. Noting that we were unable to place ourselves in this longitude until crossing the line, because of the scant winds of the 1st quarter.
ESTE DÍA LLEGAN AL PUERTO DE SAN JUAN DE: This day they arrive at the port of San Juan de Puerto Rico, where they stay until 2/2/1794, when they leave for Veracruz, but there are no position data or tables until 17/2/1794.
This day there is no description of the weather. The data have been taken in the following way: state of the sea at midday, or failing that at dusk or dawn. Latitude observed, or failing that by arrival. The commanding ship of the convoy is the Miño.
ESTE DÍA NO HAY TABLA NI POSICIÓN. LLEGA: This day there is no table or position. Arrival at the port of Havana. Navigation is interrupted until 18/7/1794, when they sail again for Cádiz.
This day there are no tables or observations. There is no journal.
ESTE DÍA NO HUBO OBSERVACIÓN: This day there was no observation.
ESTE DÍA NO SE OBSERVÓ POR MUCHA CERRAZÓ: This day no observation was made because of much overcast and downpours. Note: on the 19th at 3h 3' 59'' in the afternoon, true time on the ship, I made a longitude observation, concluded, of 13º 47' 15''. Paris east of Tenerife: 18º 52' 0''. Longitude east of Tenerife by the observation: 5º 23' 0''. That of my dead reckoning at the moment of the observation: 5º 23' 0''. Residual, the ship more to the east by the observation: 0º 18' 11''.
This day it was not possible to observe.
ESTE DÍA SE ACORTÓ LA RACIÓN DEL AGUA UN: This day the water ration was shortened by a quartillo per head.
This day an eclipse was observed.
ESTE DÍA SE RETOMA DE NUEVO LA NAVEGACIÓ: This day the voyage from Puerto Rico to Veracruz is resumed.
ESTE PUNTO ME SITUA A 3 1/2 LEGUAS DEL C: This point places me 3 1/2 leagues from Cabo Santa María. A short distance, considering we have had such clear horizons. The reasons given oblige me to take a proportional mean between the longitude of the bearing and that of the dead reckoning: thus the departure tomorrow will be 8º 35'. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms. Half-minute glass of 30 sec. First departure point on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4 ed. 66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
ESTIMA QUE ESTA A 60,25 LEGUAS DE LA ISL: Estimates that he is 60.25 leagues from the easternmost island of the Malvinas. Measurement and data from midday except descriptors, which are usually from dusk. French chart.
ESTUVO SONDANDO CON EL BOTE Y SE HACE A: He was sounding with the boat and gets under sail at 2:00. Currents to the WNW.
ESTUVO TODA LA MAÑANA A LA CAPA. DATOS D: He was hove to all morning. Data from midday or from the day's run.
ESTUVO VARIAS VECES A LA CAPA. DESCRIPTO: He was hove to several times. Descriptors from midday or the day's run. The journal begins on 31-ENE-1766 but he does not sail until 3-FEB because of the violence of the clouds and wind coming from the W and NW. He had trouble passing the Strait of the Canal.
EW: DONDER EN WEERLICHT, STORMVLAGEN. AV: EW: Thunder with lightning, squalls. Evening: had the convoy at a reasonable distance.
EW: HOGE ZEE UIT HET ZUIDEN WAARDOOR HET: EW: High sea from the south, so that the ship worked heavily and pitched. HW: The ship would not lie to for the high swell.
EW: STORM UIT NNW EN NW, DE LUCHT DIK, V: EW: Storm from NNW and NW, the sky thick, clogged and so dark that one could not tell each other apart on deck.
EW: UIT DE LUCHT VIEL EEN GROOT STUK VUU: EW: A large piece of fire fell from the sky, landing on the water next to them and giving so much light as if it were lightning.
EW: ZIEN OM 12 UUR LAND IN HET OTN. GISS: EW: See land at 12 o'clock in the east by north. Guess that this is Faijal.
EW: ZWAAR ONWEER EN STERKE REGENBUIEN: EW: Heavy thunderstorm and strong rain showers.
Exercised with cannon and small arms. Ship's council: 2 invalids. Resolution regarding the conduct of the former cook Tjaard Freederiks, and provisionally appointed Mighiel Bouman, ordinary seaman of Onddershallow, as cook, since the first was entirely incompetent for his post. Gave rations for 1/2 month to the crew.
The men exercise with small arms.
EXECUTIE VAN 5 DESERTEURS: PEITER BEIJER: Execution of 5 deserters: Peiter Beijers, Frans Hendriks, Michiel Bauer, Jan Barends and Jan Jacobs.
EXECUTIE VAN DE 3 BELANGRIJKSTE MUITERS: Execution of the 3 main mutineers (Collier, Audreo and Ravilli
EXECUTIE VOORGELEZEN AAN PIETER DE GRAAF: Execution read out to Pieter de Graaff.
EXERCEERDE MET HET GESCHUT. A. MARTIJN I: Exercised with the cannon. A. Martijn in irons.
EXERCEERDEN (VOOR HET EERST) MET HET GEW: Exercised (for the first time) with the musket.
EXERCEREN MET GESCHUT EN HANDGEWEER: Exercise with cannon and small arms.
EXERCEREN MET GESCHUT, SCHROBBEN DE KOOI: Exercise with cannon, scrub the berths. Exercised with cannon, scrubbed the berths.
EXERCEREN MET HANDGEWEREN EN GESCHUT: Exercise with small arms and cannon.
EXERCEREN SOLDATEN EN ROEIERS MET HET HA: Soldiers and rowers exercise with small arms and the throwing of grenades.
EXPERIMENTARON MUCHO FRIO: They experienced a great deal of cold.
EXTRA OORLAM IN VERBAND MET DE VERJAARDA: Extra grog on account of the birthday of H.R.H. Prince Frederik.
EXTRA OORLAM IVM VERJAARDAG HH WILHELMIN: Extra grog on account of the birthday of H.H. Wilhelmina etc., daughter of Prince Frederik.
EXTRA OORLAM IVM VERJAARDAG VD DOCHTER V: Extra grog on account of the birthday of the daughter of Prince Frederik of the Netherlands.
EXTRA OORLAM TER VERJARING VAN PRINS ALE: Extra grog on the birthday of Prince Alexander of the Netherlands.
EXTRA OORLAM WGNS VERJARING 1 DER LEDEN: Extra grog on account of the birthday of 1 of the members ..?
EXTRA SCHEEPSRAAD IVM DE VERMINDERING VA: Extra ship's council on account of the reduction of drinking water. It was found good to issue 8 small measures to everyone.
EXTRA VEEL VIS, ZIEN EEN SCHAARVOGEL: Extra many fish, see a frigatebird.
EXTRACT UIT HET JOURNAAL VAN ZM FREGAT M: Extract from the journal of H.M. frigate Maria Reigersbergen on a voyage from Texel to the East Indies along the coast of Guinea, from there around Cape Horn to Valparaiso and Lima and further through the Pacific Ocean. Together with the Pollux (Captain Lieutenant C.N. Eeq). J.P. Muller aboard with the navigator's instruments, consisting of: 3 chronometers, 1 thermometer, 1 sextant, 1 azimuth compass, 1 steering compass improved by Kleman according to the manner of Stebing, as well as the East Indian Pilot. Later a consignment of instruments came from England, consisting of: 1 sextant, 1 barometer, 1 achromatic telescope, 1 hygrometer. Since we had hardly any charts aboard other than English ones, we calculated our longitude according to the meridian of Greenwich. Muller had the task of measuring time: No 22 ran very irregularly, No 27 had a daily loss of 74 seconds, No 39 had a daily loss of 63 seconds. (Journal gives air temperature in Fahrenheit and then ,20 ,30 or ,40)
EXTRACTO DEL DIARIO DE LAS NAVEGACIONES,: Extract of the diary of the navigations, explorations and discoveries made in northern America by D._______, in the frigate of H.M. named Ntra Sra. de Aranzazu, from the port of San Blas, from where she sailed on 20 March 1792.
EXTRACTO DEL DIARIO DEL JEFE DE ESCUADRA: Extract of the diary of the squadron commander Ignacio María de Álava, who commands the one destined for the South Sea from Cádiz to the port of Concepción de Chile. It is made up of the ships Europa, Montañés and S. Pedro Apóstol and the frigates Ntra. Sra. del Pilar and Fama.
EXTRACTO DEL DIARIO DEL P. JOSÉ QUIROGA: Extract of the diary of Father José Quiroga of the Company of [?] of the voyage to the coast of the Patagonians.
EXTRACTO DEL DIARIO DEL PAQUEBOTE SANTIA: Extract of the diary of the packet boat Santiago under the command of José Grandellana, from the port of the Isla del Príncipe to the Bay of Cádiz.

Extract of the diary of the packet boat Santiago under the command of José Grandellana, from the port of the Isla del Príncipe to the Bay of Cádiz. At dawn he sights the island of Santo Tome and passes it on its north side. He let himself be carried by the current until sighting the island of Fernando Poo.
FALTAN LAS PÁGINAS CORRESPONDIENTES A LO: The pages for the days 13 and 14 of November are missing.
FALTAN LAS TABLAS Y ACAECIMIENTOS DE LOS: The tables and events for the days 3 to 6 of November are missing.
FELICITE HAD 19°50' NB EN 319°30' OL: Felicite had 19°50' N latitude at 319°30' E longitude.
FEOS CARICES(...) HORIZ. Y CIELOS CERRAD: Ugly appearances (...) horizon and skies closed in with drizzle.
FLAAUW EN HELDER TOT DIK. ONGESTADIG FLA: Light and clear to thick. Unsteady light and clearing. Alternately overcast and clouded.
FLAAUW EN STIL LEEGEN ? IN DE KIMME: Light and calm [?] on the horizon.
FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEMENDE KOEL: Light topgallant breeze and decreasing breeze
FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Light topgallant breeze and topgallant breeze
FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN FLAUWE KOELTE: Light topgallant breeze and light breeze
FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MINDERE KOELTE: Light topgallant breeze and lighter breeze
FLAUWE KOELTE EN FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and light topgallant breeze
FLAUWE ONELIJKE KOELTE. TOT 23 MEI NIETS: Light [?] breeze. Until 23 May nothing special
FLORES IS HET WESTELIJKSTE DER 9 AZOREN: Flores is the westernmost of the 9 Azores or Flemish Islands.
FONCERO IS EEN KLEIN EILAND BEOOSTEN DE: Foncero is a small island east of the Caribbean islands.
FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE CAMARIÑAS, LUEGO: Anchors in the port of Camariñas, then leaves on the 13th and arrives on the 14th at the port of La Coruña
FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO A LAS: Anchors in the port of Montevideo at 20:00
FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE SANTA CRUZ POR RE: Anchors in the port of Santa Cruz for repairs
FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DE STA. CRUZ DE TENE: Anchors in the port of Sta. Cruz de Tenerife, to take on ballast because of navigation problems
FONDEA EN EL PUERTO DETENERIFE: Anchors in the port of Tenerife
FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA A LAS 13:30 SIENDO R: Anchors at La Coruña at 13:30, being towed because of the calm. Measurement taken at dusk or for the day's run
FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA A LAS 15:30. DATOS D: Anchors at La Coruña at 15:30. Noon data (since 18 Dec the descriptors are from dusk)
FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA A LAS 19:00. MEDICIO: Anchors at La Coruña at 19:00. Noon measurement, dusk data
FONDEA EN LA CORUÑA AL PONERSE EL SOL: Anchors at La Coruña at sunset
FONDEA EN LA HABANA A LAS 17:00. MEDICIO: Anchors at La Habana at 17:00. Noon measurement, dusk data
FONDEA EN LA ISLA DE AUGERS HASTA EL DÍA: Anchors at the island of Augers until 11 August.
FONDEA EN MONTECRISTO A LAS 14:00 Y SALE: Anchors at Montecristo at 14:00 and leaves at 20:30
FONDEA EN PUERTO RICO A LAS 13:00. MEDIC: Anchors at Puerto Rico at 13:00. Noon measurement, dusk data
FONDEA EN UN PLACER FUERA DEL PUERTO DE: Anchors on a shoal outside the port of Santo Domingo at 13:30 because of the calm
FONDEA POR SER LOS VIENTOS DEMASIADO FUE: Anchors because the winds are too strong. Descriptors, wind and sea from dawn, the rest from noon
FONDEA. MEDICION Y DATOS DEL MEDIODIA ME: Anchors. Measurement and data from noon except the descriptors, which are usually from dusk. French chart
FONDEADO POR LAS MUCHAS CALMAS Y MALOS S: Anchored because of the many calms and bad-looking weather
FONDEADO POR NO ESTAR EL VIENTO FAVORABL: Anchored because the wind is not favorable and because of the bad [?] from the N with continuous squalls from the NNE and swell from the NNE
FONDEADOS AUNQUE LEVAN POSTERIORMENTE: Anchored, although they weigh anchor later
FONDEADOS HACIENDO MEDICIONES. MEDICION: Anchored, taking measurements. Noon measurement, the rest from dawn
FONDEADOS HACIENDO MEDICIONES. NO PUEDEN: Anchored, taking measurements. They cannot leave because of adverse conditions. Describes the port and its conditions. Talks about guano. Noon measurement, the rest from dawn
Anchored, taking measurements. They cannot leave because of adverse conditions. Noon measurement, the rest from dawn
FONDEADOS. INCLUYE UNA NOTA QUE DICE QUE: Anchored. Includes a note saying that from the departure from Lima until anchoring, the following died during the voyage of natural illness: 1 junior pilot, 5 sea gunners, 1 sailor, 6 ship's boys, 8 Indians of those who are aboard as prisoners by order of the Viceroy of Peru, 4 women of theirs, 1 son and 3 daughters who are minors, 2 passengers and 1 servant of theirs, total 32
FONDEAN EN EL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO EN EL: They anchor in the port of Montevideo at the usual place.
FONDEAN EN LA CORUÑA A LAS 11:00: They anchor at La Coruña at 11:00
FONDEAN EN SANTA CATALINA A LAS 4:00. ME: They anchor at Santa Catalina at 4:00. Noon measurement and data except the descriptors, which are usually from dusk
FOUTJE VAN DE TOENMALIGE FRANSEN, DIT MO: Mistake by the French of the time; this must be the 1st of Vendemiaire II. 6
FRAIS ET VARIABLE ET TRÉS FRAIS: Fresh and variable and very fresh
The wind fresh and the sea from it heavy (...) dawn came overcast and the horizons squally, the wind fresh with heavy seas from it and from the SW.
FRESQUITA LA BRISA Y PARDO ELCIELO. DESD: The breeze slightly fresh and the sky grey. Since dark the gusts began, as on the previous nights.
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEMENDE KOEL: Fresh topgallant breeze and decreasing breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Fresh topgallant breeze and topgallant breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN GEMENE BRAMZEI: Fresh topgallant breeze and ordinary topgallant breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MARSZEILSKOELT: Fresh topgallant breeze and topsail breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MEERDERE KOELT: Fresh topgallant breeze and increasing breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MINDERE KOELTE: Fresh topgallant breeze and decreasing breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN ONGELIJKE KOEL: Fresh topgallant breeze and uneven breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN ONGESTADIGE BR: Fresh topgallant breeze and unsteady topgallant breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN ONGESTADIGE KO: Fresh topgallant breeze and unsteady breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE OOK GEMENE BRAMZE: Fresh topgallant breeze, also ordinary topgallant breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE TOT GEREEFDE MARS: Fresh topgallant breeze to reefed topsail breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE TOT MARSZEILSKOEL: Fresh topgallant breeze to topsail breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE-GEREEFDE MARSZEIL: Fresh topgallant breeze to reefed topsail breeze
FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE-MARSZEILSKOELTE: Fresh topgallant breeze to topsail breeze
FRISSE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Fresh topsail breeze and topgallant breeze
FRISSE MARSZEILSKOELTE-BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Fresh topsail breeze to topgallant breeze
The wind kept freshening, with gusts [?]. A good deal of snow has fallen on us, the weather quite cold, the sea somewhat risen from the E and N.
FUERON A LA CAZA DE UN CORSARIO INGLÉS,: They went in chase of an English privateer, but had to give it up so as not to split up the squadron.
FUERTES BALANCEOS Y CABEZADAS. DATOS DEL: Heavy rolling and pitching. Data from noon or the day's run. Had an encounter with English privateers.
FUERTES CORRIENTES AL N DESDE EL PRIMER: Strong currents to the N since the first day. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. [?] Spanish.
FUERZA, MAR Y DESCRIPTORES DEL AMANECER: Force, sea and descriptors from dawn
FUERZA, MAR Y DESCRIPTORES DEL AMANECER,: Force, sea and descriptors from dawn, remainder from noon
FUSELIER BRUIN AFGESTRAFT MET 24 SLAGEN: Fusilier Bruin punished with 24 lashes for insubordination.
FUSELIER LAMMERS EN DE KORPORAAL SLIJGER: Fusilier Lammers and Corporal Slijger of the detachment of riflemen put in irons on water and bread because they had left the watch without leave. Another fusilier, Bruinier, in irons on water and bread for refusing to obey an order.
FUSELIER LIEFMANS IN DE BOEIEN OP WATER: Fusilier Liefmans in irons on water and bread for irregularities during the meal.
FUSELIER RONNENBERG GESTRAFT MET 4 UUR S: Fusilier Ronnenberg punished with 4 hours of punishment sentry duty with crowbars for irregularities during the morning meal.
FUSELIER SCHULE KROM IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS: Fusilier Schule put in irons, bent double, for brutality.
FUSELIER SCHULE WEER UIT DE BOEIEN: Fusilier Schule out of irons again.
GAAN AAN BOORD BIJ DE COMMANDANT. MEN GA: Go aboard with the commander. They are going to fetch water at the Flemish Islands.
GAAN MET VOLK OVER OP COMPAGNIESCHIP HOE: Go over with the crew onto the company ship, the hooker Dortwijk; the state frigate d'Orangezaal sold for 13220 rijksdaalders.
GAAN ONDERZEIL EN NAAR ZEE. TE 12 UUR PE: Set sail and head out to sea. At 12 o'clock the W point of St. Thomas bears SSE, 3,5 miles, and the island Passage SW 3/4 S, 5 miles. Here the reckoning begins. The charts used are named.
GAAN OP DE THUIJSREIJS: Set off on the homeward voyage.
GAAN OP ROBBEN JACHT MAAR VANGEN ER GEEN: Go seal hunting but catch none. The bay ice is very thick, so thick that they sometimes got stuck in it.
GAAN OP ZIJN HOLLANDS WAAKE, MET 25 SCHE: Go on watch in the Dutch manner, with 25 ships together.
GAAN PASJAREN. SCHIPPERS MAKEN AFSPRAKEN: Go [?]. Skippers make agreements about the reckoning and course to Corfess and Flores.
GAAT MET HET SCHIP ZUIJLEVELT KIJKEN WIE: Goes with the ship Zuijlevelt to see who is the better sailer.
GAVEN BRIEVEN MEE AAN ENGELS OORLOGS BRI: Gave letters to an English warship brig.
GAVEN BROOD MEE AAN ANDER CONVOOI SCHIP: Gave bread to another convoy ship (presumably because of a shortage).
GAVEN DE EQUIPAGE EEN EXTRA BORREL BIJ H: Gave the crew an extra tot on entering the Pacific.
GAVEN DE EQUIPAGE EEN EXTRA OORLAM TER E: Gave the crew an extra dram in honour of Prince Fredrik's birthday.
GAVEN DMV EEN KANONSCHOT TE KENNEN DAT M: Gave notice by a cannon shot that the attack to relieve Malakka would take place tomorrow.
GAVEN EEN EXTRA OORLAM AAN DE EQUIPAGE T: Gave the crew an extra dram on the occasion of the birthday of Louisa, daughter of Prince Fredrik.
GAVEN EEN EXTRA OORLAM BIJ GELEGENHEID D: Gave an extra dram on the occasion of the 48th birthday of His Royal Highness Willem Frederik George Lodewijk, Prince of Orange.
GAVEN EEN EXTRA OORLAM TER VIERING VAN D: Gave an extra dram to celebrate the memorable Battle of Waterloo.
GAVEN EXTRA BORREL EN JOELDEN VOOR DE VE: Gave an extra tot and cheered for the king's birthday.
GAVEN GEHEEL RANTSOEN VAN WATER A 10 MUT: Gave the full ration of water at 10 mugs each, since the beer had been consumed.
GAVEN MINDER RANTSOEN VAN WATER VOOR DE: Gave a smaller ration of water to the whites and the slaves.
GAVEN RIJST EN WITTE BONEN AAN DE SCHEPE: Gave rice and white beans to the seamen. In the evening sauerkraut.
GAVEN SEIN OM AF TE KOMEN: Gave a signal to bear away.
GAVEN SEIN OM MEER ZEIL TE MAKEN: Gave a signal to make more sail.
GAVEN SPEK EN ZUURKOOL. EEN OXHOOFD FRAN: Gave bacon and sauerkraut. A hogshead of French wine was found [?].
GAVEN VERVERSING AAN DE EQUIPAGE: Gave fresh provisions to the crew.
GAVEN VERVERSING VAN SCHAPENVLEES, ZEEKR: Gave fresh provisions of mutton, samphire and olives to the seamen, 6 sheep [?]. But found that the samphire was spoiled and not fit to eat. Therefore issued sauerkraut.
GAVEN VERVERSSING A DE EQUIPAGIE. HIELDE: Gave fresh provisions to the crew. Held prayers.
GAVEN VOOR EEN MAAND AAN VOER AAN HET VO: Gave the people a month's worth of food.
GAVEN ZEEKORAAL AAN DE EQUIPAGE.ZIEN EEN: Gave samphire to the crew. Saw a frigatebird [?].
GEARRESTEERDE ERICH WIL MET CHALOUP NAAR: The arrested man Erich wants to go to the commander in the launch; wants to come on deck, it is too hot below.
GEB. KOERS SEDERT DEN 26 MEI: Z3/4W, 43,: Corrected course since 26 May: S 3/4 W, 43,25 miles.
GEBETERDE KOERS EN BERHEID VAN 6 DECEMBE: Corrected course and [?] from 6 December to 9 December SW 1/2 S 86,75 miles.

GEBETERDE KOERS EN EN VERHEID: ZTW 1/2 W: Corrected course and distance: S by W 1/2 W, 28,5 M. Changed longitude: 0° 36'
GEBETERDE KOERS EN EN VERHEID: ZTW 1/8 W: Corrected course and distance: S by W 1/8 W, 36,5 M. Changed meridian: M. West of Goudstaart: M. Changed longitude: 0° 35'
GEBETERDE KOERS EN EN VERHEID: ZWTZ 1/8: Corrected course and distance: SW by S 1/8 W, 21,5 M. Changed meridian: M. West of Goudstaart: M. Changed longitude: 1° 0'

Corrected course and distance: SSW 1/4 W, 9 M. Changed meridian: M. West of Goudstaart: M. Changed longitude: 0° 15'
GEBETERDE KOERS EN EN VERHEID:ZTW 1/2 W,: Corrected course and distance: S by W 1/2 W, 25 M. Changed meridian: M. West of Goudstaart: M. Changed longitude: 0° 30'

GESTRAFT MET 12 SLAGEN LICHTMATROOS VD P: Punished with 12 strokes the ordinary seaman Vd Pluim for abuse of trust. Under arrest the marine Den Uil for improper words against the corporal of the Africans
GESTRAFT MET 12 SLAGEN MET DE HANDDAGEN: Punished with 12 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor Pickart for slowness
GESTRAFT MET 12 SLAGEN MET HANDDAGEN MAT: Punished with 12 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor Antonis for not carrying out given orders. Dismissed the ship's cook De Bot
Punished with 12 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor R. van Dijk for slander
GESTRAFT MET 150 KNUTTELSLAGEN DEJONGENS: Punished with 150 strokes of the knotted rope the boys Zaalberg and Van Luijn for theft of the officers' goods
GESTRAFT MET 18 SLAGEN MET HANDDAGEN MAQ: Punished with 18 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor Van den Kruyt for not following the orders of a superior
GESTRAFT MET 18 SLAGEN MET HANDDAGEN MAT: Punished with 18 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor Hogenvorst for insubordination and cursing
GESTRAFT MET 2 UUR STRAFSCHILDEREN MARIN: Punished with 2 hours of punishment sentry duty the marine Nelissen for disorderly conduct on the half deck
GESTRAFT MET 24 UUR KROM IN DE BOEIEN MA: Punished with 24 hours bent over in irons the sailor Haye for improper expressions towards superiors
GESTRAFT MET 6 SLAGEN LICHTMATROOS SIJMO: Punished with 6 strokes the ordinary seaman Sijmonds for sleeping on lookout
GESTRAFT MET 6 SLAGEN MET HANDDAGEN MATR: Punished with 6 strokes with the rope's ends the sailor Graanland for inattention as lookout
GESTRAFT WEGENS HERHAALDE LIEDERLIJKHEID: Punished for repeated debauchery the marine of the 3rd class D. Janse.
GESTRAFT WEGENS HET ONTVREEMDEN VAN DRAN: Punished for stealing drink and drunkenness the ship's boy J. L. de Vries.
GESTRAFT WEGENS VERREGAANDE ONZINDELIJKH: Punished for extreme uncleanliness, jointly locked in a wooden collar, the ordinary seamen Hofman and Neau
GEVEN 'T VOLK 10 MUISJES DRINKWATER. OVE: Gave the crew 10 small measures of drinking water. Died: sailor Pieter Rienes van Rietie; also died: steward's mate Jacobus Bogaart van Middelburg.
GEVEN AAN HET WACHTVOLK 1 OORLAM VOOR HE: Gave the watch crew 1 dram for the wet and foul weather
GEVEN AAN SCHIPPERS VAN HET KONVOOI ENIG: Gave the skippers of the convoy some private signals.
GEVEN BESCHRIJVING EN TEKENING VAN AANTA: Gave description and drawing of a number of the Cocos Islands
GEVEN DE SLAVEN SOOPIJES. 2 SLAVEN AAN D: Gave the slaves soopjes. 2 slaves with burning fever
Gave the slaves salt meat and soopjes. A female slave died
Gave an extra dram to the crew.
GEVEN EEN ZILVEREN MEDAILLE AAN VAN DER: Gave a silver medal to Van der Linden for 24 years of faithful service
GEVEN EXTRA RANTSOEN GENEVER: Gave an extra ration of gin
GEVEN EXTRA RANTSOEN GENEVER. ZIEN ENIGE: Gave an extra ration of gin. Saw some casks floating
GEVEN GROBBEJAK AAN HET VOLK VAN WIJN, A: Gave grog to the crew of wine, arrack, tamarind and sugar
Gave the crew 10 inches of drinking water.
GEVEN HET VOLK EEN JOPIE GENEVER EN KINA: Gave the crew a small measure of gin and quinine as a precaution, cleaning, etc. Because of the bad weather there had been no chance to air [the ship] in the past time. Have 36 sick, not serious (list of ailments)
Gave the crew a month's ration.
GEVEN RANTSOEN GENEVER AAN DE BEMANNING: Gave ration of gin to the crew
GEVEN RANTSOEN KAAS AAN 'T VOLK: Gave ration of cheese to the crew
Gave ration of water: 6 small measures per head. Reckon to have supplies on board for another 9 weeks.
GEVEN SLAVEN VIS TE ETEN: Gave the slaves fish to eat
GEVEN SOEP VAN SCHAPENVLEES AAN 'T VOLK: Gave mutton soup to the crew
GEVEN SOEP VAN SCHAPENVLEES AAN VOLK: Gave mutton soup to the crew
GEVEN SPEK EN VLEES AAN DE SLAVEN: Gave bacon and meat to the slaves
GEVEN TIJDMETERLENGTE OP AAN ENGELSMAN,: Gave the chronometer longitude to an Englishman; he reports a difference of 0º 10' east
GEVEN VERVERSING AAN DE EQUIPAGE VAN VAR: Gave the crew fresh provisions of pork.
GEVEN VERVERSINGEN VAN SCHAPENVLEES. 6 I: Gave fresh provisions of mutton. 6 disabled
GEVEN VOLK 1,5 KAN DRINKWATER: Gave the crew 1.5 can of drinking water
GEVEN VOOR 1/2 MAAND RANTSOEN AAN 'T VOL: Gave the crew half a month's ration
GEVEN VOOR EEN HALVE MAAND RANTSOEN AAN: Gave the crew half a month's ration
GEVEN VOOR EEN MAAND RANTSOEN VAN OLIJVE: Gave a month's ration of olives, oil, vinegar, tamarind, sugar
GEVEN ZEEKRAAL AAN HET VOLK: Gave sea biscuit to the crew
Drifted west of topgallant point 39 miles.
GEWEKEN BEWESTEN DE MERIDIAAN 141,75 MIJ: Drifted west of the meridian 141.75 miles.
GEWEKEN BEWESTEN DE MERIDIAAN 15,75 MIJL: Drifted west of the meridian 15.75 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian 35.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian 50 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian 67.5 miles.
GEWEKEN BEWESTEN DE MERIDIAAN 87,75 MIJL: Drifted west of the meridian 87.75 miles.
GEWEKEN BEWESTEN DE MERIDIAAN VAN CANARI: Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 166 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 188.75 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 206.75 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 223.25 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 240.25 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 284 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 322.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 338.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 356.25 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 374.75 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 396.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 419.25 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 439.25 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 469.75 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 482.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 496 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 506.5 miles.
Drifted west of the meridian of Canaria 513.5 miles.
GINGEN AAN T VISSEN, MIDDAGS NIET AFGESE: Went fishing; did not take a noon position
GINGEN AAN WAL EN NAAR HET PLAATSJE CARA: Went ashore and to the small place Carawang Doja.
GINGEN AAN WAL MET EEN GIDS MAAR KEERDEN: Went ashore with a guide but returned on board after he had taken to his heels.
GINGEN DE ELFDE TEN ANKER OP HET VLAKKE: Anchored on the eleventh on the flats in Zeeland.
GINGEN DE TWAALFDE TEN ANKER NABIJ BRAAM: Anchored on the twelfth near Braamspunt in Suriname.
GINGEN DEZELFDE DAG WEER ONDER ZEIL. KEE: Set sail again the same day. Returned briefly on the 24th to the roads of St. Helena.
GINGEN DIE MIDDAG OM 4 UUR WEDER ONDER Z: Set sail again that afternoon at 4 o'clock.
GINGEN HARPOENEN KLAAR MAKEN: Went to get the harpoons ready
GINGEN ONGEVEER EEN DAG TEN ANKER VOOR A: Lay at anchor for about a day off Axim. Came to anchor off Elmina on 24 November.
GINGEN OOST AAN STUUREN. 'WERPEN VERSCHI: Went to steer east. Cast the lead several times, then found no bottom at 150 fathoms
GINGEN OP VOORBEELD VAN DE VLAGGEVOERDER: Set sail following the example of the flagship. In the evening anchored in 19 fathoms of muddy bottom
GINGEN WEER ONDER ZEIL. OM 12.00 UUR PEI: Set sail again. At 12:00 took bearings: the flagstaff of 'T Mannepaar N by E and the Sugarloaf NWbW and the hillock on Cape Comorin [?] 3/4 [?], by estimate 1.5 miles. At 4:00 took bearings: the beacon of Tristiaandoorn NNW. At 6:00 came to anchor under the coast. Took bearings: the point of Mannipaar SW 1/2 [?] ... through this SWbW 1/4 W.
GIS BLANCA (SPAANSE KAART) ZOTO W/Z Z, 1: Estimated position: Blanca (Spanish chart) ZOTO W/Z Z, 13 miles
GIS DANISH ROCK (TIJDMETER LENGTE) OTN 1: Estimated position: Danish Rock (chronometer longitude) OTN 1/8 N 50 miles
GIS HYSART (VOLGENS BEKOMEN LENGTE) O 1/: Estimated position: Hysart (according to obtained longitude) E 1/2 S, 53.75 miles
GIS MIDDEN VAN NATAL (VOLGENS COMMISSIEK: Estimated position: middle of Natal (according to commission chart) NW, 12.5 miles.
GIS VUURTOREN VAN ANHAGELS (?), ZW 3/4 W: Estimated position: lighthouse of Anhagels [?], SW 3/4 W 3 miles.
GIS W HOEK VAN HET EILAND OBY MAYON N 18: Estimated position: W point of the island Oby Mayon N 18.75 miles
GIS W HOEK VAN PRINCENEILAND ZW 7/8 W 2,: Estimated position: W point of Princeneiland SW 7/8 W 2.75 miles and the NE point of Princeneiland SWbW 1/2 W 1.75 miles
GIS ZW HOEK VAN OBY MAYOR NNO 13 MIJL: Estimated position: SW point of Oby Mayor NNE 13 miles
GIS ZW HOEK VAN PRINCENEILAND ZWTW 1/2 W: Estimated position: SW point of Princeneiland SWbW 1/2 W, 3.25 miles and NE point of Princeneiland SW 2/3 S 2 miles.
Estimate to have the latitude of 34° 6'.
GISSEN EILAND GEPASSEERD TE ZIJN. EILAND: Estimate to have passed an island. Island lies on the S chart at 21°17' S latitude
GISSEN NIET VER VAN KAAP FORMOSA TE ZIJN: Estimate to be not far from Cape Formosa. Longitude according to French chart: 21° 57'
GISSING LESARD 'GEEFT OP DE KAART DE NB: Estimate Lesard: gives on the chart the N latitude of 49°44' and 5°11' longitude west of Greenwich
GISSING VAN RIO HAD VOLGENS HET BESTEK O: Estimate of Rio: according to the dead reckoning it should have lain W 1/3 N 15 miles
GISSING VOLGENS GENERAL CHART OF THE ATL: Estimate according to General Chart of the Atlantick Ocean by John Purdy, 1821.
GISSING VOLGENS SPAANSE KAART VAN DE ZUI: Estimate according to Spanish chart of the south coast of the island of Cuba, improved by Don Jose del Rio in 1804 and published at Madrid in 1821.
GISTEN 2 MIJL VAN DE NAASTE WAL TE ZIJN: Estimate to be 2 miles from the nearest shore
GISTEN BOVEN DE CAAP TE ZIJN. SCHIP ZEIL: Estimate to be above the cape. Ship sails along the upper coast of Africa from Cape Lahoe to below the Gabon, while engaged in the slave trade and the purchase of teeth, crevel and wax
GISTEN EENE GRAAD LENGTE OOSTELIJKER TE: Estimate to be one degree of longitude further east; the dead reckoning set it 1 degree further east
GISTEN? MIJL VAN DE NAASTE WAL. LODEN 65: Estimate [?] miles from the nearest shore. Sounded 65 fathoms sandy bottom with black shell fragments
GISTERAVOND DOOR 4 OBSERVATIEN DE MISWIJ: Yesterday evening by 4 observations found the compass variation 2 degrees northwesterly. This morning again by 4 azimuth bearings found the variation one degree.
GISTEREN DE OBSERVEERDE LENGTE VAN DE PO: Yesterday the observed longitude of Pollux 354 degrees. Found by the distance of sun and moon longitude 354 degrees, is 43 degrees 45 minutes
GLAZENMAKER AAN BOORD OM DE GEBROKEN GLA: Glazier on board to repair the broken glass. Gave receipt for 100 pieces. Received 8 sailors on board. A sick young nobleman back on board again.
GOBERNARON AL NE CONTRA UNA MAR GRUESA Q: Steered NE against a heavy sea which indicated there was no land in that quadrant
GODLOB HEIJTER IN DE IJSERS OVER BEGAANE: Godlob Heijter in irons for theft committed
GODSDIENSTOEFENING, KRIJGSARTIKELEN EN I: Divine service, articles of war and inspection
GODSDIENSTOEFENING. BEVORDERING KWARTIER: Divine service. Promotion of quartermaster Verduin to 1st boatswain's mate
GODSDIENSTOEFENING. BEVORDERT TOT CONSTA: Divine service. Promoted to constable the constable's mate Steltenkamp
GODSDIENSTOEFENING. INSPECTIE VAN SCHIP: Divine service. Inspection of ship and crew by the commander
GOEDEREN VAN DE OVERLEDEN CUIJPER VERKOC: Goods of the deceased Cuijper sold.
GOLPE DE MAR. ENTRA AGUA EN EL BARCO. NA: Heavy sea. Water enters the ship. They sail under bare poles. Descriptors, sea and wind from dawn, the rest from midday.
Cast the lead but found no bottom. They were 30 miles further east than they had estimated, but he did not find this strange.
GOUVERNEUR AAN BOORD. ZE KOMEN OVEREEN D: Governor on board. They agree that the fortress would fire 2 more salute shots, which 'we' will answer with the same.
Limit of the southeast trade wind below north.
GROF SAND.HADDEN OP DE MIDDAG LEEZANDS P: Coarse sand. Had at noon Leezands Point by the reckoning NWbW/W 7 miles. And the general combined course of the 24 hours was SWbW¾W, distance 13½ miles.
GROND OP 76 VADEM. AMW: BEGON TOT STORM: Bottom at 76 fathoms. AMW: began to blow up to a storm.
GROOTE EN WAHL UIT DE BOEIEN: Groote and Wahl released from the irons.
GROTE CONSTERNATIE OMDAT IN DE STORM EEN: Great consternation because in the storm one of the ships sailed away.
GROTE MENIGTE VIS BIJ 'T SCHIP: Great multitude of fish near the ship
GROTE RODE BEZAANTJES EN ZEER VEEL VIS: Large red [?] and a great many fish
GROTE ZWARTE VOGEL MET RODE BEK, DIE MEN: Large black bird with red beak, which they call southern birds, near the ship
GROU WASIGE GROND, ZAND MET KLEI, STEENT: Coarse [?] bottom, sand with clay, small stones and broken little shells.
GRUESA NEBLINA Y CON LA CALMA UN EXTRAOR: Thick mist and with the calm an extraordinary heat
HA ESTADO EL DÍA (...) LLENO DE TURBONAD: The day (...) has been full of squalls, which were incessant, alternating among them drizzle, hail and snow.
HA ESTADO RELAMPAGUEANDO POR TODO EL HOR: There has been lightning all around the horizon.
HA MUERTO DE DIARREA INVETERADA EL MARIN: The sailor Manuel Díaz has died of chronic diarrhea
HA NOTADO CORRIENTES. DESCRIPTORES DEL M: Noticed currents. Descriptors from midday or the day's run. Cannot leave earlier because of the calms and strong winds.
HA PASADO MUY POCO SARGAZO Y SE HAN VIST: Very little sargasso has passed and several lines of current have been seen.
HA PASADO SARGAZO AUNQUE NO CON TANTA AB: Sargasso has passed, though not in such abundance.
HA SIDO TAL LA ABUNDANCIA DE BALLENATOS: The abundance of young whales was such that the sea seemed filled with them, and some very close to the ship
HA TENIDO QUE CAMBIAR DE MERIDIANO PARA: Had to change meridian to measure the longitude but indicates nothing
HAALDE 4 PASSAGIERS VAN DE ENGELSE BARK: Fetched 4 passengers from the English bark on board.. Some gentlemen of the government of the shore on board. At departure 9 shots. Captain goes ashore. Welcomed by the fort with 13 shots.
HAALDE DE NOORTSE LAST OPKLARENDE LUCHT: Fetched the Norwegian last. Clearing sky, to pitch the tent, clearing sky [?].
HAALDEN 11 MAN UIT HET HOSPITAAL. KWARTI: Fetched 11 men from the hospital. Quartermaster Nicolaas Pet(..) died
HAALDEN 4 GEBETERDE ZIEKEN UIT HET HOSPI: Fetched 4 recovered sick men from the hospital
HAALDEN 4 SESPONDERS CANONSTUKKEN UIT 'T: Hauled 4 six-pounder cannon from the water hold and placed them on board
HAALDEN EEN BOOT MET VERS WATER. ZONDEN: Fetched a boat with fresh water. Sent 23 whole and 12 half pigs
HAALDEN HET GESCHUT AF. KRUIT NAT. LADEN: Took the guns off. Powder wet. Loaded them again with live rounds.
HAALDEN KISTEN EN KOEIEN VAN TUSSENDEKS: Hauled chests and bunks from between decks and cleaned.
HAALDEN KISTEN EN KOIJEN OP 'T DEK EN MA: Hauled chests and bunks onto the deck and cleaned between decks. Sprinkled with vinegar, etc.
HAALDEN KISTEN EN KOOIEN OP, ROOKTEN MET: Hauled up chests and bunks, smoked with gunpowder and [?]. Sprinkled with vinegar after cleaning
HAALDEN SCHERP GAT OP. MAKEN ENIG BLOKWE: Hauled up the [?] hole. Cleaned some of the blocks.
Hauled water and beer on deck.
HAAST ALLE ZEILEN MOETEN VASTMAKEN. SCHI: Hastily all sails had to be secured. Ship again worked heavily in the high sea
HABIAN ESTADO EN CALMA TODA LA NOCHE ANT: They had been in calm all the previous night and at 8:00 a north wind blew. Interesting comment on the currents and winds in that area
HABIENDO ABONANZADO EL TPO. (...) CIELO: The weather having improved (...) sky and horizon remained overcast (...) at nightfall horizon all squally and so it remained until 11 1/2 when it cleared somewhat to the E; at 12 1/2 lightning was seen to the SE and a light breeze from the SSW came in (...) at dawn all overcast except from the SE to the NE.
HABIENDO ACLARADO (...) A LAS 12 (...) S: Having cleared (...) at 12 (...) the wind shifted to the NW with a squall of wind and rain and much lightning (...) at dawn sky clear, horizon with thick cloud banks, sea from the wind and fresh easterly.
HABIENDO ENCONTRADO BUEN ABRIGO DAN FOND: Having found good shelter they anchor at nightfall, giving this port the name Marion, where they take observations. 172º 33' corrected. On the east side they saw a large number of inhabitants in 2 divisions, which made them suspect they were at war, but when the boat went ashore they were undeceived, although all were armed
HABIENDO VIRADO EN REDONDO CON EL VTO FL: Having worn ship with light wind and heavy sea from the SW; from one to three it was almost calm (...) nightfall sky overcast and horizon squally, moderate wind, with seas from the SE and SW. (...) The wind was fresh from midnight, and in the morning a fair amount of snow fell.
HABLA CON 1 PAQUEBOTE HOLANDES QUE VENIA: He speaks with a Dutch packet boat that came from the port of Mauricio and was going to Filadelfia and it told him it had no news of any war and that it considered itself 70 leagues from Cadiz
HABLA CON EL TUCUMAN Y DECIDEN IR EN CON: Speaks with the Tucuman and they decide to go in company to La Coruña. Data from midday or the day's run.
HABLA DE LA POSICION DE LA BAHIA DE SAN: Speaks of the position of the Bay of San Jose and the port of San Blas
HABLA DE LAS DIFERENCIAS EN LAS ANOTACIO: Speaks of the differences in the notations of the various nautical charts they carry. He trusts more the notations of that of D'Aupres. "The same birds have been seen as the previous day and we have experienced the sea that the backwash from the edge of the soundings produces, which he noted (according to what the color of the sea tells me) does not follow the shape that the new charts give it but rather conforms to the old one of Mesieur D'Apres, which is this one with little difference (draws a small plan)". Next he describes the little drawing that he includes with the position of capes, points, etc.
HABLA DE LAS FUERTES CORRIENTES DE LA ZO: Speaks of the strong currents of the area and of the mouth of the Rio de la Plata. They still find no bottom. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
HABLA DE LOS ENFERMOS QUE RECAEN DE RESU: Speaks of the sick who relapse as a result of some excess in eating fish, which apparently they catch so abundantly that many times they return it to the sea
HACE LA OBSERVACION PERO NO LA DA POR BU: Makes the observation but does not consider it good because the sun had dropped and because of the heavy sea there was
HACE UN COMENTARIO SOBRE LA POSICION DE: Makes a comment on the position of the shoals of Andrade
HACE UNA ANOTACION DE LA SITUACION DE LO: Makes a note of the situation of the masts of the rigging
HACE UNA REFLEXION ACERCA DE LOS CALCULO: Makes a reflection on the calculations he does to determine the direct course and distance. Says that the formulas he uses for it are in the first appendix of the Navegación of Don Jorge Juan. Also analyzes the use of the log and the sandglass. Measurement and data from midday or the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn
HACEN AGUADA EN EL PUERTO DE SANTA CRUZ: They take on water at the port of Santa Cruz
HACEN TODA LA DILIGENCIA PARA ENTRAR EN: They make every effort to enter the SE (I suppose the prevailing winds of these latitudes)
HACER EL BARCO MUCHA AGUA. ACONSEJA QUE: The ship makes a lot of water. Advises that in case of need one anchor at La Caldera, as it is the most sheltered port and the bottom is sand, since at Samboanga there is nothing to anchor on except a sandbank of coarse sand with the tide running strongly
HACIA YA 14 PULGADAS DE AGUA CADA 24 HOR: It was already making 14 inches of water every 24 hours. The repairs continue
HAD INTENTIE OM TRISTAN D'ACUNHA AAN TE: Had the intention of calling at Tristan d'Acunha to fetch water
HAD LENGTE VAN 40G15MIN VAN LONDEN AFF: Had a longitude of 40G15MIN from London
HADDE VAN DE 6 VISSE 124 VATEN SPEK 3 PI: Had from the 6 fish 124 casks of blubber, 3 pipes, 3 [?], 3 halves, 26 casks of [?]
HADDE VOLGENS GISSING 16 GRADE LENGTE, D: Had by estimate 16 degrees longitude, so it makes quite some difference with the longitude
HADDEN 'S AVONDS HET EILAND WIGHT IN HET: In the evening had the Isle of Wight in sight
HADDEN 'S MIDDAGS DE ZON IN TOP: At noon had the sun at the zenith
HADDEN 18 ZIEKE SLAVEN, LEDEN DEELS AAN: Had 18 sick slaves, some with scarlet fever, some with chest illness, some with diarrhea
HADDEN 2G22M IN LENGTE MISGEGIST, OP DEZ: Had misestimated the longitude by 2G22M, on this parallel make 28 miles westerly
HADDEN CASELOTTEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Had sperm whales near the ship
HADDEN DE MEERGEMELDE SCHEPEN NOG BIJ ON: Had the previously mentioned ships still with us
HADDEN DE ZON IN 'T ZENITH: Had the sun at the zenith
HADDEN DOOR DE NAGT STERKE VUERING IN HE: Had strong phosphorescence in the water during the night.
HADDEN ECLIPS AAN DE MAAN, BEGINNENDE OM: Had an eclipse of the moon, beginning to darken at half past ten and it was at its greatest at half past eleven
HADDEN EEN ECCLIPS AAN DE ZON, DOCH KOND: Had an eclipse of the sun, but could not see it?
HADDEN EEN ECLIPS (MAANSVERDUISTERING) A: Had an eclipse (lunar eclipse) of the moon in EW, which was seen to darken completely. See several gannets
HADDEN EEN HAAI EN TWEE DOLFIJNEN BIJ HE: Had a shark and two dolphins near the ship
HADDEN EEN HOOGE ZEE UIJT 'T ZW, DAARIN: Had a high sea from the SW, in which we rolled heavily. Had a high swell from the NW where we rolled heavily.
HADDEN EEN HOOS DICHT BIJ HET SCHIP: Had a waterspout close to the ship
Had a young slave of 14 die.
Had a boy slave of 20 die.
HADDEN EEN MAN EN EEN JONGENSLAAF VAN 18: Had a man and a boy slave of 18 die.
Had a man slave of 22 die.
HADDEN EEN MANSLAAF VAN 23 DOOD: Had a man slave of 23 die
HADDEN EEN MENIGTE VAN BOSKOPPEN BIJ HET: Had a multitude of [?] near the ship
HADDEN EEN MENIGTE VIS EN VOGELS RONDSOM: Had a multitude of fish and birds around the ship
HADDEN EEN MENIGTE VOGELS BIJ 'T SCHIP E: Had a multitude of birds near the ship and flying fish and other fish
HADDEN EEN MENIGTE VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP: Had a multitude of birds near the ship
Had a right whale near the ship.
Had a slave girl of 15 die.
HADDEN EEN STERKE VUERING IN 'T WATER. Z: Had strong phosphorescence in the water. See some birds
HADDEN EEN TIJDMETER AAN BOORD, DAARMEE: Had a chronometer on board, with which the longitude was determined
HADDEN ENIGE MALLEMUKEN, PIJLSTAARTEN EN: Had some fulmars, pintails and a [?] near the ship
HADDEN ENIGE SPURHAAIEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Had some spiny dogfish near the ship
HADDEN GEDURENDE DAG VEEL WALVISSEN BIJ: Had many whales near the ship during the day, but the albatrosses had left us.
HADDEN GEDURENDE DEZE DAGEN, DOOR DE GRO: During these days, because of the great motion of the ship, had no opportunity to take the compass variations.
HADDEN GEEN GOED LANDZICHT, SCHIETEN LIJ: Had no good sight of land, cast lines (preparing for fishing)
HADDEN HET DES AVONDS STILL. VERLEIJDEN: Had it calm in the evening. Adjusted the compasses from 17°30' to 15°00'. Found by azimuth bearings (variation) N/W.
HADDEN HET GEHELE ETMAAL DOOR DONDER EN: Had thunder and lightning the whole day
HADDEN HET WESTELIJKE LAND VAN OMBAYE ZW: Had the western land of Ombaye SW 1/2 S
HADDEN IN TWEE ETMALEN AL 25 MINUTEN VER: In two days had already lost 25 minutes to the north through the current
HADDEN MEER GEVOGELTE BIJ HET SCHIP DAN: Had more fowl near the ship than has been usual until now.
HADDEN MENIGTE DOLFIJNEN BIJ 'T SCHIP: Had a multitude of dolphins near the ship
HADDEN MET DE MIDDAG DE HOEK VAN GOUDSTA: Had at noon the point of Goudstaard. [?]. At noon the general course since yesterday noon was W¾S, 14¾ miles. But according to the above bearing the latitude course W 1/3 S, distance 10,25. Sandy bottom
HADDEN MOEITE DE BAAI BINNEN TE ZEILEN V: Had difficulty sailing into the bay because of the scant wind. AMW, 5.00 o'clock at anchor
Had ninety seriously sick men in their bunks.
HADDEN NOG VEEL MEEUWEN EN BASTERD MALLE: Still had many gulls and bastard mallemucks near the ship.
HADDEN NOG VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: Still had a lot of fish near the ship.
HADDEN NOORDKAPERS BIJ HET SCHIP: Had North Cape whales near the ship.
HADDEN OOK OP DIT SCHIP EEN TIJDMETER AA: Also had a chronometer on board this ship.
Had very heavy dew at night.
HADDEN SEDERT ONS VERTREK UIT MADERA NOG: Since our departure from Madera we have not yet had such a moderate sea.
HADDEN SEDERT TWEE DAGEN KLEINE DRIJVEND: For two days had seen small floating islands and many tree trunks with birds on them drifting past.
HADDEN SLAVEN AAN BOORD, 101 MANNEN, 78: Had slaves on board: 101 men, 78 women, 27 boys and 20 girls.
HADDEN STERKE NOORDERLICHT VAN 'T NO TOT: Had strong northern lights from the NE to NW. Roughly found northern latitude; it comes close to the true latitude obtained.
Had strong phosphorescence in the water.
HADDEN STERKE VURING IN HET WATER: Had strong phosphorescence in the water.
Had strong phosphorescence in the water (HW). Saw a multitude of shore gulls (AMW).
HADDEN VEEL DOLFIJNEN BIJ HET SCHIP EN V: Had many dolphins near the ship and caught one.
HADDEN VEEL GROTE VISSEN BIJ 'T SCHIP: Had many large fish near the ship.
HADDEN VEEL HAAIEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Had many sharks near the ship.

Take the cartridges out of the guns.
