Brought up chests and bunks from between decks, cleaned.

Brought up chests and bunks from between decks. Cleaned there. Have 70 sick in their bunks and a further 30 to 35 who kept going about on their feet. According to the chief surgeon they have a severe overflow of bile and hot fevers, severe pain in the head, arms and legs. People are losing weight badly. It is thought that it comes from the air.
Brought up chests and bunks from between decks. Cleaned. Expect to approach Madera and Porto Santo.
Brought up chests and bunks. Cleaned. Saw a trumpet drifting and 2 more bunches of greenery.
HALEN KISTEN ENKOEIEN OP TUSSENDEKS. OVE: Brought up chests and bunks between decks. Died: sailor Jacobus Hooij of Z(ierik)zee.
HALF RANTSOEN WATER EN OPEN BIERVAT VOOR: Half ration of water and open beer cask for the crew. Cleaned above and between decks. Aired with windsails.
HALLADO LA NOTABLE DIFERENCIA DE 33' 14': Found the notable difference of 33' 14'' further north than the dead reckoning. I see that, taking as departure point yesterday's arrival corrected for currents and reduced daily, it admits no correction, since (...) could not increase without having struck a sounding or seen land or a cay.
HALLAN EL CASCO DE UNA EMBARCACION PERDI: Find the hull of a lost vessel but cannot identify it. See some whales.
HALLAN FONDO EN 120 BRAZAS, LAMA VERDE C: Find bottom at 120 fathoms, light green ooze and fine black sand. "I note that for recognizing the sounding ground, in cases when the weather does not allow sounding, nothing is better than observing whether there are sea lions, for they do not leave it, and roletes, which is another fish that in its motion seems to go rolling or turning over. Some large white birds with black wing tips also confirm it, which are called mangas de boludo (that is, velvet boots); in the whole navigation no others are found with which to confuse them, for they fly like a duck and do not leave the sounding ground or at least sight of land. There are other small blackish-brown birds the size of a turtledove with a white beak; we have seen them only on the sounding ground or immediately near it. And lastly the colour of the sea strongly indicates the bottom, so much that there seems to be less, and compared with the record of other shoals where we have found 120 fathoms, one could scarcely estimate 50 or 60; but on seeing the quality of the bottom the cause is understood, since it is green ooze and fine black sand, colours quite capable of changing the water's appearance."
HAN ESTADO LOS CARICES MALOS , LOS CIELO: The look of the weather has been bad, the skies closed in.
HAN SEGUIDO LAS FUGADAS DE LA BRISA CON: The gusts of breeze with drizzle have continued, one of them (...), the weather already settled at 2 in the morning (...). The horizons clouded and skies heavy.
HAN SEGUIDO LOS CIELOS Y HORIZ. MÁS CLAR: The skies and horizons have continued clearer.
HAN SEGUIDO LOS HORIZ. LEVANTANDO ALGUNA: The horizons have continued, with some thick cloud banks rising, some with drizzle.
HAN SEGUIDO LOS HORIZ. Y CIELOS CARGADOS: The horizons and skies have continued heavy.
HANDZAAM GEEFT AAN ALLE VERRICHTINGEN VA: Manageable; allows for all operations in the wind.
HARDE BUIEN IN EW EN ONWEER IN HET N EN: Heavy squalls in EW and thunder in the N and E.
HARDE WIND MET VLIEGENDE STORM BUIJEN, D: Strong wind with flying storm squalls, then decreasing to a reefed topsail breeze. Storm squalls.
HARPOENEERDE IN DE MORGEN OM 10 UUR EEN: Harpooned in the morning at 10 o'clock a dolphin the size of a sea lion; it tasted of mackerel and pike; its colour changed from all sorts to white.
HASTA EL MEDIO DÍA NO SE VIÓ EMBARCACIÓN: Until midday no vessel was seen.
Until 7 in the evening there was no wind (...). The weather has been too calm, the sea flat and the wind very light, although since it came in it has been increasing slowly.
HAYÁNDOME PARA ESTE PUNTO ATRACADO A LA: Finding myself at this point close in to the coast and east of the Berlengas. Note: having reached the dead-reckoning point, I place myself at longitude 1º 45' by the point of variation.
HE EXPERIMENTADO MUCHOS HILOS DE CORRIEN: I have experienced many threads of current with many heads which followed the course E 1/4 NE. Data are from midday, although some days they are from dawn. Since 9-2-1767 they are from dawn. The journal begins on 17-DIC-1766, since it sailed that day but had to return, putting back into port. On 23-DIC it sails definitively.
HE HALLADO EN LA MARCACIÓN DE HOY 14' DE: I found in today's bearing a 14' difference in longitude to the east of my dead reckoning. But having followed on those days a separate point with meridian correction, the latter gives only 5' east of that reckoning, placing me at longitude 7º 35'. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet. The mile in eight fathoms. Glass of 30 sec. First departure point on the French chart of '53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin, 4th ed. '66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
HEBBE IN ENKELDE SCHOTS IJS OP ZEE: Had occasional ice floes on the sea.

HEBBEN DONDER EN BLIKSEM. ZIEN STROOM IN: Have thunder and lightning. See current running in the water.
HEBBEN GEEN DOEK MEER OM DE LIJKEN IN TE: Have no more cloth to sew the corpses into and are short of sand.

HEBBEN HET IJS VAN DEK AF SOMS IN HET GE: Sometimes have the ice in sight from the deck.

HEBBEN MALLEFIETIES EN MEEUWEN BIJ HET S: Have [?] and gulls near the ship.

EN GEG ZB WA: The difference between the observed and estimated ZB was a good 40', yet then they reckoned 4 degrees for leeway and 1 point for the variation, which latter was at first fixed only at 9 degrees; this thus made a difference of 6 degrees 15' or a good 1/2 point, assuming the usual fudging aboard this ship

The water had its normal colour again.

HIELDEN ERBIJ DE GESTELHEID VAN DE ZIEKE: Attended to the condition of the sick.

HIELDEN GODSDIENSTOEFENING IVM KERSTFEES: Held a church service for Christmas

HIELDEN ONS AAN DE WESTER? TIJDMETER EN: Relied on the western? chronometer and steered NWTN to Sint Assension

HIELDEN SCHEEPSGEBED.DEELDEN MEEL UIT AA: Held ship's prayer. Distributed flour to the crew
HIELDEN SCHEEPSGEBED.ZIEN EEN VOGEL EN V: Held ship's prayer. See a bird and much fish near the ship. "With the help of the Almighty we had passed the Line". At night strong phosphorescence in the water
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAA. BEVONDEN 7 IMPOTENTE: Held ship's council. Found 7 invalids, mostly on the mend
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD EN VERHOREN DE ARRES: Held ship's council and questioned the prisoner and the boatswain; the sailmaker had given cause for a quarrel. Sailmaker is punished
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER DE 5 MATROZEN,: Held ship's council about the 5 sailors who had been left behind from the sloop on 29/8. They received punishment.
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER DE BEMANNING EN: Held ship's council about the crew and established that 2 a little ..?
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER DE EQUIPAGE, HE: Held ship's council about the crew, have 15 invalids. Sailor Jurgen Andries Oth from the Gusfeler office (no. 2) died. Distribute flour. Inspected the estate of the 2 deceased, found nothing but old worn clothing, divide it
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER GESTELDHEID VAN: Held ship's council about the condition of the ship
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD WEEGENS DE ZIEKEN. H: Held ship's council about the sick. Had 6 invalids, 5 with fevers and 1 with scurvy.
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD WEEGERS DE ZIEKEN. B: Held ship's council about the sick. Found 6 invalids. Suffering from fevers and scurvy. Resolved to supply sauerkraut and sea coral [?] to the crew twice a week. Issued 1/2 month's ration to the crew. Aired with the windsail, etc.
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD: DE KOK JAN JANSEN W: Held ship's council: the cook Jan Jansen was demoted to sailor and sailor Jan Schaak was appointed cook, because of the poor performance of the former
HIELDEN SCHEEPSRAAD: DE KOK JAN SCHAAK W: Hielden ship's council: The cook Jan Schaak was relieved of his duty and demoted to sailor, while the sailor Andries took over his place as cook; the former did his work poorly
HIELDEN SCHOOL VOOR DE SCHEEPSJONGENS: Hielden school for the ship's boys
HIELDEN VERGADERING: MAAKTEN ENIGE SOLDA: Hielden meeting: Some soldiers were made sailors and some sailors soldiers. Decided not to call at St. Jago. They have no other shortcomings than 40 sick. Sailor Pieter Roode van Bergen becomes provost and soldier Guilliam Porthuijse van Ossel becomes cook's mate.
HIELDEN VERKOOP VAN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE D: Hielden sale of the goods of the deserters Fischer and Kaijk.
HIELDEN VERKOOP VAN DE NAGELATEN GOEDERE: Hielden sale of the belongings left by the deceased
HIELDEN VERKOOP VAN DE PLUNJES VAN DE DE: Hielden sale of the personal effects of the deserters.
HIELDEN VERKOPING VAN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE: Hielden sale of the goods of the deceased widow Kortleven
HIELDEN VERKOPING VAN DE GOEDEREN VAN WI: Hielden sale of the goods of the late Captain Roelofs
HIER BEGINT DE REIS LANGS DE KUST VAN AF: Here begins the voyage along the coast of Africa. On 18 November sighted the Banana Islands off the coast of present-day Sierra Leone.
HIER EINDIGT DEZE REIS. HET JOURNAAL GAA: Here this voyage ends. The journal continues with the voyage from Texel to Castle St. George d'Elmina on the African coast.
HIER HEB IK GEBRUIK GEMAAKT VAN EEN INGE: Here I made use of an imported extract, and added the data from the original journal; where they differed I wrote the 'found' position in the 'obtained' fields. For the other markings I used . to indicate that after this sign data from the journal follow.
HIER HEB IK TIJDMETER NO. 980 WEER GEBRU: Here I used chronometer no. 980 again.
HIER LAG NOG STEEDS DE ADM. EVERTSEN, HE: Here the Adm. Evertsen was still lying; the journal of the Adm. Evertsen has also been copied from 25 May to 2 October
HIER WAS HET, DAAR ONS DE NO PASSAAT VER: Here it was, where the NE trade wind left us
HIER WORDT VOOR HET EERST IN DE VMW MELD: Here for the first time the VMW reports an S BK. I assume that this is a stiff topgallant breeze.
HIERNA GEEN POSITIES MEER. OP 23 FEBRUAR: After this no more positions. On 23 February three male slaves and one female slave died, nos. 56-59. On 1 March came to anchor before Paramaribo. In the meantime 3 more male slaves and 2 female slaves had died, nos. 60-64. In the roads three more female slaves died. A sailor deserted.
HIERNA VAART HET SCHIP NOG NAAR SOERABAJ: After this the ship sails on to Soerabaja, Samarang, Sumanap, Padang
HIJSEN VLAG EN WIMPEL VOOR EEN SCHIP, DA: Hoisting flag and pennant for a ship, which shows no flag. Later in the day it showed an English flag
HIJSEN VLAG WGNS VERJARING VAN 1 DER LED: Hoisting flag on account of the birthday of one of the members of the royal house
HIJZEN DAGELIJKS DE KOELZEILEN EN ZETTEN: Daily hoist the cooling sails and, in warm weather, open the hatches of the holds and the doors of the storage rooms for the venting of fumes.
HIJZEN DE VLAG TER ERE VAN VERJAARDAG VA: Hoist the flag in honor of the birthday of the Crown Prince of the Netherlands.
Hoist flag and fire a shot.
HIJZEN VLAG TER ERE VAN DE GEBOORTE VAN: Hoist flag in honor of the birth of Prince Frederik of the Netherlands.
HILOS DE CORRIENTES MUY NOTABLES Y TENDI: Threads of very notable currents, stretching from NW to SE
HIZO EL CMTE. SEÑAL PARA PONERNOS A PIQU: The commander made signal for us to scuttle ourselves, which we did
HOEK VAN FORTARENTURA VLGS DE LANDVERTON: Cape of Fortarentura according to the landfall view of that cape in the new Spanish chart, by Knight D. Joseph Varela, published in 1794 by G. Hubst van Keulen
HOEWEL DIT EILAND NOG AL REDELIJK HOOG I: Although this island is still fairly high, no land.
HOGE VERBOLGEN ZEE WAARDOOR MEN GENOODZA: High swollen sea, because of which one was forced to steer SSE for the ease of the ship
HOGE ZEE UIT HET W (IN DE EW): High sea from the W (in the EW)
HOLLE ZEE WAARDOOR HET SCHIP ALSMAAR SLI: Hollow sea, because of which the ship rolled continually
HOLLE ZEE WAARDOOR HET SCHIP SLINGERDE: Hollow sea, because of which the ship rolled
HOREN DAT 'S LANDS FREGAT ALPHEN DE 17E: Hear that the state's frigate Alphen blew up in the harbor of Curacao on the 17th. Only a few survivors. ADM_193_20_0109 is a list of Dutch merchant ships

Horizons clear (...) At nightfall (...) horizons the same but the wind was always diminishing.

HORIZ. CLAROS, A LAS 3 ENTRÓ LA VENTOLIN: Horizons clear, at 3 a light breeze came in from the NW (...) At nightfall horizons dark, gentle wind and sea from the SW and at dawn the same.

At 9 an aurora borealis was seen, which was a red patch from the NNW to the NE and from an altitude of 10° up to 50°; until 10 it stayed lit, with some like columns of a lighter color, (...) it began to fade and remained as a great brightness; at 11½ it lit up again and at 1 it dispersed entirely, but at 2 it was seen again somewhat more to the WNW and clear until 3½. At dawn skies and horizons with clear cloud, light fresh wind, some sea from the NW that kept growing and (causing) heavy rolling.
HORIZ. CLAROS, VTO N FRESQUITO, MAR LLAN: Horizons clear, light fresh N wind, smooth sea (...) At nightfall the same. Horizons with cloud (...) At nightfall horizons dark (...) wind freshening and in squalls (...). At dawn horizons dark, sea ahead, wind less fresh.
HORIZ. CON CELAJ. CLARA (...) AL ANOCHEC: Horizons with clear cloud (...) At nightfall the wind began to freshen (...) All night there was strong wind with much sea, but at dawn it kept dropping and shifting to the W.
Horizons with scattered cloud (...) At nightfall light fresh wind (which) continued all night (...) several squalls (...) squalls and then with hail.
HORIZ. CON CELAJ. SUELTA (...)ANOCHEC. H: Horizons with scattered cloud (...) At nightfall horizons with thick dark cloud, fresh wind (...) many squalls (...).

Horizons with cloud and swell from the E.

HORIZ. DE MALISIMO SEMBLANTE CAYENDO CON: Horizon of a most wretched look, continuous downpour falling, the sea dropped much in the night.
HORIZ. DEL NO HASTA EL ESE ATURBONADOS Y: Horizons from the NW to the ESE squally and the rest with clear cloud (...). At nightfall skies and horizons with scattered clear cloud, light fresh NNE wind, smooth sea (...) At dawn clear sky, horizons with dark cloud, wind almost calm and smooth sea.
HORIZ. DESDE EL NO HASTA EL ESE ATURBONA: Horizons from the NW to the ESE squally and the rest with clear cloud. At 1½ (...) a squall (...) At nightfall with horizons clear (...) At dawn with sky and horizons clear.
HORIZ. FOSCOS CON ARRUMAZÓN Y CIELOS TOL: Horizons gloomy with haze and overcast skies.
HORIZ. FOSCOS, MAR DEL E: Horizons gloomy, sea from the E
HORIZ. FUSCOS Y CIELO TOLDADO (...) ANOC: Horizons gloomy and sky overcast (...) At nightfall sky covered with dark cloud, horizons gloomy, sea from the wind and this fresh E (...) At dawn the same.
HORIZ. MUY CARGADOS CON ALGUNA GARÚA: Horizons very heavy with some drizzle
HORIZ. MUY MALOS Y VENTADO FRESCAMENTE A: Horizons very bad and wind blowing freshly in gusts and squalls with much sea from the wind and the SW.
HORIZ. MÁS CLAROS QUE LOS DÍAS ANTECEDEN: Horizons clearer than the preceding days.
HORIZ. NEBLINOSOS, CIELO CLARO (...) ANO: Horizons misty, clear sky (...) At nightfall horizons heavy, heavy sea and fresh wind with plenty of downpours
HORIZ. OFUSCOS Y CELAJ. GRUESA (...)ANOC: Horizons dim and thick cloud (...) At nightfall gentle wind and the rest the same (...) At dawn clear sky, horizons streaked with cloud, sea from the W and light fresh wind.
HORIZ. OFUSCOS(...). ANOCHEC. HORIZ. OSU: Horizons dim (...). At nightfall horizons dim but it kept clearing and the sea dropping; at 32 the wind shifted to the W (...) at 4 the wind being gentle and the horizons clear.
HORIZ. OSCUROS (...) CON MUCHA NIEVE, EL: Horizons dark (...) with much snow, the wind and snow were heavy (...) At nightfall the weather not improving and afterwards the wind kept dropping, shifting to the N (...) At dawn skies and horizons heavy, sea from the SE, the wind kept freshening.
HORIZ. OSCUROS Y MUCHO FRIO. FUE CAYENDO: Horizons dark and much cold. The wind kept dropping and it fell calm (...). We continued all night with the wind freshening more with much cold (...). At dawn with horizons dark, fresh wind with some sea.

HORIZ. TOLDADOS CON ALGUNA CELAJ. SUELTA: Horizons overcast with some scattered cloud

HORIZ. Y CIELO OFUSCOS CON CELAJ. GRUESA: Horizons and sky dim with thick cloud (...) At nightfall sky clear, horizons and sea as stated (...) At dawn sky clear, horizons streaked with cloud, heavy sea from the W and fresh wind.

HORIZ. Y CIELOS ACELAJADOS: Horizons and skies streaked with cloud
HORIZ. Y CIELOS CON CELAJ. PARDA. ANOCHE: Horizons and skies with dark cloud. At nightfall skies and horizons with thick dark cloud, gentle wind E by NE and sea from the NE. At dawn skies with cloud and horizons with haze and thick dark cloud, fresh wind and a light swell.

HORIZONTES ACELAJADOS Y CIELOS CLAROS: Horizons streaked with cloud and skies clear

HOUDEN GOEDE UITKIJKE DOCH KONDEN NIETS: Keeping a good lookout but could see nothing. In the evening hazy sky
HOUDEN KOERSBERAMING, HEBBEN GEEN VAN DE: Making a reckoning of the course, have not seen any of the islands.
HOUDEN SCHEEPSKRIJGSRAAD OVER DE BOTTELI: Holding a ship's council of war about the steward.
HOUDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER 'T SLECHTE GEDRA: Holding a ship's council about the bad conduct of the 2nd mate
HOUDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER (GEBREK AAN) GOR: Holding a ship's council about the (lack of) groats
HOUDEN SCHEEPSRAAD OVER EERDER GENOEMDE: Holding a ship's council about the previously named Clement.
HOUDEN SCHEEPSRAAD, BESLUITEN 1 VD KAAP: Holding a ship's council, resolving to call at 1 of the Cape Verde Islands
HOUDEN VENDU VD NALATENSCHAPPEN VD GEDES: Holding an auction of the estates of the deserters Richards and F. Lewis
HOUDEN VERKOPING VAN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE: Holding a sale of the goods of the 4 deserted sailors (Madsen, Petterson, J. de Voogd and Schullz
HOUDEN WEER VERSCHILLENDE SEINOEFENINGEN: Again holding various signal drills. Again toward transport ship no. 13 to urge it to make more sail
Today at noon I find myself 1º 32' of longitude farther east of the point at which the route says to go and seek the lat. of 41º 45', and consequently I am 190 leagues east of the place where they locate the island discovered in the year 1767, having searched for it along its parallel for 230 leagues without finding any sign of land except the presence of birds.
HOY AL MEDIO DÍA SE DEMARCARON LAS SIERR: Today at noon the Sierras de Monchique were sighted at NW 1/4 N 6º, which datum and that of the observed latitude place me at longitude 8º 48', which differs from the dead-reckoning point by one degree more to the east. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet, the mile in eight fathoms. Sandglass of 30 sec. First departure point on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4 ed.66. Corrections with the Meridi. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
HOY AL MEDIODIA HABIENDO DEMARCADO LAS S: Today at noon, having sighted the Sierras de Monchique at NE (...) this datum with the observed latitude places me at 7º 25' of longitude. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet, the mile in eight fathoms. Sandglass of 30 sec. First departure point on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4 ed.66. Corrections with the Meridi. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
HOY AL MEDIODIA NO SE HA PODIDO OBSERVAR: Today at noon no observation could be made because everything was overcast.
HOY EL NAVIO ANDUVO 9 MILLAS QUE ES LO M: Today the ship made 9 miles, which is the most it has done since it left Rio de Janeiro.
HOY HA CAMBIADO LA LETRA DE QUIEN ESCRIB: Today the handwriting of the person writing the log has changed. Note (from the log): this book having been finished, I continued on loose sheets that are included here. The head of the log is missing, and the table to be filled in, which with the continual duties of my charge I have not had time to do. Adrián Valcárcel.
HUBO SUS CHUBASQUITOS: There were a few little showers.
HUBO UN ECLIPSE TOTAL DE LUNA. RUMBO Y D: There was a total eclipse of the moon. Course and direction of the wind at noon / rest of general references.
HUTSPOT VAN AARDAPPELEN VOOR DE BEMANNIN: Hotchpotch of potatoes for the crew.
HW + VM: LODEN DE DIEPTE. ZIEN DE VUURTO: Dog watch and forenoon: sounded the depth. Saw the lighthouse of the Sorlings (Scilly Isles). By our position on the flat chart we are 11.5 miles too far west, and on the round chart too far east.
HW EN DW: DONDERBUIEN EN REGEN: Dog watch and day watch: thunderstorms and rain.
HW MET? GLAZEN UIT (ZAGEN ZIJ HET EILAND: Dog watch, with? glasses out (they saw the island Groot Canaria), steered somewhat more westerly to pass to the north of it. Day watch: steered west by south along Groot Canaria. Forenoon: steered between Groot Canaria and Tenerife.
HW: DE WIND VAN OTN TOT OTZ, ZEER ONGELI: Dog watch: the wind from east by north to east by south, very uneven breeze with rain. Forenoon watch: the wind shifting out and in, with unsettled weather and squally sky.
HW: SCHIEMANSMAAT MULDER IN DE BOEIEN. D: Dog watch: boatswain's mate Mulder in irons. Day watch: boatswain's mate Mulder out of irons and sailor Leur in irons. Afternoon watch: 'At 0h30 the 2nd Lieutenant Quartermaster of the colonial troops De Ruijter died of the consequences of a cramp in the lung.'
HW: VLIEGENDE STORM. WEST MERIDIAAN 259: Dog watch: raging storm. West meridian distance 259 miles. Changed 16.75 miles W. Obtained 275.75 miles.
HW: WACHTVOLK EXTRA OORLAM: Dog watch: watch crew [given] an extra dram of oorlam.
IEDERE DAG MELDING V/E ENGELS SCHIP: Every day a report of an English ship.
IEDERE DAG WORDT DE KOMPASAFWIJKING GEGE: Every day the compass variation is given. I have taken the data from the forenoon as much as possible, but it is often not given; the day watch usually is, so then I took that.
IEDEREEN POMPTE MEE, OFFICIEREN, PASSAGI: Everyone pumped, officers, passengers, idlers, while the SBN kept watch on deck.
IEDERRE AVOND STRERKE VUURRING IN HET WA: Every evening strong phosphorescence in the water.
IGUAL BUEN SEMBLANTE Y MAR LLANA HASTA L: Same fair appearance and smooth sea until five in the morning, when in a squall with much rain and little wind…
IGUAL EN TODO HA SIDO ESTA SINGLADURA A: This day's run has been the same in everything, except for the showers, which have left us.
IIN AREST WEGENS HET NIET NAKOMEN DER GE: Under arrest for not carrying out given orders, the marine J. Bendels.
I keep to the values of chronometer 23.
IK ONDERGETEKENDE (SCHRIJVER) KWAM IN AR: I, the undersigned (clerk), was placed under arrest.
IK SCHEIJDE VAN DE SBN AF, MET 5 KOOPVAA: I part from the SBN, with 5 merchantmen on station: Magnus Mobik, Jasper Koenriwert, Klaase Kuyper, Corn Eberts and Paulus Paulusse.

IN DIT JOURNAAL WORDT EEN AANTAL EXTRA Z: In this journal a number of extra items are given, such as 'barometer level' (starboard and port). I do not copy this because an atmospheric barometer reading is also given. Under 'state of the sea' abbreviations are used, which I assume mean the following: K=calm. D=swell. H=high. A problem forms A. Is this decreasing, worsening, increasing or sharply rising? I will use the abbreviations as much as possible. These abbreviations are noted in the journal with a capital letter, I use a small letter.

INCLUYE ANOTACIONES DE LATITUD Y LONGITU: Includes notes of latitude and longitude of the islands it passes (for example, the island of Flores) and establishes differences or variations between the meridian of Tenerife and that of Cadiz. Measurement and data of noon or of the day's run, unless otherwise indicated.
INCLUYE UN DIBUJO DEL PERFIL DE ISLA ROD: Includes a drawing of the profile of Rodriguez Island and the calculation of the landfall at Rodriguez Island according to the Tenerife meridian and the Berlin chart. In the afternoon they see many birds of different species, among them tropicbirds and frigatebirds, which in the evening return in flocks to the island, as they gather on its beaches at night. Describes the anchorage and the (French) settlement of the island, its houses, turtle fishing, the reefs, etc.
INICIA LAS MANIOBRAS EL DIA 17 PERO NO S: Begins the manoeuvres on the 17th but does not leave earlier because of the north winds. Measurement and data of noon minus descriptors that are usually from nightfall. French chart.
INTENTA ARRIBAR A CEDERA PERO FRACASA. D: Tries to make Cedera but fails. Noon data (since 18 Dec the descriptors are from nightfall).
INVENTARISATIE VAN HET GOED VAN DEN OVER: Inventory of the goods of the deceased captain lieutenant.
IS OVERLEDEN NO 3 SOLDAAT JOHAN TOBIAS C: Died NO 3 soldier Johan Tobias Corn, craftsman.
ISLA DE FLORES, AL L 1/4 SE, DIST. DE 67: Island of Flores, bearing L 1/4 SE, distance 67 leagues.
ISLA GRACIOSA AL SSO DIST. 27 1/2 LEGUAS: Isla Graciosa to the SSE distance 27 1/2 leagues and the island of El Cuervo to the ESE distance 40 1/2 leagues.
ISLA TRINIDAD, POR LA CARTA, ME HALLO SO: Trinidad Island, by the chart, I find myself on it.
ISLOTE GRANDE DE MARTIN BAS DEMORA AL E: Islote Grande de Martin Bas bears E 1/4 SE.
IVM EERDER GENOEMD SCHIP: MAAKTE ALLES K: Because of the previously mentioned ship: made everything ready for defence, could no longer see the ship at sunset.
J. SMIT IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS BRUTALITEIT: J. Smit in irons for brutality.
J. VAN DUIN WEGENS DRONKENSCHAP IN DE BO: J. van Duin in irons for drunkenness.
J.VAN DE HORST VERZOCHT OM SOLDAAT TE WO: J. van de Horst requested to become a soldier since he did not dare climb into the rigging, which they granted him.
JAGEN EN SCHIETEN OP EEN VREEMD SCHIP, S: Chased and fired on a strange ship, SBN hoists an English flag, the strange ship a Spanish one, whereupon the SBN showed a Batavian flag.
JAGEN OP SCHIP MET PORTUGESE VLAG: Chased a ship with Portuguese flag.
JAGEN OP VREEMD SCHIP, BLIJKT EEN DEENSE: Chased a strange ship, turns out to be a Danish brig loaded with general cargo on the way from Livorno to Hamburg, Captain Johan Daniel Reijners, the ship Proviventia.
JAGEN TOT ZONSONDERGANG TUSSEN HET W EN: Chased until sunset between the W and the N to see land.
Chased between the W and N to see land.
JAN BRANDSTEKER OVERLEDEN (26). CHRISTIA: Jan Brandsteker died (26). Christiaan Topezen died (27).
JAN GODEFRID VAN BOCKOM, DE EERSTE SCHRI: Jan Godefrid van Bockom, the first clerk, takes back the effects and papers of the 2nd clerk Abraham van Sull. Cadet F 210 Charles Rielach becomes lieutenant on Princes Louisa.
JAN HULSLOOT, KUIPER, OVERLDEN (MET ZIEK: Jan Hulsloot, cooper, died (with description of the illness).
JAN QUAAKEL IN DE BOEIEN GEZET. MATROOS,: Jan Quaakel put in irons. Sailor Jacob de Gelen died. Articles read.
JAN VAN KLEEFF OVERLEEDEN, ANTHONIE AART: Jan van Kleeff died, Anthonie Aarts died.
JAN VERMEULEN, JAN GREEVE, PHILIP HENDRI: Jan Vermeulen, Jan Greeve, Philip Hendrik de Haart aboard.
JE PROLONGEAI LA CÔTE DU JAPON, ET PASSA: I coasted along the coast of Japan, and passed to the east of the island of Jootsi-Sima, which at 4 o'clock on the 6th bore E. and W.
JOHAN JOOST ERGHUIZEN GEARRESTEERD WEGEN: Johan Joost Erghuizen arrested for theft, with mention of what he had stolen.
JOHAN PEDRO VAN SALOUHE KRIJGT 200 KEER: Johan Pedro van Salouhe receives 200 strokes with the boot.
JOLI FRAIS, PETIT FRAIS: Fine fresh breeze, light fresh breeze.
JOLIE FRAIS ET PETITE FRAIS: Fine fresh breeze and light fresh breeze.
JOLIE FRAIS ET PRESQUE CALME: Fine fresh breeze and almost calm.
JON MATROOS IN DE BOEIEN DOOR BEGANE DIE: Young sailor in irons for theft committed.
JONG MATROOS F. ESSENHONST ZWAAR AAN 'T: Young sailor F. Essenhonst badly wounded in the head. Lieut. C. de Mantrots under arrest.
JONG MATROOS GENOEMD AUGASTI ANTOF VAN P: Young sailor named Augasti Antof of Papenborg has been killed in an accident.
JONG MATROOS JAN FREDRIK MEIJERS VAN STA: Young sailor Jan Fredrik Meijers of Stamel fell overboard and was killed.
JONG MATROOS MICHIEL LECOURT VAN AMSTERD: Young sailor Michiel Lecourt of Amsterdam died.
JONGEN DE KORT OPNIEUW GESTOLEN EN UIT B: The boy De Kort, having stolen again and, out of wantonness, having books worth nothing, was severely punished with cudgels and locked in a wooden collar for 8 days.
JONGEN R. DE KORT GESTRAFT WEGENS DIEFST: The boy R. De Kort was punished for stealing gin, punished with cudgels.
JONGEN SLAAF OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN VERDR: The slave boy fell overboard and drowned, 250 still alive.
JONGEN VAN HAARLEM ONTSLAGEN VAN DE STRA: The boy from Haarlem was released from the punishment in the plank but locked in leg irons so that he must keep walking around in them continually.

The boy from Haarlem was released from the punishment of walking around in leg irons, in view of the difficult movements of the ship, the increasing cold and his complete lack of footwear, while his account does not allow him to be issued shoes.
JONGEN VAN HAARLEM STRENGELIJK MET KNUTT: The boy from Haarlem was severely punished with cudgels for stealing a hat. The officers' cook Duffels was locked in irons, bent over, for deliberately or out of laziness cooking badly (1 time 24 hours).
JONGEN VAN HAARLEM, DIE VAN DE MATROOS H: The boy from Haarlem, who had stolen a jacket and a pair of trousers from the sailor Hofman, for which he had been punished on the 22nd, was severely punished with cudgels and then locked by the head in a plank with 1 hole in it.
JONGEN VAN VLAANDEREN HAD ZICH VERHANGEN: The boy from Flanders had hanged himself but could be cut loose in time; he was locked in handcuffs and the next day punished with 50 blows with cudgels and kept under arrest a few more days.
The boy S.H. of Leerdam died.
JONGENS EN MATROZEN AFGESTRAFT WGNS LIED: Boys and sailors punished for debauchery.
JONGENSLAAF OVERLEDEN, NO. 55. SPRINGEN: The slave boy died, no. 55. Jumping with lime juice.
JONGMATROOS CHRISTIAAN BERGMAN VAN AMSTE: Young sailor Christiaan Bergman of Amsterdam died.
JONGMATROOS HARBERT LAMMERS VAN AMSTERDA: Young sailor Harbert Lammers of Amsterdam died.
JONGMATROOS JACOBUS MANHAVEN VAN CADSANT: Young sailor Jacobus Manhaven of Cadsant died.
JONKER S. VALCKENBURG OVERLEED, WERD HET: Midshipman S. Valckenburg died; the ship was carried around and he was put overboard.
JOOURNAAL OFTE DAGREGISTER GEHOUDEN DOOR: Journal or daily register kept by me, Volkert Groeneweg of Oudshoorn, cadet on the E company ship Polanen, commanded by the valiant skipper Hilde Hendricksz Hoek.
JOURNAAL GAAT NOG VERDER TOT SEPTEMBER 1: Journal continues until September 1850, but only cruising on the North Sea from Hellevoetsluis.
JOURNAAL GEHOUDEN AAN BOORD VAN 'S LANDS: Journal kept aboard the state's frigate Bellona, under the command of the honourable, stern gentleman Captain Willem Francois Imbert de Martines, by the undersigned serving as lieutenant on the said frigate, begun 23 April 1783.
JOURNAAL VAN DE UYT REYZE MET HET SCHIP: Journal of the outward voyage with the ship Straalen, sailing with God's help to Bengal, sailed by me Arie Dams on 17 December 1785 from Texel to the Cape of Good Hope. Transferred our dead reckoning into the round chart, from where our dead reckoning begins, awaiting God's blessing.
JUSTITIE GEDAAN OVER DE 2 MEERGEMELDE MA: Justice done on the 2 aforementioned sailors. They were sentenced to be [?] at the discretion of the commissioners.
JUSTITIE GEDAAN OVER DE MATROOS VAN SCHI: Justice done on the sailor of skipper David de Jong. Sentenced to: fall from the yard 3 times, be [?] at the discretion of the commissioners, and to continue serving as a sailor on the Maarsen. Afternoon: got a sailor aboard from the fort who had gone ashore on 12 Dec with permission. He was locked in irons. Forenoon: when the clerk was ashore he found there a second sailor who had also gone ashore on 12 Dec with consent. The clerk brought him aboard with the longboat where he was put in irons.
JUSTITIE GEDAAN OVER VOORNOEMDE MATROOS,: Justice done on the aforementioned sailor; sentenced to be 'gelaerst' [?] at the discretion of the commissioners and to continue serving as a sailor on the Maarsen. Forenoon and afternoon: the clerk goes with an officer to the merchant ship of David de Jong to make a statement about his sailor who was in irons on the Maarsen.
JUSTITIE GEHOUDEN OVER DESERTEUR JAN VAN: Justice held over the deserter Jan van Lave [?]
KAAP FRIO VOLGENS CHRONOMETERS LENGTE WT: Cape Frio by chronometers, longitude WSW 1/4 S, 97 miles.
KAAP ST. AUGUSTIN LIGT VOLGENS DE FRANSE: Cape St. Augustin lies according to the French chart 37 degrees 28 minutes west of Paris, according to the Spanish 37 degrees 22 minutes and according to the English sea book 37 degrees 53 minutes.
KAAP VACHES VOLGENS KAART VAN NOURIE: NT: Cape Vaches according to the chart of Nourie: NNW 1/4 W, 6 miles. Sounded 64 fathoms.
KAAPSCHE DUIVEN EN MEEUWEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Cape pigeons and gulls near the ship.
KAAPSE DUIVEN VERLIETEN HET SCHIP, ZE HA: Cape pigeons left the ship; they had accompanied the ship about 600 miles west of the Cape of Good Hope.
KAAPSE DUIVEN, BASTAARD MALLEGANZEN EN A: Saw Cape pigeons, bastard fulmars and other birds flying.
KAART: OVERZEILER NAAR DE WESTINDIEN VAN: Chart: Oversailer to the West Indies by Van Keulen (image 150). Book: Geography, by A. du Bois (image 150). Result of the dead reckoning: "Stand with the reckoning on the [?] corner of the island of Flores. Bearings of the said corner (see above) were with the reckoning only [?] miles further west.
KAN DE PASSAATWIND MAAR NIET OPLOPEN: Cannot manage to catch up with the trade wind.
KANONNIER SCHEINECKER EERST TEGEN DE SCH: Gunner Scheinecker, having been extremely brutal first towards the boatswain's mate and then towards me, was locked in irons, bent over, for 3 days on water and bread.
KANONNIER SCHIERNECKER NA 8 DAGEN IN HET: Gunner Schiernecker, after sitting under arrest in the hold for 8 days, was released from it and in the meantime locked in leg irons and fastened to an eyebolt as a precaution against his extreme ravings.
KANONNIER SCHIERNECKER, TERWIJL HIJ NOG: Gunner Schiernecker, while still in irons bent over, having again made himself guilty of extreme brutalities and insults directed at me, first had a trumpet bag tied over his head, and then, when he had calmed somewhat, was put in the hold on the ballast, with 1 foot in irons and this fastened to an eyebolt.
KAPITEIN BESLUIT ST HELENA AAN TE DOEN O: Captain decides to call at St Helena to replenish the supplies.
KAPITEIN D'ARMES H. ZOETEMANS OVERLEEDEN: Captain at arms H. Zoetemans died.
KAPITEIN DABENES NEEMT AFSCHEIDT NA EEN: Captain Dabenes takes his leave after a salute to Captain Huyghens with 9 shots. He was thanked with an equal one. A sailor (Antonij de Nijs) died.
KAPITEIN DER INFANTERIE D. ROELOFS OVERL: Captain of infantry D. Roelofs died.
KAPITEIN DUIF ZEILT DOOR. VISSER OP ZIJD: Captain Duif sails on. Fisherman alongside who informed that many ships on the coasts of England had been lost in the storms from S to W. Asks the pilots to stay with them until they would be through the Channel with the wrecked rigging, named John Casswell.
KAPITEIN EN ENIGE OFFICIEREN AAN LAND. B: Captain and some officers ashore. Brought 21 empty water casks ashore.
KAPITEIN EN ENIGE OFFICIEREN GAAN AAN LA: Captain and some officers go ashore. Clean the ship.
KAPITEIN GING MET CHINEESE PRAIJBOOT NAA: Captain went with a Chinese prau boat to Macoa; the clerk omits 23 April, but I already did that when passing the date line. This day is 23 April in Greenwich.
KAPITEIN GING MET DOCTOR IN EEN SLOEP NA: Captain went with the doctor in a launch to the commandant, came back with the doctor and two surgeons.
KAPITEIN HUIJGHENS GAF HET SEIN OM ONZE: Captain Huijghens gave the signal to speak to our captains.
KAPITEIN J. T HOOFT, VAN DE RUIJTER, OVE: Captain J. t Hooft, of the Ruijter, died.
KAPITEIN LT POLKEIJN VAN SCHIP NASSAU OV: Captain-lieutenant Polkeijn of the ship Nassau died.
KAPITEIN LUITENANT GEESTERANUS GAAT NAAR: Captain-lieutenant Geesteranus goes to Lima to compliment Bolivar; the captain himself is still ill.
KAPITEIN OORTHUIJS (WASSENAAR) WERD VERZ: Captain Oorthuijs (Wassenaar) was asked to pass on his dead reckoning to the Utrecht; he did so. Reckoning of Wassenaar: 17: 31 94: 41 17: 31
KAPITEIN TER ZEE H.Z.A. GUINOSEAU IN DE: Captain at sea H.Z.A. Guinoseau died at the age of 44 years, 3 months and a few days.
KAPITEIN VAN BRAAM EN MAJOOR HAMELL, NAA: Captain Van Braam and Major Hamell went to the Wassenaar to have lunch there. On their return they have the reckoning of the Wassenaar: course: N7/8W. Miles: 32.5. Reckoned N lat: 19: 36'. Longitudes: 346: 28'. Observed N lat: 19: 35
KAPITEIN VAN DE POLLUX DACHT DAT HET OM: The captain of the Pollux thought it was a group of islands and wanted to call it the Pollux group, but later it turned out to be only a small island; then they decided to call it Dutch Island, because it was so low.
KAPITEIN VAN HET SCHIP DE AMERONGEN IS O: The captain of the ship Amerongen is unwell. Decide not to wait any longer for the other ships. Difference is too great: 5 miles per day.
KAPITEIN VAN RECHT DOOR ZEE KOMT AAN BOO: Captain Van Recht Door Zee comes aboard. The longitude of that ship was: 341°6'
KAPPEN 12 VAAM VAN 'T STOPTOUW VOOR WORS: Cut 12 fathoms of the stopper rope for sausages.
KAPTEIN HUIJGHENS NEEMT AFSCHEID MET UIT: Captain Huijghens takes his leave with exchange of flag and pennant and 9 salute shots.
KAPTEIN VAART NAAR DE ROTTERDAM 'OM DAAR: Captain sails to the Rotterdam to attend the justice of 6 sailors who were rebels, of whom 5 had to fall from the yard.
KARDOESEN UIT DE KRUITKAMER DOOR RATTEN: Cartridges from the powder room gnawed by rats.
KEERDEN 'T KRUIJD, EN BELEIJDEN DE WEKEL: Turned the powder and held the weekly ship's council. Among the sick found 8 invalids, mostly suffering from fevers.
KENAU HASSELAAR, DE KOTTER THE ROSE EN H: Kenau Hasselaar, the cutter The Rose and the transport ship separate themselves.
KEREN KRUIT EN ZWARTEN DE RAAS EN HET BL: Turning powder and blacking the yard and the blocks.
KIJKEN HOEVEEL GORT ER NOG IS. ALS ZIJ H: Checking how much barley is left. If they give the slaves a hundred cans per day, they still have provisions for 10 to 11 weeks, or for 7 weeks of barley and 7 weeks of beans and 7 weeks of [?].
KIMPEILING EN AZIMUTH BEVONDEN 24 GR. NW: Horizon bearing and azimuth found 24 degrees westerly variation; shifted the compass for that error.
KISTEN GEVISITEERD EN TUSSENDEKS GEROOKT: Chests inspected and smoked between decks.
KLAAR OM TE FLENSEN, HADDEN VIER VISSEN: Ready to flense, had four fish left over.
KLAART EVEN OP EN ZIEN HET EILAND ST. NI: Clears up briefly and see the island of St. Nicolaas and sail along it. Estimate in the evening after 9.00 that all the islands are passed.
KLAPPER EILAND WEST. KOMT TER REDE ANJER: Klapper Island west. Comes to the roads, anchor.
KLARE WOLKDRIJVENDE TOT BETROKKEN REGENA: Clear, cloud-drifting to overcast rainy sky.
Clearing rope and scraping port side.
KLAREN TOUW, VERS WATER AAN BOORD, HEER: Clearing rope, fresh water aboard, Mr. Fiscal comes alongside in a tent boat.
KLEIN FORTUIN KOMT OP DE LENGTE VAN 119°: Klein Fortuin comes at longitude 119°25', so that we found ourselves 25.75 miles further east since the last bearing of Punte Gale 1°43' off. Bearings of the high hill of Prince Island ESE W/S S. Klein Fortuijn NW 1/2 W, 1 mile.
KLEINE LANDVOGELTJES BIJ HET SCHIP: Small land birds near the ship.
KLEINE REGENBUIEN, WEERLICHT.ZIEN KWALLE: Small rain squalls, lightning. See jellyfish drifting. Prayer. Passing squalls.
KLEUR VAN 'T WATER WAS ZEER VERANDERD: Colour of the water was much changed.
KLEUR VH WATER BLIJFT DONKERGROEN: Colour of the water remains dark green.
KLIPGROENTE DRIJVEN. (ZIEN) EEN MENIGTE: Rock-vegetables drifting. (See) a multitude of large clumps of vegetables.
KLIPPEN VAN TRINIDAD BLIJKEN REDELIJK HO: Cliffs of Trinidad appear reasonably high. The easternmost seem the highest. The cliffs lie close together, about 0.25 miles.
KLOPT DE LENGTE? IN ORIGINEEL STAAN AANH: Is the longitude correct? In the original there are quotation marks under '44' of the N lat.
KOCHTEN PROVIAND VAN ENGELS SCHIP: Cooked provisions from an English ship.
KOERS BEWESTEN DE HEN MET DE KUIKENS EN: Course west of the Hen with the Chicks and the northern Ravallas. Salute with 9 cannon shots, hoist flag and pennant. Commissioners came aboard. Pass the Dapenberg at half past four. Still more exchanges of salutes. At half past 7 at anchor.
KOERS EN VERHEID IN TWEE ETMALEN: Course and distance in two days.
KOERS EN VERHEID IS DE GISSING VAN GOUST: Course and distance is the estimate from Goudstaart. Put the reckoning in the round chart. When night or dog watch (HW) is mentioned, it concerns the night and the dog watch of the following day; the journal days run from day watch to day watch.
KOERS EN VERHEID IS SEDERT HET PUNT VAN: Course and distance is since the point of the previous day's [?].
KOERS EN VERHEID NIET GEGEVEN I.V.M. WIN: Course and distance not given because of calm.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT 8 UUR IN DE MORG: Course and distance since 8 o'clock in the morning. In the afternoon see St. Eustatius, St. Christopher, St. Bartholomew, Nevis and Rodondo. Bearings of Nevis S point N 1/4 E. Bearings of Rodondo NE 1/4 E. Bearings of Montserrat N point E 3/4 N. Comes to 16° 44'N and 62° 35'W.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT DE LAATSTE LANDP: Course and distance since the last land bearing, meridian west of Lesard 5.25 miles. Here begins our reckoning.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT GISTERAVOND 6 UU: Course and distance since yesterday evening 6 o'clock.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT GISTERAVOND 8 UU: Course and distance since yesterday evening 8 o'clock.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT GISTERMIDDAG 1 U: Course and distance since yesterday afternoon 1 o'clock.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEDERT? UUR DEZE MORGEN: Course and distance since [?] o'clock this morning from Goudstaart. Our reckoning begins here at this longitude.
KOERS EN VERHEID SEEDERT GISTEREN NA DE: Course and distance since yesterday afternoon after the bearing on Goudstaart. Here the reckoning begins.
KOERS EN VERHEID SINDS 7 UUR GISTERAVOND: Course and distance since 7 o'clock last evening
KOERS EN VERHEID SINDS DE AVOND: Course and distance since the evening
KOERS EN VERHEID SINDS GISTERENAVOND MET: Course and distance since yesterday evening at sunset
KOERS EN VERHEID STAAT GENOTEERD ALS 21°: Course and distance is recorded as 21°6' east of south. I note this as Z21:06O
KOERS EN VERHEID TOT ZIJ LAND ZAGEN: Course and distance until they sighted land
KOERS EN VERHEID WORDT EERST GEGEVEN TOT: Course and distance is first given until 2:00 (at night): NNE 32.25 miles. Then from 12:00 (since 2:00): N 19 miles
Course and distance are unclear as regards the digits after the decimal point. There are 2 chronometer west longitudes: N 10=69 degrees 26 minutes 40 seconds and N 91=69 degrees 26 minutes 34 seconds. If there is another number after the seconds in the journal, I have always taken it as a digit after the decimal point, for example 14,5: the 14 of the seconds and the 5 after it as the decimal digit
KOERS EN VERHEID ZIJN ONDUIDELIJK, ER LI: Course and distance are unclear, it seems to say E 7.5 miles (from yesterday?)
KOERS EN VERHEID: IN EEN ETMAAL 19' N: Course and distance: in a day and night 19' N
KOERS IS ONDUIDELIJK. AFSTAND TOT MONA I: Course is unclear. Distance to Mona is unclear. Minutes of the true longitude obtained are unclear
KOERS IS RECHTWIJZEND: Course is true (as the compass points)
KOERS WERD AANGEGEVEN ALS RECHTWIJZEND: Course was given as true (as the compass points)
KOK EN ZIJN MAAT BEKENDE DIEFSTAL, DE KO: The cook and his mate, the theft is admitted; the cook did not admit it, not even after torture
KOK JOSEF FRANS VAN LISBON UIT DIENST GE: Cook Josef Frans from Lisbon discharged from service. Pieter Sijmonse appointed as cook in his place.
KOK, GUSTAVUS BRIKBINDER, VAN DESSAUW, O: Cook, Gustavus Brikbinder, from Dessau, died.
KOKEN GROBBEJAK VOOR 'T VOLK: Cooking coarse pea soup for the crew
KOKEN GROBBIJAK VOOR 'T VOLK: Cooking coarse pea soup for the crew
KOKSMAAT IN DE BOEIEN VOOR HET OVERBOORD: Cook's mate in irons for throwing the midday meal overboard
Cook's mate M. De Groot and temporary cook A. Koek under arrest for damaging the ship. The prisoners were punished in the forenoon watch and released from arrest.
KOKSMAAT PIETER DE PAARUN VAN OOSTERHOUT: Cook's mate Pieter de Paarun from Oosterhout
KOKSMAAT UIT DE BOEIEN: Cook's mate out of the irons
KOLONIALE SOLDAAT S. VAN BEMMEL OVERLEDE: Colonial soldier S. van Bemmel died.
KOMEN 2 ENGELS SCHEPEN TEGEN. ENKELE SCH: Meet 2 English ships. A few shots are fired back and forth
KOMEN BIJ T IJS, 17 GR. LANGTE 70:15 BRE: Come upon the ice, 17 degrees longitude 70:15 latitude (unclear what is meant by the position indication)
KOMEN BOVEN DE DROOGTES VAN ABROLHOS WAA: Arrive above the shoals of Abrolhos, for which thanks were given
KOMEN DE VOLGENDE DAG IN STRAAT SUNDA: Arrive in Sunda Strait the following day
KOMEN DE VOLGENDE DAG TEN ANKER OP DE RE: Arrive the following day at anchor in the roads of Paramaribo.
KOMEN EEN ENGELS SCHIP TEGEN DAT ENKELE: Meet an English ship that fires a few shots
KOMEN IN DE BOCHT VAN BANTAM TEN ANKER: Arrive at anchor in the bay of Bantam
KOMEN IN DE EW TEGEN HET IJS: Come upon the ice in the EW
Arrive in the NE trade winds.
KOMEN OP 26 SEPTEMBER TEN ANKER VOOR HEL: Arrive at anchor before Hellevoetsluis on 26 September
KOMEN OP 9 OKTOBER AAN OP DE REDE VAN HE: Arrive in the roads of Hellevoetsluis on 9 October.
KOMEN TEGEN DE VASTE KUST VAN HET IJS: Come up against the solid edge of the ice
KOMEN TWEE DAGEN ZONDER BESTEK, IN DE BU: Come two days without a position fix, in the neighbourhood of St. Thomas and Cape Lopez
KOMEN UIT HET KANAAL OP DE GRONDEN. SCHE: Coming out of the Channel into soundings. Ship's journal probably kept by a passenger, not so systematic. For example, no distance run is given either.
KOMEN VOOR HET IJS, LEIJD HEEL VAST: Come before the ice, lies quite fast
KOMEN VOOR HET IJS, MAKEN KLAAR OM TE GA: Come before the ice, make ready to go fishing, are Greenland [?]
KOMEN WEER BIJ DE SCHEPEN VAN RIEMS EN O: Come again to the ships of Riems and Oepkes. Position by Riems: 41° 19' N, 2° 22' E
KOMPAS OP OOST. KLOKSCHIP THEEWIJCK? VER: Compass at east. Clock ship Theewijck? Terrible southerly swell off the Cape
KOMT DE KLIP SALVAGES OTZ 9 MIJL. BEWEST: Come to the Salvages rock ENE 9 miles. West of Cape Lizard 129.5 miles
KOMT DE POSITIE OP 359°40' O.L EN 27°15': The position comes to 359°40' E.L. and 27°15' N.
KOMT VLGS DIEN DE LINIE OP 2º WL: Comes according to this the line at 2º W
KOMT VLGS DIEN W HULE BOEK IN DE KAART D: Comes according to this W Hule Boek in the chart of the W Islands by Owen E 3/4 S. 7.5 miles. Heijzand NNE 360 miles in the N Atlantic Ocean chart by Purdey
KON NIETS ANDERS ZIJN DAN DE KUST VAN TE: Could be nothing other than the coast of Terra dos Fumos, although then in the NW and N they seem to have to see the coast of Pauoaca do Inhagna or the land south of the bay of Rio de Lagoa… which according to the Dutch … and plane chart sticks out some 8 miles east of the first-mentioned coast
KONDE DOOR DE NABIJHEID VAN DE SON GEEN: Could not obtain a true latitude because of the nearness of the sun
KONDE NOORDEN ZEIJLE MET HOLWATER: Could sail north with hollow water
KONDEN 'T LAND NIET GOED ONDERSCHEIDEN: Could not make out the land well
KONDEN 'T LAND NIET VERKENNEN OMDAT WE E: Could not recognise the land because we were too far from it
KONDEN DE TWEE VOORUIT GEZEILDE SCHEPEN: Could no longer see the two ships sailed ahead.
KONDEN DOOR DE DIJNZIGE LUCHT GEEN BREED: Could not obtain a latitude because of the hazy sky.
KONDEN DOOR DE DIKKE LUCHT GEEN BREEDTE: Could not obtain a latitude because of the thick sky.
KONDEN DOOR DE HARDE WIND GEEN VUUR AANM: Could not light a fire because of the strong wind, and because of the heavy work could not cook either
KONDEN DOOR DE HOGE OZO EN O TIGT HET SC: Because of the high ESE and E swell could not keep the ship close to the wind
KONDEN DOOR DE VORST GEEN HAVEN BEREIKEN: Because of the frost could not reach any harbour.
KONDEN DOOR REGEN EN DIKKE LUCHT TOTAAL: Because of rain and thick sky could get no observation at all.
KONDEN GEEN BESCHEID VAN 'T LAND ZIEN: Could not make out the land
KONDEN GEEN BESCHEID VAN HET LAND ZIEN: Could not make out the land
KONDEN GEEN BESCHEID ZIEN. VOLGENS DE TE: Could not make anything out. According to the text we were 22 minutes further east than we estimated, according to the margin line we were 22 minutes further west than we estimated. Ship comes to anchor a little later before Cape Mesurado and then sails along the African coast to Elmina, while engaged in the slave trade
KONDEN GEEN BREEDTE BEKOMEN WEGENS DE DI: Could not obtain a latitude because of the thick sky.
KONDEN GEEN BREEDTE NEMEN OMDAT ZE 'TE N: Could not take a latitude because they were 'too near under the sun'.
KONDEN GEEN GOEDE BREEDTE NEMEN DOOR DE: Could not take a good latitude because of the nearness of the sun.
KONDEN GEEN KENNIS KRIJGEN: Could get no sight of land
KONDEN GEEN KENNIS KRIJGEN DOOR DE DIKKE: Could get no sight of land because of the thick sky
KONDEN GEEN KENNIS KRIJGEN VAN 'T LAND D: Could get no sight of the land because of the thick sky
KONDEN GEEN KENNIS VAN 'T LAND KRIJGEN: Could get no sight of the land
KONDEN GEEN LAND ZIEN DOOR DE NEVEL. DEN: Could not see land because of the fog. Think the land lies to the N. Set double lookouts.
Could not see land because of thick sky.
KONDEN HET COMMERCIE SCHEEPIE NIET MEER: Could no longer see the little ship Commercie.
KONDEN HET LAND NIET ZIEN DOOR DE DONKER: Could not see the land because of the dark sky, later it cleared. At anchor in 16 feet, mud.
KONDEN HET VOLK NIET MEER DAN EEN HALVE: Could not give the crew more than half a round bucket of water a day.
KONDEN NIET KOKEN VANWEGEN RUWE ZEE: Could not cook because of rough sea
KONDEN NIET STOKEN NOCH KOKEN': Could neither stoke the fire nor cook
Could not steer for lack of wind.
KONDEN NIET STUREN. POMPTEN 50 DUIM WATE: Could not steer. Pumped 50 inches of bilge water in a day and night.
KONDEN NIETS ALS ENIGE TROMPETTEN ONTWAR: Could make out nothing but a few trumpets [?]
KONDEN NIETS ONTWAREN. LAGEN MET SONS SE: Could make out nothing. Lay with sun [?] set to the SW.
KONDEN NIETS VAN HET EERDERGENOEMDE SCHI: Could see nothing of the previously mentioned ship at sunrise.
KONDEN PRINS WILLEM DE VIJFDE NIET MEER: Could no longer see Prins Willem de Vijfde
KONDEN SCHIPPER CORNELIS EVERTS NIET ZIE: Could not see Skipper Cornelis Everts, wait for him.
KONDEN VAN STENG NIETS ONTDEKKEN: Could discover nothing from the topmast
KONDEN VAN STING NIETS ZIEN DOOR DIKKE L: Could see nothing from the topmast [?] because of the thick sky. Sounded at night, but no bottom.
KONDEN VAN TOP GEEN LAND ZIEN: Could not see land from the top
KONING VAN GOAH, MET VIJFTIG MAN GEVOLG,: King of Goah, with a following of fifty men, visits the ship
KONING VAN SIAK AAN BOORD BIJ COMMANDANT: King of Siak aboard with the commander
KONSTABEL MAJOOR C. HURNUS OVERLBOORD GE: Master gunner C. Hurnus knocked overboard and died.
Gunner's mate J. Jansen in irons.
KOOME TEGEN DEN AVOND BIJ HET HOLLANDZE: Come towards evening to the Dutch convoy, the sea is full of French privateers, they are as many as 160 sail
KORPORAAL HOBEIN IN DE BOEIEN IVM HET NI: Corporal Hobein in irons for not keeping his watch
KORPORAAL JOHAN DANIEL SEEDERMAN VAN STO: Corporal Johan Daniel Seedermann from Stokholm, and soldier Christiaan Schaper from Gootlijn.
KORT VOOR DE MIDDAG PASSEERDEN DE MERIDI: Shortly before noon passed the meridian of Cape Horn at 59 deg. 24'.
KORTEN OP NA ONRUST (SCHIP KOMT VOOR DE: Shorten sail towards Onrust (ship comes under the shore)
KPT GEEFT ZB AAN, ZAL NB MOETEN ZIJN: Captain gives S latitude, must be N
KPT WILDE VOOR ANKER OP ANZUANA, DIT LUK: Captain wanted to anchor at Anzuana, this did not work because of current and headwind, so went on to Ponne Caijl
Infant born in confinement on 26 November died.
KREEGEN EEN SWARE ORCAAN' ZODAT DE PUNTE: Got a heavy hurricane so that the yardarm tips dipped in the water and the captain said: 'If God gives no way out our ship cannot hold out half a quarter longer'
KREGEN 'S MIDDAGS DE LOOTS K. VOS AAN BO: In the afternoon got the pilot K. Vos aboard.
KREGEN 2 GEBETERDE ZIEKEN UIT HET HOSPIT: Received 2 recovered sick men from the hospital
KREGEN 2 MAN VAN HET SCHIP UTRECHT OM BI: Received 2 men from the ship Utrecht to serve with us. 4 petty officers proposed: boatswain Juriaan Corneleesen, mate Willem Wouter (both from the ship Utrecht), boatswain's mate Henderik Ringer, quartermaster Jan Elins
KREGEN BIJ AFWISSELING ELEKTRICE VUURBOL: Alternately saw electric fireballs on the tops of the masts.
KREGEN EEN BRAA? HARING VAN EEN BUIJS GE: Received a [?] herring from a buyze, brought by mate Jan Willemse Groen, and cod from mate Jacob Sevenhusen.
KREGEN EEN KOEBEEST, HOENDERS EN GROENTE: Received a head of cattle, chickens and vegetables on board.
KREGEN EEN LEGGER WATER EN EEN VAT SPEK: Received a leaguer of water and a cask of bacon.
KREGEN EEN LOODS VAN PORTLAND AAN BOORD: Took a pilot from Portland on board.
KREGEN EEN OFFICIER GENAAMD BOUWMAN MET: Received an officer named Bouwman on board with his chest.
KREGEN EEN STUURMAN EN TWEE MATROZEN AAN: Received a mate and two sailors on board.
KREGEN EEN VREEMDE MATROOS AAN BOORD: Received a foreign sailor on board.
KREGEN ENIGE ZIEKEN ONDER DE EQUIPANGIE: Had several sick among the crew with diarrhea and dysentery.
KREGEN ENKELE VISSERS AAN BOORD WAARVAN: Had a few fishermen on board, from whom fresh fish and other fresh produce were bought for the crew. Also a European came on board who told us that the governor of Ceylon had died.
KREGEN ENKELE VOGELS ROND HET SCHIP: Had a few birds around the ship.
KREGEN NU DE WIND VAN HET OOSTEN EN KWAM: Now got the wind from the east and arrived at Batavia on the 22nd of July.
KREGEN OM HALF 10 DE KASTELEN ST. JAGO,: At half past 9 the castles of St. Jago, St. George d'Elmina and the English fort Cape Coast came into view. In a depth of 30 fathoms, sandy bottom with shells.
KREGEN RIJST VAN PASSEREND SCHIP: Received rice from a passing ship.
KREGEN TWEE LOODSEN AAN BOORD EN LATEN O: Took two pilots on board and let ourselves drift further inward. Moored again with five anchors, 2 of the ship's own and 3 of the Company's.
KREGEN UITSCHOT VAN WIND VAN HET ZTO TOT: Got a shift of wind from the south-southeast to west-northwest and back to west, with heavy rain and thunder.
KREGEN VAN DE OOST-INDISCHE VLOOT DE LEN: Got the longitude of 3°52' from the East Indian fleet.
KREGEN VEEL WATER BIJ DE POMPEN, POMPEN: Took in a lot of water at the pumps; pumped continuously with the chain pumps. Presume it must be strongly [?] put about.
KREGEN VEEL WATER BINNEN DOOR DE LIJFNAD: Took in a lot of water through the seams and through a leak in the bow on the starboard side. Found it strongly [?] put about. Decided to put about with full sails.
Shipped a lot of water over the side.
KREGEN VEEL ZIEKEN MET HOGE KOORTSEN. VI: Had many sick with high fevers. Caught a fish for the first time.
Several seas came over onto the deck.
KREGEN WATER EN BRANDHOUT VAN DE KOOPVAA: Received water and firewood from the merchant ships.
Received wine and lemons from the commodore.
KRIJGEN 'S NACHTS VEEL WATER OVER WAARDO: At night shipped a lot of water, so that the crew is constantly wet.
KRIJGEN EEN UITSCHIETER VAN'T OOSTEN MET: Got a squall from the east with a gust of 19. Afterwards with clear sky veering around towards WSW [?] from the south.
KRIJGEN GEBREK AAN WATER EN BRANDHOUT: Running short of water and firewood.
KRIJGEN ORDERS OM OP LAND TE JAGEN: Received orders to hunt on land.
KRIJGEN SOMS ZEEWATER OVER.WEST MERIDIAA: Sometimes shipped sea water. West meridian [?] 31, 5 miles. Changed to the west 15.5 miles. Gained 47 miles.
KRIJGEN WATER AAN BOORD. KRIJGEN 7 ZIEKE: Taking in water on board. Took 7 sick men from the hospital on board. Taking in provisions.
KRIJGSRAAD AAN BOORD BIJ KAPITEIN HUIJGH: Council of war on board with Captain Huijghens (with the captain, 2 commanders, the commander of the soldiers and the aforementioned boy). Towards noon the prisoner came back on board.
KRIJGSRAAD BIJ DE COMMANDANT. BRANDHOUT: Council of war with the commandant. Firewood on board. Chief mate Jochum Turitz died.
KRIJGSRAAD IN VERBAND MET DE MUITERIJ (2: Council of war regarding the mutiny (21 soldiers arrested). The three main conspirators are sentenced to death.
KRIJGSRAAD KOMT BIJEEN OM TE ONDERZOEKEN: Council of war convenes to investigate what had become of the grenadier.
KRIJGSRAAD OP VERZOEK VAN DE KOOPVAARDIJ: Council of war at the request of the merchant skippers to postpone the sailing day by another 14 days. New date set for 7 January 1761. They will then be ready and can then benefit from the convoy.
KRIJGSRAAD OVER DE 2 MATROZEN DIE ZONDER: Council of war about the 2 sailors who stayed ashore without permission.
KRIJGSRAAD OVER DE MATROOS VAN SCHIPPER: Council of war about the sailor of skipper David de Jong.
KRIJGSRAAD OVER MATROOS VAN SCHIPPER ROE: Council of war about the sailor of skipper Roelof Zuijderstroom.
KRIJGSRAAD VANWEGE HET HOGE AANTAL ZIEKE: Council of war because of the high number of sick (30) and several dead (8) from scurvy.
KRIJGSRAAD VERHOORT BOTTELIER: Council of war interrogates the steward.
KROM IN DE BOEIEN BOTTELIERSMAAT MOOK WG: Krom in irons, the steward's mate Mook, for carelessness.
KROM IN DE BOEIEN KWARTIERMEESTER WEHING: Krom in irons, quartermaster Wehinger, for sleeping on watch.
KROM IN DE BOEIEN VOOR 24 UUR MET WAARNE: Krom in irons for 24 hours with duty continuing, the cook's mate J. Sliep, for carelessly making the tea water badly.
KROM IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS NIET OPVOLGEN V: Krom in irons for not following given orders, the sick-bay attendant Gericken.
KROM IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS VECHTERIJ DE FU: Krom in irons for fighting, the fusilier Schut.
KRUISPEILING.BEVOND HET BESTEK SEDERT 7: Cross-bearing. Found the reckoning since 7 October 1790 (Lizard) to be 5° 53' too far west.
KRUISTEN AF EN TOE HET VUUR OM OP VOORME: Tacked now and then, keeping the fire lit, to wait for the aforementioned bark.
KRUISTEN OVER EN WEER BIJ HET LAND: Tacked back and forth near the land.
KUNNEN DOOR DIKKE LUCHT (HET LAND NIET H: Could not make out the land because of thick weather. Recognised the land at 7.45 a.m., depth 30 fathoms, distance from the land 1.5 miles. Saw the flag of P. Gale flying in the ESE 1/2 E. At 10.45 a.m. had the [?] north of the fort [?] flagstaff bearing W/S E. 12.00: pilot comes out, depths 29-27-25-23 fathoms. Took a bearing of the flagstaff of P. Gale ENE 2/3 E, 0.25 mile, depth 20, 15 fathoms. Afternoon: pilots come on board.
KUNNEN GEEN BEVONDEN BREEDTE KRIJGEN OMD: Cannot get an observed latitude because they are close under the sun.
KUNNEN GEEN LAND VAN STING ZIEN, OOK GEE: Cannot see the land from the topmast, nor any ships.
KUNNEN IN DE MORGEN HET EILAND NIET ZIEN: Cannot see the island in the morning because of clouds.
KUNNEN LUCHTPOMPEN NIET MEER GEBRUIKEN T: Can no longer use the air pumps in the between-decks. The sick get too cold on the half deck, go to the between-decks, where it is stuffy.
KUNNEN MAAR 10 SCHEPEN ZIEN DOOR DE DIKK: Can only see 10 ships because of the thick, misty weather.
KUNNEN MEEST NIET STUREN. 17.30 UUR: ZIE: Mostly unable to steer. 17.30 hours: sight Palma.
KUNNEN PALMA NIET MEER ZIEN DOOR DE WOLK: Can no longer see Palma because of the clouds.
Cannot see any land from the topmast.
KUNNEN VAN STENG NIETS ZIEN DOOR DIKKE L: Cannot see anything from the topmast because of thick weather.
KUST VAN AFRIKA TUSSEN NW EN NOTN. DIEPT: Coast of Africa between NW and NNW. Depth 120 fathoms, coarse sand.
KWAM OVERBOORD TE VALLEN TE VERONGELUKKE: Fell overboard and was lost, the sailor Jan Fredrick Kemph of Laxen - Gotha.
Fell overboard and was lost, the sailor Jan Pieter Koopmann of Amsterdam, leaving no estate. Could not be rescued because of the strong speed of the ship in a high sea.
KWAMEN 'S MIDDAGS OM 4 UUR OP DE REDE VA: Came to anchor at 4 o'clock in the afternoon in the roads of Hellevoetsluis.
KWAMEN 'S MORGENS? UUR TEN ANKER TER RED: Came to anchor at [?] o'clock in the morning in the roads of St. Jago. 48 inches of water pumped in the day and night. Tried with a kedge anchor to warp the ship closer under the shore, but the anchor cable broke and so we lost our kedge anchor and two cables. Afterwards put out another kedge. Sent a sloop with an officer to the shore.
KWAMEN (VOOR HET EERST) TEGEN HET JONGE: Came up against the young ice (for the first time).
KWAMEN 22 JULI 'S MIDDAGS OM 14.00 UUR B: Arrived safely on 22 July at 14.00 hours at anchor at Hellevoetsluis.
KWAMEN 23 MAART OM HALF VIJF 'S MIDDAGS: Arrived on 23 March at half past four in the afternoon inside Hellevoetsluis. The voyage from Batavia to Rotterdam took 127 days.
KWAMEN 6 MEI 1839 AAN OP DE REDE VAN HEL: Arrived on 6 May 1839 in the roads of Hellevoetsluis. End of journal.
KWAMEN DE 20STE TEN ANKER VOOR PARAMARIB: Came to anchor off Paramaribo on the 20th.
KWAMEN DE 27E 'S NAMIDDAGS OM 1 UUR OP D: Came to anchor on the 27th at 1 o'clock in the afternoon in the roads of Batavia in 5.5 fathoms.
KWAMEN DES S'MIDDAGS, BEHOUDEN OP DE REE: Arrived safely in the afternoon in the roads of Batavia, at anchor in 6 fathoms of water.
Met a group of people in canoes. Tried to talk with them using Cook's word list, but were not understood. Traded old rags for coconuts.
KWAMEN OP 10 FEBRUARI TEN ANKER IN DE RI: Came to anchor on 10 February in the river Suriname. Came to anchor on 12 February in the roads of Paramaribo.
KWAMEN OP 16 SEPTEMBER TEN ANKER OP DE R: Came to anchor on 16 September in the roads of Hellevoetsluis.
KWAMEN OP 2 NOVEMBER TEN ANKER OP DE RED: Came to anchor on 2 November in the roads of Rammekens.
KWAMEN OP 20 JULI BEHOUDEN TE TEXEL TEN: Arrived safely at anchor at Texel on 20 July.
KWAMEN OP 4 JANUARI 1835 AAN OP DE REDE: Arrived on 4 January 1835 in the roads of Batavia.
KWAMEN OP 6 OKTOBER OP DE REDE VAN BATAV: Came to anchor on 6 October in the roads of Batavia.
KWAMEN TEN 10 URE OP DE REEDE VAN HELLEV: Arrived at 10 o'clock in the roads of Hellevoetsluis.
KWAMEN TER REDE ASCENSION EN OM 7 UUR WE: Came to the roads of Ascension and at 7 o'clock were under sail again.
KWAMEN VERSCHEIJDENE VAN 'T MEEDE GEGEEV: Several of the livestock given along with us died. Because of cold etc. found: half a leaguer of water to be ½ [?].
KWAMEN WEEGENS KOUDE EN SLEGT WEER VERSC: Because of cold and bad weather several pigs died.
KWARTIERMEESTER ENGEL LAZARIJNNE VAN 'T: Quartermaster Engel Lazarijnne from the island of Corsica becomes boatswain and sailor Pieter Marpee from Sluis in Flanders becomes quartermaster. A few cases of scurvy.
KWARTIERMEESTER GIJSBERTS IN DE BOEIEN W: Quartermaster Gijsberts in irons for brutality against first-class midshipman J. Osti.
KWARTIERMEESTER GROENMAN IN DE BOEIEN WE: Quartermaster Groenman in irons for brutality.
KWARTIERMEESTER J. W. SUKEMEIJER IN DE B: Quartermaster J. W. Sukemeijer in irons for dereliction of duty.
KWARTIERMEESTER OOS PIEDES OVERLEDEN (39: Quartermaster Oos Piedes died (39). Sailor Teyke Jacobs died (40).
KWARTIERMEESTER PHILIP DE VELDUIJSE WORD: Quartermaster Philip de Velduijse becomes 4th mate. Gunner's mate Dirk Kraame becomes quartermaster. Jan Bosman becomes gunner's mate.
KWARTIERMEESTER PIETER ZANSZE VAN LEENS,: Quartermaster Pieter Zansze of Leens fell overboard and was lost.
KWARTIERMEESTER VAN VEEN VOOR 24 UUR IN: Quartermaster Van Veen in irons for 24 hours with duty continuing, for carelessness.
KWARTIERS VOLK EXTRA OORLAM: Quarters crew [given] an extra ration of grog.
L'AIGLE SHOAL IS EEN DROOGTE LIGGEND IN: L'Aigle Shoal is a shoal lying in the middle of the fairway, between the Falkland Islands and the coast of Patagonia.
L'ENTRÉE DE LA BAIE D'AVATSCHA RESTAIT A: The entrance of the Bay of Avatscha bore N50E, and the volcano N5E.
L'ENTRÉE DU PORT RESTAIT AU S1/4 SW: The entrance of the port bore S1/4 SW.
LA BRISA HA CONTINUADO FRESCA TODA LA SI: The breeze has continued fresh throughout the day's run.
LA BRISA HA ESTADO FRESQUITA E IGUAL, EL: The breeze has been fairly fresh and steady, the weather overcast until the morning when it cleared, and although at the beginning of the night there were some light squalls.
LA BRISA HA ESTADO FRESQUITA TDAS 24 HOR: The breeze has been fairly fresh all 24 hours and especially from 9 in the morning, during which there have been some brief squalls of little consequence.
LA BRISA HA SIDO FRESQUITA DESDE MEDIANO: The breeze has been fairly fresh since midnight, weather always clear and sea smooth.
LA CALMA (...) A LAS 5 1/2 DE LA TARDE (: The calm (...) at 5 1/2 in the afternoon (...) gave us a light squall of some wind from the east-southeast (...) from then on the wind was settled (...) Night fell with the sky overcast and the horizons squally, but nevertheless the night was very clear and the wind came in with it. At dawn the sky was clear and the horizons with scattered clouds and banks of cloud, the sea smooth and the wind moderate.
LA CALMA DURÓ HASTA LAS 7 1/2 DE LA NOCH: The calm lasted until 7 1/2 at night, when with a light breeze from the west (...). The wind shifted weakly toward the third quarter, but the sky and horizons always stayed closed with thick mist as when it was calm. At dawn the weather was the same, and the wind lighter, but with the sun it freshened and the drizzle dispersed at the same time, so that it became a beautiful day.
LA CORREDERA TIENE DE NUDO A NUDO 46 PIE: The log line has 46 English feet from knot to knot, the mile being divided into eight fathoms. Sand glass of 30 seconds. First point of departure on the French chart of 1853, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4th ed. 66. Corrections with the meridian. It gives miles, but nothing more.
LA CORRIENTE VENIA DEL N. A LAS 20:00 FO: The current was coming from the north. At 20:00 they anchor 3 leagues from the coast.
LA COSTA MÁS PRÓXIMA, DIST. 6 LEGUAS \"L: The nearest coast, distance 6 leagues. "Latitude by the land: 36° 36'"
LA EMBARCACION MUY DISTANTE. MEDICION Y: The vessel very distant. Measurement and data of noon or of the day's run, many times the descriptions are from dawn.
LA EMBARCACIÓN SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 1: The vessel sets sail at 10 and three quarters in the morning. Although the journal begins on 2 February, it is not until the 16th that the vessel sets sail. Reference is taken from observed latitude and longitude of arrival.
LA ESCUADRA ALGO DISPERSA POR LA NOCHE Y: The squadron somewhat dispersed during the night and united at dawn.
LA ESCUADRA INCORPORADA A EXCEPCIÓN DE L: The squadron joined together except for the frigate Magdalena.
LA ESCUADRA NO SE VE: The squadron is not in sight.
LA ESCUADRA UNIDA MENOS LA MONICA: The squadron united except the Monica.
LA FRAGATA FAMA \"VIO UN PATO DESGARITAD: The frigate Fama "saw a stunned duck, all of which (this also refers to the storm of the previous day) indicates nearness to land where the charts show nothing"
LA FRAGATA FAMA, QUE EN OBEDECIMIENTO DE: The frigate Fama, which in obedience to a signal inspected a small American frigate, was told by it that it had left one of the ports of the colonies in mid-October for whale fishing in this sound, in which up to 20 ships of its own nation were currently counted engaged in the same business. The sounding was 60 fathoms, brown sand. They make a moderate catch of a kind of cod which, although somewhat bland, was a great treat to them
LA FRAGATA PORTUGUESA NOS DIO LA NOTICIA: The Portuguese frigate gave us the news that on the (blank) of the current month an English convoy of 40 vessels escorted by three warships, coming from Gibraltar, had entered Lisbon. And that the day before yesterday two English privateers had stopped it and plundered several things from it.
LA LATITUD Y LA LONGITUD ES LA QUE APARE: The latitude and longitude are as they appear in the log, although it makes a large jump that is corrected the next day (the team of interns corrected it). Data relating to the whole day
LA LONGITUD NO SE APRECIA. RUMBO Y DIREC: The longitude cannot be determined. Course and wind direction at noon / wind force the nearest to noon
LA LUNA ESTABA CON UN CERCO CRECIDO: The moon had a wide halo
LA MAR ESTABA BLANCA COMO UNA SABANA POR: The sea was white as a sheet from the force of the wind
LA MAR GRUESA DEL SO Y NO (...) ANOCHECI: Heavy sea from the southwest and north (...). Evening came overcast, fresh wind with a good deal of sea from it and from the southwest. (...) Dawn broke fully closed in with fine rain falling, the wind fresh and the sea heavy.
LA MAR GRUESA. A LAS 12 1/2 (...) UNA TU: Heavy sea. At 12 1/2 (...) a squall (...). Evening came with sky and horizons showing thick and clear streaky cloud, heavy sea from the southwest and light wind. At 8 3/4 (...) calm.
LA MAR MANTUVO ALGUN COLOR DE FONDO, TUV: The sea kept some color of the bottom, we had a good deal of choppy current and a ripple with so much noise that, in case it was a shock on some shoal, soundings were taken, but no bottom was found, with 120 fathoms of line
LA MAR POCA DEL VTO, Y LA BRISA FRESQUIT: Little sea from the wind, and the breeze freshening a little (...) moderating (...) has freshened more (...) the rest of the time has been clear.
LA MARÉE N'ÉTAIT POINT SENSIBLE, A CE MO: The tide was not noticeable at this anchorage.
LA MAYOR PARTE DE LAS CALMAS (...) ALGUN: Mostly calms (...) some squalls (...) the wind continuing to freshen (...) the sea continuing very heavy from the southwest.
LA MAYOR PARTE DE LOS DESCRIPTORES SON D: Most of the descriptors are from the evening
LA OBSERVACION NO ES CON TODA SATISFACCI: The observation is not entirely satisfactory
LA OBSERVACION NO ES DEL TODO SATISFACTO: The observation is not entirely satisfactory
LA OBSERVACION NO FUE DE LAS MEJORES: The observation was not one of the best
LA OBSERVACIÓN NO HA SIDO DE MI SATISFAC: The observation has not been to my satisfaction, so I do not correct it
LA OTRA FRAGATA DE GUERRA INGLESA, SE LL: The other English warship was called "La Chana" and its captain was Mr. Medos (?)
LA PARTE FINAL DE LA SINGLADURA ESTÁ ILE: The final part of the day's run is illegible because of the faint ink of the writing.
LA POSICION ANOTADA CORRESPONDE A LA DE: The recorded position corresponds to that of Drake Island
LA PUNTA MÁS N DE LA ISLA TERCERA AL SO: The northernmost point of Isla Tercera bears southwest by south, distance 44 1/2 leagues. The island of Cuervo bears west-southwest 3 degrees west, distance 72 1/2 leagues.
LA SONDE A RAPPORTÉ DE 45 À 24 BRASSES,: The sounding reported from 45 to 24 fathoms, muddy bottom.
LA SONDE RAPPORTAIT LE FOND DE 80 À 45 B: The sounding reported the bottom from 80 to 45 fathoms, running along the coast of Ségalien Island. Anchored at 1 1/2 leagues from land, in 42 fathoms, muddy bottom (14:30).
LA TARDE Y LA NOCHE EN LAS MISMAS CONDIC: Afternoon and night in the same conditions
LA TENACIDAD DE LOS TIEMPOS CONTRARIOS P: The persistence of contrary weather for 20 days obliges Malaspina to order that the Atrevida set course for Acapulco and San Blas, recommending the survey of Cocos Island, while the Descubierta heads for Guatemala to land the high officials it carries as passengers. The observation does not earn much confidence from him. Journal of the commander of the Atrevida from when it separates from the Descubierta until several ships meet at Acapulco
LA VARIACIÓN OBSERVADA EN LA BAHÍA ES DE: The variation observed in the bay is 20° west. "Journal of the navigation, movements and operations of the squadron under my command, made up of the ships listed in the attached roll of the line of battle, from its departure from the port of Cádiz on 20 July 1790" (25 ships of the line, 3 frigates and 2 brigantines.)
LA VENTOLINA QUE NOS ENTRÓ DESPUÉS DE LA: The light breeze that came on after the calm (...) gradually freshened with some sea during the night (...) at dawn finding itself quite fresh (...) the horizons and skies have been of very bad appearance, continually squally and with gusts with drizzle.
LA VENTOLINA SIGUIÓ CUASI CALMA HASTA LA: The light breeze continued almost calm until 8 (...).
LAAG VOORLAND, ZOALS BIJ KAAP AGULHAS: Low foreland, like at Cape Agulhas
LAARSDEN DE MATROOS JAN VAN SANTEN: The sailor Jan van Santen was loading
Allow a quarter point NW here.
LAAT INFORMATIE OVER BOTTELIER, PIETER D: Keep information about the purser, Pieter de Graaff.
LAAT NA GIS 3/4 VAN EEN STREEK NW REKENE: Reckon 3/4 of a point NW after the estimate.
LAAT OFFICIEREN TOEZIEN OP DE VERDELING: Have the officers supervise the distribution of hammocks and chests. Have it cleaned. Smoking in between decks.
Reckon no error in the compass bearing from here.
LAATSTE 3 ETMALEN ZETTE DE STROOM ONS OM: The last 3 days the current set us to the south
LAATSTE DEEL TEN 7 1/2 V.M. SCHOOT DE WI: Last part, at 7 1/2 a.m., the wind shifted with a squall to the southwest
LAATSTE KWARTIER MAAN. ZAGEN DE GANSE DA: Last quarter moon. Did not see the sun the whole day.
LABBER BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Light topgallant breeze and topgallant breeze
LABBER BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN GEMENE BRAMZEI: Light topgallant breeze and ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MINDERE KOELTE: Light topgallant breeze and lesser breeze
LABBER BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN ONGESTADIGE KO: Light topgallant breeze and unsteady breeze
LABBER EN EEN GEMENE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and an ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER EN FLAUWE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and weak topgallant breeze
LABBER EN FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and fresh topgallant breeze
LABBER EN GEM BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER EN GEMEENE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER EN GEMENE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER EN GEMENE MARSZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and ordinary topsail breeze
LABBER EN GEMENE TOT FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOE: Light breeze and ordinary to fresh topgallant breeze
LABBER EN ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and unsteady topgallant breeze
LABBER EN SLAPPE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze and slack topgallant breeze
LABBER EN STIL TOT FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELT: Light breeze and calm to fresh topgallant breeze
LABBER EN STIL TOT GEMENE BRAMZEILSKOELT: Light breeze and calm to ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER STIL TOT GEM BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze, calm to ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER TOT FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze to fresh topgallant breeze
LABBER TOT GEM BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze to ordinary topgallant breeze
LABBER TOT GEMENE BRAMZEILSKOELTE: Light breeze to ordinary topgallant breeze

The weather and wind were the same at dawn, but the wind shifted during the night to astern.
LAS 5 1/2 DE LA MAÑANA SE VIO SARGAZÓ Y: At 5 1/2 in the morning sargassum was seen, and at 12 a white bird was seen that looked like a tropicbird.

LAS CIRCUNSTANCIAS POCO FAVORABLES EN QU: The unfavorable circumstances in which we found ourselves (says Captain Cook) and the darkness of the nights in this season of the year, now calming, discouraged me entirely from putting into practice my resolution to cross the Antarctic Circle again.
LAS CORRIENTES LE HAN TIRADO DESDE MONTE: The currents have carried them from Montecristo to the mouth of Cayo Confites. Descriptors of noon or of the day's run.
LAS CORRIENTES ME HAN TIRADO EN LA CANAL: The currents have carried me into the Old Channel 12 miles to the west, and on leaving that channel they took me 15 miles north toward the Bahama channel. Descriptors of noon or of the day's run. Could not leave earlier because of the calms and strong winds.
LAS FRAGATAS SABOYANAS QUE ESCOLTABAN LO: The Savoyard frigates that were escorting the Spanish warships sighted were going from Málaga to England, with wine, figs and raisins.
LAS GRUESAS MARES OCASIONABAN GRANDES SA: The heavy seas caused great jolts or slattings in the sails, and in one of them the fore yard almost gave way at the cross. They repair it.
LAS MARES MUY GRUESAS DEL SO Y O (...) L: Very heavy seas from the SW and W (...) The rolling was continuous, strong and violent (...) Night fell with the horizons and sky stormy, sea and wind as in the afternoon, but from midnight both wind and sea eased, and at dawn the weather was milder.
LAS NEVADAS ERAN TERRIBLES, SIGUEN ECHAN: The snowfalls were terrible; they keep throwing the snow overboard but cannot prevent it from piling up on the deck (more than a hand's breadth), hindering the maneuvers. The sea was also very high.
