LEVAN A LAS 00:00 Y NAVEGAN AL E 5º S PA: They weigh anchor at 00:00 and sail E 5° S to round the Cabo de San Antonio and the bank at its point safely
LEVAN A LAS 12:30 PARA IR EN DEMANDA DEL: They weigh anchor at 12:30 to head for the port of the city, where they afterwards anchor. He describes the coast: Isla Raza, the channel, Castillo de la Lapa, Isla das Cobras or Culebras, etc.
LEVAN A LAS 5:00. A LAS 10:30 FONDEAN DE: They weigh anchor at 5:00. At 10:30 they anchor again and set out to explore. The tide began to rise at 15:00 and rises and falls a great deal. They are persuaded that the so-called Rio Gallegos is not a river but an inlet of the sea. From the afternoon they head for the Rio de Santa Cruz. At 19:30 they anchor when the wind drops.
LEVAN A LAS 5:00. A LAS 8:00 ESTAN E-O C: They weigh anchor at 5:00. At 8:00 they are east-west with the Isla de los Reyes. He describes it. At 15:30 the wind calmed and they anchor, weigh anchor at 17:30 and anchor again at 19:00. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 5:00. FONDEAN A LAS 14:00 AL: They weigh anchor at 5:00. They anchor at 14:00 when the wind drops, 3 leagues from land. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 5:00. VUELVEN SOBRE LA COSTA: They weigh anchor at 5:00. They turn back toward the coast to reconnoitre a large inlet on the north side of Cabo San Jorge; he describes the coast and the peak they call Santo Tomas. They anchor at 20:00 when the wind drops, 4 leagues from land, but at 21:00 the SW wind began to blow and they weigh anchor. The wind increases in strength and "carried with it a lot of dust"; "they run that night in a violent storm". The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 5:30. A LAS 18:00 CALMO EL V: They weigh anchor at 5:30. At 18:00 the wind calmed and they anchor. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 5:30. LOS DATOS SUELEN SER D: They weigh anchor at 5:30. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 6:00. A MEDIODIA MARCAN EL C: They weigh anchor at 6:00. At noon they sight Cabo de Santa Helena to the NNW at 3 leagues. He describes it. At 19:00 the SE wind began to blow. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 6:30. LOS DATOS SUELEN SER D: They weigh anchor at 6:30. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN A LAS 7:00 Y NAVEGAN HACIA TIERRA: They weigh anchor at 7:00 and sail toward land to survey a bay. At 12:30 they anchor at the entrance of the bay and go ashore to explore the barren coast. They return on board at nightfall. They name the bay Bahia de San Gregorio and the cape on the north side Cabo de Dos Bahias. He describes the Bahia de San Gregorio. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
They weigh anchor at 7:00 and sail toward land. They anchor at 12:30 at the entrance of the bay to explore it; they called it San Gregorio. They describe the Bahia de San Gregorio and the Cabo de Matas (location, characteristics for navigation).
LEVAN A LAS 8:00. VAN A POCA DISTANCIA D: They weigh anchor at 8:00. They go a short distance from land. At 15:00, becalmed and with contrary currents, they anchor. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
LEVAN ANCLAS DEL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO. R: They weigh anchor from the port of Montevideo. Wind references from half past 8 in the morning.
LEVAN DE LA CORUÑA A LAS 02:00; HAY DOS: They set sail from La Coruña at 02:00; there are two earlier attempts to leave La Coruña, on 30-11-1765 and 3-12-1765, with weather notes. He stays 4 days in Pto. Rico, and does not leave until 19-Jan for Havana.
LEZEN DE KRIJGSARTIKELEN VOOR EN DAARNA: Reading the articles of war first and then the sailing orders, containing the sentences passed against the crew of this ship who in the month of July 1835 had been guilty of mutiny and refusal of duty.
LICHTEN 'S MORGENS HET ANKER EN WAREN OM: Weighed anchor in the morning and were outside the bay at about 10 o'clock.
LICHTEN ANKER EN GAAN ONDER ZEI. DIEPTEN: Weigh anchor and set sail. Depths 8 to 45 fathoms, [?] bottom.
LICHTEN ANKER OP 2 DECEMBER 1756 EN VARE: Weigh anchor on 2 December 1756 and sail toward the Sunda Strait. Only on 29 December do they sail out of the Sunda Strait.
LICHTEN ANKER SAMEN MET DE LIEFDE. DIEPT: Weigh anchor together with the Liefde. Depths 26 to 43 fathoms.
Weigh anchor, course for St. Eustatius.
LICHTEN ANKER, RICHTING WNW. TEN ANKER O: Weigh anchor, heading WNW. At anchor in 12 fathoms, black sand bottom.
LICHTEN ANKER, TEN ANKER EN ANKER WEER G: Weigh anchor, anchor, and weigh anchor again
LICHTEN ANKER, VERTREK VAN JAVA NAAR AMB: Weigh anchor, departure from Java for Ambon.
LICHTEN ANKER, WEER TEN ANKER. 'S AVONDS: Weigh anchor, at anchor again. In the evening little Combuijs SSW, Duifjes Eiland [?].
LICHTEN ANKER. PASSEREN DIEPTEN VAN 22 T: Weigh anchor. Pass depths of 22 to 30 fathoms. Anchor again because of current and wind. Position relative to land: Hoek van Bantam NNE by W/S N. Toppershoedje WNW by W/S W. Brabants Hoedje SSE by W/S S, estimated distance from Geertruid Eiland 0.75 mile.
LICHTEN ANKER. WEER TEN ANKER. WEER ONDE: Weigh anchor. At anchor again. Under sail again. Sunset: the westernmost of the Wapens van Hoorn NNE 1/2 N, the Grote Combuijs E by S, the Menscheneter ESE 1/2 S. Come to anchor again.
LICHTEN ANKERS NET ALS ONZE MAAT.. STERK: Weigh anchors just like our consort. Strong, SW and SSW
LICHTEN ANKERS, KOMEN WEER TEN ANKER. ZE: Weigh anchors, come to anchor again. Sail a short distance. In the evening at anchor again. Sunset bearings: the Grote Combuijs E 1/2 S, the Mensenete SE by E, the westernmost of the islands the Wapens van Hoorn ENE, the Hoek van Pontang SW.
LICHTEN HET ANKER EN GAAN ONDER ZEIL, TE: Weigh anchor and set sail; by 5 o'clock they lost sight of land.
LICHTEN HET ANKER EN ONDER ZEIL. DIEPTEN: Weigh anchor and under sail. Depths 9.5 to 11 fathoms. Depths 10 fathoms. Course and distance since weighing anchor.
Weigh anchor at 7 o'clock in the morning. Dead reckoning since weighing anchor. Sail along the coast of Suriname, no good observations any more. Anchored on 5 February before the Suriname river.
LICHTEN HET ANKER, KOMEN IVM STILTE IN D: Weigh anchor, come to anchor in the [?] because of a calm. Storm in the evening.
LICHTEN HET ANKER. 'S AVONDS MET ONZE MA: Weigh anchor. In the evening at anchor with our consort. Sunset: middle of P. Baby ENE W/S E and the Hoek van Pontang SE and Groot Mady SSW W/S W.
LICHTEN HET ANKER. DIEPTEN VAN 35 TOT 50: Weigh anchor. Depths of 35 to 50 fathoms. Evening: at anchor again. Sunset: the high hill of Krakatou WSW. The hill of Sleijpzee NNW 1/2 W.
LICHTEN ONZE BEIDE ANKERS. DE WASSENAAR: Weigh both our anchors. The Wassenaar and the Goes get outside.
LICHTMATROOS NEAU, DIE AL ONEINDIGE MALE: Ordinary seaman Neau, who had been punished countless times for indifference, extreme slovenliness, and untidiness in his clothes, let his recently issued Scotch cap blow off the ship through carelessness. He was punished with the cudgels
LICHTMATROOS SPORRY, WEGENS VERREGAANDE: Ordinary seaman Sporry, for extreme carelessness with a light, punished with 24 strokes
LIEPEN MET KLEIN ZEIL OM DE SURSEANCE IN: Ran under small sail to await the suspension of arms. Could see her briefly from the topmast
LIEPEN MET KLEINZEIL OM HET SCHIP NOORDB: Ran under small sail to await the ship Noordbeveland.
LIET ALLE SLAVEN UIT DE BOEIEN SLAAN: Had all the slaves' irons struck off
LIET DE DIEF JAN VAN KERKWIJK NA STELEN: Had the thief Jan van Kerkwijk punished with 50 strokes after stealing provisions, Gerret Vengu and Michiel Meijer 20 strokes each
LIET DE SLAVEN WASEN EN SMEEREN EN LIET: Had the slaves washed and anointed and had the slave quarters fumigated
LIET HET LIJK GISTEREN OVERLEDEN, OVERBO: Had the corpse of the man who died yesterday put overboard, with his belongings and bedding, at the request of the doctor. Had the cable locker cleaned out and an auction held of the estate of the 2 aforementioned sailors.
LIET HET VOLK HUNNEN PLUNJE WASSEN: Had the crew wash their belongings
LIET IN DE YZER FLUITEN DEN ONDER MEESTE: Had the under-master Jacob Willem Hofmans and the gunner's mate Pieter Klus put in irons because of a quarrel with each other
LIET KLEINE SLOEP MET DE EERSTE OFFICIER: Had the small sloop with the first officer observe the course of the current, and found its course SSW one mile per watch
LIET OP RAPPORT VD CHIRURGIJN DUMONT HET: On the report of the surgeon Dumont, had the bedding (3 mattresses, 3 large and 1 small pillow and 4 cotton blankets) brought on deck; the bedding is so worn from use that, if the doctor does not need it, I will have it thrown overboard
LIETEN (EEN AANTAL) MANNEN AAN LAND GAAN: Let (a number of) men go ashore. Fetched 6 recovered sick men from the hospital.
LIETEN 11 MAN VOOR PLEZIER AAN LAND GAAN: Let 11 men go ashore for pleasure.
LIETEN 18 DUIM WATER DOOR DE KRAAN: Let 18 inches of water through the tap
LIETEN 9 MAN VOOR PLEZIER AAN LAND GAAN: Let 9 men go ashore for pleasure
LIETEN DE ARTIKULBRIEF LESEN. GOOIJDEN V: Had the articles of war read. Cast the lead several times but found no bottom with 150 fathoms
LIETEN DE EQUIPAGE AANKLEDEN, HIELDEN PA: Had the crew dress, held parade and hoisted flag and pennant with the usual ceremony. Because of the offences mentioned on 2 May and in view of earlier bad and improper conduct as shown by the punishment record, demoted the 2nd smith Beugeling to 3rd class sailor and afterwards punished him with strokes. 2 casks of hard bread rejected by a commission appointed for that purpose. Hunter Makking died
LIETEN DE EQUIPAGE HUN PLUNJES WASSEN, H: Had the crew wash their belongings, held theory lessons on the guns
LIETEN DE EQUIPAGE KLEDEN. HIELDEN ER IN: Had the crew dress. Held inspection over them and they read out their offences.
LIETEN DE KOMPASSEN VERLEGGEN VAN 2° NOO: Had the compasses adjusted from 2° northeasterly variation to 0°.
LIETEN DE MANSCHAPPEN HUN HANGMATTEN EN: Had the men scrub their hammocks and knapsacks
LIETEN DE SLAVEN KOMBUIS MAKEN: Had the slaves make a galley
LIETEN DEN JONGEN HUYBREGT BOUWENS VAN D: Had the boy Huybregt Bouwens of Domburg earn the monthly pay of the deceased
LIETEN EQUIPAGE LAPPEN EN NAAIEN: Had the crew mend and sew
LIETEN KISTEN EN KOOIEN OPHALEN. MAAKTEN: Had chests and bunks brought up. Cleaned between decks. Fumigated with gunpowder and juniper berries and sprinkled with vinegar.
LIETEN OM 14.00 UUR HET ANKER VOOR PARAM: Let the anchor fall before Paramaribo at 14.00 hours. Mr and Mrs Poppelman left the ship.
LIETEN POETSEN EN AANKLEDEN. HIELDEN BAK: Had things cleaned and had them dress. Held inspection by messes
LIETEN POETSEN EN AANKLEDEN. HIELDEN INS: Had things cleaned and had them dress. Held inspection and divine service
LIETEN SOLDATEN EN ROEIERS VUREN: Had the soldiers and rowers fire
LIETEN WATER DOOR DE KRAAN: Had water run through the crane
LIEUTENANT HIERONIMUS VAN DOKKUM OVERLED: Lieutenant Hieronimus van Dokkum died. On account of his good qualities he is greatly mourned by many of us.
LIGGEN IN HET MIDDEN VAN DE HARINGVLOOT: Lying in the middle of the herring fleet
LIGGEN TE WACHTEN TOT ZE DE HAVEN VAN GU: Lying waiting until they can sail into the harbour of Guayaquil
LIGGING VAN 'T EILAND TRISTAN DA CUNHA I: The position of the island of Tristan da Cunha is, according to the French chart, 37 degrees 15 minutes south latitude and 16 degrees longitude west of Paris; according to the Spanish, 37 degrees 5 minutes south latitude and 14 degrees 42 minutes longitude west of Paris; and according to the English, 37 degrees 7 minutes south latitude and 13 degrees 57 minutes west of Paris.
LIGT BUIJIGE EN RONDWERKENDE LUCHT, VERV: Squally sky with shifting winds, then clear and cloudy.
LIGTEN ANKER EN ZEILDEN NAAR ZEE: Weighed anchor and sailed to sea
LIGTEN ANKER, DEDEN WEL 25 SLAGEN: Weighed anchor, made as many as 25 tacks
Weighed the anchor and got under sail.
LIGTEN ONS ANKER EN GINGEN NAAR ZEE. (GE: Weighed our anchor and went to sea. (From here on use the journal of Commander Maarten Mooij, SMA, Cat. KII, 303)
LIJDEN DE KOMPASSEN 13 GR. NOORD WESTERI: The compasses showed 13 degrees of north-west variation
LIJK VAN KAPITEIN TAALMAN WORDT OVERBOOR: Body of Captain Taalman is committed overboard
LIJK VAN OVERLEDENE OVERBOORD. ORDINAIRE: Body of the deceased overboard. Ordinary ritual with shots and salutes.
LIJST MET BESTEKKEN VAN DE VERSCHILLENDE: List of the positions of the various ships of the convoy: Revolutie N lat 35°3', longitude 1°54'. Tromp N lat 34°58', longitude 2°37'. De Brave N lat 34°54', longitude 2°. Bellona N lat 35°3', longitude 4°28'. Sirene N lat 34°50', longitude 1°28. Havik N lat 35°5', longitude 2°52'. Vrouwe Maria N lat 35°1', longitude 2°45' and Dortrecht N lat 34°58', longitude 3°17'
LIJST VAN LENGTES VAN ENKELE ANDERE SCHE: List of longitudes of some other ships of the convoy: De Havik 3°10'. Revolutie 3°7'. Bellona 4°57'. De Vrouwe Maria 4°4'. Dort 3°54' and Tromp 2°57'
LLEGA A LA CORUÑA. VIENTO, MAR Y DESCRIP: Arrives at La Coruña. Wind, sea and descriptors from dawn, the rest from midday
LLEGA A LA LONGITUD DE SAN MARTIN: Arrives at the longitude of San Martin
LLEGA EL NAVIO SAN PEDRO. DICE QUE LAS A: The ship San Pedro arrives. It says that the changes of the barometer and thermometer were recorded constantly every 4 hours by the officers of the watch. Speaks of the usefulness of these instruments for navigation, especially in high latitudes: "I will note in passing that from latitude 44º S the mercury fell to 27 inches and 6 lines of the French measure, and in this state it always indicated good weather with moderate winds, it being an excess of fairness the few times it passed that limit. In gales the fall was always great compared with what is experienced in our climates, and the most considerable, of 26 inches, 4 lines and 8 tenths, was noticed on 18 February at 57º 50' south latitude. This instrument, built by Dollond, predicted exactly the hurricanes or winds of extraordinary force, always with the necessary advance to be able to take precautions and avoid mishaps. Never less than two hours passed between the warning and the onset of the weather, and in the strong gale we suffered on 14 February at latitude 56º 30' south it indicated it eight hours before, even though at the time the northeast wind was blowing, which in these waters heavily charges the atmosphere; and finally I can assure that in the many years this instrument has accompanied me it was never so useful to me as in the present campaign." Sails for Talcahuano, from where the diary is written. Accompanies a beautiful route chart in which some notes of dates, positions, etc. are indicated.
Arrival at Cádiz. End of the diary.
LLEGADA A CÁDIZ. RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL V: Arrival at Cádiz. Course and wind direction at midday / rest of the references, those nearest to midday
LLEGADA A CÁDIZ. RUMBO Y VIENTO - MEDIOD: Arrival at Cádiz. Course and wind - midday / sea - nightfall
LLEGADA AL PUERTO DE CÁDIZ: Arrival at the port of Cádiz
Arrival at the port of destination.
LLEGADA AL PUERTO DE MATANZAS, DONDE HAC: Arrival at the port of Matanzas, where they make a stop. The ship stops at Matanzas, where it stays from 23-5 until 21-6.
LLEGÓ AL SURGIDERO DE AMPANAM EN EL ESTR: Reached the anchorage of Ampanam in the Strait of Lombock, where it stayed until the morning of the 29th
LO MAS DEL TIEMPO LO PASA CAPEANDO: Spends most of the time hove to
LO MISMO QUE LOS DEMÁS DÍAS: The same as the other days
LO MÁS N DE LA ISLA TERCERA AL S 1/4 SO: The northernmost point of the island of Terceira bears south 1/4 southwest, distance 36 leagues. The island of Cuervo bears west-southwest 4° south, distance 54 1/2 leagues.
LO MÁS N DE LA ISLA TERCERA AL SO 8º S D: The northernmost point of the island of Terceira bears southwest 8° south, distance 46 leagues, and the easternmost point of Cuervo bears west-southwest 2° west, distance 75 leagues.
LO MÁS N DE LA ISLA TERCERA, AL SSO 9º O: The northernmost point of the island of Terceira bears south-southwest 9° west, distance 41 leagues. The island of Cuervo bears west-southwest 3° west, distance 67 leagues
LOBOS DE MALVINAS FIJAMENTE: Sea lions of the Malvinas, constantly
Sounded at night but found no bottom.
LODEN 35 VADEM, GROVE GRAUWE ZANDGROND M: Sounding 35 fathoms, coarse grey sandy bottom with red stones, very sharp bottom. At noon the high hill of Krakatau bore east-northeast a little east, and the east corner of Prinseneiland southeast by east 1/2 east. At sunset the east corner of Prinseneiland bore southeast 1/2 east, Krakatau east-northeast 1/2 east, and Kijzers Island north by west
LODEN 50-40 VAAM. KOMEN IN DE HW WEER TE: Sounding 50-40 fathoms. Anchored again at high water.
LODEN 65, 72 EN 50 VADEM GROF ZAND MET S: Sounding 65, 72 and 50 fathoms, coarse sand with shells..
Sounding 90 fathoms of water at 12 o'clock.
LODEN ALLE 2 GLAZEN DOCH KREGEN GEEN GRO: Sounded every 2 glasses but found no bottom.. Midday: and took bearings of the east corner of Prinseneiland southeast by east. At sunset the high hill of Krakatau bore east-northeast, the east corner of Prinseneiland southeast, and the middle of Kijzers Island north by west 1/2 west. At midnight the high hill of Krakatau bore northeast 1/2 east.
LODEN DE DIEPTE VAN 90 VAAM WAZIGE GROND: Sounding the depth of 90 fathoms, soft muddy bottom.
LODEN DIEPTE 40 EN 36 VADEM WATER, ROTSA: Sounding depth 40 and 36 fathoms of water, rocky and sharp sand. Accordingly Cape Rozo bears south by east 3/4 east, 41 miles
LODEN DIEPTE 75 VAAM WIT GRAUW ZAND MET: Sounding depth 75 fathoms, white-grey sand with pieces of shell.
LODEN DIEPTE VAN 54 VAAM.. IN DE AVOND P: Sounding depth of 54 fathoms.. In the evening took bearings of the middle of Fulo at northeast 1/2 east, 5.5 to 6 miles.
LODEN DIEPTE VAN 60 VAAM.. OOST MERIDIAA: Sounding depth of 60 fathoms.. East meridian 800 miles. Changed 40.25 miles to the east. Obtained 840.25 miles.
LODEN DIEPTE VAN 62 TOT 63 VADEM WITTE Z: Sounding depth of 62 to 63 fathoms, white sandy bottom with red specks and little blue shells with needles. Think they are close to the Sorlings..
LODEN DIEPTEN VAN 30, 20 EN 12 VADEM WIT: Sounding depths of 30, 20 and 12 fathoms, white ooze and sandy bottom.
LODEN DOCH KREGEN MET 90 VADEM GEEN GRON: Sounded but with 90 fathoms found no bottom. At night unsteady breeze with thunder, lightning and continuous downpours.
Sounded and had a depth of 60 fathoms..
LODEN EN KREGEN GROND MET 45 VADEM GRAUW: Sounded and found bottom at 45 fathoms, grey sand with mud. Then sounded every 4 glasses and had depths of 38, 37, 36 and 35 fathoms, the same bottom.
LODEN GEEN GROND MET 200 VAAM. STERK WEE: Sounding, no bottom with 200 fathoms. Strong lightning from the northeast to northwest..
LODEN GEEN GROND.. REKENEN VAN HIER 1 3/: Sounding, no bottom.. Reckon from here 1 3/4 points northwest.
LODEN GROND OP 85 TOT 90 VAAM. GISSEN DE: Sounding, bottom at 85 to 90 fathoms. Guess the Sorlings, but no direction (east?) or distance.
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND MET 110 VAAM, ZOUD: Sounded but no bottom with 110 fathoms; according to the reckoning they should be on the shore of the coast of Guinana, between Rio Cawi (Rio Kaw?) and Tolabamare
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND, ZETTEN DUBBELE UI: Sounding but no bottom, set double lookouts..
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND. HADDEN VERANDERIN: Sounding but no bottom. Had a change of water, (think?) they are approaching the coast.
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND. VERWACHTEN ILE DE: Sounding but no bottom. Expected to see Ile de Sal.
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND.. DENKEN DAT HET H: Sounding but no bottom.. Think that the high land they sight at sunrise is the beginning of the Wijn Coops mountains. At sunset the corner of the Wijn Coops mountains bore west-northwest and the easternmost east-northeast; guess to be 2 miles from the nearest shore.
LODEN MAAR GEEN GROND.. KOERS EN VERHEID: Sounding but no bottom.. Course and distance at noon was since yesterday afternoon (after) the reckoning had been corrected.
LODEN MET 115 VAAM LIJN GEEN GROND: Sounding with 115 fathoms of line, no bottom
Sounding with 115 fathoms of line, no bottom.
LODEN MET 120 VADEM GEEN GROND. ZIEN MET: Sounding with 120 fathoms, no bottom. At sunrise see the Sumatran shore from east-northeast to north-northwest. At sunset took bearings of the highest part of Kijzers Island northeast by north, the flat corner of Sumatra, the easternmost we could see of it north-northeast 1/3 east, and the [?] of the highland of Lamproy (?) at northeast 1/2 north of us. Guessed to be 4 miles from the nearest land
LODEN MET 130 VAAM MAAR GEEN GROND: Sounding with 130 fathoms but no bottom
LODEN MET 150 VADEM MAAR GEEN GROND. IN: Sounding with 150 fathoms but no bottom. In PV had depths of 55 to 60 fathoms, fine sand. Distance unclear in original: 29. Set the reckoning 45 miles west [?] on the same latitude. N lat 49° 23', longitude 8° 20'.
LODEN MET 160 VAAM EN GEEN GROND. MERIDI: Sounding with 160 fathoms and no bottom. Meridian east of the island of Floris 214.75 miles. Since 24-08 still also gives the commander's reckoning.
LODEN MET 53 VAAM WIT ZAND MET ZWARTE SP: Sounding with 53 fathoms, white sand with black specks
LODEN MET 60 VAAM ZAND MET GEBROKEN SCHE: Sounding with 60 fathoms, sand with broken shells
LODEN MET 73 VADEM ZANDGROND MET STEENTJ: Sounding with 73 fathoms, sandy bottom with little stones.
LODEN MET GEHELE LIJN GEEN GROND: Sounding with the whole line, no bottom
LODEN OP 70 VADEM FIJN ZAND MET GEBROKEN: Sounding at 70 fathoms, fine sand with broken shells
LODEN OP 80 VADEM DIEPTE, GROVE ZANDGRON: Sounding at 80 fathoms depth, coarse sandy bottom. Meridian east of the island of Floris 241 miles.
LODEN OP DIEPTE VAN 72 VAAM FIJN WIT ZAN: Sounding at a depth of 72 fathoms, fine white sand with black specks and a few shells.
LODEN WIT ZAND MET ZWARTE STIPPELTJES OP: Sounding, white sand with black specks at 45 fathoms of water.. West meridian 574.25 miles. Changed 19.25 miles west. Obtained 603.5 miles. According to this reckoning one should be close to the shore. They see no land. Move the reckoning and the round chart 30 miles west.
Sounding, but no bottom at 160 fathoms.
LONG. CORR. PAR DES OBSERV. DE DISTANCES: Longitude corrected by observations of distances
LONG: 48' AL O DEL MERIDIANO DE SAN BLAS: Longitude: 48' west of the meridian of San Blas
LONGITUD CORREGIDA 162º 31'. ENVIAN EL B: Corrected longitude 162º 31'. They send the boat ashore, but seeing no inhabitants that day they decide to anchor in 22 fathoms in an inlet they had surveyed. Strong current to the east. The Castries loses 3 cables in a gust of wind.
LONGITUD DE PARIS 33º 8'. MEDICION Y DAT: Longitude of Paris 33º 8'. Measurement and data from noon or from the day's run; many times the figures are from dawn.
LONGITUD DEL CRONÓMETRO. LA OTRA PARECE: Longitude by chronometer. The other seems to be 4´E (almost illegible because of the ink).
Longitude by chronometer. The other seems to be 3º 7´.
LONGITUD RESPECTO A SAN BERNARDINO. \"SE: Longitude relative to San Bernardino. "A terrible storm of thunder, lightning and bolts was experienced, with an unbearable smell of sulphur, a great rarity at such a latitude according to all the experienced hands."
LONGITUD SEGÚN EL MERIDIANO DE PARÍS: Longitude according to the meridian of Paris.
LONGITUD TOMADA RESPECTO AL MERIDIANO DE: Longitude taken relative to the meridian of Cádiz, 320º 45' 15'' relative to that of Tenerife. This is done every day, though I will only include the Cádiz figure. Data generally from dawn and the bearing from noon.
LONGITUDE ET LATITUDE S. DE LILE DAGELET: Longitude and latitude south of the island of Dagelet
LOODDE 35 VADEM GROFZAND MET STEENTJES: Sounding 35 fathoms, coarse sand with small stones
LOODDE OP DE H.WACHT 55 VADEM GROFZAND S: Sounding on the [?] watch 55 fathoms, coarse sand, small stones with small shells
LOODDEN 43 VADEM ZAND SCHULPEN EN STEENT: Soundings 43 fathoms, sand, shell fragments and small stones
LOODDEN 51 EN 52 VADEM. TEN 11 U. V.M. 9: Soundings 51 and 52 fathoms. At 11 in the forenoon 90 fathoms, no ground. That is …(..) watch or no ground.
LOODDEN 75 VADEM ZWARTE SPIKKELS. (S' AV: Soundings 75 fathoms, black specks. (In the evening): soundings 65 fathoms, grey sand, broken shells
LOODDEN OP DE DIEPTEN VAN 70 TOT 80 VAAM: Soundings at depths of 70 to 80 fathoms, extra fine white muddy sand with black and bran-like specks, a few very small stones
LOODEN IN DE EW MET 120 VADEM LIJN, DOG: Sounded in the EW with a 120 fathom line, yet found no ground. The compasses (in the EW) changed from 22° 30' to 20° 00' north westerly variation; in the morning at sunrise could make out nothing of the topmast.
LOODEN MET 85 VAAM, MAAR KREGEN GEEN GRO: Sounded with 85 fathoms, but found no ground
LOODS HENDRIK VAN EIJK AAN BOORD. ZIEN D: Pilot Hendrik van Eijk on board. See the French coast
LOPEN TUSSEN TENERIFE EN GRAND CANARIA D: Pass between Tenerife and Grand Canaria. 18.00 hours: Punte de Nago, northeast corner of Tenerife: NW 1/2 N 1.5 miles
LOS CHUBASCOS Y FUGADAS SIGUIERON A MENU: The showers and squalls often continued (...) at dawn the day clearer; we experienced a mild temperature, warm air and some sea.
LOS CIELOS Y HORIZ. HAN SEGUIDO HERMOSOS: The skies and horizons have continued beautiful.
LOS DATOS SUELEN SER DEL AMANECER Y LA O: The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
LOS ENFERMOS, YA POCOS, VAN MEJOR PERO E: The sick, now few, are improving, but the fish do not come as much.
LOS MISMOS PAJAROS DE AYER MENOS LOS CAR: The same birds as yesterday except the carneros [?]. Overcast sky, horizons with cloud bank and thick cloud streaks. At 13:15 one shower falls. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
LOS PROBLEMAS SIGUEN Y SON INNUMERABLES: The problems continue and are innumerable.
LOS RABIJUNCOS HASTA HOY POR LA MAÑANA S: The tropicbirds have been seen near the ship up to this morning.
LOSSEN WATERVATEN EN BRENGEN DIE NAAR HE: Unload water casks and bring them to the island Cuiper (!). VOC ship the Bovenkerkerpolder comes alongside. Make ready to unload into her.
LT RAUWS IN ARREST OVER DISPUTS MET DEN: Lieutenant Rauws under arrest over disputes with the commander
LT TISHAUSER VAN SCHONER NR2 OMGEBRACHT: Lieutenant Tishauser of schooner no. 2 killed by pirates
LUCAS GROEN VAN CRIMPEN PLOTSELING OVERL: Lucas Groen of Crimpen suddenly died
LUCHTDRUKMETING IS VOOR 2 DAGEN: Barometer reading is from 2 days ago
LUCHTEN DAGELIJKS MET HET KOELZEI. VINGE: Aired daily with the cooling sail. Caught some water for the cattle. Had phosphorescence in the water.
LUCHTEN DAGELIJKS MET HET KOELZEIL. MAAK: Aired daily with the cooling sail. Cleaned the between-decks. Smoked with gunpowder and vinegar. Held a ship's council because of the sick: 8 incapacitated men suffering from fever and 2 from scurvy. Turned the gunpowder. The sailmaker named Pieter Roosenhout was put in irons for rowdiness and drunkenness.
LUCHTEN HET LEDEREN GOED EN DE ROKZAKJES: Aired the leather goods and the coat bags of the crew
LUCHTEN MET HET KOELZEIL. HIELDEN SCHEEP: Aired with the cooling sail. Held ship's prayers
LUEGO QUE FONDEAMOS EN ALICANTE EL COMAN: As soon as we anchored at Alicante, the commander of the brig Jasson presented to the commander of this vessel a statement for him to forward to H.M., in which he set out the insubordination and poor discipline that reigned on his ship for lack of punishments; putting a man to the arra [?] was said to be an anti-constitutional act, and an officer of the watch had been called servile because he ordered a delinquent secured on it (...)
LUITENANT 1E KLAS J.J. LEBLEIS OVERBOORD: First-class lieutenant J.J. Lebleis fell overboard. "Turned about, and fished him up again, nearly half drowned."
LUITENANT BEIJERINK BEGRAVEN, LUITENANT: Lieutenant Beijerink buried, Lieutenant HPN 't Hooft receives the Willems Order, on 4 December all the crew left the Cadmus, Veerman departs for his family in Amsterdam, also receives the Willems Order on 3/7/1820
LUITENANT DE BRUIN (WEER) IN ARREST WGNS: Lieutenant De Bruin again under arrest for brutalities
LUITENANT F 3 JOHAN HENDRIK POMPE, MATRO: Lieutenant F 3 Johan Hendrik Pompe, sailor F 102 Jacobus Fredrik Dafil died
LUITENANT HEND. ANTH. RIJSTERBORCH IN AR: Lieutenant Hend. Anth. Rijsterborch under arrest, was denied the captain's table, had to eat ship's rations.
LUITENANT J. HARMEL UIT ARREST OP HOOP V: Lieutenant J. Harmel released from arrest in hope of reform
LUITENANT MEYBURGH GEARRESTEERD (IN ZIJN: Lieutenant Meyburgh arrested (in his cabin on ship's rations) after contradicting the commander, after the latter had told him that the main-top lantern was not burning during the lieutenant's watch.
LUITENANT TER ZEE 2E KLAS M. H. JANSEN I: Second-class lieutenant at sea M. H. Jansen under arrest for neglect of duty. Colonial fusilier L. van Druten died.
LUITENANT TITUS EN MATROOSMAAT IN SCHEEP: Lieutenant Titus and a sailor's mate confined to the ship under arrest
LUITENANT TITUS OVERLEDEN. ER WORDT EEN: Lieutenant Titus died. A coffin is being made for him.
LUITENANT VAN SON EN ONDERGETEKENDE IN A: Lieutenant Van Son and the undersigned under arrest until ...?
LUKT NIET OM BOVEN HET EILAND ST JAGO HE: Does not manage to pass above the island St Jago, cannot sail close to the wind because of the sails, nor below it because of the too strong westerly current, wanted [?] to Porto Prajo. Decided to go to the island del Feugo.
M.B.T. KOERS EN VERHEID: GEZEILD TOT 12: M.B.T. Course and [?]: sailed until 12 o'clock (after the [?] there is also a Z and something unclear). Chronometers proved to show 8 minutes too far west. Without changing the assumed rate, I include that in the next reckoning.
M.B.T. RIVIER DE MAROWIJNE: RICHTING EN: M.B.T. River Marowijne: direction and distance according to the chart of Vos, 1845
MAAKT SCHETS VAN HET EILAND: Makes a sketch of the island
MAAKTE VOLGENS GEWOONTE DAGELIJKS SCHOON: As usual cleaned the ship daily and held inspection of the baggage
MAAKTEN BIJ HET NADEREN VAN DE SPAANSE B: On approaching the Spanish brig made everything ready for defence. Took out the old powder and loaded anew (with live rounds)
MAAKTEN DE POMPEN SCHOON. LEK IN DE RIJS: Cleaned the pumps. Leak in the rice room.
MAAKTEN KRACHT VAN ZEIL.VERANDERDE MERID: Crowded on sail. Changed meridian to W 18 3/4
MAAKTEN SCHOON SCHIP, LUCHTEN DAGELIJKS: Cleaned the ship, aired daily with the cooling sail.
MAAKTEN SCHOON TUSSEN DECKS EN ROOKTEN M: Cleaned between decks and smoked with gunpowder and sprinkled with vinegar
MAAKTEN SCHOON TUSSENDEKS. GAVEN VERVERS: Cleaned between decks. Gave fresh food of sheep and onions in the soup
MAAKTEN SCHOON TUSSENDEKS. GAVEN ZUURKOO: Cleaned between decks. Gave sauerkraut to the men
MAAKTEN SCHOON TUSSENDEKS.BEVONDEN EEN L: Cleaned between decks. Found a large cask to be 10 inches [?] of water. See some [?] floating
MAAKTEN ZIEKENGRENS AAN BAKBOORD: Made the sick berth on the port side
MAANECLIPS TUSSEN 21:19 EN 23:30, MET TO: Lunar eclipse between 21:19 and 23:30, with total eclipse at 22:13
Lunar eclipse, but not visible here.
MADELINE RIF: 'DIT RIF HEEFT ZIJNEN NAAM: Madeline Reef: 'This reef got its name from an English brig, Capt.: Hamilton, which struck it on 5 April 1834 and then sank; the crew arrived by boat at Porte Praije.'
MAKEN EQUIPAGE BEKEND MET DE OVERPLAATSI: Inform the crew of the transfer of Lieutenant G. vd Velden. Entry of A. W. de Ruyter punished with being put in irons, bent double
MAKEN HET HANDGEWEER SCHOON, VISITEREN D: Clean the small arms, inspect the guns, check the boatswain's gear.
MAKEN HET ZIEKENVERBLIJF SCHOON. OVERLED: Clean the sick quarters. Soldier Gerrit van Assenberg van Erp died.
Clean with gunpowder and vinegar and …..
Clean the ship with the fire pump.
MAKEN SCHOON SCHIP ONDER EN BOVEN: Clean the ship below and above
MAKEN SCHOON SCHIP, KRIJGEN VICTUALIE, T: Clean the ship, receive provisions, rope, water and fresh food on board
Clean the ship, smoke between decks.
MAKEN SCHOON SCHIP. 6 ZIEKEN NAAR HET HO: Clean the ship. 6 sick to the hospital. Provisions on board.
MAKEN SCHOON SCHP. ROOKTEN EN SPRENGELDE: Clean the ship. Smoked and sprinkled
MAKEN SCHOON TUSSENDEKS. STELLEN DUBBELE: Cleaning the between decks. Set double lookouts during the night.
MAKEN SCHOON, ROKEN MET WIEROOK EN JENEV: Cleaning, fumigating with incense and juniper berries.
MAKEN SCHOON. HET BROEIDE STERK TUSSENDE: Cleaning. It was very stuffy between decks.
MAKEN VERGELIJKEN TUSSEN RONDE EN PLATTE: Comparing the round chart with the flat chart.
MAL CARIZ (...) SE MANTUVIERON LOS CIELO: Bad look (...) The skies and horizons stayed closed, the weather squally with lulls in the wind.
MAL CARIZ(...) ANOCHEC. HORIZ. DEL SO AL: Bad look (...) Night fell. Horizons from the southwest to the northwest squally and of bad look, with a heavy sea from the southwest and west, the skies clear. The night turned out to look better, for with the moon high everything cleared and the horizons became thinner, and so dawn broke.
MALAGUESCHEN GEZIEN EN OOK VEEL STRONKEN: Malaguesen seen and also many [?]. Birds noted were, like jan-van-genten, according to their shape some grey and others white. Black wings.
MALLEVIETEN EN ANDERE VOGELS BIJ HET SCH: Fulmars and other birds near the ship.
MALOS HORIZONTES, CELAJERIA Y REPETIDOS: Bad horizons, cloud banks and repeated squalls.
MAN EN MEISJESSLAAF OVERLEDEN (NRS. 8 EN: Man and girl slave died (nos. 8 and 9). Now 203 slaves in the ship.
MAN EN VROUW SLAAF OVERLEDEN. LIETEN SCH: Man and woman slave died. Had the ship cleaned. There is much fire and unhealthiness in the ship because of the heavy rain. Slaves began to suffer from very sore eyes. Also had 3 male slaves with smallpox.
MAN ONVERWACHT OVERBOORD GESPRONGEN (MAT: Man suddenly jumped overboard (sailor Christiaan Pieters). A futile attempt was made to save the sailor. 6 sick on board.
MAN OVERBOORD DIE WEER BINNENBOORD WORDT: Man overboard who is hauled back on board.
MAN OVERBOORD EN VERDRONKEN TIJDENS WERK: Man overboard and drowned during work. The person was Jan Hendrik Andriesen of Middelburg.
MAN OVERBOORD, KONDEN HEM REDDEN: Man overboard, were able to save him.
MAN OVERBOORD: ABRAHAM PIETER VAN MASTER: Man overboard: Abraham Pieter van Masterlandt.
MANOUVREREN OM DE FORTUIJN OP ZIJN POST: Maneuvering to bring the [?] to its post.
MANTENIDO EN LA MISMA DISPOSICIÓN QUE EN: Kept in the same arrangement as in the previous day's run. Log line from knot to knot 46 English feet, the mile in eight fathoms. Sandglass of 30 seconds. First point of departure on the French chart of 53, transferred to that of Mr. Belin 4th ed. 66. Corrections with the meridian. It says miles, but nothing more. It is a squadron.
MAR ALGO GRUESA DEL S Y CIELO Y HORIZONT: Sea somewhat heavy from the south, and sky and horizons with some scattered cloud. Evening fell with a clear sky and the horizons with heavy cloud, the southern sea less heavy and the wind gentle. At 11 1/2 (...) a squall (...) Dawn came with a clear sky, the horizons with hazy cloud, and a dull swell from the southeast.
Sea from the east, overcast sky.
MAR DEL E, HORIZ. CLAROS CON CELAJ. SUEL: Sea from the east, clear horizons with scattered cloud.
MAR DEL N, CIELO Y HORIZ. CUBIERTOS DE C: Sea from the north, sky and horizons covered with cloud.
Sea from the northeast, cloudy horizons.
Sea from the northeast, cloudy horizons.
Sea from the northwest and southwest.
Sea from the northwest, clear horizons.
MAR DEL SE Y SO CON TURBONADAS DE GRANIZ: Sea from the southeast and southwest with squalls of hail and snow.
MAR DEL SO (...) A LAS 11 1/2 (NOCHE) UN: Sea from the southwest (...) At 11 1/2 (night) a squall of fresh wind which then repeated (...) Dawn came with dark cloud, a light fresh wind and heavy seas from the northwest and southwest. At 8 1/2 in the morning the wind eased off toward the south with gusts and squalls of hail.
MAR DEL VTO Y ESTE BONANCIBLE (...) ANOC: Sea from the wind and east, gentle (...) Evening fell with sky and horizons cloudy, a light fresh wind and seas from the southwest and west (...) At 5 1/2 the wind shifted suddenly to the south (...) Dawn came with everything closed in with drizzle, a light fresh wind with seas from the west and southwest.
MAR GRUESA DEL NO, Y TIEMPO CERRADO DE G: Heavy sea from the northwest, and weather closed in with drizzle; so we remained until 12 at night, when the wind being very little and the sea heavy (...) At dawn it fell completely calm.
MAR GRUESA DEL SE, HORIZ. CARGADOS CON C: Heavy sea from the southeast, horizons loaded with heavy cloud.
MAR GRUESA, VTO DEL NO 1/4 O AL OSO, MAR: Heavy sea, wind from the northwest by west toward the west-southwest, heavy sea from the northeast to the southwest.
MARCA LA ISLA DE LOS REYES Y CON ESOS DA: Takes a bearing on the Isla de los Reyes and with those data makes the relevant corrections according to the notes of Jorge Juan. Reflection on the variation. Describes the Isla de los Reyes (history, orography, location, characteristics for navigation, etc.). Makes notes on sketches of these coasts that other travelers made earlier, such as Chion, Norborough, etc. Then describes Puerto Deseado. They put the boats ashore. They take new bearings. Measurement and data of noon or of the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn.
MARCAN LA ISLA DE LOS REYES SEGÚN LA CAR: They take a bearing on the Isla de los Reyes according to Bellin's chart and according to that establish its position. They sight land and determine that it is the inlet of Santa Cruz. Measurement and data of noon or of the day's run, many times the descriptors are from dawn.
MARCAN LA TIERRA ALTA DEL CABO BLANCO: They take a bearing on the high land of Cabo Blanco.
MARCAN Y RECONOCEN EL RIO LOA. MEDICION: They take bearings on and recognize the Loa river. Noon measurement, the rest from dawn.
MARES DEL O Y DEL S. (...) ANOCHECIÓ TOL: Seas from the west and south. (...) Evening fell with overcast sky, the horizons loaded (...) choppy sea from the northwest (...) Dawn came overcast, the wind gentle, and seas from the west-northwest and southwest.
MARES GRUESAS DEL NO Y ONO(...) ANOCHECI: Heavy seas from the northwest and west-northwest (...) Evening fell closed in with drizzle, the wind calm, and the heavy seas as at noon. At one o'clock the wind pointed in from the northwest (...) Dawn came with the sea and the look of things as the day before and the wind fresh.
MARINIER 2E KLAS P. DE GIE OVERLEDEN AAN: Marine 2nd class P. de Gie died of dysentery.
MARINIER 3E KLAS J. SPELT AFGESTRAFT MET: Marine 3rd class J. Spelt punished with 50 strokes of the rattan and released from arrest for extreme brutality toward his superiors.
MARINIER 3E KLAS M. HARTOG IN ARREST GEZ: Marine 3rd class M. Hartog put under arrest for threatening Sergeant Moreau de Reindt.
MARINIER BLANKEN SLAPEND OP ZIJN POST AA: Marine Blanken found sleeping at his post. Punished with 36 strokes.
MARINIER BOERSORM OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN: Marine Boersorm fell overboard and drowned.
MARINIER COENRAADS GESTRAFT MET 1724 UUR: Marine Coenraads punished with 1724 hours bent in irons while performing duty, for neglect of duty, namely arbitrarily leaving his post as sentry.
MARINIER H. TEUNISSEN OVERLEDEN AAN EEN: Marine H. Teunissen died of a contagious disease.
MARINIER J.O. MEIJER IN ARRAST WEGENS DR: Marine J.O. Meijer under arrest for drunkenness and improper language toward his superiors.
MARINIER LAMAN IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS DESER: Marine Laman in irons for desertion.
MARINIER MAUCK IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS DRONK: Marine Mauck in irons for drunkenness.
MARINIER MOL IN DE BOEIEN GESLOTEN WEGEN: Marine Mol locked in irons for fighting.
MARINIER N. HAHN EN BOOTSMANS LEERLING F: Marine N. Hahn and boatswain's apprentice F. Bossers died.
MARINIER RUBELING IN ARREST, WEGENS HET: Marine Rubeling under arrest for refusing to be at his post.
MARINIER SCHELLING IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS B: Marine Schelling in irons for brutality toward a corporal.
MARINIER V. DER HEIJDEN MET 2 UUR STRAFS: Marine V. der Heijden punished with 2 hours of punishment sentry duty for improper language toward the corporal. The bunk of the sick-bay attendant Terhorst was found on inspection to be full of vermin, for which he was punished with close confinement in irons for 4 days, having his head and chin shaved bare and being washed by 2 strong sailors.
MARINIER VERMEER EN MATROOS NEIT OVERLED: Marine Vermeer and sailor Neit died.
MARINIERS AAN DE SCHEEPSPISTOLEN. WE HIE: Marines at the ship's pistols. We held a wash day.
MARINIERS HOUDEN THEORIE IN DE ARTILLERI: Marines hold theory lessons in artillery.
MARSZEILSKOELTE AFNEMENDE TOT BRAMZEILSK: Topsail breeze decreasing to topgallant breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEMENDE TOT BRAMZEI: Topsail breeze and decreasing to topgallant breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN FRISSE BRAMZEILSKOELT: Topsail breeze and fresh topgallant breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN FRISSE DITO KOELTE: Topsail breeze and fresh ditto breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOE: Topsail breeze and reefed topsail breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELT: Topsail breeze and stiff topgallant breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZ: Topsail breeze and stiff reefed topsail breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE EN STIJVE MARSZEILSKOELT: Topsail breeze and stiff topsail breeze.
MARSZEILSKOELTE TOT GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKO: Topsail breeze to reefed topsail breeze.
MARTIN PLACAS O PAMPERITOS EN ABUNDANCIA: Martin Placas or Pamperitos in abundance. Some boobies, sky very clear and beautiful and horizon with some scattered clouds. (...) At 8 in the evening the horizons became overcast. At dawn sky clearer, horizons less overcast, sea calm, wind with some squalls of little strength.
MARTINIQUE A LA DOMINIQUE, DAINTE LUCIE,: Martinique to Dominica, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent, Guadeloupe, Barbados.
MAS O MENOS FRESQUITO: More or less a little fresh.
MATA DE SARGAZO Y 1 TABLERO CARNERO. CIE: Clump of sargasso weed and 1 board of a ram [?]. Skies and horizons closed in with mist, fine rain falling. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
Clump of sargasso weed and at times in abundance. Skies and horizons with brownish cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
MATOOS 3 KLASSE W. EIJKMAN OVERBOORD GEV: Sailor 3rd class W. Eijkman fell overboard and drowned.
MATROO PIETER DE JONG VAN VLISSINGEN EN: Sailor Pieter de Jong of Vlissingen and the soldier Johan Caspers Kittel of Spandouw died.
MATROOS 1E KLAS G. BOSCH CLOESMEIJER OVE: Sailor 1st class G. Bosch Cloesmeijer died.
MATROOS 1E KLAS J HOP IN DE BOEIEN WEGEN: Sailor 1st class J Hop put in irons for improper language against sailor 1st class Gerritsen.
Sailor 1st class J. de Koning drowned.
MATROOS 1E KLAS JOHAN FREDERIK SCHULTZ O: Sailor 1st class Johan Frederik Schultz died of consumption.
MATROOS 291? PIETER MENDORP, F 165 WILLE: Sailor 291? Pieter Mendorp, F 165 Willem Bosman, soldier F 403 Hartman Sterkel died.
MATROOS 2E KLAS B. G. DE VRIES OVER BOOR: Sailor 2nd class B. G. de Vries fell overboard and drowned.
MATROOS 2E KLAS FRENCH IN DE BOEIEN GESL: Sailor 2nd class French put in irons for extreme brutality and insubordination.
MATROOS 2E KLASSE J. P. PFEIFFER OVERLED: Sailor 2nd class J. P. Pfeiffer died.
MATROOS 2E KLASSE J. VALENTEIN OVERLEDEN: Sailor 2nd class J. Valentein died of a wasting illness and was put overboard. The rest of the crew were perfectly healthy.
MATROOS 3E KLARE J. DE LARIE? OVERLEDEN: Sailor 3rd class J. de Larie? died.
MATROOS 3E KLAS A. VAN DEN BURG OVERLEDE: Sailor 3rd class A. van den Burg died.
MATROOS 3E KLAS HENDERIKS (VERREGAANDE B: Sailor 3rd class Henderiks, being extremely drunk, threatened the skipper Klaassen with a knife; because of his drunkenness and others preventing it, he was put in irons.
MATROOS 3E KLAS HENDERIKS WEGENS HET FEI: Sailor 3rd class Henderiks punished for the incident reported yesterday; skipper Klaassen, out of pity, wanted the matter settled without a court martial. Fusilier Lammers under arrest for threats against the cooper, who was acting as steward; the other day punished with 45 lashes.
MATROOS 3E KLAS J. J. BRETTMULLER OVERLE: Sailor 3rd class J. J. Brettmuller died.
MATROOS 3E KLAS JAN VAN VEEN IN ARREST W: Sailor 3rd class Jan van Veen under arrest for theft.
MATROOS 3E KLAS W. VAN WERKUM VOOR HET R: Sailor 3rd class W. van Werkum punished at the grating with 60 blows with handlines [?] for deliberately wounding one of his comrades with a knife.
MATROOS 3E KLASSE A. KOTTENHAGE OVERLEDE: Sailor 3rd class A. Kottenhage died, aged 20, after an illness of 20 days of bile and nerve fever. 8 sick in total on the voyage. Adjutant of the Governor General ad interim van Starkenborgh on board, with a request from him to be escorted by the Komeet under convoy to the Spanish coast.
MATROOS ? BOUT OVERLEDEN. ZETTEN HET LIJ: Sailor ? Bout died. Put the body overboard.
MATROOS ABRAHAM SPOOR VAN ZIERIKZEE OVER: Sailor Abraham Spoor of Zierikzee died.
MATROOS ABRAM ZOETEN SPRONG OVERBOORD. H: Sailor Abram Zoeten jumped overboard. He had received some punishment because his belongings were full of lice. Drowned.
MATROOS ADAM LANKRO UIT NIJMEGEN OVERBOO: Sailor Adam Lankro of Nijmegen was knocked overboard and killed. Could not save him because of the ship's fast progress and the freshening breeze.
MATROOS ANDRIES MELROOD IN DE BOEIEN GES: Sailor Andries Melrood put in irons.
MATROOS ANDRIES OOSTERMAN VAN ZWEDEN OVE: Sailor Andries Oosterman of Sweden died.
MATROOS ANDRIESSEN WEGENS INSUBORDINATIE: Sailor Andriessen under arrest for insubordination.
MATROOS ANTOINE DU FOUA, OVERLEDEN. BRAN: Sailor Antoine du Foua died. Branden Sissers.
MATROOS ARIJ VAN LOOBEEK VAN MIDDELBURG: Sailor Arij van Loobeek of Middelburg died.
MATROOS ASMUS WELMANS OVERBOORD GEVALLEN: Sailor Asmus Welmans fell overboard and drowned.
MATROOS BARTH VAN DER FUIK OVERLEDEN: Sailor Barth van der Fuik died.
MATROOS BENJAMIJN WAALKES VAN PUIJTHUM O: Sailor Benjamijn Waalkes of Puijthum died.
MATROOS BEUGELINK AFGESTRAFT MET 24 SLAG: Sailor Beugelink punished with 24 lashes and then released from arrest.
MATROOS C. HOGERWERFF OVERLEDEN. LUIT. C: Sailor C. Hogerwerff died. Lieut. Corbelijn under arrest.
MATROOS C.F. BLOEM OVER DRONKENSCHAP IN: Sailor C.F. Bloem put in irons for drunkenness.
MATROOS CHRISTIAAN BERGH VAN BREMEN OVER: Sailor Christiaan Bergh of Bremen died.
MATROOS CHRISTIAAN CHRISTIAANZ. VALT VAN: Sailor Christiaan Christiaanz. fell from the main topsail yard onto the large hatch without hurting himself. He did hit the smith and another man who were standing on the hatch.
MATROOS CHRISTIAAN JANSEN VAN NOORDKOOPI: Sailor Christiaan Jansen of Noordkooping died.
MATROOS CHRISTIAAN OOSTERMAN VAN STOKHOL: Sailor Christiaan Oosterman of Stockholm died, soldier Christiaan Meusken of Koxsdorp.
MATROOS CHRISTIAAN POP OVERLEDEN (61). B: Sailor Christiaan Pop died (61). Boatswain Lobbe Sijbes died (62).
MATROOS CORNELIS VAN AARHUIS. OVERLIJDEN: Sailor Cornelis van Aarhuis. Death of the provost Kasper Hendrik Reijnhart.
MATROOS CORNELIS VAN DER VEER VAN BOMMEL: Sailor Cornelis van der Veer of Bommel died.
MATROOS CORNELIS VNA DEN ENT, OVERLEDEN: Sailor Cornelis van den Ent died.
MATROOS D. VAN HEEN IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS: Sailor D. van Heen in irons for theft of plush.
MATROOS DAVID ONRAAD VALT VAN DE VOORMAS: Sailor David Onraad fell from the foremast yard on the port side overboard and got under the ship and met his death.
MATROOS DE LEEUW WORDT BESTRAFT VOOR DIE: Sailor de Leeuw punished for theft.
MATROOS DEGENHART IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS BR: Sailor Degenhart in irons for brutality.
MATROOS DER 1E KLAS S. ANDRIES KWAM AAN: Sailor 1st class S. Andries died of a haemorrhage. At 4 o'clock sailor 1st class J. Beling died.
MATROOS DIJK KRAMER VAN LASTEROP OVERLED: Sailor Dijk Kramer of Lasterop died.
MATROOS DIRK GURTS OVERLEDEN IN GEVECHT,: Sailor Dirk Gurts died in battle, and sailor no. 104, Geert Harms, died.
MATROOS DIRK PIETERS WESTERBEEK VAN MAAS: Sailor Dirk Pieters Westerbeek of Maassluis died.
MATROOS DIRRICK SONNESTIJN, GEBOREN IN L: Sailor Dirrick Sonnestijn, born in Louwisa in Sweden, died. Body put overboard.
MATROOS DOEDE FOPPES OVERLEDEN (19). JON: Sailor Doede Foppes died (19). Boy Coenraad Onstein died (20).
MATROOS DUPER VIEL OP DEK, KREEG ZWARE H: Sailor Duper fell on deck, received a severe head wound and broke his right thigh, from which he died in the evening. Put the body overboard.
MATROOS EVERT THOMASSEN UIT NOORWEGEN OV: Sailor Evert Thomassen from Norway died.
MATROOS F 139 FRANCISCUS DANUS EN SOLDAA: Sailor F 139 Franciscus Danus and soldier F 135 Jan Godfrid Siebers died.
MATROOS F 145 ANTHONIJ BONFORT, F 352 MA: Sailor F 145 Anthonij Bonfort, F 352 Matthias Cols died.
MATROOS F 151 PIETER VAN DEN WIJNGAARDE,: Sailor F 151 Pieter van den Wijngaarde, F 200 Arij van Wijck and F 7 Jurgen Moed, and soldiers F 453 Johanna Kersblick and F 354 Johan Hukkerstig.
MATROOS F. JANSSEN VAN DE RA OP HET DEEK: Sailor F. Janssen fell from the yard onto the deck and died.
MATROOS FOLIO 228 IZACK VAN DEN BERG OVE: Sailor Folio 228 Izack van den Berg died.
MATROOS FRANS HERREBERGH VAN MIDDELBURG: Sailor Frans Herrebergh of Middelburg died.
MATROOS FREDERIK HOVEN VAN NIEUWENLUIJZE: Sailor Frederik Hoven of Nieuwenluijzen fell from the main yard. He died. He fell on sailor Adriaan Schijlman of Vlissingen, who was just coming up the ladder with bread and cheese in his hand. He also died.
MATROOS GENAAMD DIRRICK VAN SOET (?) , G: Sailor named Dirrick van Soet [?], born in Cologne, died. Body put overboard and his belongings sold.
MATROOS GERRIT BARENDSE VAN GRONINGEN OV: Sailor Gerrit Barendse of Groningen died.
MATROOS GERRIT KLAASSEN IN DE BOEIEN GES: Sailor Gerrit Klaassen put in irons for theft from a chest.
MATROOS GERRIT LEENDERS VAN AMSTERDAM OV: Sailor Gerrit Leenders of Amsterdam died.
MATROOS GOET OVER BOORD GEVALLEN EN VERD: Sailor Goet fell overboard and drowned.
MATROOS HANS JURJEN EEUWIG OVERLEDEN. HO: Sailor Hans Jurjen Eeuwig died. However reluctantly, also...ration of water
MATROOS HARMANIS POL VAN AMSTERDAM OVERL: Sailor Harmanis Pol of Amsterdam died.
MATROOS HEIJERMAN SAVONDS OM 9:30 UUR OV: Sailor Heijerman died in the evening at 9:30
MATROOS HENDRIK JACOBS OVERLEDEN (52). M: Sailor Hendrik Jacobs died (52). Sailor Jan Doedes died (53). Sailor Joost Bruins died (54)
MATROOS HENDRIK JANSZ SIJTER VAN CHRISTI: Sailor Hendrik Jansz Sijter of Christiaenzant died
MATROOS HENDRIK SALON VAN IJPEREN OVERLE: Sailor Hendrik Salon of IJperen died
MATROOS HERMANUS SMIT OVERLEDEN. HAALDEN: Sailor Hermanus Smit died. Fetched water with the boats. The cabin cook and Mense Pieters were let out of the irons, but ran away as soon as they came ashore.
MATROOS HOK IS ACHTERGEBLEVEN OP TRISTAN: Sailor Hok was left behind on Tristan d'Acunha
MATROOS HUIJBERT VAN WESTERVOORT EN VROU: Sailor Huijbert van Westervoort and Mrs. Elizabeth were married because Huijbert was dangerously ill and this is his last wish.
MATROOS IJPE HENDRIKS OVERLEDEN (57). MA: Sailor Ijpe Hendriks died (57). Sailor Joost Feber died (58)
MATROOS IN DE BOEIEN GESLAGEN WEGENS BRU: Sailor put in irons for brutality towards the first clerk
MATROOS IN DE IJZERS GESLOTEN, OMDAT SCH: Sailor locked in irons because he had stolen shoe buckles.
MATROOS J. COUSINS VERONGELUKT: Sailor J. Cousins killed in an accident
MATROOS J. SMIT VRIJGELATEN EN AFGESTRAF: Sailor J. Smit released and punished
MATROOS J.H.GEURS OVERLEDEN AAN ZIEKTE: Sailor J.H. Geurs died of illness
MATROOS JACHOP BOCHIE VALT UIT HET GROOT: Sailor Jachop Bochie falls from the maintop, badly injured but still alive (both arms bent into kinks, one hand twisted out of true and a large hole in the front of his head). He is brought below and handed over to the doctor. The carpenter makes a cot for him.

MET DE 2 GL IN DE DAG SCHOOT DE WIND SUB: With 2 glasses in the day the wind suddenly shifted from N to WSW and W.
MET DE 3 GLAZEN DER VOORMIDDAG STUURDEN: With 3 glasses of the forenoon steered E by S because we presumed to have already passed St. Thomee, as by our dead reckoning we were already 20 miles west of it.
MET DE DAG AFNEMENDE KOELTE, ZETTEN DE M: With daylight decreasing breeze, set the topsails as well. Corrected course ENE 1/2 N, 23 miles. Changed longitude 1° 41'.
MET DE DAGW IS OVERLEDEN DEN MATTROOS JA: With the day watch the sailor Jan Carter of Kooningsberge died.
MET DE DAGWACHT HIELDEN AF NAAR HET EILA: With the day watch headed for the island and anchored at 9 o'clock in 16 fathoms off James-Town.
MET DE ENGELSE BARK HARPLEY VAN SOUTHAMP: With the English bark Harpley from Southampton to Melbourne, 98 days voyage.
At noon the Needles NE by N.
MET DE MIDDAG EEN TRAVAAT UIT NNO MET FR: At noon a squall from NNE with fresh breeze, thunder, lightning and rain.
MET DE? GLAZEN (IN DE HW) ZIEN EEN KLEIN: With [?] glasses (in the HW) see a small high island but without identifying it. Hauled up the courses (to wait for daylight). DW: at sunrise the island proves to be Allagranca. VM: steered for Gran Canaria.
MET DEN DONKER PORTO RICO UIT ZICHT: At dusk Porto Rico out of sight.
MET DEN DONKER WESTELIJKSTE HOEK SANTA C: At dusk westernmost point of Santa Cruz N by E 3/4 E.
Sailed up with various other ships.
MET DW DE WIND SUBIET UITSCHIETENDE VAN: With the day watch the wind suddenly veering from NW to SW.
MET EEN DER BLIKSEMSLAGEN VIEL ER EEN ST: With one of the lightning strokes a piece of fire fell out of the sky (2 feet across, and was carried away from the ship).
MET HET BREKEN VAN DE DAG IS ONZE KAPITE: At daybreak our captain Jakob Kluijter 'fell asleep in the Lord' (died).
MET HET DERDE GLAS IN DE DAGWACHT ZAGEN: At the third glass in the day watch saw an iceberg NE by E of us in sight, 3 miles. Went around to the north of it and saw several small icebergs to the east.
MET HET OPHALEN BEVONDEN ALS DAT DE BUIS: When hauling up, found that the pipe was broken.
MET HET TEREN OVERBOORD GEVALLEN DEN MAT: While tarring, the sailor Geert Hendriks of Harderwick fell overboard.
MET IEDERE BUI DE WIND ROND: With every squall the wind veers round.
MET OPKOMENDE WACHT (EW) DE MATROOS PIET: At the start of the watch (EW) the sailor Pieter Bang died and at 9.00 o'clock was sewn into his hammock and put overboard.
MET REGEN EN WEERLICHT IN HET ONO: With rain and lightning in the ENE.
MET SLAGEN MET HANDSAGEN AFGESTRAFT EN D: Punished with blows with handsaws and afterwards discharged: the first-class sailors Simons and Kaldenhoven.
MET SONS DAELING KONDEN NIETS ONTWAEREN: At sunset could make out nothing.
MET SONS RIJSING NIETS VAN TOP ONTWAREN: At sunrise could make out nothing from the top.
MET SONSONDERGANG PIJLDE DE WESTCAAP CAM: At sunset took bearings: the west cape of Camerijn ENE 1/2 N and the east cape E by S, estimated 2,5 miles from the nearest shore (…) This bearing and S. E. Comp. [?] Mercator chart at north latitude 8°00' longitude 92°30', from where our dead reckoning begins, trusting in God's blessing.
MET TIJFF EN STIFF WORDT M.I. 'STIJVE' B: By 'tijff' and 'stiff' is meant, in my opinion, 'stiff', as in stiff topsail breeze (TZK).
MET TOUPKOULTE WORDT WAARSCHIJNLIJK TOPZ: By 'toupkoulte' is probably meant topsail breeze (TZK).
MET ZIJL, MAST AANWAKKEREN UIT HET WESTE: With sail, mast: freshening from the west.
MET ZONSONDERGANG IN W STERK ROOD GEKLEU: At sunset in the W colored strongly red, soon gone.
MET ZONSONDERGANG PEILDEN DE TEEPELBERG: At sunset took bearing of the Teepelberg W by N 1/2 N.
MET ZONSONDERGANG SCHIET DE WIND OPEENS: At sunset the wind suddenly shifts from N to W with lightning and heavy rain.
MET ZONSONDERGANG: LEEUWENKOP IN HET? W/: At sunset: Leeuwenkop in the [?] W/S N.
MET ZONSOPGANG HARDE STORM MET VLIEGENDE: At sunrise hard storm with flying squalls.
MET ZONSOPGANG WORDT RIO DULSIUS WTN 4,7: At sunrise Rio Dulsius W by N, 4,75 miles. Took bearings at sunset again: Riodulsius NE 1/2 N, 6,75 miles.
MET? GLAZEN LOODDEN 30 VAAM. \"WEDER OP: With [?] glasses sounded 30 fathoms. "Again found ourselves on the Abrolhos, 22 miles [?]." Corrected longitude: 343° 48'. Found that we were 25 miles further west than we were yesterday. AMW: over the Abrolhos (soundings).
MET? GLAZEN ONDER ZEIL, LATER WEER VOOR: With [?] glasses under sail, later again at anchor because of unrest. Other tack.
METEOROLOGISCHE WAARNEMING, AAN BOORD VA: Meteorological observation, on board His Majesty's steamship Amsterdam under command of Lieutenant Captain J. Spanjaard, running from 18 July to 10 November 1853. At 8 o'clock passed the Uiterton.
MIDDAG: MIDDEN VAN GROOT PITON OZO 2/3 W: Noon: middle of Great Piton ESE 2/3 W. Salvage [?] 1/4 [?],5 miles.
MIDDAG: MIDDEN VAN P. BABY NW W/Z N. IN: Noon: middle of P. Baby NW W/S N. In the afternoon at anchor.
Noon bearing: SW point of Terreira NW 1/4 N. W point of Terreira NE by E 3/4 E. On Owen's chart of the Western Islands this gives N lat 38º 34' 20'' and W long 27º 13' 40''. See the town of Angla and the Waykus and Cabras rocks. See the land of St. George and of Pico. Divine service.
MIDDERNACHT DE VUREN VAN LEZARD (LIZART-: Midnight the lights of Lezard (Lizard Head), N by W 1/2 W, 2,25 miles. (Estimated) Lezard W by S, 8,5 miles.
MINUTEN BIJ DE WARE BEKOMEN LENGTE ZIJN: Minutes of the true longitude obtained are unclear.
MINUTEN TIJDMETER LENGTE SLECHT TE LEZEN: Minutes of chronometer longitude poorly legible. Transfer the dead reckoning onto the chart of Mr. Intact (black?) 1827.
MINUTEN VERTROUWDE LENGTE NIET GOED TE L: Minutes of trusted longitude not clearly legible.
MINUTEN WARE BEKOMEN BREEDTE WEGGEVALLEN: Minutes of true latitude obtained missing.
MISGISSING OF STROOM NO 3/4 OOST 4 3/4 M: Error in estimate or current NE 3/4 E, 4 3/4 miles.
MISMA AGUA. DESDE EL AMANECER VEN MUCHOS: Same course. Since dawn they see many birds, among them shearwaters, "and I observe that we have only seen them in abundance with these winds and not with those of the 1st and 4th quadrant."
MISMA AGUA. EN DEMANDA DE CABO FRIO. VEN: Same course. Heading for Cabo Frio. In the afternoon they see birds similar to the gulls of Europe.
MISMA AGUA. HACEN NUEVOS INTENTOS DE ARR: Same course. They make new attempts to fix the leak.
MISMA AGUA. HALLAN ALGUNAS AGUAS MALAS (: Same course. They find some 'aguas malas' (I believe jellyfish; at least that is what they are called in Huelva).
MISMA AGUA. SOLO SE HA VISTO 1 PAJARO BL: Same course. Only 1 black and white bird has been seen.
MISMA AGUA. VEN LOS MISMOS PAJAROS QUE A: Same course. They see the same birds as before. He reflects on the variations of the compass needle and the inaccuracy of observations and measurements due to having crossed the line. The French pilots they carry estimate that they are closer to the coast than it appears.
MISREKENING SEDERT LAATSTE OBSERVATIE NO: Difference in reckoning since last observation NE by E, 1/2 E, 11,75 miles.
MISSEN 2 MAN: JAN BLIKKING EN PETER MEIJ: Missing 2 men: Jan Blikking and Peter Meijer. Get 2 pigs and some vegetables and water on board.
MISSEN EEN SCHIP. HET KONVOOI IS UIT ELK: Missing a ship. The convoy has been scattered by heavy storm. PV: ship is back in position.
MISTIGE LUCHT OPKLARENDE LUCHT GOED WEER: Foggy sky, clearing sky, good weather.
MISWIJZING COMMANDANT 21°54'. MISWIJZING: Compass variation Commandant 21°54'. Compass variation De Beschermer 20° 49'. (1 of the ships had suffered damage during the storm). Changed longitude 1° 46'.
MISWIJZING COMMANDANT: 19° 47' EN VAN. D: Compass variation Commandant: 19° 47' and De Beschermer: 20° 47'. Changed longitude 2° 8'. In the evening: "Here our dead reckoning came to an end."
MISWIJZING DOOR AZIMUTHPEILING 16\"52' N: Compass variation by azimuth bearing 16°52' northwesterly.
MMAKEN TUSSENDEKS SCHOON, VERDELEN DE KI: Clean the between-decks, distribute the chests, with 2 men to a chest.
MOEILIJK ANKER OP TEN 10 \" EN KOERSDEN: Difficult to weigh anchor at 10 o'clock and steered SSE.
MOESTEN VANWEGE DE TE HARDE WIND BIJLIGG: Had to lie to because of the too hard wind.
MOESTEN VOLGENS HET BESTEK HET LAND GEZI: According to the dead reckoning must have seen the land, but did not see it, so shifted the dead reckoning 3 degrees further west.
MOESTEN WEER OP SCHIPPER MOBEK WACHTEN: Had to wait again for Captain Mobek.
MOESTEN ZICH VOLGENS MEERVLIET GEREED HO: Had to hold themselves ready for defence, according to Meervliet, because the Malays had fought with them, 6 dead, 30 wounded.
MOETEN DE BREEDTE VD KLIPPEN PASSEREN: Must pass the latitude of the rocks.
Must steer ENE because of the difficult sea.
MONSTERDEN EN VERDEELDEN HET VOLK AAN HU: Mustered the crew and assigned them to their messes.
MONTAN EL CABO DE SAN AGUSTIN. DATOS DEL: They round Cape San Agustín. Data from dawn.
MORSDOOD NEERGEVALLEN DE JONG MATROOS FR: Fell down stone dead: the young sailor Frans Sisent of Leers.
MOUILLE AU MOLE. APAREILLÉ. MOUILLÉ: Anchored at the mole. Weighed anchor. Anchored.
MOUILLE PAR 44 BRASSES, FOND DE SABLE FI: Anchored in 44 fathoms, fine sand bottom (18:00). At eight o'clock in the morning on the 4th, weighed anchor.
MOUILLÉ A 6 HS. AU CAP SALOMON ET APAREI: Anchored at 6 o'clock at Cap Salomon and weighed anchor.
MOUILLÉ A CUL DE SAC DU FORT ROYAL A MID: Anchored in the cul-de-sac of Fort Royal at noon.
MOUILLÉ A LA RADE DU FORT ROYAL A 1 HS A: Anchored in the roads of Fort Royal at 1 o'clock in the afternoon.
MOUILLÉ A' LA GRANDE RADE DE CAYENNÉ ET: Anchored in the great roads of Cayenne and departed.
MOUILLÉ AU E DE LA RADE DU BASQUE: Anchored at the E of the roads of the Basque.
MOUILLÉ DANS LA RADE DE DUPALLAY DE L'IS: Anchored in the roads of Dupallay on L'Isle Dieu.
MOUILLÉ DANS LA RADE DE FUNCHAL, ÎLE DE: Anchored in the roads of Funchal, Île de Madère (20:00h).
MOUILLÉ DANS LA RADE DU CAP A 4 HS: Anchored in the roads of the Cap at 4 o'clock.
MOUILLÉ DANS LE PERTUIS BRETON. APAREILL: Anchored in the Pertuis Breton. Weighed anchor. Anchored at Port des Barques.
MOUILLÉ DANS LE PORT DE MIRABELLE (17:00: Anchored in the port of Mirabelle (17:00).
MOUILLÉ PAR 14 BRASSES DANS LA BAIE DE L: Anchored in 14 fathoms in the bay of Langle on the coast of Île Ségalien (18:00).
MOUILLÉ PAR 20 BRASSES, FOND DE VASE, À: Anchored in 20 fathoms, mud bottom, 3/4 league from land, in the bay of Estaing. Latitude and longitude of the anchorage.
MOUILLÉ À DEUX LIEUES DE LA CÔTE, PAR 40: Anchored two leagues from the coast, in 40 fathoms, sand bottom (19:00).
MOUILLÉ À I LIEUE DE TERRE PAR 39 BRASSE: Anchored 1 league from land in 39 fathoms, fine sand bottom (19:00).
MOUILLÉ À L'ÎLE DE PÂQUE (13:00), PAR 36: Anchored at Île de Pâque (13:00), in 36 fathoms, fine grey sand bottom.
MOUILLÉ À SAINTE-CATHERINE (16:00), PAR: Anchored at Sainte-Catherine (16:00), in 7 fathoms, muddy sand bottom.
MUCHA GARÚA CON REPETIDOS CHUBASCOS DE A: Much drizzle with repeated heavy showers and wind. (...) During the night the showers were stronger. (...) It improved in the morning.
Much mist in the sky and on the horizon.
MUCHAS TONINAS QUE IBAN AL NO, VEN MULTI: Many porpoises going to the NW, and they see a multitude of small white birds and others.
MUCHO VIENTO A LAS 9 DE LA MAÑANA. LLEGA: Much wind at 9 in the morning. Arrives at Montecristo. Descriptors, sea and wind from dawn, the rest from noon.
MUERE 1 MARINERO DE UN GOLPE EN LA CABEZ: 1 sailor dies from a blow to the head.
MUITERIJ ONDER DE SOLDATEN WORDT OP HET: Mutiny among the soldiers is prevented at the last moment. The soldiers wanted to seize the ship, murder opponents and sail to America.
MUIZEN HEBBEN NESTEN GEMAAKT IN STUKKEN: Mice have made nests in pieces of paper in a hammock.
The ship's boy Antonio Pedroso died.
A ship's boy, Joseph Belmon, died.
MUY BONANCIBLE Y EN VECES CALMA: Very calm and at times becalmed.
MUY CARGADOS DE MAL SEMBLANTE: Very overcast, with a bad look.
MUY CERCA DE PUERTO RICO. DATOS DEL MEDI: Very near Puerto Rico. Data from noon or from the day's run.
MUY DE MAÑANA DESCUBREN LA TIERRA A 6 LE: Very early in the morning they sight land at 6 leagues and approach, but at 8:00 the wind calmed and they anchor at 4 leagues. They weigh anchor at 14:00. At 20:00 the wind freshened too much from the NE and caused a great swell, increasing during the night. Lying to. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
Very bad look of the weather all around the horizon.
MUY TORMENTOSO DE BALANCES CON MOTIVO DE: Very stormy, with rolling because of the so [?] sea. Data from noon or from the day's run.
N.B. SPRONGEN IN DAT TUSSEN OPVOLGENDE I: N.B. Skipped ahead there between successive images.
NA 10.00 UUR BEGON HET STIJV UIT HET NOO: After 10:00 the wind began to freshen strongly from the north. Corrected course and distance NE 1/2? 7 miles.
NA DATO GEEN POSITIES MEER. KWAMEN OP 7: After this date no more positions. On 7 May they arrived at the roads of Batavia.
NA DE MIDDAG DE WIND Z-NNW, LABBER EN ST: In the afternoon the wind S-NNW, slack and still, overcast and the sky clearing again. Dead reckoning begins.
NA DE MIDDAG EN 'S NACHTS OZK EN TZK: In the afternoon and at night [?] and [?].
NA DE MIDDAG EN 'S NACHTS OZK, REGEN EN: In the afternoon and at night [?], rain and thunder.
NA DE MIDDAG FLAUWE KOELTE UIT HET NO EN: In the afternoon light breeze from the NE and NW.
NA DE MIDDAG WORDT EEN OBSERVATIE GEDAAN: In the afternoon an observation is made using the sun and the moon; they find themselves at 3°30'.
NA DEZE DAG GEEN GOEDE GEGEVENS MEER. OP: After this day no more good data. On 19 September the journal stops, probably at the roads of Accra.
NA DIT RECORD VOLGT NIETS MEER, ZE ZIJN: After this record nothing more follows; they had, however, not yet arrived in the Netherlands.
NA EEN KANONSSCHOT STOOKT MEN HET VUUR V: After a cannon shot the fire of Robbeneiland is lit. In the dog watch they enter the roads of Kaap de Goede Hoop, at half past eight at anchor in the Tafelbaai.
NA PEILINGEN VAN POSITIE OPGEMAAKT. NACH: After bearings the position was worked out. Night at anchor.
NA SCHEEPSRAAD WERD BOOTSMAN JAN ADAMS W: After the ship's council, boatswain Jan Adams was demoted to sailor for incompetence, at 16 guilders per month. The boatswain's mate Pieter Montanje became boatswain at 22 guilders per month.
NA'T PLAT VAN DE MERIDIAAN BEOOSTEN DE C: According to the plane chart, east of the meridian of the cape 15 deg: 20 min:
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN DE PEILINGEN WORDT G: Based on the bearings it is concluded that the chronometer was found to be 7'30'' too far east.
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN GISSING WORDT GECONC: Based on estimation it is concluded that the western land of Ierland lay 16,5 further east.
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN OBSERVATIE VAN ZON E: Based on observation of sun and moon the longitude comes to 86°44'30''. The reckoning is still too far east.
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN PEILEN EILAND AMSTER: Based on bearings of the island Amsterdam the reckoning is adjusted.
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN PEILINGEN EN GISSING: Based on bearings and estimates the chronometer is adjusted to 19°4'0''.
NAAR AANLEIDING VAN PEILINGEN VAN GISTER: Based on the bearings of yesterday and today the true position of Pulo Comba turns out to be: south latitude 7°45' and longitude 123°21'.
NAAR DE REDE VAN BRIDGETOWN EN DOOR NAAR: To the roads of Bridgetown and on to the roads of Barbados.
NAAST DE DAGAANDUIDING VAN DEZE RECORD S: Next to the date marking of this record, the journal still states trade wind.
Next to the wind force figure there is an X.
NADAT DE LOODS EEN PLAATS AAN HAD GEWEZE: After the pilot had indicated a place to anchor, a health boat with free pratique came. 'Then sent a boat with an officer ashore to visit the governor of the island and the consul and to give notice of our arrival.' The Dutch consul general, Mr. A. Beruft, then came aboard. 'The governor of all the islands is the Marquis de la Concorde.'
NADERDE WIJ DE RIVIER OF KREEK VOOR T ST: We approached the river or creek by the beach, into which some enemy small ships or vessels of the King of Riouw had run and made their landing; saw the OIC ship 't Hoff ter Linde
NALATENSCHAP VAN MATROOS F. DRAUMAN VERK: Estate of sailor F. Drauman sold (not known when he died)
NAM EEN STREEK NWESTERING (HADDEN DUS GE: Took a course more to the northwest (so we had no sliding compass card)
NAME AFSCHEID VAN MALKANDEREN OP DE BREE: Took leave of each other at the latitude of Cabo Verde
NAMEN BESTEK VAN DE VUURTOREN VAN ROBBEN: Took the position from the lighthouse of Robben Island, on the round chart 33°50' S and 35°30' longitude
NAMEN DE LENGTE OVER VAN EEN VOC-SCHIP D: Took the longitude from a VOC ship that they had hailed.
NAMEN HET BESTEK VAN DE HEER VAILLANT ZI: Took the position of Mr. Vaillant, being 30°48' at noon
NAMEN SPAANS SCHIP, EEN SCHOENER, IN BES: Seized a Spanish ship, a schooner, with 11 Black boys and some fresh provisions; the captain was allowed to continue his voyage
NAMEN VAN HIER HET BESTEK, VAREN IN KONV: Took the position from here, sailing in convoy with the Texelstroom and Schoonderloo
NAMEN VEEL WATER OVER, VERSCHRIKKELIJK Z: Took a lot of water over the deck, terribly heavy rolling
NAMEN VOORNAMELIJK SUIKER EN KOFFIE ALS: Took in mainly sugar and coffee as cargo.
NAMIDDAG: BETER WEER. WACHTEN KOOPVAARDE: Afternoon: better weather. Waiting for merchant ships.
NAMIDDAG: BETROKKEN LUCHT NA EEN ZWARE D: Afternoon: overcast sky after a heavy thunderstorm, wind west.
Afternoon: the sky is clouding over very heavily. At night squally storms, accompanied by hail and lightning all around. With an enormously high, onrushing sea.
NAUWE ? EEN ANDERE KELLY ? VOOR DE TIJDM: Narrow [?] another Kelly [?] for the chronometer to that of 91° 30' to 92° 33 or [?]. [?] thunder, lightning, rain, squalls
NAVEGA A PASAR MUCHO MAS CERCA DE LAS IS: Sailing so as to pass much closer to the islands than to Cabo Verde
NAVEGACIÓN DE LA CORUÑA A MONTEVIDEO: Voyage from La Coruña to Montevideo
NAVEGAN AL ENE. A LAS 12:00 MARCAN EL CA: They sail ENE. At 12:00 they take a bearing of Cabo Santa Elena at NNW, 3 leagues away. At 19:00 the wind began to blow from the SW and they sail NE
NAVEGAN AL N 1/4 NE. A LAS 19:00 CALMO E: They sail N 1/4 NE. At 19:00 the wind dropped and the current carries them toward land, so they decide to anchor, having the Isla de los Reyes to the NW at 3 leagues. They are heading for the Bahia de San Gregorio
NAVEGAN AL N REGISTRANDO TODAS LAS ENSEN: They sail north, surveying all the inlets of the coast. That afternoon they recognize the Bahia de Spring. At nightfall they are near the Isla de los Reyes
NAVEGAN CAPEANDO. A LAS 15:00 AQMAINO AL: They sail hove to. At 15:00 the wind eases somewhat and shifts to the S. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
NAVEGAN CON EL CABO CORRIENTES A CORTA D: They sail with Cabo Corrientes a short distance away, heading for Cabo de San Antonio
NAVEGAN HASTA FONDEAR A MEDIA MILLA DE L: They sail until anchoring half a mile from land at the mouth of the port of Santa Cruz, surrounded by shoals. Describes the port. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
NB ? DE LOG IS DIT ETMAAL MET 1, OP 10 M: NB [?] of log, this day's run has been made up by 1, to 10 miles.
NB BUITEN DE MIDDAG: 42° 24'. GEBETERDE: NB outside noon: 42° 24'. Corrected course and distance: [?] 1/2 E. 19,25 miles.
NB VAN ARIE VAN HAARST 38°0' LENGTE 334°: North latitude of Arie van Haarst 38°0' longitude 334°46'
NB VAN ARIE VAN HAARST IS 38°7' LENGTE 3: North latitude of Arie van Haarst is 38°7' longitude 335°22'. North latitude of Krijn Rutjes is 38°0' longitude 334°46'
NB VAN HET SCHIP VAN ARIE VAN HAARST 34°: North latitude of the ship of Arie van Haarst 34°6' longitude 328°57'. The north latitude of Captain Coster 34°5' longitude 329°30'
NB VAN KAPTEIN MULDER 37°34' LENGTE 335°: North latitude of Captain Mulder 37°34' longitude 335°12. North latitude of Captain Coster 37°34' longitude 334°40'
NB VAN SCHIPPER HULT IS 35°11' LENGTE 33: North latitude of Captain Hult is 35°11' longitude 331°5'. North latitude of Captain Arie van Haarst 35°1' longitude 330°4'
NB. WARE BEKOMEN LENGTE IS STEEDS TIJDME: NB. The true longitude obtained is always from chronometer no. 51
NB: ANDER HANDSCHRIFT. NU BEGINT HET ETM: NB: Different handwriting. Now the day begins at 0.00 hours.
NB: BIJ DE NUMMERING VAN HET AANTAL OVER: NB: In numbering the deaths the journal keeper skipped two deaths. Starting with Teunis Willems I keep my own numbering.
NB: VERSCHIL GIS LENGTE EN GEOBSERVEERDE: NB: The difference between estimated longitude and observed longitude is extremely large
Take 3 observations between sun and moon. Found the longitude 357°56'
NEMEN DE LENGTE OP ZEE AAN DE STER DE PO: Take the longitude at sea from the star Pollux, found 4° 5' 14''
NEMEN HET BESTEK OP VAN DE ANDERE SCHEPE: Take the position of the other ships sailing along. At the same time the compasses are adjusted.
NEMEN HET BESTEK VAN DE ANDERE SCHEPEN: Take the position of the other ships
NIET MEER DAN 2,5 TOT 3 MIJL ZICHT DOOR: No more than 2,5 to 3 miles visibility because of hazy sky
NIETS ONTWAARD DAN ZWARTE MEEUWEN EN ZUI: Nothing noticed except black gulls and southern birds
NIETS ONTWAARD. JAN WILLEM SCHAUKELJEN A: Nothing noticed. Jan Willem Schaukeljen died of his wounds, was no longer conscious (No. 1)
NIETS VAN TOP TE ZIEN: Nothing to be seen of the top
NIETTEGENSTAANDE HET KOMPAS 8° TE VEEL N: Despite the compass being 8° too far NW, set to north 17'
NIEUWE MAAN. BESTEK VAN KAPITEIN OOSTHUI: New moon. Position of Captain Oosthuijse: S 3/4 E. 22,5. 17°36'. 349°47'. 11°35'.
NIEUWE MAAN. KONDEN HET HOGE LAND VAN SU: New moon. Could see the high land of Sumatra from NNW to E by S, on which last bearing we saw the high peak of Kijzers Eiland.
NIEUWE SCHUTROL GEMAAKT. HEBBEN ENIGE ZI: New duty roster made. Have some sick
NMW: GROTE OEFENING MET GESCHUT EN GEWEE: NMW: Great exercise with guns and muskets
NMW: KREGEN EEN OPPERMEESTER MET ZIJN GO: NMW: Received a chief master with his belongings aboard. Again received some foreigners aboard.
NMW: ZAGEN EEN SCHILDPAD DRIJVEN. ZETTEN: NMW: Saw a turtle floating. Put out a boat and it was caught by a Black sailor who dived after it. It was a hawksbill turtle that weighed 40 pounds
NO CONCUERDA LA REFERENCIA DE DIRECCIÓN: The wind direction reference in the table (O) does not match that of the attached text (L)
NO DA POR BUENA LA OBSERVACION: Does not accept the observation as good
NO DA POR BUENA LA OBSERVACION. DATOS DE: Does not accept the observation as good. Data from noon or from the day's run, although there is barely any data
NO DA PUNTO DE REFERENCIA NI DISTANCIA R: Gives no reference point or distance covered. Says some frigatebirds have been seen.
NO ESTÁN LAS PRIMERAS PÁGINAS DEL DIARIO: The first pages of the diary are missing, so not all the data of the header fields are available. The port of departure has been taken from the reference given on the first page of the diary that exists.

The first pages of the diary are missing, so not all the data of the header fields are available. The port of departure has been taken from the reference given on the first page of the diary that exists. It is signed by Francisco Evias.
NO HAY CORRECCION POR SER CONOCIDA LA DI: No correction, because the difference to the N due to the currents of the Canal de Bahama is known
NO HAY DATOS DE POSICIÓN. DÍA DE LLEGADA: No position data. Day of arrival at Cádiz
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO NI DIRECCIÓN DEL V: No course data or wind direction at noon
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VI: No course and wind direction data
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO Y VIENTO A MEDIODÍ: No course and wind data at noon. The ship's name is the alias of Nª Sª del Valle, whose earlier voyage Cádiz-La Habana has been recorded
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO Y VIENTO EN LA TAB: No course and wind data in the table
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO Y VIENTO HASTA LAS: No course and wind data until 6 in the evening, which are the ones taken for this day. The data have been taken as follows: state of the sea at noon and, failing that, at dusk or dawn. Observed latitude and, failing that, arrival latitude. The commanding ship of the convoy is the Miño.
NO HAY DATOS DE RUMBO, VIENTO, NI DESCRI: No course, wind or weather description data
