At 3 o'clock the navigator's apprentice J. W. van Praag died of the prevailing sickness
OM 3 UURE PEIJLDEN HET WESTHOOFT ZUIJDEN: At 3 o'clock sighted the west headland to the south by the magnetic compass, 2½ miles from us; SSE true bears ahead of us
OM 4 UUR NA DE MIDDAG PASSEERDE HET SCHI: At 4 in the afternoon the ship passed the lighthouse of Cape Recife.
OM 4 UUR PASSEERDE DE UTRECHT DE TROPICU: At 4 o'clock the Utrecht passed the Tropic of Cancer
OM 4H30 OVERLEED DE HEER GENERAAL MAJOOR: At 4H30 died Major General J. Vererer, commander-in-chief of the expedition to the coast of Guinea, Knight of the Military William Order and of the Order of the Netherlands Lion.
OM 5 UUR (PV) WESTELIJKSTE LAND NNW 3/4: At 5 o'clock (PV) westernmost land NNW 3/4 W and the easternmost ENE
OM 5.30 UUR DW, KRIJGEN DE WIND OPEENS U: At 5.30 DW, the wind suddenly came from the NW with heavy rain and a dark sky, so that we could see nothing more.
OM 6 UUR ('S AVONDS) ZIEN DE MAANECLIPS,: At 6 o'clock (in the evening) saw the lunar eclipse; at 7 o'clock about 1/3 of the moon darkened. At 8 o'clock it had ended.
OM 6 UUR: ZHOEK KRAKATAU ONO1/4O. OHOEK: At 6 o'clock: S point of Krakatau ENE 1/4 E. E point of the Keizerlijk Eiland N by W 1/4 W. NE point of Princen Eiland SE 1/2 E
OM 6.30 UUR ZAGEN DIEGO GARCIA IN HET NN: At 6.30 saw Diego Garcia in the NNW, gave up the ship after deliberation.
OM 7 UUR WENDEN ZIJ OM DE ZZO. VM: WENDE: At 7 o'clock they tacked toward the SSE. Forenoon: tacked toward the W.
OM 8 UREN OVERLEED DEN MATTROOS JOHAN JO: At 8 o'clock the sailor Johan Jong died.
OM 8 UUR PEILEN ANTIQUA WNW EN GUADELOUP: At 8 o'clock took bearings: Antiqua WNW and Guadeloupe SSW. At 12 o'clock took bearings: the middle of Antiqua W 1/4 N. This gives 61º 28' longitude.
OM CIRCA 5 UUR KREGEN ZE EEN SCHOENER IN: At about 5 o'clock they sighted a schooner, with which they nearly collided. 'Meanwhile the said schooner ran so close astern of us that it hit the spanker boom.'
OM HALF 1 WAS HET BESTEK VAN DE NEPTUNUS: At half past 12 the position of the Neptunus was: 37 degrees 22 minutes north latitude and 325 degrees 16 minutes longitude; of the Joan de Witt: 37 degrees 24 minutes north latitude and 325 degrees 7 minutes longitude; of the Ajax: 37 degrees 23 minutes north latitude and 325 degrees 14 minutes longitude.

At half past 12 the position of the Neptunus was: 49 degrees 6 minutes north latitude and 9 degrees 49 minutes longitude; of the Joan de Witt: 49 degrees 7 minutes north latitude and 8 degrees 6 minutes longitude; of the Ajax: 49 degrees 11 minutes north latitude and 9 degrees 21 minutes longitude.
OM HALF 2 PASSEREN DE TROPICUS OP 27° 16: At half past 1 they crossed the Tropic at 27° 16' W longitude (in the early morning).
OM HALF 3 'S MIDDAGS WAS DE GEOBSERVEERD: At half past 3 in the afternoon the observed longitude of the Cortenaar was 77 degrees 40 minutes, of the Pluto 77 degrees 33 minutes, and ours 77 degrees 47 minutes.
OM HALF 7 IN DE PV KAAP FEBURON NO 1/2 N: At half past 7 in the [?] Cape Feburon NE 1/2 N.
OM HALF FELL TWEE DONDER, BLIKSEM EN STO: At half past 2 [?] thunder, lightning and downpours.
OM MIDDERNACHT WENDEN OM DE OOST OM HET: At midnight tacked toward the east to avoid Coringa Island. In the forenoon, with the wind decreasing, sighted an island to the W by S of us. At a distance of 1 mile, at the same time sighted a sandy reef just above water to the WNW of us. Estimated the island to be Coringa Island. The sandy reef is not shown on the chart. Remark by Captain D. Hofker: The island that I saw and took for Coringa Island I placed at 16 25'20". To the NNE of the island I also discovered a reef or sandbank. The island is about 1/8 mile long, with a reef of 1/16 mile where the sea broke heavily.
OM VERSCHILLENDE REDENEN WENSTE IK HET L: For various reasons I wished to bring the general's body to the Netherlands, for which I had no other means than to pack the body into a half-leaguer cask and fill it with genever. Making a chest was out of the question, as there would not have been enough genever on board for it. So I had it done, filled the cask with 210 kan of genever and stowed it in the carpenter's storeroom, where it could lie undisturbed.
OM? U. CRACATOU. OM? U. TER REEDE VAN AN: At [?] o'clock Cracatou. At [?] o'clock in the roads of Anjer.
At [?] o'clock Goudstaart NE. Took the position.
OMDAT DE TIJDMETERS BIJ GEBREK AAN GELEG: Because the chronometers had not been set with certainty, for lack of opportunity at Falmouth, we decided to sail within sight of Madera in order to verify our position.
OMLOPENDE WINDEN, BUIIG.HAALDEN EEN DER: Shifting winds, squally. Hauled one of the heavy ropes from aft out of the hold, and sheets that were forward in the cable tier. Issued flour.
ONBEKEND SYMBOOL IN KOLOM WINDRICHTING: Unknown symbol in the wind direction column.
ONBEKEND TEKEN IN KOLOM BREEDTE: Unknown sign in the latitude column.
ONBEPAALD GESTRAFT, KROM IN DE BOEIEN EN: Punished indefinitely: the boatswain's mate C. de Keijzer, shackled doubled up in irons and on water and bread, for not following orders given to him by the skipper and afterwards insulting remarks toward the chief petty officer.
ONDER BEVONDEN BREEDTE STAAT 3' ZUID. BE: Under found latitude stands 3' south. Position Captain Grave: 18°48'. 345°2'. 19°48'. Position Captain Oosthuijse: SSW. 21,75. 19°55'. 347°33'. 19°54'.
ONDER DE KUST VAN ZUID-AMERIKA, GEEN LEN: Along the coast of South America, no longitude and latitude any more. On 31 January the ship anchored at Braamspunt.
ONDER DE PORTUGEZE KUST TE VERVALLEN: To fall to leeward under the Portuguese coast.
ONDER HET SYMBOOL VOOR DE ZEETOESTAND ST: Under the symbol for sea state there are two more strokes; these do not appear in the list of symbols, however.
ONDER WARE BEKOMEN LENGTE WORDT HIER DE: By true obtained longitude, the obtained corrected longitude is meant here.
ONDER ZEIL IN DE HONDEWACHT VAN KAAP DE: Under sail in the dog watch from the Cape of Good Hope to St. Helena.
ONDER ZEIL, ZETTEN KOERS LANGS DE WAL NA: Under sail, set course along the shore to St. Eustatius.
ONDER ZEIL. VERANDERDE MERIDIAAN OM DE W: Under sail. Changed meridian to the west, 4 miles.
ONDER ZEIL. VOEREN OP DE RIO DE LA PLATA: Under sail. Sailed on the Rio de la Plata.
ONDERKUIJPER HENDRIK STAAL VAN OSNABRUGG: Assistant cooper Hendrik Staal of Osnabrugge and soldier Leendert Hageman of Utrecht and soldier Pieter Jacob Doulag of Iperen died.
ONDERSTUURMAN EN BOOTSMAN KRIJGEN WOORDE: Second mate and boatswain have words.
ONDERZEIL EN OP ENKHUISEN AAN. 'S MIDDAG: Under sail and headed for Enkhuisen. At noon at anchor.
ONDERZEIL NAAR DE BOVENKUST. OP 29 APRIL: Under sail to the upper coast. Departed from Prinsies on 29 April. Only now latitude and longitude data.
ONDERZEILSKOELTE-GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELT: Lower-sail breeze to reefed topsail breeze.
ONDERZOCHTEN KLEINE EILANDJES VOOR DE KU: Examined small islets off the coast of South Poggij.
ONDUIDELIJK OF HET GAAT OM EEN BUI EN ZE: Unclear whether it concerns a squall and a setting sky or a squall-setting sky.
ONDUIDELIJK VERHAAL OVER VERKEERDE BEREK: Unclear account of a wrong calculation. 14 miles, which amounts to 1gr.4min.
ONGELIJKE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MARSZEILSKO: Uneven topgallant breeze and topsail breeze.
ONGEMEEN HECHT WATER. ZIEN VEEL GROEN EN: Unusually thick water. See much greenery and other seaweed floating. A multitude of birds near the ship.
ONGESTADIGDE KOELTE OPWERKENDE BUIIGE LU: Unsteady breeze, squally sky building up.
ONGESTADIGE BETROKKEN EN OPHELDERENDE OV: Unsteady, overcast and clearing, passing squally sky.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILS: Unsteady topgallant breeze and topgallant breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN FLAUWE KO: Unsteady topgallant breeze and light breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MARSZEILS: Unsteady topgallant breeze and topsail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MEERDERE: Unsteady topgallant breeze and stronger breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MINDERE K: Unsteady topgallant breeze and lesser breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN STIJVE BR: Unsteady topgallant breeze and stiff topgallant breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE TOT MARSZEIL: Unsteady topgallant breeze to topsail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE-GEREEFDE MAR: Unsteady topgallant breeze to reefed topsail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE BRAMZEILSKOELTE-MARSZEILSKOE: Unsteady topgallant breeze to topsail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN: Unsteady reefed topsail breeze and decreasing breeze.
Unsteady reefed topsail breeze and topgallant breeze.
Unsteady reefed topsail breeze and lesser breeze.
Unsteady reefed topsail breeze and lower-sail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEMENDE: Unsteady topsail breeze and decreasing breeze.
ONGESTADIGE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILS: Unsteady topsail breeze and topgallant breeze.
ONGESTADIGE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN GEREEFDE: Unsteady topsail breeze and reefed topsail breeze.
ONGESTADIGE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN STIJVE BR: Unsteady topsail breeze and stiff topgallant breeze.
ONGESTADIGE MARSZEILSKOELTE-BRAMZEILSKOE: Unsteady topsail breeze to topgallant breeze.
ONGESTADIGE OVERDRIJVENDE BEWOLKTE EN BE: Unsteady, passing cloudy and overcast sky.
ONGESTADIGE WEER VAN WINDEN EN KOELTE ME: Unsteady weather with winds and breezes, with a thick, overcast, squally sky.
ONGESTUIJMIG MET EEN HOOGE ZEE, STORTEND: Tempestuous with a high sea, a breaking sea in which the ship worked violently. Lay with the 8 glasses of the [?] with the bowsprit to the west.
ONS BESTEK 16,5 MIJL TE OOSTELIJK. HET L: Our position was 16.5 miles too far east. The land they sighted yesterday as the NW point of Fortarentura is the W point of that island.
ONS BESTEK 17 MEIJLEN TE WESTELIJK STOND: Our position was 17 miles too far west.
ONS BESTEK ZIJN AANVANG NEMENDE VAN DE Z: Our position, taking its start from the south latitude of 35° 0' and longitude 35° 37'. Changed longitude 0° 2'.
ONS VOORNEMEN WAS NA T VADERLANDT: Our intention was to go to the fatherland.
ONSTOTEN DEN SOLDAAT JEAN CHAMBER UIT DE: Released the soldier Jean Chamber from the irons with the recommendation never to undertake such [?] again, which he had done yesterday.
ONTDEKKEN EEN ZIEKTE ONDER DE BEMANNING,: Discovered a sickness among the crew, already 16 in their bunks with severe headaches, tightness in the belly and lameness in all limbs; nursed the sufferers under the gangways and the half deck. Fumigated the ship from time to time.
ONTDEKKEN TWEE EILANDEN. BIJ BEREKENING: Discovered two islands. By calculation of the true obtained latitude the islands lie S and N of each other (estimated distance from each other 5 miles). One island lies at 40 deg. 51 min. and is given the name Dinae. The other island is given the name Masseveen, which lies at 41 deg. 13 min. 'and by estimate [?] 43 deg. 40 min.' (?)
ONTDEKKEN VERSCHEIDENE BRETSCHILDPADDEN,: Discovered several [?] turtles, caught 2 of them.
ONTDEKKEN ZWARE BRANDING, MAAR ZIEN GEEN: Discovered heavy surf, but saw no land because of the thick haze in the SW to NW. By estimate 0.75 miles. Deviation to the west [?] miles. Change of longitude 0° 29'. Afternoon watch: saw the surf in the [?] but still no land because of the thick haze.
ONTDEKTE ALS VERSCHIJDE NOORD KAPERS EN: Discovered several northern privateers and 2 pintails.
ONTDEKTEN DAT 'T EILAND AMSTERDAM 10 GRA: Discovered that the island of Amsterdam was placed 10 degrees 0 minutes too far north on the chart of Van Keulen. Longitude obtained since the last one: 93 degrees 48 minutes.
ONTDEKTEN DE VASTE KUST VAN AFRIKA OP DE: Discovered the mainland coast of Africa at the latitude of the river Cijpriano.
Discovered seaweed for the first time.
ONTMOETEN EEN ENGELSE VLOOT VAN 14 OORLO: Met an English fleet of 14 warships, which were cruising against the French.
ONTMOETTEN DE OOST-INDISCHE RETOURVLOOT,: Met the East Indies return fleet and hailed the ship Oud-Haarlem, which was coming from China. Obtained the longitude 341°52.
ONTSLAAN MATROOS PIETER LEE UIT DE BOEIE: Released sailor Pieter Lee from the irons.
ONTSLAGEN UIT DE BOEIEN DE 2E ZEILMAKER: Released from the irons the 2nd sailmaker J.W. Hamel and Krom. Confined in irons on water and bread the 2nd cooper, acting steward P. van het Hof, because of a significant shortage of the sick bread, this having been stored in the bread room in his keeping.
ONTSLOEGEN DE EERSTE TIMMERMAN S. HUISMA: Released the first carpenter S. Huisman from the irons.
ONTSLOEGEN DE GESTRAFTE MATROOS ANTONIE: Released the punished sailor Antonie from the same irons.
ONTVINGEN NEPTUNES MET DE GEBRUIKELIJKE: Received Neptune with the customary ceremonies.
ONTWAARDE DAT DE MUISEN EN ROTTEN HIER E: Noticed that the mice and rats had damaged the sails here and there; mended them. Even the cabin and quarters were not free of mice. Also got an increase of sick.
ONTWAARDEN DES MORGENS EEN KLIP WAARVAN: In the morning noticed a rock, a description of which is attached.
OOK DIT ETMAAL ZWARE DONDERBUIEN EN OMLO: Also this day heavy thunder squalls and shifting winds, at times completely calm.
OOK DOOR HOGE DEINING TEGEN HET RIF VAN: Also running into high swell against the reef of Aiguilles (Cape Agulhas?), on whose southernmost point we found ourselves. Therefore steered SE at 4 o'clock.
OOK HET SCHIP VAN P. MEIJER HAD EEN LEK: The ship of P. Meijer also had a leak.
OOK IS OVERLEDEN DEN MATTROOS GERRIT BRU: Also died the sailor Gerrit Brugman of Haarlem.
OOK IS OVERLEDEN DEN MATTROOS PIETERSE A: Also died the sailor Pieterse Augaart of Flensburg.
OOK VARIABEL EN STIL STERKE WEERLIGT IN: Also variable and calm, strong lightning all around.

OOSTELIJKSTE VAN DE WIJN COOPS BERGEN OT: The easternmost of the Wijn Coops Bergen [?], estimated 2,5 to [?] miles. Sunset: the westernmost land that could be seen NW and the easternmost NNE, estimated [?] miles. NB. They were not the Wijn Koops Bergen, but double high land.
OP 1 FEBRUARI UIT FRUXILLO VERTROKKEN NA: On 1 February departed from Fruxillo for Havana.
OP 10 VAAM TEN ANKER OM TIJ TE STOPPEN: At 10 fathoms came to anchor to stem the tide.
OP 15 FEBRUARI OVERLEED NO 4, MATROOS FR: On 15 February died no. 4, sailor Frederik Busch of Statijn.
OP 22 JUNI VAART HET SCHIP NAAR ST. PIER: On 22 June the ship sails to St. Pierre (Martinique), then to Basse Terre (Guadeloupe), and back again to St. Pierre.
OP 22-10 KWAMEN TEN ANKER VOOR PARAMARIB: On 22-10 came to anchor before Paramaribo.
OP 23 JANUARI 1834 KOMT J.J. RAMMELMAN E: On 23 January 1834 J.J. Rammelman Elsevier comes aboard, together with family and slaves, among them one Francisco Rosseman; the other slaves are named by first name only.
OP 25 FEBRUARI 1788 VERTREKT HET SCHIP V: On 25 February 1788 the ship departs from Parimaribo and then sails via Bramspunt to Demerarij. On Sunday 9 March course is set for St. Eustatius.
OP 25 MAART 1851 VAREN ZE WEG UIT HELLEV: On 25 March 1851 they sail away from Hellevoetsluis.
OP 3 JULI DESERTEERDE DE MATROOS FRANCOO: On 3 July the sailor Francooijs Michel deserted.
OP 30 VAAM ROOD EN WIT ZAND. DW: WAREN O: At 30 fathoms red and white sand. Day watch: were on a bank.
OP 31 MEI DESERTEERDEN DE BOOTSMAN JACOB: On 31 May the boatswain Jacob Cornelis Quast and the under-master Johannes de Vries of Rotterdam deserted.
On 5 September in the roads of Riouw.
OP 6 NOVEMBER OVERLEED LUIT GUICHARD, OP: On 6 November died Luit Guichard, on 22 December died M.A. de Smidt of Roijen.
OP 9 FEBRUARI OVERLEED EEN VROUWSLAAF, N: On 9 February a female slave died, no. 30. Still 219 living slaves in the ship. On 24 February died the ship's corporal Johannes Jacobus Janse. On 5 March a girl slave died, no. 31. 218 slaves sold.
OP ADVIES VAN DE CHIRURG MAJOOR WORD ER: On the advice of the surgeon Majoor, given the growing number of sick, it was decided to return to Curacao and not to go to Porte Cabello again.
OP BEZOEK OP DE HAVICK: On a visit to the Havick.
OP D' MIDDAG WAS D' GEENERALE GECOPPELDE: At noon the general combined course and distance since yesterday's bearing of the island Wight: WSW 2/3 W, 12 miles. Because of the thick haze we could not get the latitude.
OP DE AMW PRAAIDE SIJMON HOOGERZEIL EN H: In the afternoon watch hailed Sijmon Hoogerzeil, who had 17,5 fish and 220 barrels of blubber.
OP DE DIEPTE VAM 10 VAADEMS, TEN ANKER G: At a depth of 10 fathoms, came to anchor.
OP DE EW ZAGEN WE 3 VUURBALLEN UIT DE LU: In the first watch we saw 3 fireballs fall from the sky.
OP DE EW: NOORDERLICHT. ZEEWATERTEMPERAT: In the first watch: northern lights. Sea water temperature at noon.
OP DE GRONDE EN IN HET KANAAL: On the grounds and in the Channel.
OP DE GRONDE. ZAGEN? SCHEPEN ÉÉN TOONDE: On the grounds. Saw [?] ships, one showed a Dutch flag.
OP DE GRONDEN. SCHIPPER POT (KOOPVAARDER: On the grounds. Hailed Captain Pot (merchantman in the convoy). He had a leak in his ship.
OP DE HOLLANDSE KAART LIGT FERNANDE W 1/: On the Dutch chart Fernande lies W 1/2 S, 20 miles. According to the English chart 119 miles.
OP DE KAART VAN J.W. NORIE UITGEGEVEN IN: On the chart of J.W. Norie published in 1816 the islands Deniu and Marseveen lie 10 miles NNW and SSE of each other, but whether those islands exist, or at least lie where they are placed on the chart, I greatly doubt, since according to our reckoning, which was good, they should have been seen by us.
OP DE KUST VAN ZUID-AMERIKA. ER VOLGEN L: On the coast of South America. Lists follow of the sale of the slaves and of the deaths among slaves and crew.
OP DE MIDDAG HADDEN VOLGENS DIEN HET EIJ: At noon, according to that, we had the island Madeira by the corrected longitude due east 4,5 miles from us, and according to our reckoning east 8 miles. In future I will record only the compass bearing (due east).
At noon took bearings: the west point of St. Christopher WSW, 2 miles, and the south side of St Eustatius W 1/2 S, 3 or 4 miles from us.
OP DE MIDDAG PEILDEN BOVENGEMELDE PIEKEN: At noon the above-mentioned peaks bore as above, and the point named above SW 1/2 S.
OP DE MIDDAG PIJLDE HAIJERIL IN 'T ZTW 1: At noon took bearings: Haijeril in the SSW 1/2 W, and the point of Fitle bore [?], and the south point of Hitland NE 1/2 E.
OP DE MIDDAG STIL MET MOOI WEER. GEBETER: At noon calm with fine weather. Corrected course and distance SSW 1/8 W, 15 miles.
OP DE MIDDAG WAS DE GENERALE KOERS VAN H: At noon the general course of the day had remained in the same direction without any progress made. Consultation about the reckoning with the commander.
At noon the clock shows 45' fast.
OP DE MIDDAG: WIJDERS ? ONGEREEFDE MZK,: At noon: furthermore [?] unreefed [?], put a reef in it …?
OP DE VOORMIDDAG WAS DE ZEE ZEER ONSTUIM: In the forenoon the sea was very rough, which obliged us to reduce sail although the wind had lessened. We were at that time at 41 8 S and 21 12 E, the place where on the chart of Novie the doubtful island Maartevleer lies.
OP DEN MIDDAG WARENDE LINIE EQUINOCTIAAL: At noon, being on the line, passed the equinoctial.
OP DEZE DATUM WORDT VOOR HET EERST DE BA: On this date the barometer reading is mentioned for the first time. The reading is described as: 28 inches 4 lines.
OP DIEPTE VAN 58 VAAM GEBROKEN SCHULPGRO: At a depth of 58 fathoms broken shell bottom with some small stones.
OP DONDERDAG 25 MEI OVERLEED JOHANNES PA: On Thursday 25 May died Johannes Pavelt, on 1 June began making the women's house, Willem Bok died 5 June.
OP EEN KAART VAN PIETER GOOS HADDEN WIJ: On a chart by Pieter Goos we had the island Desinda W 13 miles from us. And according to the charts of Van Keulen we had already sailed over the land.
OP HET SCHIP VAN SCHIPPER RAANES WAS RUZ: On the ship of Captain Raanes there was a quarrel between the crew and the captain; the commander intervened, after which it became calm again.
OP PAGINA 155 INFORMATIE OVER WEER EN WI: On page 155 information on weather and wind along the coast of Guinea.
OP SATURDAG DEN 22 MAART WIERD ER OP BAT: On Saturday 22 March a heavy execution was carried out at Batavia of three Europeans: a gunner's mate who had stabbed the boatswain to death, who was hanged after his right hand was chopped off; and two sodomites, one of whom was only 16 years old, both hanged; and then a black man who had murdered a captain, who was broken on the wheel alive without receiving the mercy stroke; and then 13 more flogged, which I went to see in the morning at 7 o'clock.
OP SCHIP REVOLUTIE BREEKT IN AMW DE FOKK: On the ship a revolution breaks out. In the afternoon watch the foreyard [?].
OPENEN 'S EDELE OI COMPAGNIES SECRETE PA: Opened the Noble East India Company's secret papers.
OPGAVE VAN POSITIES DOOR DE SCHEPEN IN H: Report of positions by the ships in the squadron. Utrecht: 9° 0' S, 97° 3' E. Goes?: 9° 0' S, 97° 0' E. Prices Louisa: 9° 0' S, 98° 19' E. Juno: 8° 59' S, 96° 19' E. Wassenaar: 8° 59' S, 97° 42' E.
OPGAVE VAN POSITIES DOOR DE SCHEPEN VAN: Report of positions by the ships of the squadron. Utrecht: 5° 0' S, 94° 34' E. Goes: 5° 0' S, 94° 33' E. Princes Louisa: -------. Juno: 5° 0' S, 93° 59' E. Wassenaar: 5° 0' S, 95° 19' E.
OPKLARENDE WEDER DIKKE BUIIGE LUCHT TOT: Clearing weather, thick squally sky until the sky cleared again.
OPMERKING OVER BESTEK VOLGENS RONDE KAAR: Remark about the reckoning according to the round chart.
OPMERKING OVER DAT TIJDMETER N:9 EEN AAN: Remark that chronometer N:9 had a considerable difference.
OPMERKING OVER DE VREEMDE POSITIEBEPALIN: Remark about the strange position determination of the Messeurs.
OPMERKING OVER HET BESTEK EN DE LIGGING: Remark about the reckoning and the position of Madeira. HV: east point of Porto Sancto NW. See the east point of Madeira SW. See also the Sertres. Meridian west of Lezar 121,25 miles. At anchor: west point of the bay, the castle De Leeuw north, the east point of the bay [?].
OPMERKING OVER HOOGTE EN AFSTANDEN EN DE: Remark about altitude and distances and the almanac of Cadiz.
OPMERKINGEN OVER AFSTAND EN HOOGTE IN GR: Remarks about distance and altitude in degrees, minutes and seconds, a comparison with a Spanish nautical almanac and the meridian of Tenerife.
Remarks on the dead reckoning and position.
OPMERKINGEN OVER DE KAART VAN HEATHER EN: Remarks on the chart of Heather and that of Norie 1829. Ditto on the chronometers
OPMERKINGEN OVER DE PEILINGEN EN DE KAAR: Remarks on the soundings and the chart of Purdy and the charts of Norie from 1822 and 1825 and the current. At sunset saw the high land of Granada in NW and NW to W
OPMERKINGEN OVER DE RICHTING VAN DE STRO: Remarks on the direction of the current and the dead reckoning
OPMERKINGEN OVER DE STROOM EN DE SNELHEI: Remarks on the current and the speed of the ship in the original
OPMERKINGEN OVER DE STROOM EN SNELHEID V: Remarks on the current and speed of the ship
OPMERKINGEN OVER DIVERSE KAARTEN EN DE L: Remarks on various charts and the lie of the coast. Remarks on the chronometers
OPMERKINGEN OVER HET BESTEK OP DEZE POSI: Remarks on the dead reckoning at this position (difficult to make up). Cannot yet sound the bottom
OPMERKINGEN OVER HET BESTEK. WORDT BIJGE: Remarks on the dead reckoning. Being adjusted
OPMERKINGEN OVER KAARTGEGEVENS. IMAGE 00: Remarks on chart data. Image 0014 observations.
OPMERKINGEN OVER LIGGING PHILIPSBURG: Remarks on the position of Philipsburg
OPMERKINGEN OVER PLAATS VAN SINT ANTONIO: Remarks on the place of Sint Antonio on the charts
OPMERKINGEN OVER STROOMVERSCHILLEN EN WI: Remarks on differences in current and wind force
OPPER EN ONDERSTUURMAN NAAR DE BURGH. DI: First and second mate to the Burgh, which is heavily damaged. I go to the Burgh with the merchant Engelbertus C. Stoesak. Meeting [?] the Honourable Armenaut, chief merchant and head of Japan
OPPERCONSTAPEL ERNST HENDRIK FIETTE OVER: Chief gunner Ernst Hendrik Fiette died, no. 21
OPPERCONSTAPEL HARMANUS VAN SELDAM, OVER: Chief gunner Harmanus van Seldam, died
OPPERKUIJPER JAN VAN WEESEL, GEBOORTE VA: Chief cooper Jan van Weesel, born in Gastel, died
OPPERSCHIPPER KAREL METSKER OVERBOORD EN: Chief skipper Karel Metsker overboard and drowned
OPPERSTUURMAN LEENDERT KOMMERS VAN MIDDE: First mate Leendert Kommers of Middelburg died
OPPERSTUURMAN PIETER MARTENSZ KRAAIJ NA: First mate Pieter Martensz Kraaij died after a short illness of the so-called miserere. Burial: carried around the pit 3 times, followed by all the petty officers, with the flag at half-mast.
OPPERZEILMAKER HERMANNIS BURGERMANS IN D: Chief sailmaker Hermannis Burgermans in irons; he struck the boatswain with his hands under the forecastle
OPWERKENDE BUIJIGE LUCHT MET REGEN V/H Z: Beating up, squally sky with rain from the SW and subsequently clear sky.
ORDERS VAN KAPITEIN MEUZER OM TE BLIJVEN: Orders from Captain Meuzer to stay lying to
OS AAN BOORD, EN 2 MAN UIT DE BOEIEN: Ox on board, and 2 men out of irons
OTRO PTO. REFERENCIA: CABO SAN VICENTE A: Other reference point: Cabo San Vicente at E 36º S, distance 29 leagues.
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: CABO DE SANTA: Other reference point: Cabo de Santa María, at N 1/4 NE, distance 15 1/3 leagues.
Other reference point: Cabo de Santa María, at N 6º E, distance 18 leagues. No general weather data.
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: ISLA DE FLORES: Other reference point: Isla de Flores at N, distance 78 leagues.
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: LA TIERRA MÁS: Other reference point: the nearest land, at W 1/4 NW, distance 35 leagues.
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: OVESSANT AL E: Other reference point: Ovessant at E 1/4 SE, 17 leagues
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: OVESSANT AL NE: Other reference point: Ovessant at NE 1/4 N, 42 leagues
OTRO PUNTO DE REFERENCIA: PUNTA DE NAGA: Other reference point: Punta de Naga at SW 1/4 W, distance 44 leagues
OTROS PUNTOS DE REFERENCIA: CABO ESPICHE: Other reference points: Cabo Espichel at N 52º E, distance 59 leagues. Cabo La Roca at N 43º E, distance 61 leagues.
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN DEN JONG MATROOS PIET: The young sailor Pieter Hommus van der Werth fell overboard and died
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN VERDRONKEN DE JONG: The boy Roelog van den Berge of Middelburgh fell overboard and drowned
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN VERDRONKEN DE SOLD: The soldier A. Lust fell overboard and drowned
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN EN VERONGELUKT HUISTI: House carpenter Pieter Blommerd of Steenbergen fell overboard and was killed. 52 sick.
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN SOLDAAT WILLEM WILLE: Soldier Willem Wille from Meijrighause fell overboard. Died: sailors Jan Willem Steinboom from Ham and Anton Wally from Fustenberg, and soldier Pieter Wijnbrender from Ankeschout
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN UIT DE BAZAANSRUST DE: The under-cooper Jacobus Pikhart of Middelburg fell overboard from the mizzen channels
OVERBOORD GEVALLEN: MATROOS HENDRIK VAN: Sailor Hendrik van Weyeren of Leiden fell overboard
OVERD. LEDEN MAXIM EVERING UIT TER GOES,: Deceased: Maxim Evering from ter Goes, craftsman.
OVERDRIJVENDE EN BETROKKEN LUCHT WEER OV: Passing and overcast sky, weather again passing and clear sky
OVERDRIJVENDE LUCHT BUIIGE VERSTOPTE KIM: Passing sky, squally, obscured horizon, changing to cloudy and clear sky
OVERDRIJVENDE LUCHT HELDERE LUCHT GOED W: Passing sky, clear sky, good weather
OVERDRIJVENDE LUCHT HELDERE LUCHT MOOI W: Passing sky, clear sky, fine weather
OVERDRIJVENDE LUCHT OOK DROOG GOED WEER: Passing sky, also dry, good weather
OVERDRIJVENDE LUCHT OOK GOED DROOG WEER: Passing sky, also good dry weather
OVERDRIJVENDE TOT BUIIGE LUCHT, WEDER EE: Passing to squally sky, again clearing a little
OVERDRIJVENDE TRAVATIGE LUCHT BUIEN GOED: Passing squally sky, squalls, good weather
OVERIGE BESTEKKEN VAN HET ESKADER: UTREC: Other reckonings of the squadron: Utrecht: 8°57'. 104°16'. Goes: 9°0'. 104°3'. Princes Louisa: 9°0. 105°25'. Juno: 9°3'. 103°26'
OVERIGE LENGTEN: LIJCOCTHON 15,23. HUIS: Other longitudes: Lijcocthon 15,23. Huis ten Donk 16,53. Hoff d'Uno 15,33. Akerendam 16,53. Average 16 degrees 10 minutes 1/2 (they take this as the new longitude; should they not see St Helena today on course NW, then keep steering NW, then NW to N to be sure of coming east of Ascension)
OVERIGE SCHEPEN, DIE MEEVAREN (WAARONDER: The other ships sailing along (including Revolutie, Tromp and Bravo) are expected to submit their reckoning.
OVERLEDE MATROOS LEENDERT PAUW VAN MOORD: Sailor Leendert Pauw of Moordrecht died.
OVERLEDEN 2E SCHIEMANSMAAT T. ARRALSEN: Second boatswain's mate T. Arralsen died
OVERLEDEN 3E STUURMAN G. BROERTJES (AAN: Third mate G. Broertjes died (from the effects of Batavian sickness)
OVERLEDEN 3E WAAK ANTHONIE BERTRAM GEBOO: Third watchman Anthonie Bertram, native of Heijmen, died
OVERLEDEN 3E WAAK, HENDRIK EVERTSZ VAN O: Third watchman Hendrik Evertsz of Oosteroud died
OVERLEDEN ADOLBORST VOLUNTAIR F.W.H. VAN: Volunteer midshipman F.W.H. van de Velde died
OVERLEDEN BOEKHOUDER EN SEKRETARIS VAN D: Died: bookkeeper and secretary of the return fleet, Jan F. Sels of Kleefft.
OVERLEDEN BOTTELIER CHRISTOFFEL LIEPKE V: Died: steward Christoffel Liepke of Ekermunde.
OVERLEDEN BOTTELIER FRANSOEIJS SMOOR VAN: Died: steward Fransoeijs Smoor of Bresies. They have 90 invalids. Those who can still walk about did not notice the sickness lessening. Everything is being done to offer the crew comfort.
OVERLEDEN COMMANDEUR VAN DE SOLDATEN, DH: Died: commander of the soldiers, Mr Engelbert Menthen of Zutphen.
OVERLEDEN CONSTAPEL J. VAN ROSMALEN. ZIE: Died: gunner J. van Rosmalen. Saw a kind of [?] drifting past the ship. Sick: more than 100, and dead: 26.
OVERLEDEN DE BANDELING GENAAMD JAMIES VA: Died: the exile named Jamies of Seribon.
OVERLEDEN DE BEELDHOUWER ALBERTUS HOEDES: Died: the sculptor Albertus Hoedesman of Amsterdam.
OVERLEDEN DE BUSCHIETER KLAAS VAN VIJFHU: Died: the gunner Klaas van Vijfhuysen of Amsterdam.
OVERLEDEN DE CUIJPER JAN JOCHIM KIN, OVE: Died: the cooper Jan Jochim Kin, put overboard.
OVERLEDEN DE EUROPESE FOURIER DONDELBERI: Died: the European quartermaster Dondelberi. In irons: the first-class sailor P. Heinzien for neglect of duty, and the third-class sailor B. Broeksmit for not being present at work on deck.
OVERLEDEN DE GEPENSIONEERDE LUIT.-KOLONE: Died: the retired lieutenant colonel of artillery de Rochemont.
Died: the retired lieutenant O. Scholl.
OVERLEDEN DE GEVALLEN MATROOS WILLEM VAN: Died: the sailor Willem van Campen, who had fallen.
OVERLEDEN DE HEER JACOB CHRISTOFFEL SCHO: Died: the gentleman Jacob Christoffel Schover of Straalzun.
OVERLEDEN DE INLANDSE PASSAGIER JAN ALEX: Died: the native passenger Jan Alexander of Tutetcoreijn. Many sick with hot fevers and dizziness in the head, afflicted with severe headache, and all very sudden [?]. There are as many as 40 men in their bunks.
OVERLEDEN DE JONG MATROOS J.J. ELTZMAN: Died: the ordinary seaman J.J. Eltzman.
OVERLEDEN DE KOK FREDERIK PIERSON VAN HE: Died: the cook Frederik Pierson of Hessencasselen.
OVERLEDEN DE KORPORAAL VAN DE MEURONS AT: Died: the corporal of De Meuron's regiment, Athanase le Duc of Lebre; they inventoried the estate. 41 sick.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS ANDRIES BOEDEL, LIJ: Died: the sailor Andries Boedel, body put overboard.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS CORNELIS ABRAHAM VA: Died: the sailor Cornelis Abraham van Uiland [?], left nothing behind. 38 sick.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS CORNELIS VAN DER KR: Died: the sailor Cornelis van der Kruyf [?], was put overboard.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS GERHARD LAMEER VAN: Died: the sailor Gerhard Lameer of Lillo, without an estate.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS HENDRIK SJOERT VAN: Died: the sailor Hendrik Sjoert of Bytewaert, with no. 4.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS I. GERRITS VAN MIDD: Died: the sailor I. Gerrits of Middelburg, left nothing behind. 46 sick.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JACOB HENDRICK BOKK: Died: the sailor Jacob Hendrick Bokkentien of Lubek.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JACOBUS DE PUTTER V: Died: the sailor Jacobus de Putter of The Hague.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JAN ADAMS. OVERBOOR: Died: the sailor Jan Adams. Put overboard and his goods sold.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JAN COERS VAN ……: Died: the sailor Jan Coers of ……
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JAN HOLLING. 2 MANN: Died: the sailor Jan Holling. 2 men who had been put in irons on 21 September were released. Died: the ordinary seaman Jec [?] Wolley.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS JAN KONING VAN NAPE: Died: the sailor Jan Koning of Napels.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS MICHIEL RAUSIH VAN: Died: the sailor Michiel Rausih of Mamel.
OVERLEDEN DE MATROOS PIETER AUGUSTINUS,: Died: the sailor Pieter Augustinus, body put overboard.
OVERLEDEN DE SCHEEPSKOK HENDRIK BIELEVEL: Died: the ship's cook Hendrik Bieleveld, of a catarrhal illness.
OVERLEDEN DE SERGEANT DER MARINE A.S. WI: Died: the marine sergeant A.S. Wierink.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT ANDRIES CRAUSE VAN: Died: the soldier Andries Crause of Dalemburg, left nothing behind.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT DIRK TYSSEN VAN HOO: Died: the soldier Dirk Tyssen of Hoorn.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT GOODFRIED VAN SOTHE: Died: the soldier Goodfried van Sothen of Erfort, also the sailor Symen Sybrandser of Ringkopping.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT HANS JURGEN SMIT VA: Died: the soldier Hans Jurgen Smit of Hannover.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT J.(OF I.) M. KOP: Died: the soldier J. (or I.) M. Kop.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT VAN MURON HEINREICH: Died: the soldier of Muron, Heinreich Giede [?] of Paderborn, without an estate.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT W. EYGHOLDS VAN KRE: Died: the soldier W. Eygholds of Kreewitz (in AMW) and the sailor I. du Pon of Oostende (in the PVW); both left nothing behind.
OVERLEDEN DE SOLDAAT WILLUM SIJNEN(?) ,: Died: the soldier Willum Sijnen [?], put overboard.
OVERLEDEN DE TAMBOER PIETER WIL SOND VAN: Died: the drummer Pieter Wil Sond of Dornik.
OVERLEDEN DE TWEEDE MEESTER KLAAS SOLKAM: Died: the second master Klaas Solkamans of Amsterdam, no. 8.
OVERLEDEN DE TWEEDE STUURMAN JAN GEERE H: Died: the second mate Jan Geere H. Braubach, from the effects of a nervous fever, and the cabin boy Jan Niclaa Fuhri [?], at the age of 18.5 years. Peace be with him.
OVERLEDEN DEN BAAS KLEERMAKER M.J. JETTE: Died: the master tailor M.J. Jetter.
OVERLEDEN DEN BOSCHIETER PIETER SANGAAR: Died: the gunner Pieter Sangaar of Bornholm. Died: the soldier Jan Beerent Anter of Greepel.
OVERLEDEN DEN CANONIER KAREL FREDRIK ALM: Died: the gunner Karel Fredrik Almera of Hamburg.
OVERLEDEN DEN CUYPER FRANS OEL VAN WAAIJ: Died: the cooper Frans Oel of Waaijlos, and also the sailor Pieter Drinkling of Vlissingen, and the sailor Klaas Dirkse of Groeningen.
OVERLEDEN DEN GROOFSMIT JACOBUS ZEEGERS: Died: the blacksmith Jacobus Zeegers of Diest.
OVERLEDEN DEN INFANTERIST J VAN RENNE: Died: the infantryman J. van Renne.
OVERLEDEN DEN MATROOS GENAAMT JACOBUS VA: Died: the sailor named Jacobus van der Strene, born in Ijperen.
OVERLEDEN DEN MATROOS PIETER ITS VAN MID: Died: the sailor Pieter Its of Middelburg, taken from the [?].
OVERLEDEN DEN MATROOS WILLEM SOETBEEK GE: Died: the sailor Willem Soetbeek, native of Eisendam.
OVERLEDEN DEN MATTROOS JAN VESTERING VAN: Died: the sailor Jan Vestering of Deventer.
OVERLEDEN DEN MOOR BRAMDY, HERMANUS PIET: Died: the Moor Bramdy; Hermanus Pieters a week earlier.
OVERLEDEN DEN ONDERKOOPMAN HERMANUS HEND: Died: the junior merchant Hermanus Henderick Deijts of Vlissingen.
OVERLEDEN DEN SOLDAAT JACOBUS MENS VAN S: Died: the soldier Jacobus Mens of The Hague.
OVERLEDEN DERDE WAAK LUCAS BOOGERS VAN Z: Died: third watch Lucas Boogers of Zierikzee.
OVERLEDEN EEN MATROOS GENAAMD MARIUS (?): Died: a sailor named Marius [?] of Reijnswout, born in Leiden. Body put overboard.
OVERLEDEN GIJSBERT VAN OGGEN, 3E KOK: Died: Gijsbert van Oggen, third cook.
OVERLEDEN IJZAAC DE BOER EN FRANS ALTHUI: Died: Ijzaac de Boer and Frans Althuis.
OVERLEDEN JONG MATROOS CONSTANTINUS HOFT: Died: ordinary seaman Constantinus Hoftman of Buichem and soldier Nicolaas Albrecht Matras of Wismar. Saw a trumpet floating. Heavy dew at night.
OVERLEDEN JONG MATROOS JACOBUS DE WIT VA: Died: ordinary seaman Jacobus de Wit of Storlingen.
OVERLEDEN JONG MATROOS KARSTEN MULLER, E: Died: ordinary seaman Karsten Muller, and sailor Galfe Sybrand of Medenblik.
OVERLEDEN JONG MATROOS NICOLS DOORMA VAN: Died: ordinary seaman Nicols Doorma of Middelburg.
OVERLEDEN JONG MATROOS PIETER MENE VAN G: Died: ordinary seaman Pieter Mene of Gent.
OVERLEDEN JONGE THEYS BASRTELS VAN AMELA: Died: the young Theys Basrtels of Ameland.
OVERLEDEN JONGMATROOS JOHANNES TOEREE VA: Died: ordinary seaman Johannes Toeree of Gent.
OVERLEDEN JURGEN SCHREUDER OVERBOORD GEV: Died: Jurgen Schreuder, fell overboard and drowned.
OVERLEDEN KAJUITKOK A. STEGCKER, WORDT I: Died: cabin cook A. Stegcker, sewn into his hammock with 2 small lots of ballast.
OVERLEDEN KOKSMAAT DOOKIS VAN DEN BROEKE: Died: cook's mate Dookis van den Broeke of Oosteland.
OVERLEDEN KOKSMAAT H. VAN DER NOOT: Died: cook's mate H. van der Noot.
OVERLEDEN KORPORAAL H. GROENEMEYER, OOK: Died: corporal H. Groenemeyer; also the gunner's mate J.W. Kraft dies.
OVERLEDEN KWARTIERMEESTER WILLEM RUDOLF: Died: quartermaster Willem Rudolf, sailor Joseph Haag and soldier Jan Hendrik Gerwin.
OVERLEDEN LICHTMATROOS JAN WILLEMSE UIT: Died: ordinary seaman Jan Willemse of Emden.
OVERLEDEN LTZ W. P. S. JONQUIERE: Died: naval lieutenant W. P. S. Jonquiere.
OVERLEDEN LUITENANT J.J. VAN SON. ZE MAK: Died: lieutenant J.J. van Son. They are making a coffin for him.
OVERLEDEN MANSLAAF, NR. 18 (194 SLAVEN I: Died: a male slave, no. 18 (194 slaves in the ship).
OVERLEDEN MARINIER SIEVERS, SCHEEPSJONGE: Died: marine Sievers, ship's boy J. van Wijk, sailor C.G. Pasterkamp, sailor A. Landa. Smoked between decks and sprinkled vinegar.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ABRAHAM VAN WANNINGEN: Died: sailor Abraham van Wanningen of Amsterdam, also soldier Johannes Hartmans of Milhousen.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ABRAM HATTEM VAN DE GR: Died: sailor Abram Hattem van de Graaf.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ADAM KNIJPES UIT DRIEL: Died: sailor Adam Knijpes of Drielllen and the boy Henrik Beudeker of Amsterdam.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ALBERT HENDRIK BERING: Died: sailor Albert Hendrik Bering of Hanoversmuide.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ANTHON STAUTES VAN COL: Died: sailor Anthon Stautes of Colmes.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ANTHONY BERGLONT VAN V: Died: sailor Anthony Berglont of Vrijburg.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS BARTHOLOMEUS QUANLAAR: Died: sailor Bartholomeus Quanlaar of Switserland.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS C. DE GRAAF. MAAKTEN S: Died: sailor C. de Graaf. They cleaned the ship. Several small prahus came aboard with gold to sell.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CAREL FREDRIK VOERMAN: Died: sailor Carel Fredrik Voerman of Zaven.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CAREL WIEHARD VAN FRAN: Died: sailor Carel Wiehard of Frankfort am Main.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CLAAS FRUST UIT HAMBUR: Died: sailor Claas Frust of Hamburg.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS COENRAAD MAURINIUS. VE: Died: sailor Coenraad Maurinius. Missing: the sailor Isack Lourens of Bergen, Norway.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CONSTIAAN VAN DER MAST: Died: sailor Constiaan van der Mast.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CORNELIS BREDA VAN NAA: Died: sailor Cornelis Breda of Naaburgh.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CORNELIS BUKELAAR VAN: Died: sailor Cornelis Bukelaar of Steenbergen.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CORNELIS ULBES GEBOORT: Died: sailor Cornelis Ulbes, native of Harlingen.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CORNELIS VAN ALMKERK V: Died: sailor Cornelis van Almkerk of Brouwershaven.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CORNELIS VAN DER SCHEL: Died: sailor Cornelis van der Schelde of Bergen op Zoom. At sunset they think they see land in the east-southeast, but had no sight of it.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS CRISTIAAN HANSEN VAN C: Died: sailor Cristiaan Hansen of Copenhagen, without an estate.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS DINK SCHRITT EN MATROO: Died: sailor Dink Schritt and sailor Thomas Ras of Dronten.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS DIRK DULKES VAN CLEEFF: Died: sailor Dirk Dulkes of Cleeff.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS DIRK HANSEN BARTH? VAN: Died: sailor Dirk Hansen Barth [?] of Ameland.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS ELDERT LOERTSE VAN WID: Died: sailor Eldert Loertse of Widdemeer.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS FRANCES KANAR UIT KORT: Died: sailor Frances Kanar of Kortrijk.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS FRANS ARNMAN VAN STRAA: Died: sailor Frans Arnman of Straatburgh.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS FRANS COEIJS VAN LOO,: Died: sailor Frans Coeijs of Loo, of Gent. They give 1 1/2 cans of drinking water to the crew, because it is very warm every day. The number of sick keeps increasing.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS FRANS HENDRIK WILLEM N: Died: sailor Frans Hendrik Willem Nieman of Essen.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS FRANSZ. STAATS VAN LOK: Died: sailor Fransz. Staats of Lokeren.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS G. VAN DER BENT: Died: sailor G. van der Bent.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS GEN. LOUWEREN JANSEN V: Died: sailor Gen. Louweren Jansen of Borvenholm.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS GEORGE MEIJER, VBAN CH: Died: sailor George Meijer, [?] Christiaan Zant.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS GERRIT THOBIAS VAN MID: Died: sailor Gerrit Thobias of Middelburg.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS GUILLIEAM JULLIAM VAN: Sailor Guillieam Julliam van Loriens died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HENDRIK MEIJER VAN CLU: Sailor Hendrik Meijer van Cluijie died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HENDRIK SCHEER VAN DIE: Sailor Hendrik Scheer van Diezen, Pieter Jansen van Coppenhage and Michiel Pielekaan van Stockholm died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HENDRIK VAN DER LINDE,: Sailor Hendrik van der Linde and the soldier Hendrik Grave van Osnabrugh died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HENDRIK VRIJMOEDT. AW-: Sailor Hendrik Vrijmoedt died. [?]: saw a sulphurous substance in the air, by which it was as bright and clear on deck as in daytime.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HERMANUS CASTPERS VAN: Sailor Hermanus Castpers van Coppendhagen died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS HUBERT DUHEN UIT DORDR: Sailor Hubert Duhen from Dordrecht died, leaving nothing behind.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JACOB ANDRIESEN UIT ST: Sailor Jacob Andriesen from St. Jacob died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JACOB BEKKER VAN LEUVE: Sailor Jacob Bekker van Leuven died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JACOB CROMBEL VAN BENT: Sailor Jacob Crombel van Benthem died.
Sailor Jacob van der Kaa died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JACOBUS STERK VAN SCHR: Sailor Jacobus Sterk van Schravenhage died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN ADMIRAAL VAN AMSTE: Sailor Jan Admiraal van Amsterdam and soldier Coenraad Detfers van Wietshauzen died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN ANDREAS KORP VAN M: Sailor Jan Andreas Korp van Mustralito died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN BEECKMAN VAN AMSTE: Sailor Jan Beeckman van Amsterdam died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN BROUWERS VAN THOOL: Sailor Jan Brouwers van Thoolen died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN CHRISTOFF FILIPS V: Sailor Jan Christoff Filips van Weender died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN DAMEN VAN WULLEM: Sailor Jan Damen van Wullem died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN DANE VAN MIDDELBUR: Sailor Jan Dane van Middelburgh died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN DOGGER VAN STATIJN: Sailor Jan Dogger van Statijn died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN HAAG UIT WITTENBER: Sailor Jan Haag from Wittenberg and soldier John Fred Haaike from Hessengassel died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN HB STOMITZ VAN ANS: Sailor Jan HB Stomitz van Ansterd died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN HOESEN JOHAN KNOEK: Sailor Jan Hoesen, Johan Knoek from Hamburg and the soldier George Franck died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN JACOB BLUS VAN NIJ: Sailor Jan Jacob Blus van Nijmegen died.
OVERLEDEN MATROOS JAN JACOB CORNELSSEN V: Sailor Jan Jacob Cornelssen van Dansigh died.
