OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT JAN FREDERIK REIJNIKE: Deceased: soldier Jan Frederik Reijnike of Wackense
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT JAN GROEN VAN ALKMAAR: Deceased: soldier Jan Groen of Alkmaar. Deceased: assistant cooper Frederik Kahr of Kommelosen (?)
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT JAN STERK VAN AMSTERD: Deceased: soldier Jan Sterk of Amsterdam
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT JOHAN ANTONIE SIMONTS: Deceased: soldier Johan Antonie Simonts Pollenhiem of Wolfensboule
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT JOHAN CASPER HOUG VAN: Deceased: soldier Johan Casper Houg of Zurich
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT LOUWRENS NUTS VAN SAN: Deceased: soldier Louwrens Nuts of Sante
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT PIETER WEESELMAN VAN: Deceased: soldier Pieter Weeselman of Holstein
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT VALENTIJN RABOFF VAN: Deceased: soldier Valentijn Raboff of Wolsteijn
OVERLEDEN: SOLDAAT WILLEM VAN DER BELDEN: Deceased: soldier Willem van der Belden of Leiden
OVERLEDEN: SOLDATEN BASTIAANS DE RUIJTER: Deceased: soldiers Bastiaans de Ruijter of Lesnoord and Jos Koekoek of Krikhousen
OVERLEDEN: SOLDATEN JOHANNES ROOSE VAN …: Deceased: soldiers Johannes Roose of … and Leendert Scheepers of Striepe
OVERLEDEN: TIMMERMAN DANIEL WENSKE VAN C: Deceased: carpenter Daniel Wenske of Coningsbergen
OVERLEDENEN: MATROOS JACOB POULUSZE VAN: Deceased: sailor Jacob Poulusze of Holsteyn and soldier Bernardis Zwart of Meenen, both without heirs
A Chinese man named Torjours died. At 7 o'clock put the body overboard. Held ship's prayers.
OVERLEEDT EEN CHINEES MET NAAM OU. SETTE: A Chinese man named Ou died. Put the said man overboard.
OVERLEGGINGEN OVER INSTRUCTIES VAN GOUVE: Deliberations on the governor's instructions regarding the sailing route
OVERLEGGINGEN OVER KAARTEN, POSITIE, BES: Deliberations on charts, position, dead reckoning
OVERLIJDEN BOOTMANSMAAT HENDRIK BAKMAN: Death of boatswain's mate Hendrik Bakman
OVERLIJDEN MATROOS H.J. VAN LATENA: Death of sailor H.J. van Latena
OVERLIJDEN VAN MARINIER P. BRADO (DW). Z: Death of marine P. Brado (DW). Put his body overboard.
OVERLIJDEN VAN OPPERKUIPER JAN CHRISTIAA: Death of head cooper Jan Christiaanse. 19 men sick.
OVERLIJDEN VAN SOLDAAT FRANCISCUS ANTWAP: Death of soldier Franciscus Antwapen. Held a ship's council on the condition of the sick soldiers
P. TEN DAM EN J. VAN VEEN OVERLEDEN: P. ten Dam and J. van Veen deceased
P.V. LODEN 34 VADEM KORAALGROND. E.W. LO: P.V. soundings 34 fathoms, coral bottom. E.W. soundings 25 fathoms, coral bottom. A.W. soundings 25,32 fathoms, coral bottom
PAAIEN RENSWOUDE. DIT SCHIP BEVINDT ZICH: Hailed Renswoude. This ship is at a longitude of 2°45'
PAJAROS CARNEROS CORBAS TABLEROS Y MARTI: Birds: carneros, corbas, tableros and martín placas. Skies and horizons with broken cloud, horizons squally with heavy cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS CORBAS Y TABLEROS. CIEL: Birds: carneros, corbas and tableros. Skies and horizons with dark cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS Y OTROS PARECIDOS A LOS: Birds: carneros and others resembling plovers, such as beach terns. Horizons closed in with mist and raining. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
Birds: carneros and others resembling plovers, such as beach terns. Whales were also seen.
PAJAROS CARNEROS, CORBAS Y 1 CHORLITO. H: Birds: carneros, corbas and 1 plover. Horizons from the SW to the NW squally and threatening. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS, CORBAS Y TABLEROS. TIE: Birds: carneros, corbas and tableros. Overcast weather with snow falling. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS, CORBAS Y UN TABLERO. T: Birds: carneros, corbas and one tablero. Overcast weather with downpours. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS, ENTENARES Y CORBAS. CI: Birds: carneros, entenares and corbas. Skies and horizons with brown cloud. At 12:30 a rain shower falls. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CARNEROS, ENTENARES, CORBAS Y OT: Birds: carneros, entenares, corbas and other small ones that look like plovers. Skies and horizons closed in. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CORBAS Y 2 CARNEROS. CIELOS Y HO: Birds: corbas and 2 carneros. Skies and horizons with light cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CORBAS Y GABIOTON. CIELOS Y HORI: Birds: corbas and gabioton. Skies and horizons with scattered light cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CORBAS Y GABIOTON. DESDE EL MERI: Birds: corbas and gabioton. From the meridian of Cape Horn until today, when we cross the parallel of the Río de la Plata, the ship has travelled by log 739 leagues and 2 1/2 miles, at 20 leagues to the degree. Skies and horizons overcast. Raining. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CORBAS Y OTROS NEGROS. CIELOS Y: Birds: corbas and other black ones. Skies and horizons with cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS CORBAS, CARNEROS Y TABLEROS. TIE: Birds: corbas, carneros and tableros. Misty weather. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS DE DIVERSA ESPECIE EN ABUNDANCIA: Birds of various species in abundance
PAJAROS ENTENARES Y CORBAS Y OTROS QUE P: Birds: entenares, corbas and others that look like binosas. Clear sky and horizons with double layers of cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS ENTENARES, CORBAS Y MARTIN PLACA: Birds: entenares, corbas and martín placas. Skies and horizons with heavy cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS TABLEROS Y 1 CARNERO. CIELOS Y H: Birds: tableros and 1 carnero. Skies and horizons with light cloud. Later heavily overcast. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS TABLEROS Y CORBAS. CIELOS Y HORI: Birds: tableros and corbas. Skies and horizons with heavy brown cloud. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS TABLEROS Y MARTIN PLACAS. CIELOS: Birds: tableros and martín placas. Skies and horizons dim. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAJAROS TABLEROS. TIEMPO OFUSCO. LOS DAT: Birds: tableros. Dim weather. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon
PAPEL CURIOSO QUE HACE VER LOS EFECTOS D: Curious paper showing the effects of currents in the vicinity of the Bahama Channel (...) drawn up by the frigate lieutenant D. Juan Coronado, one of the officers of its crew
PARA HUIR DE UNAS NAVES ENEMIGAS, DECIDI: To flee some enemy ships, they decided to pass through a strait between the islands of Flores and Fayal, although no one in the crew had ever passed through that strait.
PARA SEGUIR EN ELLA LA COMISIÓN DE TRAZA: To continue in it the commission of drawing the charts of our coasts
PARALELOS AL CABO SAN VICENTE. MEDICION: Parallels to Cape San Vicente. Measurement and data from noon, without the descriptors that are usually from dusk
PARECE QUE FALTA BASTANTE VINO TINTILLA: It seems that quite a lot of Tintilla de Rota wine is missing and they investigate its disappearance
PARECE QUE FALTA HOJAS ANTES. EMPIEZA CO: It seems pages are missing before. It begins with "Rocks and a chain of them that at noon bore as follows: the southernmost rock at S 40º E 3,5 leagues. The rock southernmost of the chain of stone reef at S 40,5º E. The northernmost of them at S 42º 10' E at 3 leagues. A large rock north of the said reef at S 46º E. The south point of a more northerly islet at E 36º 30' S 2 2/3 leagues. A rock further north at E 26º S 5 leagues". It says that the corrected longitude is 161º 07'
PARTANCE DE LA RADE DECHEF DE BAYE: Departure from the roads of Dechef de Baye
PARTE DE EL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA RUMBO AL: Departs from the port of La Coruña heading for Montevideo
PARTE DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTINO A MONTEVI: Departs La Coruña bound for Montevideo
PARTE DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTINO AL PUERTO: Departs La Coruña bound for the port of Montevideo
PARTE DE LA CORUÑA RUMBO A MONTEVIDEO: Departs La Coruña heading for Montevideo
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO AL PUERTO DE LA CORU: Departs Montevideo for the port of La Coruña
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO CON DESTINO A LA COR: Departs Montevideo bound for La Coruña
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO DE REGRESO A LA CORU: Departs Montevideo returning to La Coruña
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO DE REGRESO AL PUERTO: Departs Montevideo returning to the port of La Coruña
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO RUMBO A LA CORUÑA: Departs Montevideo heading for La Coruña
PARTE DE MONTEVIDEO RUMBO AL PUERTO DE L: Departs Montevideo heading for the port of La Coruña
PARTE DE REGRESO A LA CORUÑA: Departs on the return to La Coruña
PARTE DE REGRESO AL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA: Departs on the return to the port of La Coruña
PARTE DE REGRESO DE MONTEVIDEO A LA CORU: Departs on the return from Montevideo to La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERO DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTINO: Departs from the port of La Coruña bound for Montevideo
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE BUENOS AIRES RUMBO A: Departs from the port of Buenos Aires heading for La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTIN: Departs from the port of La Coruña bound for Montevideo
Departs from the port of La Coruña bound for that of Montevideo
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA DE REGRESO: Departs from the port of La Coruña on the return to Montevideo
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA RUMBO A MO: Departs from the port of La Coruña heading for Montevideo
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA RUMBO AL D: Departs from the port of La Coruña heading for that of Montevideo
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO CON DESTI: Departs from the port of Montevideo bound for La Coruña
Departs from the port of Montevideo bound for that of La Coruña
Departs from the port of Montevideo bound for that of La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO DE REGRES: Departs from the port of Montevideo on the return to La Coruña
Departs from the port of Montevideo on the return to that of La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO RUMBO A L: Departs from the port of Montevideo heading for La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO RUMBO AL: Departs from the port of Montevideo heading for that of La Coruña
PARTE DEL PUERTO DE SANTA CRUZ DE TENERI: Departs from the port of Santa Cruz de Tenerife
PARTE RUMBO AL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO: Departs heading for the port of Montevideo
PARTEN A LAS 9 DE LA MAÑANA DEL PUERTO D: They depart from the port of Havana at 9 in the morning; the wind and sea references are from the morning. There is no table for this day.
PARTEN DE MONTEVIDEO A LAS 5 Y MEDIA DE: They depart from Montevideo at half past 5 in the morning of the previous day. The sea reference is from nightfall.
PARTEN DE REGRESO A LA CORUÑA: They depart on the return to La Coruña
PARTIDA DE CARTAGENA. LA REFERENCIA TOMA: Departure from Cartagena. The wind reference taken corresponds to 6 in the evening, since there is no more data.
PARTIDA DE CÁDIZ. RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL: Departure from Cádiz. Course and wind direction at noon / other data [?] or dawn
PARTIDA DE LA CORUÑA A MONTEVIDEO: Departure from La Coruña to Montevideo
PARTIDA DE MONTEVIDEO A LA CORUÑA: Departure from Montevideo to La Coruña
PARTIDA DE SANTA CATALINA. MEDIODÍA RUMB: Departure from Santa Catalina. Noon course and wind / sea nearest to noon
Departure from the port of Havana.
PARTIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA HABANA. NI DE V: Departure from the port of Havana. No wind or sea [data].
Departure from the port of Santa Catalina.
PARTIDA DEL PUERTO DE SANTA CATALINA. ME: Departure from the port of Santa Catalina. Noon course and wind / dawn sea
PARTIDA DEL PUERTO DE VERACRUZ. NO HAY A: Departure from the port of Veracruz. There is no wind entry.
PARTIE DE L'ISLE DE RÉ A 6 HS DU MATIN: Departed from the Isle de Ré at 6 in the morning
PARTIE DE LA RADE DE L'ISLE ST. PIERRE P: Departed from the roadstead of the Isle St. Pierre for France
PARTIE POUR LE FORT ST. PIERRE. MOUILLÉ: Departed for Fort St. Pierre. Anchored
PARTIE POUR SAINT DOMINGUE ET MOUILLÉ DU: Departed for Saint Domingue and anchored at Fort Royal
PARTY DE LANCE ET MOUILLÉ AU LA BASSE TE: Departed from Lance and anchored at Basse Terre of Guadeloupe
PARTY DE SAINTE LUCIE ET MOUILLÉ AU FORT: Departed from Sainte Lucie and anchored at Fort Royal
PARTY DU FORT ROYAL POUR AU FORT SAINT P: Departed from Fort Royal for Fort Saint Pierre and anchored
PASA DEL CUARTERON DEL SENO MEXICANO A L: Passes from the quarter of the Gulf of Mexico to the Dutch chart. Measurement at noon or of the day's run, except the descriptors, which are from nightfall.
PASA MUCHO TIEMPO A LA CAPA. VA CORRIEND: Spends a long time hove to. Runs along the coast until 16:15, when it anchors at Montecristo. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. It could not leave earlier because of the calms and strong winds.
PASA TODA LA MAÑANA A LA CAPA: Spends the whole morning hove to
Passenger J.G. van der Bruggen died.
PASAN EL TROPICO A LAS 15:00 CON CORTA D: They cross the tropic at 15:00, give or take. The voyage is 3 months old.
PASAN LA ISLA DE PALMA (POSICIÓN CORRESP: They pass the island of Palma (position corresponds to this point)
PASAN POR LA IZQUIERDA DE LA ISLA DE MAY: They pass to the left of the island of Mayo and in the afternoon anchor at Puerto Praya on the island of Santiago in 18 fathoms (describes the port)
PASAN TODO EL DIA DANDO BORDOS AL E Y AL: They spend the whole day tacking east and west. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
PASJAREN OM TE HOREN WELKE SCHEPEN ONDER: [?] to hear which ships wanted to sail under the convoy.
PASSAGIER PLEEGT ZELFMOORD DOOR OVERBOOR: Passenger commits suicide by jumping overboard
PASSEERDE EEN STROOKJE IJS EN ZAGE HIER: Passed a strip of ice and saw here and there a single floe.
PASSEERDEN 'S MORGENS HALF 7 IETS HETGEE: At half past 7 in the morning passed something that appeared to be a cliff.
PASSEERDEN DE LINIE IN 24° 12' LW. 34 ET: Passed the line in 24° 12' LW. 34 days out of the Channel
PASSEERDEN DEN MIDDAG DE VUURTOREN VAN K: At noon passed the lighthouse of Cape Recife, N by W 0,5 W.
PASSEERDEN EEN GROOTE WITTIGEHEID IN HET: Passed a great whiteness in the water without being able to discover what it was.
Passed a piece of a wreck.
PASSEERDEN ENKELDE SCHOTSJES IJS: Passed a few small floes of ice
PASSEERDEN ENKELE SCHOTSJES ALSOOK STROO: Passed a few small floes as well as strips of ice
PASSEERDEN IN DE ACHTERMIDDAG DE ZUIDERK: In the afternoon passed the southern tropic
PASSEERDEN IN DE EERSTE WAGT DE ZUIDER K: In the first watch passed the southern tropic
PASSEERDEN IN DE VOORMIDDAG DE BARK ANET: In the forenoon passed the bark Anette from Callaste to Genoa, having a 54-day voyage.
PASSEERDEN IN DE VOORMIDDAG DE BARK MARI: In the forenoon passed the bark Marie Julie Fredericks from Callao to Rotterdam, having an 81-day voyage.
Passed the Tropic of Cancer at [?] o'clock DW. Rolled heavily in the high sea
PASSEERDEN NOG ENKELE PAKJES IJS: Still passed a few packs of ice
PASSEERDEN OP 21 APRIL DE CONSTAPELS, DU: On 21 April passed the Constapels, Duivelseilanden and the Marowijne. Arrived on 23 April at 16.00 before Paramaribo.
PASSEERDEN TROPICANUS CAPRICORNIUS. HESE: Passed the Tropicus Capricornius. Hoisted the remainder of the cannons aboard
PASSEERDEN VEEL IJS, MAAKTEN KLAAR OM WA: Passed a lot of ice, made ready to catch whales
PASSERDE DE WEST HOEK VAN ST. CHRISTOFFE: Passed the west point of St. Christoffel at around 11 o'clock
PASSERE VRIJ WAT IJS: Passed quite a bit of ice
PASSEREN 'S MORGENS DE EQUATOR IN 22 15: In the morning passed the equator at 22 15 west longitude. 41 days at sea.
PASSEREN DE LINIE EQUINOQTIAAL OP DE LEN: Pass the equinoctial line at longitude 357° 54'.
PASSEREN DE LINIE EQUITORIAAL. WORDEN DO: Pass the equatorial line. Are welcomed by the fleet. Salute shots.
PASSEREN DE LINIE. (VOLGENS COMPAS?) 21°: Pass the line. (According to compass?) 21° 52' observed west. The suns were 23° 5' observed W. This gives 1° 13' northwest variation.
PASSEREN DE LINIE. PRAAIDEN DE COMMANDAN: Pass the line. Hailed the commander, who had at noon: 18' ZB, longitude 353° 25'. Variation 7° 52' N/W (of which ship?). Changed longitude 10'. Commander hoisted flag and standard on account of the line. Hoist flag and pennant, salute with 11 shots. The captain of the Beschermer saluted with 9 shots.
PASSEREN GROTE EN KLEINE KOMBUIS, MIDDEL: Pass Grote and Kleine Kombuis, Middelburg, Onrust.
PASSEREN IN DE AVOND DE KLIP DIE ZOTO VA: In the evening pass the rock that lies SE by E of Cape Finisterre
PASSEREN OM 6U.22' DE EQUATOR OP CIRCA 2: Pass the equator at 6h 22' at about 24° longitude west of Greenwich
PASSEREN ST. NICHOLAS PUNT ZO NA DAT MEN: Pass St. Nicholas Point SE so close that one could throw a stone onto it
PASSÉ LE TROPIQUE ENTRE LE 36° ET 37° DE: Passed the tropic between 36° and 37° of longitude, meridian of Paris
PEIJLDEN MET 4 GLAZEN DER DAGWAGT DE VUE: Took bearings with 4 glasses of the day watch: the lighthouse or its light WNW½W. With the 6 glasses were signalled [?] by the Company's galliot. Because of the transfer of the pilots, made the sloop ready. At that time had the Cingels NW and the corner of Vuerlay W by N. At 8 o'clock put the pilots off. Parted with 5 cannon shots and were thanked by the Company's galliot with the same. Sent off letters to the Heeren Bewindhebbers, together with a list of absent crew. Wished the others well and set the course to the SW R/W [?]. At noon the general course and distance since the bearing of Zuidvoorland to the below: SW 3/4 W 10 miles. Took bearings suddenly of the corner of Bevozier W by N and Vuerleij NNW.
Sighted the island of Palma in the SE by E.
PEILDE KAAP WILSON O (R/W), EILAND RODON: Sighted Cape Wilson E (R/W), island Rodondo E 3/4 S (R/W). Two ships in sight that lay with us and a schooner. At midnight the light of Deal island (R/W) S by W 1/4 W.
PEILDE OM 12 UREN HET EILAND PORTO SANTO: At 12 o'clock sighted the island of Porto Santo in the SW.
The next day took bearings of Goudstaart.
PEILDEN DE ZON BIJ ONDERGANG EN BEVONDT: Took the bearing of the sun at sunset and found 19 minutes of northwest variation
Bearings of Eng. End N by W, 2 miles.
PEILDEN GOUDSTAART. KWAMEN OP 15 JULI 17: Took bearings of Goudstaart. Arrived on 15 July 1752 on the roads of Rammekens.
PEILDEN HET EILAND FRIO IN HET NOORDEN 2: Sighted the island of Frio in the north 27° east or NNE 3/8 east. Lying off Rio Janeiro.
PEILDEN MET ZONSONDERGANG LAND IN ONO 1/: At sunset sighted land in ENE 1/2 E, depth of 9 fathoms, gray sand
PEILDEN OM 16.00U GOUDSTAART NOORD, 2.5: At 16.00 took bearings of Goudstaart north, 2.5 miles. On 6 September entered the roads of Texel. The ship sails further back and forth between Texel and Vlissingen. The journal ends on 5 November at Amsterdam.
PEILDEN OM 5 UUR DE OOSTHOEK VAN SAPODIE: At 5 o'clock the east point of Sapodie and Gilion E 1/2 N, the west point NNW. At 6 o'clock the east point of Gilion NE and the west point NNW 1/4 W, the east point of Raaos ENE 1/2 E
PEILDEN OM 7 UUR DE TAFELBERG NNO HET ZU: At 7 o'clock the Tafelberg NNE, the southernmost land NE by E 1/2 E, comes to 18-5 longitude by chronometer 0-86, then 18-0, N 54 18-2. According to the observation of 4 o'clock, when it gave 17-41. According to that, 23 minutes had been set to the west since the morning.
PEILDEN OP DE MIDDAG 7 VOETEN WATER BIJ: At noon sounded 7 feet of water at the mainmast, at 3.00 three more men were fetched from the ship who lay drunk in the apothecary, at 6.00 another shot fell, then the 1st constable R. Valk was also taken off the ship. Everyone was now on the brig Pecering or Boston. Admiral Evertsen has perished
At noon took bearings of Trinidad and [?] …. E by N - ENE 4 1/4 compass in 29°19' - CB. 29° 18'
PEILDEN VOLGENS STREKKING DER JAVAKUST: Took bearings according to the stretch of the Java coast
PEILDEN VOLGENS TIJDMETERSBESTEK IN HET: Took bearings according to the chronometer reckoning in the English chart book.
PEILDEN ZON IN T OPKOMEN EN BEVONDEN 10G: Took the bearing of the sun at rising and found 10gr34min
PEILEN (14:00) ZUIDELIJKSTE LAND VAN KAA: Bearings (14:00) southernmost land of Cape Aguilhas NE
PEILEN BIJ ZONSONDERGANG LAND DAT ZEER O: Bearings at sunset land that looks very much like Cape Agulhas, but it cannot be, because the wrong kind of bottom is sounded.
PEILEN BLANCA OM 6 UUR N EN DE GROOTSTE: Bearings Blanca at 6 o'clock N and the largest of the Hermanos rocks NE
PEILEN DE ORCHILLEN NOTO 1/2 O EN DE O H: Bearings the Orchillas NE by E 1/2 E and the E point of Rocca or Grand Key NW 1/4 N. (Estimated) Curacao W 1/2 N 30 miles. See the avis in NW. Still some latitudes and longitudes
PEILEN DE SLANGEKOP (MET ZONSONDERGANG): Bearing: the Slangekop (at sunset) NE by N, 1 mile
PEILEN DE Z HOEK VAN ST. CATHARINA ONO W: Bearing: the south point of St. Catherine ENE W/S N. At 4 o'clock bearing: the south point of Wight WNW and Salsai (Selsey/Weenbrug?) N. At 12.00 bearing: B(eachy) Head [?] NE by E, 4 miles. Bearing: Bevesier WNW and the high land of Hastings NE 1/2 E. 8 o'clock lighthouse of the Singels NE by N. At 12.00 the South Foreland NE by N. Dungeness SW by W. Folkestone NW. (Estimated) Dungeness ENE W/S N 11.5 miles
PEILEN DOMINIQUE O 1/4 Z. TIJDMETERS LOP: Bearing: Dominique E 1/4 S. Chronometers running very irregularly
PEILEN EILAND ST. BARTHOLOMEUS O 1/2 N: Bearing: St. Bartholomeus island E 1/2 N
PEILEN FLORISHOEK ZTW 1/2 W: Bearing: Florishoek S by W 1/2 W
PEILEN FONEICO OP 17° 0' BEZUIDEN HET WE: Bearing: Foneico at 17° 0' south of west
PEILEN FORT VAN TRUXILLO, ZOTZ 0,375 MIJ: Bearing: fort of Truxillo, SE by S, 0.375 miles
PEILEN HEBESE (?) NOTO 1/4 O: Bearing: Hebese [?] NE by E 1/4 E
PEILEN HET MIDDEN VAN SANTA CRUZ ONO 3/4: Bearing: the middle of Santa Cruz ENE 3/4 E. On Norie's chart this gives a longitude of 65º 22'
PEILEN HET OOSTELIJKSTE LAND ZO 1/2 O: Bearing: the easternmost land SE 1/2 E
PEILEN HET WESTELIJKE ZICHTBARE LAND VAN: Bearing: the westernmost visible land of Pinos NNE
PEILEN HET ZWLIJKSTE VAN GUADELOUPE Z 1/: Bearing: the southwesternmost part of Guadeloupe S 1/4 E and the easternmost SE by E 1/2 E and the middle of Monserrat NW
PEILEN HOGE LAND VAN LOS ROCQUES DIT GEE: Bearing: high land of Los Rocques; this gives longitude 66º 27' on the chart
PEILEN IN VMW OOK SABA O/M W 3/4 N. (GIS: Bearings in the forenoon also: Saba E/M W 3/4 N. (Estimated) St. Martin NW by N 7.5 miles
PEILEN KALESHOEK ZTO 1/2 O. PEILEN LAND: Bearing: Kaleshoek S by E 1/2 E. Bearing: land of Boulogne S 1/2 E
PEILEN LA PALMA OP DE 11E STREEK. DOEN S: Bearing: La Palma on the 11th point. Made signal for the Zuijlevelt [?]
PEILEN LAND WAARNA HET BESTEK WORDT AANG: Bearing: land, after which the reckoning is adjusted.
PEILEN MIDDEN VAN DESENDA ZZW EN OOSTELI: Bearing: middle of Desenda SSW and easternmost S by W 1/2 W; this gives 61º 00' in Norie
PEILEN N HOEK VAN FLORIS W 23° Z: Bearing: N point of Floris W 23° S
PEILEN NEVIS O 3/4 N, ST. EUSTACIUS NNO: Bearing: Nevis E 3/4 N, St. Eustacius NNE 3/4 E, Saba N 3/4 W. Bearing St. Christoffel ENE
PEILEN NO HOEK MADERA ZZW. W HOEK VAN PO: Bearing: NE point of Madera SSW. W point of Porto Sancto S by E. E point of Porto Sancto SE 1/2 S
PEILEN NOORDELIJKSTE VAN DESERDA NW 1/4: Bearing: northernmost of Deserda NW 1/4 W
PEILEN OM 12 UUR MIDDEN VAN NIWIS WZW 1/: Bearing at 12 o'clock: middle of Niwis WSW 1/2 W. Redonda SSW. This gives the longitude of 62º 19' (this is also the chronometer longitude). Bearing S point of Antiqua SSE 1/2 E
PEILEN OM 8 UUR WESTELIJKSTE GUADELOUPE: Bearing at 8 o'clock: westernmost Guadeloupe S. S point of Monserrat W. E point of Antiqua N 1/2 E. At 12 o'clock bearing E point of Antiqua NNE. This gives longitude 61º 51'
PEILEN OM HALF 6 P. MOULACIQUE/ST LUCIE: Bearing at half past 6 p.m.: Moulacique/St Lucie N 1.5 miles; comes to 13° 29' N and 60° 1 W
PEILEN PIEK VAN LOMBOK ZO 1/2 Z: Bearing: peak of Lombok SE 1/2 S
PEILEN PORTO SANCTO'S HOOGSTE PUNT: NO 3: Bearing: Porto Sancto's highest point: NE 3/4 E
PEILEN S. DOMINGO NNO EN DE N HOEK VAN S: Bearing: S. Domingo NNE and the N point of Saone E
PEILEN SABA NTO 1/4 O. ST. EUSTACIUS NO: Bearing: Saba N by E 1/4 E. St. Eustacius NE 3/4 E and Rodondo E 1/2 S
PEILEN ST. EUSTATIUS Z 1/3 O. SCHIP VAAR: Bearing: St. Eustatius S 1/3 E. Ship sails on to St. Maarten
PEILEN W HOEK VAN OBY MINOR NTW 3/4 W. N: Bearing: W point of Oby Minor N by W 3/4 W. Based on the bearings, the probable position of Gomono is determined as: S lat 1°45', longitude 127°31'. The probable position of Oby Minor is determined as: S lat 1°27' and longitude 127°5'
PEILEN WESTELIJKSTE LAND (VAN AFRIKA), N: Bearing: westernmost land (of Africa), NW by W
PEILEN WLAND VAN PRINCENEILAND, NNO 1/4: Bearing: W land of Prince Island, NNE 1/4 E. Other pressure reading: 751
PEILEN Z HOEK VAN NANKION ZOTO 1/2 O: Bearing: S point of Nankion SE by E 1/2 E
PEILEN Z PUNT VAN EILAND NOEJA LAND (?): Bearing: S point of island Noeja land [?] ENE a little N
PEILINGEN KOMEN OP DE KAART VAN NORIE OV: Bearings agree on Norie's chart with 62º 38' longitude
PEILINGEN KOMEN VLGS SPAANSE KAARTEN (CA: Bearings come, according to Spanish charts (Carta Esfenicon del Seno Meynionno etc. from 1813 and 1814), to 18° 21' N and 61° 25 longitude west of Cadiz. Discussion of reckoning, compass variation, currents, etc. Bearing the island Desecho NNE and Mona NW by W 1/2 W. So this puts NW point of Bonaire S 1/2 W 35 (or 55?) miles and E point of Curacao S 3/4 W 90 miles, according to the chart of Pierdig from 1830. See the Mona
PEILINGEN VAN GOENONG APIE BETEKENT DE L: Bearings of Goenong Apie mean the location of the island is: S lat 6°23', longitude 126°30'
PERMANECI ANCLADO TODA LA TARDE Y NOCHE: I remained anchored all afternoon and night
PERMANECIÓ EL TPO Y VTO. COMO LOS ANTERI: The weather and wind remained as on the previous days until half past one in the afternoon, when a squall from the SW to NW with much wind overcame the wind of the 4th quarter, ushering in a pampero (...) Immediately everything cleared, leaving the sky with clear, scattered cloud and the horizons with banks of cloud and very layered cloud. Thus night fell.
PERROQUET=BRAMSTENGZEIL, PERRUCHE=BOVENK: Perroquet = topgallant sail, perruche = mizzen topsail
PETITE FRAIS ET PRESQUE CALME: Light fresh breeze and almost calm
PICO DE TENERIFFA GEPASSEERD.HET SCHIP S: Passed the Peak of Tenerife. The ship rolls violently in the high swell
Loses sight of the Montevideo mail ship. The distance covered is enormous but that figure is what the source gives. Noon data except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. Spanish quarteron
PIERDEN DE VISTA AL CORSARIO: They lose sight of the privateer
PIJLDEN DOEN 'T ROBBENEIJLAND ZTO 1/2 O,: Took bearings: the Robben Island SE by S 1/2 E, the point of Houtbaai S 1/2 W. This bearing comes out on the S E. Comp. chart at S lat 33°55', longitude 35°30', from where our reckoning begins, awaiting God's dear blessing
PIJLEN MATURE IN 'T NTW 1/2 W NAA 'T OOG: Took bearings: Mature in the N by W 1/2 W by eye 6.5 miles. From this same bearing it comes to N lat 5°20' and longitude 96°10'. Had on this date the observed latitude of 5°42', where our reckoning begins in the name of the Lord
PIJLSTAARTEN, ZIEN GEEN KAAPSE DUIVEN ME: Tropicbirds, see no more Cape pigeons
Platvoet; the ship still in sight.
Platvoet beating up out of the NW.
POCA MAR (...) DURANTE LA NOCHE HUBO ALG: Little sea (...) During the night there were a few light showers of little harm and dawn broke clear.
POCA MAR (...) EL CIELO TOLDADO Y LOS HO: Little sea (...) The sky overcast and the horizons cloudy; these remained so. At sunset the sky was clear. (...) A small squall that did not look good; these continued during the night though not as frequent or as fresh as the previous ones.
POCA MAR Y TIEMPO CLARO; A LAS DOS SE EM: Little sea and clear weather; at two some sea from the SE began to be felt, which kept growing (...) At 8 (night) the wind was fresh with heavy sea from the SE and the sky cloudy. Dawn broke the same way but the day was clear.
POCO ANTES DE LAS 21:00 AVISTAN UNA PUNT: Shortly before 21:00 they sight a point which they take to be the northern one of Rio Gallegos. At 5:00 sights the Cabo de las Virgenes to the SE. At 7:45 sights the Punta de San Demetrio. At 9:30 sights the Cabo de Posesion. They take bearings of the Monte de Denero and the Punta de Miera. At 10:30 they sight another very notable mount toward the Bahia de Posesion, which must be the same that Bouganville called Amond. Currents toward the W. Describes the Cabo de las Virgenes (history, location, orography). Measurement and noon data or of the day's run; many times the descriptors are from dawn
POCO DESPUES DE LAS 13:00 EL SAN PEDRO P: Shortly after 13:00 the San Pedro loses several spars but only 2 sailors were slightly hurt. The topmast that gave way was of pine, from those cut in the Cordillera of Chile
POCO DESPUES DEL AMANECER AVISTAN LAS IS: Shortly after dawn they sight the islands of Flores and Cuervo. Measurement and noon data or of the day's run; many times the descriptors are from dawn
POINT D'ARRIVÉ LA TERRE DE VENT NOUR: Point of arrival: the Terre de Vent Nour
POMPEN 3 DUIM WATER PER WACHT: Pumped 3 inches of water per watch
POMPEN DIT ETMAAL 27 DUIM LENS. VERANDER: Pumped 27 inches from the bilge this day. Changed longitude to the W: 2° 26' (that is, he is still in east longitude, because the number of degrees decreases)
POMPEN DIT ETMAAL TOTAAL 56 DUIM WATER L: Pumped a total of 56 inches of bilge water this day
POMPTE LENS IEDERE WACHT 11 DAGEN WATER,: Pumped the bilge each watch 11 days of water, that the filling lists to the port side. Corrected course SSW S/E S, 44.25 miles. Changed longitude 1° 33'
POMPTE LENS VAN 28 OP 11 DUIM, TEGELIJKE: Pumped the bilge from 28 to 11 inches; at the same time we discovered that the pumped-up water was mixed with gin. Lieutenant F. J. Sluiter placed under arrest
POMPTEN 11 DUIM LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 11 inches of bilge water in the day
POMPTEN 40 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 40 inches of bilge water in the day.

Pumped 40 inches of bilge water in the day. Utrecht: 10° 33' S lat, 110° 8' E long. Goes: 10° 33' S lat, 111° 8' E long. Princes: 10° 45' S lat, 111° 8' E long. Wassenaar: 10° 45' S lat, 109° 4' E long. Munnikkendam: 10° 34' S lat, 110° 20' E long. Juno: 10° 34' S lat, 111° 33' E long
POMPTEN 42 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 42 inches of bilge water in the day
POMPTEN 43 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 43 inches of bilge water in the day
Pumped 43 inches of bilge water in the day. DW: poured water into the forehold, pumped it out again.
POMPTEN 48 DUIM LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 48 inches of bilge water in the day
POMPTEN 48 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 48 inches of bilge water in the day.
POMPTEN 49 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 49 inches of bilge water in the day.
Pumped 49 inches of bilge water in the day. Weather data from the DW. AMW: positions of the ships in the convoy.
POMPTEN 50 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 50 inches of bilge water in the day.
Pumped 50 inches of bilge water in the day. (Estimated) Prinseneiland [?] miles.
POMPTEN 51 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 51 inches of bilge water in the day.
Pumped 51 inches of bilge water in the day. Trivial: after Monday the 16th follows Tuesday the 16th.
POMPTEN 52 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 52 inches of bilge water in the day.
POMPTEN 57 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET ETMAAL: Pumped 57 inches of bilge water in the day
POMPTEN CIRCA 43 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET: Pumped about 43 inches of bilge water in the day.
POMPTEN CIRCA 50 DUIM WATER LENS IN HET: Pumped about 50 inches of bilge water in the day.
POMPTEN DIT ETMAAL 40 DUIM LENS: Pumped 40 inches from the bilge this day
POMPTEN DIT ETMAAL 41 DUIM LENS: Pumped 41 inches from the bilge this day
POMPTEN DIT ETMAAL 48 DUIM LENS: Pumped 48 inches from the bilge this day
POMPTEN DIT ETMAAL 51 DUIM LENS: Pumped 51 inches from the bilge this day
POMPTEN LENS VAN 14 OP 10,5 DUIM: Pumped the bilge from 14 to 10.5 inches
POMPTEN LENS VAN 14 TOT 10 DUIM: Pumped the bilge from 14 to 10 inches
POMPTEN MET DE SLAGPOMPEN. 42 DUIM WATER: Pumped with the brake pumps. 42 inches of bilge water pumped out in the day.
PONE QUE LA LATITUD OBSERVADA ES DUDOSA: Notes that the observed latitude is doubtful
POR EL PUNTO DE REFERENCIA, NOS HALLAMOS: By the reference point, we are three leagues from the coast.
POR ENCONTRARSE ENFERMO EL CAPITAN NO SE: As the captain is ill, the log is not filled in.
POR ESTAR CALMA FONDEA EN 3 BRAZAS DE AG: Because it is calm, anchors in 3 fathoms of water, examining the bottom. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. The log begins on 31-Jan-1766 but does not set out until 3-Feb because of the violence of the clouds and wind that came from the W and NW. Had problems passing the Estrecho de la Canal
POR LA CARTA ME DEMORA EL CUERVO AL SE 5: By the chart the Cuervo bears from me SE 5º E, distance 13 leagues. No events reported
POR LA CARTA, EL CUERVO ME DEMORA 15 LEG: By the chart, the Cuervo bears 15 leagues from me.
POR LA DIFERENCIA DE LATITUD Y LONGITUD: From the difference in latitude and longitude found, 'I found that the currents throughout the Gulf have had a violent course to the SE'.
POR LA MAÑANA ARRIBA AL PUERTO DE MONTEV: In the morning arrives at the port of Montevideo
POR LA MAÑANA ARRIBA EL PUERTO DE MONTEV: In the morning arrives at the port of Montevideo
POR LA MAÑANA AVISTÓ DICHA ISLA (GORGONA: In the morning sighted the said island (Gorgona) and reached it at 3 in the afternoon
POR LA MAÑANA SE DIO EL STO. SACRO VIATI: In the morning the Holy Viaticum was given to the sea gunners Jaime Sur and Joseph (...) scurvy.
POR LA MAÑANA SE ENCONTRARON LAS DOS MAY: In the morning the two mainsails and the foresail were found split
POR LA MAÑANA SE RECIBE UN FUERTE GOLPE: In the morning a heavy sea is taken aboard
POR LA MAÑANA SE VIERON DIFERENTES PAJAR: In the morning different birds were seen, particularly some they call boobies, which resemble the [?] of the Cape of Good Hope, only that they also have the tip of the tail black
POR LA MAÑANA VIERON 1 TORTUGA MEDIANA Y: In the morning they saw 1 medium-sized turtle and a piece of wood right next to it
POR LA MAÑANA VIMOS UNA CEPA DE PLATANOS: In the morning we saw a stalk of bananas after 8 and, though far off, a flock of birds
POR LA NOCHE ESTABA TAN MAL LA SITUACION: At night the situation was so bad that they agree to make a vow to Our Lady of the Rosary and, apparently, she heeds them since the weather improved
POR LA NOCHE FUE FRESCO EL VTO AL PASO Q: During the night the wind was fresh while it hauled more to the N, but by day it was less, it returned to the WNW.
POR LA NOCHE SE PONE A LA CAPA. DESCRIPT: At night they heave to. Noon descriptors or the day's run. The journal begins on 31 Jan 1766 but they do not set sail until 3 Feb because of the violence of the clouds and the wind coming from the W and NW. Had trouble passing the Strait of the Channel
POR LA OBSERVACIÓN AL MEDIO DÍA Y MARCAC: By the noon observation and the bearing of the Ovessant tower, I get 8º west longitude from Paris, equal to 36' 15'' east of Cádiz, 45'' different from mine, being 7 leagues from the said island
POR LA TARDE RECONOCEN LA BAHIA DE SPIRI: In the afternoon they sight the bay of Spiring. They continue heading for the port of San Julian. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
POR LA TARDE SE VIERON BASTANTES PAJAROS: In the afternoon quite a few birds were seen
POR LA TARDE VEN POR LA PROA UN HILO DE: In the afternoon they see ahead a line of currents and water of a different color coming from the N with great force. They anchor west-northwest of Isla Paja, which is opposite Cabo de Matas
POR LA TARDE VIERON \"EL AGUA CON GRANDE: In the afternoon they saw "the water with large sand-colored patches and, having drawn a little up with a bucket, they found it full of small worms"
POR OBSERV. DEL CRONÓMETRO A LAS 21 H 15: By chronometer observation at 21 h 15' the result at noon is: longitude deduced from the observation....43º 08' " " Some shearwaters
POR PRIMERA VEZ VEO QUE EN LA DISTANCIA: For the first time I see that miles are stated in the distance run.
POR UN DESAJUSTE QUE COMPRUEBAN EN EL CR: Because of a fault they detect in the chronometer, they abandon this method of calculating longitude
PORQUE HABER REFRESCADO MUCHO EL VIENTO: Because the wind from the SW freshened a lot with hard gusts
PORTO SANTO Z T W OL (???) 16° 42': Porto Santo Z T W OL [?] 16° 42'
POSICION Y DIRECCION DEL VIENTO DE MEDIO: Position and direction of the wind at noon for the rest of the day, since the pilot does not specify the time
POSITIE PALMA OP DE KAART VAN PURDY: Position of Palma on Purdy's chart
POSITIE VAN BERKHOUT IS: LENGTE 83°56 EN: Position of Berkhout is: longitude 83°56 and south latitude 3°22'
POSITIE VAN DUIFIE IS: NB 5°26 EN LENGTE: Position of Duifie is: north latitude 5°26 and longitude 355°37'
POSITIE VAN HET SCHIP BERKHOUT: LENGTE 8: Position of the ship Berkhout: longitude 82°18' north latitude 5°25
POSITIE VOLGENS ZON EN MAAN 20 48 40, ZO: Position by sun and moon 20 48 40, so that the dead reckoning stood 1 28 28 too far east.
POSITIES VAN DE ANDERE SCHEPEN IN HET ES: Positions of the other ships in the squadron. Utrecht: 8° 57' S, 104° 16' E. Goes: 9° S, 104° 3' E. Prinses Louisa: 9° S, 105° 25. Wassenaar: 9° S, 105° 3'
Positions of the ships in the squadron. Utrecht: 2° 36' N, 93° 28' E. Goes: 2° 28' N. Princes Louisa: 2° 30' N. Wassenaar: 2° 27' N, 94° 40' E. * = longitude not seen, because they were astern.
PRAAI DEN COMMANDEUR STARRENBERG. DIENS: Hailed the commander Starrenberg. His longitude was 328°17
PRAAIDE DE FORTUIJN. GISTEREN WAS ZIJN B: Hailed the Fortuijn. Yesterday his latitude was 22° 40' and longitude 79° 40' and variation 13° 33' NW. Also learned that since P. Gale he had [?] dead, [?] … had [?], 23 sick and [?] … bodies. Corrected course and distance WNW 1/2 W. 8,5 miles.
PRAAIDE DE FORTUIJN. GISTERENMIDDAG HAD: Hailed the Fortuijn. Yesterday at noon he had 29° 52' south latitude and longitude 57° 40'. Corrected course and distance WSW 1/2 W. 17,5 miles.
PRAAIDE DE FORTUIJN. ZIJN LENGTE WAS GIS: Hailed the Fortuijn. His longitude yesterday was 52° 40' and variation 28° 0' NW. He also had 80 sick and 17 dead since P. Gale. Corrected course and distance S by E 1/3 E. 3,5 miles.
PRAAIDEN CAPT. PRUIJS. ZIJN BESTEK: 26°: Hailed Capt. Pruijs. His dead reckoning: 26° 49' N and his longitude 348° 19'. Meridian west of Madeira, 141 miles.
PRAAIDEN DE COMMANDANT. ZIJN BREEDTE 2°: Hailed the commander. His latitude 2° 34' and longitude 108° and 42'.
PRAAIDEN DE DRIE GEBROEDERS OM WAT AF TE: Hailed the Drie Gebroeders to keep off a little.
PRAAIDEN DE DRIE GEBROEDERS. GISTEREN WA: Hailed the Drie Gebroeders. Yesterday his south latitude was 18° 12', longitude 86° 32'.
PRAAIDEN DE DRIE GEBROEDERS: ZIJN BREEDT: Hailed the Drie Gebroeders: his latitude 22° 36' and longitude 79° 42'. His variation this morning 13° 20'. Lost sight of the other ships because of a rapidly rising squall. By 6 o'clock all the merchant ships were in sight again.
PRAAIDEN DE SCHEPEN OM ACHTEROM TE KOMEN: Hailed the ships to come astern. His latitude: 2° 9' and longitude 99° 29'. Variation 18' NE. True latitude: at [?] hours.
PRAAIDEN EEN PORTUGEES SCHIP, ZIJN LENGT: Hailed a Portuguese ship, his longitude was 15' further east than ours
PRAAIDEN ENGELSE LOGGER, VERNAMEN 'VOORN: Hailed an English lugger, learned 'that the said lugger was a privateer. Also that we were at war with the French, the same having been declared on 13 Feb'
PRAAIDEN JOH. HOOGERZEIL DIE VISTEN OM D: Hailed Joh. Hoogerzeil, who were fishing for [?] with the trawl.
PRAAIDEN ZEEUWSE HOEKER, DIE LEZART N W/: Hailed a Zeeland hooker, which had the Lezart N W/O 7 miles from it
PRAAIEN 'MIJN MAAT VAN DEN BERGH'. LENGT: Hailed 'my mate Van den Bergh'. That ship's longitude is 348°20'
PRAAIEN 'S LANDS FREGAT D'ALARM. DE NB V: Hailed the state's frigate d'Alarm. This ship's north latitude yesterday was 26°11, the longitude 324°47'
PRAAIEN ARIE VAN HAARST NB 46°14' LENGTE: Hailed Arie van Haarst north latitude 46°14' longitude 355°43'
PRAAIEN COMMANDANT (?), WIENS LENGTE DE: Hailed the commander [?], whose longitude the day before was 340°10'
PRAAIEN COMMANDANT DIENS POSITIE WAS NB: Hailed the commander, whose position was north latitude 44°2' and longitude 351°12'
PRAAIEN COMMANDANT, WIER POSITIE WAS: LE: Hailed the commander, whose position was: longitude 9°47' and north latitude 49°5'
PRAAIEN DE DRIE GEBROEDERS. ZIJN ZB OP D: Hailed the Drie Gebroeders. His south latitude at noon was 28° 36' and longitude 63° 34' and variation 24° 25'. He had no sick at all.
PRAAIEN DE HEER BALK (VAN HET SCHIP RECH: Hailed Mr. Balk (of the ship Recht door Zee). That ship's longitude was 355°42'
PRAAIEN DE JOHANNA. GISTEREN WAS ZIJN BR: Hailed the Johanna. Yesterday his latitude was 26° 26' and longitude 86° 20' and variation 22° 20' NW. Since P. Gale the Johanna had [?] sick and [?] dead. Hailed the Fortuijn. Yesterday his latitude was 26° 31' and longitude 68° 11' and variation 21° 55' NW.
PRAAIEN DE RENSWOUDE. LENGTE VAN RENSWOU: Hailed the Renswoude. Renswoude's longitude is 354°10'
PRAAIEN DE WASSENAAR EN KRIJGT ZIJN BEST: Hailed the Wassenaar and get his position. South latitude 9: 42' longitude 6: 15'
PRAAIEN EEN HOLLANDS LOODSSCHIP EN NEMEN: Hailed a Dutch pilot ship and took two pilots from Den Hoorn, Texel, named Tomas Janssen and Hendrik Hammel, aboard. Hailed a Dutch warship frigate that is waiting for return ships of the VOC
PRAAIEN HET LANDSFREGAT ALARM. DIT SCHIP: Hailed the state's frigate Alarm. This ship had a north latitude of 14°42' and a longitude of 324°1'. Skipper Krijn Rutjes signals that his ship is at a north latitude of 14°43' and a longitude of 223°52'
PRAAIEN HET SCHIP 'T DUIFJE. DIT SCHIP I: Hailed the ship 't Duifje. This ship is at longitude 36°7'
PRAAIEN HET SCHIP 'T DUIFJE. LENGTE VAN: Hailed the ship 't Duifje. Longitude of this ship was 29°0'
PRAAIEN HET SCHIP VAN DE COMMANDANT: NB: Hailed the commander's ship: north latitude 36°19' longitude 334°40'
PRAAIEN HET SCHIP WESTERVELD (LENGTE 351: Hailed the ship Westerveld (longitude 351°46') and Borsele (354°21')
PRAAIEN HET SCHIP WESTERVELD. DE LENGTE: Hailed the ship Westerveld. The longitude of this ship was 25°43
PRAAIEN KAPITEIN MULDER. ZIJN NB IS 34°3: Hailed Captain Mulder. His north latitude is 34°31' longitude 331°11'
PRAAIEN RENSWOUDE. DE LANGTE VAN DAT SCH: Hailed Renswoude. The longitude of that ship is 31°15'
PRAAIEN RENSWOUDE. DE LENGTE VAN DIT SCH: Hailed Renswoude. The longitude of this ship is 348°54'
PRAAIEN RENSWOUDE. DIT SCHIP BEVINDT ZIC: Hailed Renswoude. This ship is at a longitude of 15°3'
PRAAIEN RENSWOUDE. DIT SCHIP HEEFT EEN L: Hailed Renswoude. This ship has a longitude of 353°57'
PRAAIEN RESWOUDE, LENGTE VAN DAT SCHIP I: Hailed Reswoude, longitude of that ship is 32°31'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER ABRAM HULT, DIE GISTERE: Hailed skipper Abram Hult, who yesterday had a north latitude of 27°50', longitude 324°11'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER ABRAM HULT. ZIJN NB VAN: Hailed skipper Abram Hult. His north latitude yesterday was 18°21' and longitude 323°10'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER ABRAM HULT. ZIJN POSITI: Hailed skipper Abram Hult. His position was north latitude 46°34' longitude 357°43'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER ARIE VAN HAARST NB 42°3: Hailed skipper Arie van Haarst north latitude 42°32' longitude 345°52' and skipper Coster north latitude 42°30' longitude 346°30. The state's frigate north latitude 42°31' longitude 346°55'. Skipper Abram Hult north latitude 42°30' longitude 346°38. Joost Dankers north latitude 42°26' longitude 343°11'. Krijn Rutjes north latitude 42°33'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER ARIE VAN HAARSTE. ZIJN: Hailed skipper Arie van Haarste. His north latitude is 18°18', longitude 322°14'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER CRIJN RUTJES: NB 49°24': Hailed skipper Crijn Rutjes: north latitude 49°24' longitude 7°47
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER JURGEN COSTER. ZIJN SCH: Hailed skipper Jurgen Coster. His ship had a north latitude of 30°8' and a longitude of 326°0'
PRAAIEN SCHIPPER VAN DER MEER NB 27°45': Hailed skipper Van der Meer north latitude 27°45' longitude 304°25'
PRAAIEN VLGS ORDER NR. 13 OM TE VRAGEN W: Hailed per order no. 13 to ask why he falls so far behind at night
PRAAIJDE HET SCHIP RENSWOUDE EN VERSTOND: Hailed the ship Renswoude and understood that his longitude of the 6th had been 2°13'
PRAAIJDE SCHIPPER REUL HIJ SEIJDE ONS DA: Hailed skipper Reul. He told us that he had found his leak and was busy stopping it, that it was a nail that had come out.
PRAIDE ONSE MAAT RENSWOUDE EN VERSTINDE: Hailed our consort Renswoude and understood that his longitude was 355°35'
PRAIJDE ONSE MAAT (RENSWOUDE) EN VERSTON: Hailed our consort (Renswoude) and understood that his longitude had been 354°14'
PRESUMEERDE LAND TE ZIEN IN HET OZO. DE: Presumed to see land in the ESE. The 23rd is not in the journal.
PRESUMEERDEN ONS VOLGENS DE DIEPTEN IN G: Presumed ourselves, by the soundings on the bottom, to be off and on Caap Angulas
PRETENDE AVISTAR LA ISLA DE SANTA MARIA: Intends to sight the island of Santa Maria
PRIMER DÍA DE ESTE DIARIÓ CON TABLAS Y D: First day of this journal with tables and position data.
PRIMER DÍA DEL DIARIO EN QUE HAY TABLA Y: First day of the journal with a table and position data
PRIS POUR POINT DU DÉPART LA LATITUDE ET: Taking as the starting point the latitude and longitude entered in the column of the 30th, the day of our departure from Sainte-Croix.
PROBABLEMENTE EN LA DESEMBOCADURA DEL RÍ: Probably at the mouth of the Pindaré River, in the province of Maranhao
PROBEERDEN EEN DOORTOCHT NAAR DE NOORD T: Tried to find a passage to the north
PROBEREN DOOR TE WENDEN DE WESTELIJKE WI: Try to tack to find the westerly winds.
PROBEREN OM BIJ HET SCHIP TE KOMEN, OMDA: Try to reach the ship, because we have little water left and about eighty sick. Show the flag and fire a cannon shot. The ship comes toward us and shows the English flag. Send a sloop with Lieutenant Zeigers to it. The Englishman cannot spare any water, because the storm had kept him from calling at Baai Falso.
PROBEREN OP DE BREEDTE VD ROLOS TE KOMEN: Try to reach the latitude of the Rolos
PROBLEEM MET DE PRECIESE LIGGING VAN MAD: Problem with the exact position of Madeira
PROSIGUE EL SARGAZO. CIELOS Y HORIZONTES: The sargasso continues. Skies and horizons with thick, hazy cloud. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
The sargasso continues. Skies and horizons with scattered clear cloud. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
The sargasso continues. Skies and horizons with scattered cloud. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
The sargasso continues. Skies and horizons with overcast cloud. At 12:30 a rain shower falls. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
PROSIGUE EL SARGAZO. HORIZONTES CALIMOSO: The sargasso continues. Hazy horizons, skies with cloud. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation
PROSIGUE EL SARGAZO. HORIZONTES DEL NO A: The sargasso continues. Horizons from the NW to the ESE squally and the rest with clear cloud
PUNTA DE LA PIEDAD AL NNE 5º E: Punta de la Piedad to the NNE 5º E
PUNTA DE SAGRESA AL ONO. PUNTA DE LAGOS: Punta de Sagresa to the WNW. Punta de Lagos to the N 5º NE. Distance from the nearest coast: 7 miles
PUSO DESPUÉS EL NAVÍO LA SEÑAL DE PREPAR: Afterwards the ship put up the signal to prepare to anchor.
PV + DW: LODEN DE DIEPTE. VERANDERDE MER: PV + DW: Sounded the depth. Changed meridian to the E 20,25 miles.

When the sun rose the fog disappeared and they sight the coast of the Isla de los Reyes as far as beyond the point that forms the north side of the entrance of Puerto Deseado. He describes the birds, fish and animals, as well as the coast they sight. A boat with 7 men comes up to them and tells them that 'they belonged to an English brigantine whose captain left them in those deserted regions with some provisions and the hope that he would return for them after 8 months. The Indians, who made some incursions from the interior of the continent, began to pursue them, took prisoner the pilot, who was able to be ransomed with a small quantity of brandy, and another unfortunate man who would naturally perish or had perished among those inhuman men. The rest took refuge in a launch on the beach where they established their dwelling and spent the last winter. They roamed the land along the shore occupied in killing seals, already having a store of 12000 skins, and with these and 50 casks of fat they awaited their captain, but the period he had set for them had expired, provisions had diminished, and in these unhappy circumstances they decided to prepare the launch, putting to sea and seeking the first European settlement, preferring an uncertain hope to a certain death. The commander received them kindly, stopped and sent the boats for their baggage and a boy who had remained with them, leaving in a barrel in a visible spot notice of the fate of these men, and in it a testimony to the English captain and his nation of the way the Spaniards fulfil the duties of hospitality.'
