ROKEN MET LAVENDEL, BLOEMEN EN GENEVERBE: Fumigated with lavender, flowers and juniper berries.
ROKEN TUSSENDEKS MET JENEVERBESSEN EN BR: Fumigated between decks with juniper berries and burnt gunpowder mixed with brandy.
ROND 6 UUR WAS DE BREEDTE VAN DE AJAX 18: Around 6 o'clock the latitude of the Ajax was 18 degrees 6 minutes and its distance to Barbuda SW by W, 8 miles.
RONDLOOPENDE WINDEN VAN W DOOR Z VAN O E: Winds veering from W through S, from E and N.
ROOKTEN TUSSCHENDEKS, MET KRUIDSISSENS (: Fumigated between decks with gunpowder squibs (but the sick could not stand the air).
Fumigated between decks with berries etc.
ROOKTEN TUSSENDEKS MET JENEVERBESSEN EN: Fumigated between decks with juniper berries and gunpowder.
ROOKTEN TUSSENDEKS MET KRUIT EN AZIJN: Fumigated between decks with gunpowder and vinegar.
Fumigated between decks with gunpowder etc.
ROSENBURG HAD LENGTE 352G37M, VOORLAND H: Rosenburg had longitude 352G37M, Voorland had longitude 351G14M.
ROTJES=ROTIES=VOGELS. BEGONNE ENKELDE SC: Rotjes = roties = birds. Began to see a few ice floes.
RUIMEN HET RUIM OP. GAAN BIJ JOODSE SAVA: Cleared the hold. Go to Joodse Savanna to fetch water.
RUMBO LOS CORRESPONDIENTES PARA ENTRAR E: Course as appropriate to enter Arica (...) a small anchor was laid out...
RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VIENTO DEL MEDIODÍ: Course and wind direction at midday / other data from nightfall or dawn.
Course and direction of the noon wind / other data from [?] or dawn
Course and direction of the noon wind / rest of the general references
RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VIENTO MEDIODÍA /: Course and direction of the noon wind / wind force and sea state closest to noon
Course and direction of the noon wind / rest of the references closest to noon
RUMBO Y DIRECCIÓN DEL VIENTO: MEDIODÍA /: Course and direction of the wind: noon / other references: the closest to noon
RUMBO Y VIENTO - MEDIODÍA / MAR - ANOCHE: Course and wind - noon / sea - dusk
RUMBO Y VIENTO DE MEDIODÍA / MAR DEL ANO: Course and wind at noon / sea at [?] or dawn.
RUMBO Y VIENTO MEDIODÍA / MAR ANOCHECER: Course and wind noon / sea dusk
RUMBO Y VIENTO MEDIODÍA / REFERENCIA DEL: Course and wind noon / reference for the sea at dawn.
S AVONDS TZK, ONWEER, HAGEL EN REGEN: In the evening [?], thunder, hail and rain
S' AVONDS KLAART HET OP EN HET WEERLICHT: In the evening it clears up and the lightning is strong on the horizon.
At night strong phosphorescence in the water.
S.B.N. DOET SEIN AAN MIJ OM MET DE SCHEP: S.B.N. signals to me to separate from the convoy with the ships for Suriname.
S.B.N. DOET SEIN OM TE SEPAREEREN VAN ON: S.B.N. signals to separate from us; the captain sails out with the aforementioned schooner, both to Surinam
SAAGEN EEN SCHILPAD ALSMEDE GROENTE EN S: Saw a turtle as well as greenery and pieces of wood drifting past, also saw a tropicbird, a fulmar and a seagull
SAAGEN VERSCHIJDEN ZEEQUALLEN EN VEUIJLI: Saw various jellyfish and filth drifting past
SAGEN EEN MALEVIT EN VERSCHIJDE ANDRE GE: Saw a gannet and various other birds as well as a small clump of greenery
SAGEN EEN VREDE VUURTJE OP ONSE GROTE TO: Saw a St Elmo's fire on our main top
SAGEN ENIGE KLEINE STRANDMEEUWEN, 2 MALL: Saw some small shore gulls, 2 gannets and still daily very many fish called laret and benijt
SAGEN ENKELDE STUKKEN IJS: Saw a few pieces of ice
SAGEN NOG DAAGELIJKS VERSCHIJDEN WITTE P: Still saw daily various white tropicbirds
SAGEN VERSCHIJDE BESAANTJES DRIJVEN: Saw various small sail-like jellyfish drifting
SALE CON DOS CORREOS DE BUENOS AIRES Y C: Leaves with two mail ships from Buenos Aires and Canarias, due to the war.
SALE DE CAMARIÑAS CON DESTINO A LA HABAN: Leaves Camariñas bound for La Habana. Descriptors, sea and wind from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE LA CORUÑA A LAS 6:00. DESCRIPTOR: Leaves La Coruña at 6:00. Descriptors, sea and wind from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE LA CORUÑA PERO DEBE VOLVER A FON: Leaves La Coruña but must anchor again because of heavy rains, where it remains until 17-12-1791. Force and descriptors from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE LA CORUÑA. DESCRIPTORES, VIENTO: Leaves La Coruña. Descriptors, wind and sea from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE LA CORUÑA. EL DIARIO COMIENZA EL: Leaves La Coruña. The log begins on 31-MAR but 8 days are spent in La Coruña because of unsuitable winds. Noon data, although some dawn data are included in the descriptors
SALE DE MARAÑÓN PARA BARCELONA. POSICIÓN: Leaves Marañón for Barcelona. Position at 18.00
SALE DE MONTECRISTO. DESCRIPCION, VIENTO: Leaves Montecristo. Description, wind and sea from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE MONTEVIDEO DE REGRESO A LA CORUÑ: Leaves Montevideo on the return to La Coruña
SALE DE PUERTO RICO. DESCRIPCION, VIENTO: Leaves Puerto Rico. Description, wind and sea from dawn, the rest from noon
SALE DE SANTA CRUZ DE TENERIFE PARA CÁDI: Leaves Santa Cruz de Tenerife for Cádiz. Position and bearing at 19.00
SALE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA: Leaves the port of La Coruña
SALE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA AL PUERTO D: Leaves the port of La Coruña for the port of Montevideo
SALE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTINO: Leaves the port of La Coruña bound for Montevideo
SALE DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA PARA EL DE: Leaves the port of La Coruña for Montevideo
SALE NUEVAMENTE DE LA CORUÑA. FUERZA Y D: Leaves La Coruña again. Force and descriptors from dawn, the rest from noon
SALEN DEL PUERTO DE CADIZ PRIMERO LA DES: The Descubierta and then the Atrevida leave the port of Cádiz. Olavide arrives aboard the Descubierta with the pilots. At 11:15 they set course for Canarias.
SALIDA DE CARTAGENA CON DESTINO CÁDIZ: Departure from Cartagena bound for Cádiz
SALIDA DE CÁDIZ A CRUZAR SOBRE HUELVA EN: Departure from Cádiz to cruise off Huelva together with the brigantine Jacinta
SALIDA DE CÁDIZ CON LA ESPEDICIÓN SECRET: Departure from Cádiz with the secret expedition under the command of the Marquis Cassa Tilli, (...) and D. Pedro Ceballos (...)
SALIDA DE CÁDIZ PARA EL BLOQUEO DE LA PL: Departure from Cádiz for the blockade of the fortress of Gibraltar, the cruise to be on the west side of the Strait (...) under the command of His Excellency Sr. D. Antonio Ulloa, lieutenant general embarked in this ship named the Rl. Fénix
SALIDA DE CÁDIZ PARA TÁNGER EN UNIÓN DEL: Departure from Cádiz for Tánger together with the brigantine-schooner Encantadora. By telegraph the general of the department ordered that these vessels set sail...
SALIDA DE LA BAHÍA DE MONTERREY EN 14 DE: Departure from the Bay of Monterrey on 14 January 1793, located at lat. north 36º 36' and long. west of San Blas 16º 36', for the port of San Blas. Course of the frigate Aranzazu from the Bay of Monterrey to the port of San Blas
SALIDA DE LA CONCEPCIÓN Y FONDEADERO DE: Departure from the Concepción and the anchorage of Talcaguano
SALIDA DE LA CORUÑA AL PUERTO DE MONTEVI: Departure from La Coruña to the port of Montevideo
SALIDA DE LA HABANA. POSIBLEMENTE CON DE: Departure from La Habana. Possibly bound for Cádiz.
SALIDA DE LA HABANA. PRIMER DÍA DE DATOS: Departure from La Habana. First day of data and tables.
SALIDA DE MONTEVIDEO PARA EL PUERTO DE S: Departure from Montevideo for the port of Santa Cathalina with provisions and pesos for the garrison of the island and the ships of the squadron
SALIDA DE MONTEVIDEO PARA LA COSTA PATAG: Departure from Montevideo for the Patagonian coast
SALIDA DE MONTEVIDEO PARA SANTA CATHALIN: Departure from Montevideo for Santa Cathalina
SALIDA DE MONTEVIDEO PARA STA. CATALINA: Departure from Montevideo for Sta. Catalina, commissioned to carry provisions
SALIDA DE MOTEVIDEO PARA STA CATALINA: Departure from Motevideo for Sta Catalina
SALIDA DE SANTA CATALINA PARA RIO GRANDE: Departure from Santa Catalina for Rio Grande or Montevideo
SALIDA DE STA CATALINA PARA MONTEVIDEO: Departure from Sta Catalina for Montevideo
SALIDA DE STA. CATALINA PARA MONTEVIDEO: Departure from Sta. Catalina for Montevideo
SALIDA DE VALPARAÍSO PARA LIMA Y PUERTOS: Departure from Valparaíso for Lima and intermediate ports
SALIDA DEL FERROL. REFERENCIA DE VIENTO: Departure from Ferrol. Wind reference from the afternoon.
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE ARICA PARA LIMA: Departure from the port of Arica for Lima
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE BUCARELY EN 11 DE J: Departure from the port of Bucarely on 11 July 1792 to explore and survey the coast between it and Noka
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE BUCARELY EN 17 DE J: Departure from the port of Bucarely on 17 July 1792 to explore and survey the coast between it and Noca. Course of the frigate Aranzazu from the port of Bucarely to Florida Blanca
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE CARTAGENA PARA CÁDI: Departure from the port of Cartagena for Cádiz in company with the ships S. Pablo and Guerrero
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE CARTAGENA PARA LOS: Departure from the port of Cartagena for Palma in Mallorca and Barcelona, escorting as far as the 1st 5 feluccas and 1 xebec loaded with prisoners
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE FLORIDA BLANCA EN 2: Departure from the port of Florida Blanca on 22 July 1792, located on the Isla de la Reina Carlota, at lat. north 54º 14' and long. west of San Blas (not legible) degrees, 33 minutes, to explore and survey the coast between it and
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA A MONTEVI: Departure from the port of La Coruña to Montevideo
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA AL DE MON: Departure from the port of La Coruña to that of Montevideo
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA CORUÑA CON DESTI: Departure from the port of La Coruña bound for that of Montevideo
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA HABANA PARA EL D: Departure from the port of La Habana for that of Cádiz in convoy. The reference for wind and sea closest to noon has been taken.
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE LA ISLA DE JUAN FER: Departure from the port of the island of Juan Fernández to that of Concepción de Chile.
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE NOKA EN 13 DE JUNIO: Departure from the port of Noka on 13 June 1792 for Bucarely, located on the same coast at lat. north 55º 15' and long. 30º 10' west of San Blas
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE NOKA EN 3 DE OCT. D: Departure from the port of Noka on 3 Oct. 1792, located at lat. north 49º and 36' and long. west of San Blas 21º 20', for Monterrey. Course of the frigate Aranzazu from the port of Noka to Monterrey
SALIDA DEL PUERTO DE STAN CATHALINA PARA: Departure from the port of Stan Cathalina for Spain with the troops who remained [?] said island
SALIDA DEL SURGIDERO DE SAN ROQUE EN 29: Departure from the anchorage of San Roque on 29 August 1792, located at lat. north 53º 25' and long. west of San Blas 25º 40', to explore and survey the coast between it and the port of Noka. Course of the frigate Aranzazu
SALIDA DESDE EL PUERTO DE LA CONCEPCIÓN: Departure from the port of Concepción de Chile to Callao. The coast in sight
SALIDA DESDE SANTA CATHALINA EN (COMPAÑÍ: Departure from Santa Cathalina in (company?) with the ships and frigates named below, in order to convoy the vessels that have taken leave and continue to Europe, and afterwards to go to Montevideo to take on provisions
SALIDA EN ESTA MISMA FRAGATA LIEBRE DE E: Departure in this same frigate Liebre from the port of Valparaíso for the presidio and port of Valdivia, year 1769
SALIDA PARA EL PUERTO DE LA HABANA: Departure for the port of La Habana
SALIDA PARA LA ISLA DE BOJOL: Departure for the island of Bojol
SALIDA PARA LA ISLA DE NEGROS: Departure for the island of Negros
SALIDA PARA MONTEVIDEO DESDE SANTA CATAL: Departure for Montevideo from Santa Catalina
SALOMON STRUNG VAN ZWOLLE WERD HET BEEN: Salomon Strung of Zwolle had his leg amputated, after which he died
SALUEERDE DE KAPITEIN LOOPMIJT VAN LANDS: Captain Loopmijt of the state's ship Prinses Caroline saluted with nine shots.
SALUEERDEN MET 15 SCHOTEN, WERD DOOR DE: Saluted with 15 shots, were thanked by the Volage with 17 and by the brig Lijden with 11 shots, by the fort with 13 shots, also by two Dutch merchantmen with 17 and 11 shots; returned a salute with 17 shots and the Spion one of 11 shots; afterwards a gunboat schooner saluted with 4 shots and we another with 11 shots; pitched the awnings and braced the yards.
SALUUT WORDT SLECHTS MET EEN SCHOT BEANT: Salute is answered with only one shot
SALUUTSCHOTEN. DANKEN GOD VOOR DE BEHOUD: Salute shots. Thank God for the safe voyage.
SANSEERDEN BEIDE KUIPERS TOT SOLDAAT, EN: Changed both coopers into soldiers, and appointed 2 soldiers as coopers. Changed the cook's mate with a soldier and some soldiers into sailors. Inspected the guns. Decide not to call at St. Jago. Also for the 30 sick there is no need to call at St. Jago: none of them have scurvy or other contagious diseases. 'We' therefore need not lengthen the voyage unnecessarily and put the gentlemen to expense.
SARGAZO, PAJAROS CARNEROS CORBAS Y TABLE: Sargassum, [?] birds, [?] and planks. Clear skies, horizons with thick cloud banks, squally. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SARGAZOS Y TABLEROS EN ABUNDANCIA. CIELO: Sargassum and planks in abundance. Skies and horizons overcast. At 15:30 an ugly squall comes in. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SAVONS PEIJLDE DE SON EN BEVONDT 5 GR 34: In the evening took the sun's bearing and found 5 gr 34 min northwesterly variation
SAVONTS WARE WIJ BENEVENS ONS MAAT ENGEL: In the evening we were, together with our mate Engelbertus Lucas, in the open sea
SBN DEED SEIN OM MET SCHEEPEN 'T EXCERCE: S.B.N. signals the ships to exercise and to form up in lines of battle
SBN DOET SEIN AAN OORLOGSSCHEPEN OM (EEN: S.B.N. signals to the warships to sail ahead (a couple of hours).
SBN WIL OP DE RHEDE VAN PORTEPRAAIJ OP H: S.B.N. wants to anchor in the roads of Portepraaij on the island of Sintjago and possibly do damage to English ships
SCHAARVOGELS, MANTEL EN ANDERE MEEUWEN E: Shearwaters, mantle gulls and other gulls and fish. Phosphorescence in the water
SCHAARVOGELS, PIJLSTAARTEN EN VEEL VIS: Shearwaters, tropicbirds and lots of fish
SCHEEPSJONGEN A. VAN OOSTERDORP OVERLEDE: Ship's boy A. van Oosterdorp died.
SCHEEPSJONGEN DE ZEE AFGESTRAFT WGNS KLE: Ship's boy punished at sea for petty theft
SCHEEPSJONGEN E. WHITLOO OVER BOORD GEVA: Ship's boy E. Whitloo fell overboard and drowned.
SCHEEPSJONGEN UIT HET GROOTWAND GEVALLEN: Ship's boy fell from the main shrouds
SCHEEPSKOK DE BOT IN DE BOEIEN WGNS NALA: Ship's cook De Bot put in irons for negligence
SCHEEPSMAAT RITTERSEN IN DE BOEIEN EN BA: Ship's mate Rittersen in irons and baker Schaber under arrest for insubordination and drunkenness.
SCHEEPSRAAD BELEGD: WILLEM VAN DER VLIER: Ship's council held: Willem van der Vlier appointed gunner's mate and Pieter Angelvorst van Molde appointed quartermaster.
SCHEEPSRAAD OVER DE BEHOEFTEN VAN DE BEM: Ship's council on the needs of the crew. Christiaan Windel appointed quartermaster
Ship's council on the crew and the sick. Have 8 invalids
SCHEEPSRAAD OVER DE ZIEKEN. 24 INPOTENTE: Ship's council on the sick. 24 invalids. Use ventilator
SCHEEPSRAAD OVER EQUIPAGE EN ZIEKEN, HEB: Ship's council on the crew and the sick, have 12 invalids, at the surgeon's request make a separate compartment or sick partition of sailcloth
Ship's council on the crew and the sick, have 4 invalids, but not of importance, distribute a hogshead of beer
SCHEEPSRAAD OVER IMPOTENTEN EN GESTELDHE: Ship's council on invalids and the condition of the people
SCHEEPSRAAD OVER VOLK EN ZIEKEN: Ship's council on the people and the sick
SCHEEPSRAAD WEGENS DE ZIEKEN. GEEN IMPOT: Ship's council because of the sick. No invalids. Inspection: all well
SCHEEPSRAAD: 5 IMPOTENTEN, WAARONDER EEN: Ship's council: 5 invalids, one of whom suffers from dropsy. Gave half a month's rations.
SCHEEPSRAAD: 5 ZIEKEN, KEERDEN HET KRUIT: Ship's council: 5 sick, turned the gunpowder, drizzle
SCHEEPSRAAD: 7 IMPOTENTEN, DOCH TOT NOG: Ship's council: 7 invalids, but so far without danger
SCHEEPSRAAD: 8 ZIEKEN, WAARVAN 4 MET SCH: Ship's council: 8 sick, 4 of them with scurvy. Applied every means to halt the spread of that affliction. Issued rations of butter, vinegar, sugar.
SCHEEPSRAAD: 8 ZIEKEN.VERSTREKTEN VOOR 8: Ship's council: 8 sick. Issued 8 days' rations to the crew.
SCHEEPSRAAD: 9 IMPOTENTEN, MEEST LABOURE: Ship's council: 9 invalids, mostly suffering from scurvy. Gave rations of butter, oil, vinegar, sugar.
SCHEEPSRAAD: BLEKEN ER 3 ZIEK TE ZIJN, B: Ship's council: 3 turned out to be sick, at inspection all still well
SCHEEPSRAAD: STELLEN MATROOS S. WEERUS K: Ship's council: appoint sailor S. Weerus Kroeze as third watch
SCHEEPTEN 24 ZIEKEN NAAR LAND IN HET HOS: Shipped 24 sick ashore to the hospital.
SCHEIDEN MET KAPITEIN MINKEVELDT VAN KAP: Parted from Captain Minkeveldt and Captain Tuijneman because there was too much difference in the sailing position. Laid the compasses at 10 degrees east of the needle.
SCHEMA VAN SCHIPPERS EN SCHEPEN DIE VOOR: Diagram of skippers and ships lying off Paramaribo.
SCHEPEN GAVEN BESTEK, STAAN MET BESTEK O: Ships gave their reckonings; their reckoning places them on land
SCHEPEN HIJSEN BATAAFSE VLAG IVM PASSERE: Ships hoist the Batavian flag for crossing the line
SCHEPEN VAN KONVOOI WISSELEN BESTEK UIT: Ships of the convoy exchange reckonings
SCHEPEN VD VLOOT GEVEN BESTEK OP. GAAN N: Ships of the fleet give in their reckonings. Go to [?] for a council of war.
SCHERMUTSELING MET EEN ENGELSE SNAUW OP: Skirmish with an English snow on its way from London to New York: this little ship seemed to be equipped for privateering or for war
SCHERP IN DEN WIND OM NIET OP DE KUST VA: Close-hauled to avoid falling onto the coast of Brazil
SCHIEMANSMAAT DIRK COSTER OVERLEDEN. SOL: Assistant mate Dirk Coster died. Soldier Matthijs Hamstra died
SCHIEMANSMAAT HENDRIK JANSEN VIEL BUYTEN: Assistant mate Hendrik Jansen fell overboard and drowned
SCHIEMANSMAAT JAN BATIST DE LAZARIA VAN: Assistant mate Jan Batist de Lazaria of Livorno died
SCHIEMANSMAAT PIETERSEN WEGENS INSURBORD: Assistant mate Pietersen under arrest for insubordination.
SCHIET DE LIJN IN DE SLOEP, MAKEN ALLES: Stow the line in the boat, make everything ready to go catching
SCHIETEN LIJN IN DE SLOEPE EN BRENGE SLO: Stow the line in the boat and get the boats ready for fishing
SCHIETEN LIJNEN IN DE SLOEPEN (MAKEN KLA: Stow lines in the boats (make ready to go fishing)
Painting the ship on the outside.
Ship 'Rhoon' is still having a hard time.
SCHIP BEVINDT ZICH OP EEN LENGTE VAN 335: Ship is at a longitude of 335°38'24'' east of Teneriffe
SCHIP BEVINDT ZICH OP LENGTE VAN 344°39': Ship is at a longitude of 344°39'33'' east of Teneriffe
SCHIP BURGH LAAT WITTE VLAG WAAIEN, ONDA: Ship Burgh flies a white flag; despite pumping, the water in the ship does not decrease. It is decided to abandon this hull to save the souls. Transfer the crew over.
Ship had strong phosphorescence in the water.
SCHIP IS BIJ DE OOSTVAARWATER VAN SOERAB: Ship is at the east channel of Soerabaja
SCHIP KOMT NAUWELIJKS VOORUIT VANWEGE ST: Ship barely makes headway because of storm, still lies at anchor in England
SCHIP LAVEERT NAAR BOVEN EN KOMT BIJ DE: Ship tacks to windward and arrives at the roadstead of Elmina, where it prepares for the crossing to America and takes aboard more slaves, water, firewood, ballast
SCHIP MAAKT DE OVERSTEEK NAAR DE BOCHT V: Ship makes the crossing to the Bight of Gabon
SCHIP RAAKT DOOR ZIJN VOORRADEN HEEN EN: Ship is running through its supplies and it is decided first to go back to Menado to replenish the supplies. After this they will work eastward of the Celebes through the Strait Sabijer.
SCHIP SLINGERT STERK VANGEN 6 OXHOOFDEN: Ship rolls heavily. Caught 6 hogsheads and 3.5 half leaguers of water. The two Chinese are let out of irons.
SCHIP STAMPTE ZWAAR IN DE ZEE: Ship pitched heavily in the sea
SCHIP STAMPTE ZWAAR IN ZEE DOOR DE HOGE: Ship pitched heavily in the sea because of the high swell
SCHIP UIT BREMEN GISTE LENGTE VAN 25 GRA: Ship from Bremen estimated a longitude of 25 degrees
SCHIP VAART NU IN DE BOGT NAAR DE REDE V: Ship now sails in the bight toward the roadstead of Nazareth and on to the Rio Gabon and again to the roadstead of Nazareth, and finally goes via St. Thomee back to the fatherland, while engaged in buying teeth, crevel, wax, redwood and the slave trade
SCHIP VAART NU IN HET KANAAL. WE WAREN 1: Ship now sails in the Channel. We were 1 degree 10 minutes further east than we estimated
SCHIP VAART NU IN HET KANAAL. ZAGEN BRAN: Ship now sails in the Channel. Saw breakers. Were drawn toward the shore
SCHIP VAART OP DE KUST VAN SURINAME: Ship sails on the coast of Suriname
SCHIP VAART VAN BATAVIA NAAR O.A. SEMARA: Ship sails from Batavia to, among others, Semarang, Soerabaya, Bali, Macasser, Coepang and Timor, to finally sail from Batavia back to the Netherlands
Ship sails from Elmina to the Bight.
SCHIP VAART VERDER ALLEEN NOG ROND IN DE: Ship now only sails around in the North Sea.
SCHIP VAART VERDER NAAR DE BOCHT EN ZEIL: Ship sails on to the Bight and sails between Nazareth and Rio de Gabon, while engaged in the slave trade and buying teeth, crevel and wax
SCHIP VAART VERVOLGENS IN DE NOORDZEE EN: Ship then sails in the North Sea and along the Norwegian coast before finally anchoring at Bergen in Norway.
SCHIP VAART VERVOLGENS LANGS DE KUST VAN: Ship then sails along the coast of Africa from the Basjes to Elmina, while engaged in the slave trade and buying teeth and crevel
SCHIP VERTREKT NAAR DE BOGT. AFGEVAREN B: Ship departs for the Bight. Reckoning sailed off
Ship departs for the open sea.
Ship departs again for the fatherland.
SCHIP VERTREKT WEER NAAR VOLLE ZEE: Ship departs again for the open sea
Ship departs again for the open sea.
SCHIP VERTREKT WEER NAAR VOLLE ZEE. ZETT: Ship departs again for the open sea. Put our reckoning in the Mercator chart
SCHIP VERTREKT WEER. GENERALE KOERS EN V: Ship departs again. General course and distance for the day since the estimate: 5 miles south by east 1/2 east of the Bramspunt
Ship departs again for the open sea.
SCHIP ZEILT NAAR DE REDE VAN ST. ANDRIES: Ship sails to the roadstead of St. Andries and then sails along the African coast to the roadstead of Klein Popo, while engaged in the slave trade. Image 0031 21 December 1756: Revolt among the slaves on the ship, the master cook and the smith are struck dead and stabbed, other whites wounded. We had to shoot with the small arms and use the hand grenade. In the end, after a new revolt, we got the slaves under control. Also casualties among the slaves, for example because they jumped overboard and drowned. Image 0034 27 January 1757: The King of France was said to have declared war on the state, according to an English boat. A French fleet was said to be along the coast, at the roadstead of Accra, and to have captured several Dutchmen. Also a fleet at Axim with the castle Elmina
SCHIPPER BONTJENIA GEEFT EEN BRIEF VOOR: Skipper Bontjenia gives a letter for his shipowner in Rotterdam.
SCHIPPER CORVON VAN EEN ZEEUWSE SLAVENHA: Skipper Corvon of a Zeeland slave trader died
SCHIPPER JAMES DIEGO WIL KONVOOI VERLATE: Skipper James Diego wants to leave convoy
SCHIPPER JAN BAAK BEWEERT DAT GEEN SCHIP: Skipper Jan Baak claims that no ship sails faster than his, whereupon they hold a little race ('we' win). This one (… was more than) 30 miles over land with his reckoning and (it differed) 125 miles from ours.
SCHIPPERS SIJMON KLINT EN HILKES VERMIST: Skippers Sijmon Klint and Hilkes missing
SCHOON SCHIP GEMAAKT. DE MATROOS 3E CC.:: Cleaned the ship. The sailor 3rd [?] Laporte died, the body taken outside the bay in the afternoon.
SCHOREN ENKELE HALZEN ENSCHOTEN IN DE ON: [?] some tacks and sheets in the lower sails.
SCHOT MET SCHERP OP EEN BARK OM ACHTER O: Fired a live shot at a barque to make it come round astern.
SCHOTEN 1 X MET SCHERP OP EEN BARK WAARO: Fired 1 time with live ammunition at a barque, whereupon it anchored. Then another 2 shots with live ammunition at an English barque that was cruising here, to make it come round astern. Then fetched this skipper from his barque with an officer and had him pay for the 2 shots. The money is put in the poor box [?].
SCHOTEN 4 X MET SCHERP OP 3 BARKEN DIE N: Fired 4 times with live ammunition at 3 barques that had not sailed astern of us. One of them saluted with 9 shots (we thanked with 7).
Fired 6 times with live ammunition at a barque.
SCHOTEN LIJNEN IN ONS 6 SLOEPEN EN VERDE: Stowed lines in our 6 boats and distributed oars and bailers
SCHOUT BIJ NACHT (SBN) GEEFT SEIN OM TE: Rear admiral (SBN) gives signal to range (to line up?). Remark about the position of Porto Santo. Compass bearings.
SCHOUT BIJ NACHT DOET SEIN AAN DE KOOPVA: Rear admiral signals the merchantmen and warships bound for the Bight of France, the coast of Biscay and Cadiz and the Mediterranean to separate. Salute shots. We continued with 4 warships and 11 merchantmen. Illustration included of the diagram in which the ships of the convoy sail.
SCHOUT BIJ NACHT EN RIDDER WOLTERBEEK KE: Rear admiral and Knight Wolterbeek announce that today is the 66th birthday of the Dowager Princess of Orange.
SCHOUT BIJ NACHT GEEFT PAPIEREN OM MANEU: Rear admiral gives papers for performing maneuvers in case of battles.
SCHRIJVER BESCHRIJFT DE PASSAGE VAN DE L: Clerk describes the crossing of the line and relates at length that the officers are smeared with soap and the crew with grease, and that they were rinsed off in a large sail with water in it
SCHRIJVER BRENGT SEINBOEK NAAR DE KOOPVA: Clerk takes signal book to the merchantmen. Name of the skipper: Jumes Dupo, on his way to Middelburg. The last barque parted from the convoy.
SCHRIJVER EN LUITENANT INNEN 30 HOLLANDS: Clerk and lieutenant collect 30 Dutch guilders in fines on the Johanna and the Susanna
Clerk of the depot in Batavia J.P. Ligtvoet died.
SCHRIJVER WERD NAAR HET SCHIP VAN SCHIPP: Clerk was sent to the ship of skipper Roelof Zuiderstroom to fetch a sailor who had abused his skipper with brutal words. At the Maarsen he was put in irons. A statement against this sailor was also made there.
SE ACERCAN A LA COSTA. AL PONERSE EL SOL: They approach the coast. At sunset they felt the air very warm, which on that coast is a sign of a SW wind that notably disturbs the sea and tends to come on suddenly, placing in the greatest danger the ships it finds under full sail. At nightfall they anchor 6 leagues from the coast
SE ACERCAN A TIERRA Y FONDEAN A 4 LEGUAS: They approach land and anchor 4 leagues from the coast. At 14:00 they weigh anchor
SE CELEBRA EL PASO DEL CABO DE HORNOS: The passing of Cape Horn is celebrated
SE CENTRA EN COMENTARIOS SOBRE LA ACTIVI: Focuses on comments about the squadron's activity.
SE CONSIDERA MUY CERCA DEL ECUADOR. FUER: They consider themselves very close to the equator. Strong currents to the N
SE CONSIDERA N-S CON LO MAS ORIENTAL DE: They consider themselves N-S with the easternmost part of Malvina Island at a distance of 107 leagues
SE CONSIDERAN EN LAS INMEDIACIONES DE LO: They consider themselves in the vicinity of the general winds of the SE and SSE
SE DA FONDO EN EL PUERTO DE MONTEVIDEO A: Anchor is dropped in the port of Montevideo at 9:45 h
SE DA LA LONGITUD DE LLEGADA AL O DE CÁD: The longitude of arrival west of Cádiz is given
SE DA LA LONGITUD OCCIDENTAL DE CÁDIZ: The longitude west of Cádiz is given
SE DEMARCARON EL ISLOTE GRANDE DE MARTIN: Bearing taken on the large islet of Martin Bas at ESE 5º E
Bearing taken on Cape Monchic at NE 1/4 [?].
SE DESPIDE DEL CORREO EL PRINCIPE: Takes leave of the mail ship El Principe
SE DIRIGEN AL MORRO DE ARICA. FONDEAN FR: They head for the Morro de Arica. Anchor off a small island in the bay. Noon measurement, the rest from dawn
SE ECHÓ AL AGUA EL CADÁVER DEL ARTILLERO: The body of the sea gunner Pedro Merodio, native of Llanes, was thrown into the water
SE ENFERMA GRAN PARTE DE LA TRIPULACION: A large part of the crew falls ill
The ships of the convoy are awaited.
SE HA COGIDO UNA TONINA AL ARPÓN Y (...): A porpoise was caught with the harpoon and (...) we have found its animal anatomy to be, its structure similar to that of a pig
SE HA MANTENIDO ALGO CERRADO CAYENDO UNA: It has stayed somewhat overcast, with a drizzle falling similar to that of Lima
SE HA TOMADO EL ESTADO DE LA MAR AL MEDI: The state of the sea was taken at noon, and failing that at nightfall or dawn.
SE HA VISTO CANTIDAD DE BONITOS, VOLADOR: A quantity of bonitos, flying fish and some small birds were seen.
SE HA VISTO CERCA DEL MEDIODIA UN PAJARO: Near midday a dark bird the size of a pigeon was seen, with brown wings and a broad fan-shaped tail, in my opinion similar to the little eagle.
SE HA VISTO INFINIDAD DE SARGAZO, BONITO: A great quantity of sargasso, bonitos and flying fish were seen, and a frigatebird.
SE HA VISTO MÁS SARGAZO QUE LOS ANTERIOR: More sargasso was seen than on the previous days, many birds and some young whales.
SE HA VISTO SARGAZO CON MUCHA ABUNDANCIA: Sargasso was seen in great abundance, a fresh breeze, the weather overcast and the sea smooth. (...) From 10 at night the weather turned squally, the wind freshening with some sea. (...) The sky dawned clear and the horizons squally, the wind moderate, and after the sun rose it began to freshen.
SE HA VISTO SOBE DE BALLENAS Y TORTUGAS: A [?] of whales and turtles was seen.
SE HA VISTO UN PÁJARO BOBO Y BANDADAS DE: A booby and flocks of frigatebirds were seen.
A bird and some sargasso were seen.
SE HA VISTO UNA TORTUGA LA PRIMERA QUE V: A turtle was seen, the first I have seen. According to the current streaks I have made one mile per hour until 8 o'clock, when we tacked toward the corrected west.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 10 DE LA MAÑANA: Sets sail at 10 in the morning with a light southeast wind, but it lasted so little that it then jumped to the east-northeast with 1 rain shower that forced them to anchor with 1 kedge anchor.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 10:00. DESCRIPTO: Sets sail at 10:00. Descriptors from noon or the day's run.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 10:00. MEDICION: Sets sail at 10:00. Measurement from noon or the day's run, except the descriptors, which are from nightfall. French chart.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 10:00. PASA 6 DÍ: Sets sail at 10:00. Spends 6 days in Cumaná. They went from Cumaná to Cuba by another route because Admiral Razney was at the Islas Víboras y Caimanes with his whole squadron. They depart in company with the packet boat El Principe.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 11:00. DESCRIPTO: Sets sail at 11:00. Descriptors from noon or the day's run. Cannot leave earlier because of calms and strong winds.

Had trouble passing the Strait of the Channel.
SE HACE A LA VELA A LAS 12:00. MEDICION: Sets sail at 12:00. Measurement from nightfall or the day's run.

SE HACEN A LA VELA A LAS 16:00. NO PUDO: They set sail at 16:00. Could not observe. Measurement and data from noon, except the descriptors, which are usually from nightfall. Navigation diary from El Ferrol to the Río de la Plata by the frigate ensign Don Gregorio de José y Llaños, kept aboard the frigate Santa Perpetua under the command of Capt. José Postillo from 1-2-1774. They follow the Dutch chart.
SE HACEN A LA VELA A LAS 2:00. VAN EN DE: They set sail at 2:00. They head for Cabo Corrientes in search of some supposed shoals where the San Juan Nepomuceno had previously run aground, but he does not find them, so he thinks the reports were false.
SE HACEN A LA VELA A LAS 5:00 Y FONDEAN: They set sail at 5:00 and anchor at 10:30 to explore the south side of the inlet. The tide rises and falls a great deal. They weigh anchor in the afternoon heading for the Río de Santa Cruz. They anchor at 19:30 when the wind calms. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
SE HACEN A LA VELA A LAS 5:00. TODO EL D: They set sail at 5:00. All day they sail near land. The data are usually from dawn and the observation from noon.
SE HACEN A LA VELA A LAS 6:30. LLEGAN AL: They set sail at 6:30. They arrive at the Morro de Topocalma.
SE HAN CONTINUADO EN VER AUN HOY AL MEDI: Birds of the island have continued to be seen even today at noon, particularly (Paylle en cus), that is, tropicbirds, which screech near the ship many times, but not always are so many seen in this part of the island.
SE HAN MANTENIDO MUY CLAROS LOS CIELOS Y: The skies and horizons have stayed very clear.
SE HAN TOMADO LOS DATOS DE LA SIGUIENTE: The data have been taken as follows: state of the sea at noon, and failing that at nightfall or dawn. Latitude observed, and failing that latitude of arrival. The ship commanding the convoy is El Miño.
SE HAN VISTO (...) MULTITUD DE PARDELAS: A multitude of shearwaters were seen (...)
SE HAN VISTO A LAS 16:00 UNOS PAJAROS CO: At 16:00 some birds like pigeons, white and black, and a tropicbird were seen.
SE HAN VISTO ABUNDANCIA DE AGUAS MALAS Y: Abundant jellyfish and porpoises were seen.
SE HAN VISTO ALGUNOS BONITOS Y ALBACORAS: Some bonitos and albacores were seen.
SE HAN VISTO DISTINTAS ESPECIES DE PÁJAR: Several kinds of birds, some young whales and some sargassum were seen.
SE HAN VISTO INFINITAS MATAS DE BEJUQUIL: Countless clumps of bejuquillo weed and [?] were seen.
SE HAN VISTO LAS MISMAS AVES Y BALLENATO: The same birds and young whales were seen.
SE HAN VISTO LOBOS Y UN TRONCO DE ÁRBOL: Sea lions and a very large tree trunk were seen.
SE HAN VISTO LOBOS, BALLENATOS Y DELFINE: Sea lions, young whales and dolphins were seen, and large birds, all black with yellow and white beaks, and [?] on the port side.
SE HAN VISTO MUCHA ABUNDANCIA DE LOBOS A: A great abundance of sea lions in very large herds, six young whales. Very small birds like plovers and cachichullo [?] were seen.
White and black birds were seen.
SE HAN VISTO PÁJAROS NEGROS Y BLANCOS PE: Small black and white birds were seen.
SE HAN VISTO PÁJAROS NINOS Y ALGUNOS BAL: Penguins and some young whales were seen.
SE HAN VISTO PÁJAROS Y BALLENAS Y HEMOS: Birds and whales were seen, and during the night we heard some penguins wailing or screeching.
SE HAN VISTO PÁJAROS Y EL AGUA SE HA MAN: Birds were seen and the water remained greenish.
SE HAN VISTO SALTAR MUCHOS PECES Y POR L: Many fish were seen jumping and in the morning 3 or 4 ships.
SE HAN VISTO TONINAS ABUNDANCIA DE AGUAS: Porpoises and an abundance of jellyfish were seen.
SE HAN VISTO UN RABIAHORCADO Y UNA PORCI: A frigatebird and a number of pigeons were seen.
SE HAN VISTO UNOS PÁJAROS BLANCOS Y NEGR: Some white and black birds the size of seagulls were seen.
SE HAN VISTO VARIAS PARDELAS Y RAVIJUNCO: Several shearwaters and tropicbirds were seen, skies and horizons somewhat heavy, and so night fell; at daybreak horizons somewhat clearer, wind and sea as stated.
Several gabiñas [?] birds (...) and jellyfish, a turtle were seen.
SE INDICA QUE ESTE DÍA SE SALE DE LA BAH: It is noted that on this day they leave the Bahía de Tabla.
SE INICIA EL VIAJE LA CORUÑA - MONTEVIDE: The voyage La Coruña - Montevideo begins.
SE LARGO LA BANDERA POR SER EL DIA DEL R: The flag was flown because it was the King's Day and kept up until sunset.
SE LEYERON ESTA MAÑANA LAS LEYES PENALES: The penal laws were read this morning.
SE NOTO EL AGUA DE COLOR DE SONDA: The water was noticed to be the color of the sounding ground.
SE PASA A LA CARTA FRANCESA Y ESTA A 296: Switched to the French chart and it is at 296º 13' from Tenerife.
SE PASA DE ESTE DÍA SÁBADO 6 DE SEPTIEMB: Skipped from this day, Saturday 6 September, to Monday 8 September. There is no journal for 7 September of that month.
SE PASARON ALGUNOS MANCHONES DE AGUA BLA: Some patches of white water passed close by us.
SE PIERDEN DE VISTA LAS 2 FRAGATAS EXTRA: The 2 foreign frigates are lost from sight.
SE PONE A LA CAPA. DATOS DEL MEDIODIA O: Heaves to. Noon or day's run data. Modern French chart.
SE PONE A LA CAPA. DESCRIPTORES DEL MEDI: Heaves to. Noon or day's run details. The journal begins on 31-Jan-1766 but they do not sail until 3-Feb because of the violence of the clouds and the wind, which came from the west and northwest. Had problems passing the strait of the Canal.
SE PUSO TODA LA GENTE A RACION DE AGUA E: All the people were put on water ration this day. Page misplaced.
SE PUSO UNA AURORA BOREAL MUY ENCENDIDA: A very bright aurora borealis appeared.
SE QUEDAN ATRAVESADOS AGUARDANDO AL QUIR: They lie hove to waiting for the Quiros.
SE REABASTECE EN EL PUERTO DE CANARIAS: Resupplies at the port of Canarias.
SE SIGUE DANDO A LA BOMBA CONTINUAMENTE: Pumping continues without pause and it is known that the water is decreasing.
SE SIGUIÓ ACHICANDO EL AGUA QUE HACÍA EL: Continued bailing out the water the ship was taking in, without ceasing.
SE SITUA A 110 LEGUAS AL E 1/4 NE DEL CA: Positioned 110 leagues E 1/4 NE of the Cabo de San Roque on the coast of Brazil.
SE SONDA Y CON 150 BRAZAS NO HALLAN FOND: Sounding taken and with 150 fathoms they find no bottom, although the signals continue.
SE SONDÓ EL FONDO VARIAS VECES: The bottom was sounded several times.
SE SUMINISTRÓ EL SANTÍSIMO SACRAMENTEO D: The Most Holy Sacrament of the Eucharist and extreme unction were administered to two sick men with scurvy.
SE SUPONE QUE HA CAMBIADO DE REFERENCIA: It is assumed that the reference for measuring longitude has changed, but nothing is indicated. French chart.
SE TOMA LA REFERENCIA DE VIENTO Y MAR DE: The reference for wind and sea is taken from daybreak. (See 30 March to 31 March)
SE TRATA DE OTRO DIARIO DE NAVEGACIÓN DE: This is another navigation journal of the same voyage of the frigate between La Habana and Cádiz in 1794.
SE VEN ABUNDANTES PAJAROS QUE INDICABAN: Abundant birds are seen, which indicated the nearness of the Isla de la Posesión.
SE VEN BALLENAS, LOBOS Y MULTITUD DE PAJ: Whales, sea lions and a multitude of birds are seen, and a frigate that appears to be American or English; it did not fly a flag. The Isla de San Gallan was seen at 1:00.
SE VIERON MUCHAS MOTAS DE CACHILLULLO: Many clumps of cachillullo [?] were seen.
SE VIERON MUCHOS PAJAROS LOCOS Y BOBOS: Many crazy birds and boobies were seen.
SE VIERON MUCHÍSIMOS LANGOSTINOS PASAR P: A great many prawns were seen passing alongside.
SE VIERON MULTITUD DE PARDELAS Y DE OTRO: Multitudes of shearwaters and other small black birds, similar to the [?] that show themselves when there is a gale, were seen.
SE VIO UN PAJARO TABLERO UNICO QUE HEMOS: A single tablero bird [?] was seen, the only one of its kind we have seen on the voyage.
SE VIO UNA AURORA BOREAL DURANTE LA SING: An aurora borealis was seen during the day's run, from the northwest to the northeast. Measurement and data from nightfall or the day's run; some days described at dawn.
SECUNDEMEESTER HARTWIG HENDRIK KLIJN OVE: Second mate Hartwig Hendrik Klijn deceased.
