SEDERT ENIGE TIJD HADDEN 7 A 8 ZIEKEN ME: For some time 7 or 8 sick men, mostly with bilious fevers, had begun to improve.
SEDERT P. GALE HAD MEN OP DE JOHANNA 25: Since P. Gale there were 25 sick on the Johanna (mostly military). The crew was still fairly well.
SEGUIMOS CON (...) BRISA FRESQUITA, ESTA: We continued with (...) a light fresh breeze, the horizons murky with cloud banks and the skies overcast. So night fell, though the wind was a little fresher, continuing the same way until 12 at night (...) From midnight the wind was very gentle, though the sea choppy, and rippling water was seen. Dawn broke the same way.
SEGUIMOS CON (...) EL VTO BONANCIBLE, Y: We continued with (...) the wind gentle, and sea from the northwest until 4 1/2 (...) bad look. (...) At 12 1/2 (night) the wind freshened and at 1 lightning was seen to the north, the look being bad (...) until 3 the lightning continued to the north. Dawn broke with sky and horizon having broken cloud, a light fresh wind and heavy sea from the northwest. (...) weather (...) of thick drizzle.
SEGUIMOS LA DERROTA EN DEMANDA DEL RÍO D: We continued the course heading for the Río de la Plata.
SEGUÍA LA TEMPESTAD DE VTO Y MAR (...) H: The storm of wind and sea continued (...) the horizons having been closed in with a cloud bank, with squalls, gusts and some drizzle.
SEGÚN ALGUNOS SE VIO 1 LOBO MARINO AYER: According to some, 1 sea lion was seen yesterday morning.
SEGÚN LA CARTA EL CUERVO ME DEMORA 21 LE: According to the chart El Cuervo bears 21 leagues from me, but according to the course set down, 37 leagues.
SEGÚN LA CARTA, ISLA TRINIDAD AL N 1/4 N: According to the chart, Isla Trinidad bears N 1/4 NE, distance 15 leagues.
SEIJLDE SOO DE RUIJMTE ONS LEIJDE IN HET: Sailed as the sea room led us, up to the north. Came into quite a lot of ice.
SEIN BIJ DE COMMANDANT TOT ART. 244 GZB: Signal from the commander up to art. 244 GZB for Hippomenes.
SEIN VAN DE COMMANDANT ART. 244, DAARNA: Signal from the commander art. 244, then art. 117, no. 31, etc.
SEINEN EN TELEGRAFEREN MET DE ANDERE SCH: Signaling and telegraphing with the other ships.
SEINEN EN TELEGRAFEREN MET DE JASON EN D: Signaling and telegraphing with the Jason and the Echo.
SEMBLANTE DE VENTAR PERO TODO SE REDUJO: The weather looked like wind, but it all came down to one or another light breeze from the south to southwest with drizzle.
SEMBLANTE MALO, (...) VTO POR LA PROA CO: Bad look, (...) wind ahead with heavy sea (...) night fell with the wind gentle, sky and horizons so closed in that the bow of the ship could hardly be seen, and as much snow falling as the day before. (...) Very cold and the snow (...) At dawn it was no longer snowing except at times, because the wind freshened in gusts and kept pressing, so that at eleven in a gust the ship made nine and a half miles, and at 12 barely ten (...) besides the wind being strong, the look gave worse signs.
SEMBLANTES FEÍSIMOS (...) CON VARIAS FUG: Very ugly looks (...) with several dreadful gusts.
SENTENTIE GESLAGEN OVER PIETER, DE GRAAF: Sentence passed on Pieter, de Graaff, the steward.
SERGANT L. BERKMEIJER IN DE BOEIEN GESLA: Sergeant L. Berkmeijer put in irons for neglect of duty.
SETTE ONS BESTEK 1,5 MIJL WESTELIJKER OP: Set our reckoning 1,5 miles more westerly at 16:48 (sic).
SETTEN BESTEK IN DE RONDE KAART: Set the reckoned position on the plane chart
SETTEN DEN MATROOS BENJAMIN JARDUS MAMME: Lowered the sailor Benjamin Jardus Mammem van Haegen's pay from 16 to 14 guilders because he was not fit to be a sailor
SETTEN HET BESTEK OP 19 GRADEN: Set the reckoned position at 19 degrees
SETTEN HET BESTEK OVER IN DE KAART VAN C: Transferred the reckoned position onto the chart from Cabo Verde to Cabo de Goede Hoop
SETTEN ONS BESTEK TWEE GRADE OOSTELIJKER: Set our reckoned position two degrees further east, at longitude 26:10, because the land lies further east than on the chart
SI MI CUENTA ESTÁ BUENA DEBERÉ VER LA IS: If my reckoning is right, I should see Isla Trinidad this afternoon
SIEMPRE CERCA DE LA COSTA. DESCRIBE ALGU: Always near the coast. Describes some features of the coast near the Rio de Santa Cruz. A pilot struck himself in the face during a maneuver and was badly wounded in the face. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation.
SIEN 2 SWARE HOOSE DIGTE BIJ ONS DEWELKE: Saw 2 heavy waterspouts close to us, which for a full quarter of an hour drew up a great deal of water; closed up all the sails, but the spouts vanished again.
SIEN CAAPSE DUIJVEN EN EEN MEENIGTE NOOR: Saw Cape pigeons and a multitude of noordkapers [?]
SIEN EEN HOOS ZEER SCHIELIJK OPKOMEN: Saw a waterspout form very suddenly
SIEN EEN KANO DRIJVEN VAN 33 VOET EN OOK: Saw a canoe of 33 feet drifting, and also greenery
SIEN EEN KOKXHEN ALSOOK WITTE EN SWARTE: Saw a black-headed gull [?], as well as white and black shore gulls and many noordkapers [?]
SIEN EEN LANGE STRIEM, VOORUIJT OFF HET: Saw a long streak ahead, or there was surf' (will sail less latitude)
SIEN EEN LIJK VOORBIJ ONS DRIJVEN ALS ME: Saw a corpse drift past us, as well as various pieces of broken-off wood and chopped splinters
SIEN EEN MENIGTE LANDVOGELS: Saw a multitude of land birds
SIEN EEN OUDE BOOM BENEFFENS EENIGE STUK: Saw an old tree along with some coconuts, likewise drifting by; also saw a tropicbird and 2 fulmars
SIEN EEN STER VERSCH. HETWELKE ZIG ALS E: Saw a bright star that looked like a fiery ball and showed a tail trailing from itself, which stayed for about 3 minutes and gradually [?] then vanished.
SIEN EEN STUK RIET DRIJVEN: Saw a piece of reed drifting
SIEN GROENTE DRIJVEN, SIEN VEEL NOORDKAP: Saw greenery drifting; saw many noordkapers [?]
SIEN HELE TROEPEN MET MALLEMAKKEN EN MEU: Saw whole flocks of fulmars and gulls
SIEN HOUT, KLAPPERS EN VEEL VUIJLIGHEID: Saw wood, coconuts and much filth drifting
SIEN SOORT VAN WITTE VOGELS VAN GEDAANTE: Saw a kind of white birds shaped like white herons, called flamingos by some, flying; also a tropicbird and small land birds
SIEN STUK HOUT DRIJVE: Saw a piece of wood drifting
SIEN VEEL GEVOGELTE DAARONDER EEN SCHAAR: Saw many fowl, among them a scissor-bird tropicbird [?] and a shore gull
SIEN VEEL ZEEVOGELS EN VLIEGENDE VIS: Saw many seabirds and flying fish
SIEN VERSCHIJDE MEEUWEN EN BASTERD MALLE: Saw various gulls and bastard fulmars
SIEN VERSCHIJDE PIJLSTAARTEN EN OOK BAMB: Saw various tropicbirds, and also bamboo drifting and the root of a tree
SIEN VERSCHIJDE VOGELS, WAARONDER MALLEG: Saw various birds, among them fulmars and a malleviet [?]
SIEN VERSCHIJDENE ZUIDVOGELS, STRANDMEEU: Saw various southern birds, shore gulls and a black-headed gull [?]
SIEN VOOR DE EERSTE MAAL KROOS DRIJVEN: Saw duckweed drifting for the first time
SIGUE A 3 PULGADAS POR HORA. VEN PAJAROS: Continues at 3 inches per hour. They see white birds and some black ones the size of gulls
SIGUE A LA CAPA. DESCRIPTORES DEL MEDIOD: Continues hove to. Noon or day's-run descriptors. The diary begins on 31-ENE-1766 but they do not sail until 3-FEB because of the violence of the clouds and the wind coming from the west and northwest. Had trouble passing the channel strait.
SIGUE EL AGUA VERDOSA. A LAS 9 DE LA MAÑ: The greenish water continues. At 9 in the morning they see a frigate to the SE that was heading west
SIGUE EL NAVIO HACIENDO 3 PULGADAS POR H: The ship continues making 3 inches per hour. Great lines of currents, mostly from E to W and from WNW to ESE
SIGUE EL SARGAZO Y VEN UN RABIJUNCO: The sargassum continues and they see a tropicbird
SIGUE EL TEMPORAL, CAPEANDO HASTA LAS 10: The storm continues, lying hove to until 10:00 when it eased somewhat. They sail again toward the coast that the storm forced them to leave. The data usually come from dawn and the noon observation.
SIGUE LA ABUNDANCIA DE PÁJAROS CON TRES: The abundance of birds continues, with three small whales.
SIGUE LA ESTRELLA. EMPIEZAN A FABRICAR M: The star continues. They begin making topmasts from a studding-sail boom and the launch's bow boom
SIGUEN A LA CAPA Y TRABAJANDO EN EL BARC: They continue hove to and working on the ship
SIGUEN ABUNDANCIA DE CHORLITOS , LOBOS Y: The abundance of plovers, lobos [?] and the other birds continues
They continue lying hove to. The sea was very cold. They try to repair the rudder and secured it.
SIGUEN CON LA ISLA ARBOLEDO A LA VISTA A: They continue with Isla Arboledo in sight at 11 leagues. Noon measurement and data, minus descriptors that are usually from nightfall. French chart.
SIGUEN FONDEADOS. POR LA TARDE VAN A TIE: They remain anchored. In the afternoon they go ashore. Mentions the firewood they gather. They kill some woodcocks and chase many guanacos. At sunset they return to the ship. Noon or day's-run measurement and data; the descriptors are often from dawn.
SIGUEN HACIENDO LA MISMA AGUA. CORRIENTE: They continue taking on the same water. Very strong current, many of its lines visible in various directions
SIGUEN LAS 6 PULGADAS. VEN MARTINPLACAS: The 6 inches continue. They see martinplacas [?] and shearwaters
SIGUEN LAS BANDADAS DE CHORLITOS Y ALGUN: The flocks of plovers continue and some night lobos [?] and salgazo [?] that others call cachilluyo, large birds with yellow beak, all with black bodies, and platoros [?].
SIGUEN LAS SEÑALES DE SONDA: The signs from the sounding continue
SIGUEN LOS BALLENATOS Y ALGUNOS LOBOS DE: The small whales continue and some night lobos [?] immediately alongside, very large; small birds all white and large ones all black with white beak and some platos [?].
SIGUEN LOS PÁJAROS, NO CON TANTA ABUNDAN: The birds continue, not so abundant
SIGUEN TRABAJANDO EN EL BARCO: They continue working on the ship
SIGUEN VIENDO BALLENAS PERO NO TANTAS \": They continue seeing whales but not as many "but the ash-grey and white birds the size of turtledoves mentioned yesterday, though not in flocks, are seen in great numbers"
SIGUEN VIENDOSE GRAN NUMERO DE PAJAROS: A great number of birds continue to be seen
Continuing the chase in the 1st quarter...
SIGUIENDO LOS CIELOS Y LOS HORIZ. ACELAJ: The skies and horizons continue cloudy and squally.
SIGUIERON CON EL TEMPORAL HASTA LAS 10:0: They continued in the storm until 10:00 when the southwest wind eased somewhat
SIGUIÓ EN LA MAÑANA GARUANDO Y CON ALGUN: It continued in the morning drizzling and with some sea.
SIGUIÓ LA CUASI CALMA HASTA EL ANOCHECER: The near calm continued until nightfall
SIN AGUAS EN AL DE 354 08' . HE VISTO AL: No waters [?] at that of 354 08'. I have seen some patches of sargassum
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 0º 36' AL E DEL PRIME: No waters [?] at that of 0º 36' east of the first meridian. I have seen sargassum and a turtle
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 1º 17'. HE VISTO ALGU: No waters [?] at that of 1º 17'. I have seen some patches of sargassum, jellyfish and men-of-war and a turtle.
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 349º 46' . HE VISTO A: No waters [?] at that of 349º 46'. I have seen some patches of sargassum
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 352º 16'. HE VISTO AL: No waters [?] at that of 352º 16'. I have seen some patches of sargassum
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 354 59 . HE VISTO ALG: No waters [?] at that of 354 59. I have seen some patches of sargassum
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 3º 35' . SE HAN VISTO: No waters [?] at that of 3º 35'. Turtles and two birds called garranchos [?], all black with a white breast, have been seen.
No waters [?] at that of 6º 45'. By the English longitude 357º 31', distance from the Cape 163 leagues
SIN AGUAS EN LA DE 7º 28'. POR LA DEL IN: No waters [?] at that of 7º 28'. By the English one 358º, distance from the Cape 155 leagues
SIN AGUAS QUEDO CUMPLIDO. SE HAN VISTO T: No waters [?] was completed. Turtles have been seen.
SIN NOVEDAD, EN LOS MISMOS TERMINOS DEL: Nothing new, in the same terms as the previous day
SIN NOVEDAD, EN LOS MISMOS TERMINOS QUE: Nothing new, in the same terms as the previous day
SIN VERSE NINGUNO DE LOS BUQUES DE LA ES: Without seeing any of the ships of the squadron
SINDS 3 DAGEN HARD DE BAROM. ZEER LAAG G: For 3 days the barometer hard [?] very low, indicates [?], but no heavy wind
SINDS AANKOMST TE CEYLON MINSTENS 11 ZIE: Since arrival at Ceylon at least 11 sick sent to the hospital, 2 died, 6 men in irons.
SINDS DE LAATSTE 3 ETMALEN DAALT DE BARO: Over the last 3 days the barometer has kept falling. Sky, weather and sea keep becoming more threatening. This led them to the theory (about) the hurricanes of A. Thom, that they were approaching the center more and more. They take precautions (very hard to read).
For some days nothing seen from the masthead. Sounded with 110 fathoms, no bottom.
SINDS SCHIP VERTROK UIT CURACAO ZIJN 12: Since the ship left Curacao 12 men have died
SLAAN EEN SOLDAAT IN DE BOEIEN WEGENS DR: Put a soldier in irons for drunkenness
SLACHTEN 4 VARKENS. MAKEN SCHOON TUSSEND: Slaughtered 4 pigs. Cleaned the between decks
SLAVEN MOPPERDEN WEER OVER HET ZOUTE WAT: Slaves grumbled again about the salt water, which they thought they had to drink, and wanted to leave the boat. Their irons were put back on.
SLAVEN OVERWOGEN WEER OM VAN HET SCHIP A: Slaves again considered running away from the ship, there was talk of mutiny, they wanted to murder everyone. They were punished and put in irons. Also a female slave died.
SLINGERDEN EN STAMPTEN GEWELDIG EN STERK: Rolled and pitched tremendously and heavily in the high sea
SLINGERDEN EN WERKTEN GEWELDIG IN DE ONS: Rolled and labored tremendously in the turbulent sea. Took a lot of water over.
SLINGERDEN GEWELDIG IN DE HOGE LOPENDE D: Rolled terribly in the high running swell. Kept as much to sea as possible.
SLINGERDEN SOMS STERK IN DE HOGE ZEE: Sometimes rolled heavily in the high sea.
Rolled heavily in the high swell.
SLINGERDEN STERK IN DE HOGE ZEE: Rolled heavily in the high sea.
SLINGERDEN STERK IN DE ZEER HOGE ZUIDELI: Rolled heavily in the very high southerly swell. Squalls.
SLINGEREN STERK DOOR ZWARE DEINING: Rolling heavily due to heavy swell.
SLOEPEN AAN LAND MET DE OVERLEDENE EN 2: Boats ashore with the deceased and 2 sick men.
SLOEPEN NAAR LAND OM WATER TE HALEN: Boats to land to fetch water.
SLP WAS NOTED AS 31.55, BUT THIS SEEMS T: SLP was noted as 31.55, but this seems to be too high.
SLP WAS NOTED AS 31.75, BUT THIS SEEMS T: SLP was noted as 31.75, but this seems to be too high.
SLP WAS NOTED AS 32, BUT THIS SEEMS TO B: SLP was noted as 32, but this seems to be too high.
SLP WAS NOTED AS 32.0, BUT THIS SEEMS TO: SLP was noted as 32.0, but this seems to be too high.
SLP WAS NOTED AS 32.50, BUT THIS SEEMS T: SLP was noted as 32.50, but this seems to be too high.
SLUITEN DE BOOTSMAN, KAJUITS EN SCHEEPS: Put the boatswain, cabin steward and ship's cook, with a sailor, in irons because of a fight.
SMEREN ALLE ASSEN VAN DE RAMPAARDEN MET: Greased all the axles of the [?] with soap.
SMIDDAGS PEIJLDEN ORNAAL OZO REGTWIJSENT: In the afternoon took a bearing of Ornaal, east-southeast true, 9 miles.
SMORGENS OM 10 UUR ONDER HET HOUDEN VAN: In the morning at 10 o'clock, during the kit inspection, a third-class sailor, J. Ridderhoff, jumped overboard. Fortunately we were lying in a dead calm and the boatswain, De Wolff, jumped after him with two sailors and he was thus rescued. His reason for wanting to drown himself was that the [?] of the mess lamp had gone missing and his shipmates had made him afraid that the blame would be thrown on him and that he would then be punished.
SNACHS IN DEN MORGENSTOND MET DONDER EN: At night in the early morning with thunder and lightning and heavy rain and squalls.
SNACHTS STERKE VURING IN HET WATER: At night strong phosphorescence in the water.
SNELSTE VAART IN HET ETMAAL VAN DE KOMEE: Fastest speed in the day during which the comet was seen, 8,5 miles. Longitude west of Greenwhich. (Estimated) point Dunosse on the island of Wicht (Wight), NWTW [?], 5 miles.
SNELSTE VAART MET BUI BIJ DE WIND 7,5 MI: Fastest speed in a squall close-hauled 7,5 miles.
SNELSTE VAART MET EEN BUI 7 MIJLEN: Fastest speed in a squall 7 miles.
SNELSTE VAART MET EEN BUI ZONDER DE BZ 7: Fastest speed in a squall without the topgallant sails 7 miles.
SNELSTE VAART SCHIP IN ETMAAL 6,25: Fastest speed of the ship in the day 6,25.
SNELSVAART IN DE VMW VAN DE WIND MET ALL: Fastest speed in the [?] of the wind with all sails set was 8 miles on the log.
SNIJDEN HET ONDERZEIL UIT ZIJN LUIKEN, G: Cut the lower sail out of its hatches, using it for slave cloth.
SOLAMENTE APARECE LA LATITUD Y LONGITUD: Only the latitude and longitude of departure appear.
SOLAMENTE CONSTAN LA LATITUD Y LONGITUD: Only the latitude and longitude of departure are recorded.
SOLDAAT ADRIAAN VAN ETTEN, VAN ZIEDE, OV: Soldier Adriaan van Etten, of Ziede, died.
SOLDAAT ALBERT GIES VAN BERGHEIM OVERLED: Soldier Albert Gies of Bergheim died.
SOLDAAT ANDRIES BON VAN IJVEBAG EN SOLDA: Soldier Andries Bon of IJvebag and soldier Johannis Eekhard of Sevenaar [?].
SOLDAAT BERNARDUS STILMAN VAN KEULEN OVE: Soldier Bernardus Stilman of Keulen died.
SOLDAAT CASPER HASBERG, VAN ZUTPHEN OVER: Soldier Casper Hasberg, of Zutphen, died.
SOLDAAT CLEMENT MOEST OP BEVEL VAN DE VI: Soldier Clement had to be kept in secure custody on the order of the vice admiral.
SOLDAAT CRISTOLF FREDRIK BUHLER VAN STOE: Soldier Cristolf Fredrik Buhler of Stoekart.
SOLDAAT DANIEL JOSEPH DEN WEVER (?) VAN: Soldier Daniel Joseph den Wever [?] of Mechelen died.
SOLDAAT DANIEL ORTLEE VAN AMSTERDAM OVER: Soldier Daniel Ortlee of Amsterdam died.
SOLDAAT DE NEGRO VAN 'T 5E REGIMENT OVER: Soldier De Negro of the 5th Regiment died. The body was put overboard.
SOLDAAT ELIAS EVENNEDER OVERLEDEN EN OVE: Soldier Elias Evenneder died and was put overboard.
SOLDAAT F 358 JEAN GRAIND JEAN OVERLEDEN: Soldier F 358 Jean Graind Jean died.
SOLDAAT F. EKHARD OVERLEDEN EN SOLDAAT H: Soldier F. Ekhard died and soldier H. Knoop died.
SOLDAAT GEERT TOMSRIES OVERLEDEN (24). M: Soldier Geert Tomsries died (24). Sailor Hendrik Smit died (25).
SOLDAAT GEORG LODEWIJK INSELBAG VAN AUGS: Soldier Georg Lodewijk Inselbag of Augsburg died. Gave the sick water instead of beer because the beer was said not to be good.
SOLDAAT GEORGE WILHEM VAN AKERENDORFF OV: Soldier George Wilhem van Akerendorff died.
SOLDAAT GODFRIED CESAS VAN CEULEN OVERLE: Soldier Godfried Cesas of Ceulen died.
SOLDAAT GOOSE LANGKAMP OVERLEDEN EN OVER: Soldier Goose Langkamp died and was put overboard.
SOLDAAT GUILIHELMUS JOSEPH DRAAK VAN BRU: Soldier Guilihelmus Joseph Draak of Brugge.
SOLDAAT HANS FREDERIKS VAN COOX OVERLEDE: Soldier Hans Frederiks of Coox died.
SOLDAAT HARMEN CORSMAN VAN DE BOURTANG E: Soldier Harmen Corsman of De Bourtang and Johannis Roos of Brugge died.
SOLDAAT HENDRICUS MAATS VAN DIETS OVERLE: Soldier Hendricus Maats of Diets died.
SOLDAAT HENDRIK TIKKENS VAN STRIEPEN OVE: Soldier Hendrik Tikkens of Striepen died.
SOLDAAT IN DE BOEIEN GEZET. EEN MATROOS,: Soldier put in irons. A sailor, Louis Rikkelman, died.
SOLDAAT JACOB BRONSWIJK OVERLEDEN AAN EE: Soldier Jacob Bronswijk died of a malignant fever.
SOLDAAT JAN BATIST SIMON VAN GENT OVERLE: Soldier Jan Batist Simon of Gent died.
SOLDAAT JAN CHRISTIAAN ZAAN VAN OLDENBUR: Soldier Jan Christiaan Zaan of Oldenburg died.
SOLDAAT JAN CIBS VAN ROSENDAAL OVERLEDEN: Soldier Jan Cibs of Rosendaal died.
SOLDAAT JAN COAVESPEL VAN THORIGNI? OVER: Soldier Jan Coavespel of Thorigni [?] jumped overboard. They did not know for certain whether he was fully in his right mind.
SOLDAAT JAN FREDERIK ITTESMET VAN ORAG O: Soldier Jan Frederik Ittesmet of Orag died.
SOLDAAT JAN GOTLIEB SMIT VAN BRESLAU OVE: Soldier Jan Gotlieb Smit of Breslau died.
SOLDAAT JAN PLUIJMAN VAN EEKERREN OVER B: Soldier Jan Pluijman of Eekerren fell overboard and drowned.
SOLDAAT JAN VALKENBRGH VAN VLISSINGEN OV: Soldier Jan Valkenbrgh of Vlissingen died.
SOLDAAT JAN VAN HALEN VAN AMSTERDAM OVER: Soldier Jan van Halen of Amsterdam died.
SOLDAAT JEAN JACOB DUROISIN VAN VONTINIS: Soldier Jean Jacob Duroisin of Vontinissie in irons.
SOLDAAT JENS ANDRIESSEN VAN WEROP OVERLE: Soldier Jens Andriessen of Werop died.
SOLDAAT JOAHN ANDRIES BIENENGRABER VAN L: Soldier Joahn Andries Bienengraber of Lypzich.
SOLDAAT JOH.ZN ANTONIE BRANTS VAN ANTWER: Soldier Joh.zn Antonie Brants of Antwerpen died.
SOLDAAT JOHANNES HAANTJES VAN BOLSWAART: Soldier Johannes Haantjes of Bolswaart died.
Soldier Johannes Rinkink died (49). A servant of the captain, Jacob Betz, died (50).
SOLDAAT JOHANNES WIJSEL VAN SILLOU, SOLD: Soldier Johannes Wijsel of Sillou, soldier Hendrik Dortman of Loenkhoosen and Jan Mattijs Ernst of Heelsteijn died.
SOLDAAT JOSEP BEEN VAN KOESVELT OVERLEDE: Soldier Josep Been of Koesvelt died.
SOLDAAT JOSEPH DEKEN VAN LUIJK OVERLEDEN: Soldier Joseph Deken of Luijk died.
SOLDAAT KURISICK NA Z'N STRAF VOOR GEPLE: Soldier Kurisick released from irons after receiving his punishment for theft committed.
SOLDAAT MAGIEL ANTHONIE DE COSTO VAN MEG: Soldier Magiel Anthonie de Costo of Meggelen.
SOLDAAT METRIFANT(?) CLEMENT WEGENS GEWE: Soldier Metrifant [?] Clement put in irons for violence against Lieutenant Schotman.
SOLDAAT MICHIEL JOSEP PHAAS VAN RENSBURG: Soldier Michiel Josep Phaas of Rensburg died.
SOLDAAT MICHIEL THIL VAN MARSELJE OVERLE: Soldier Michiel Thil of Marselje died.
SOLDAAT N. GOOSEMAN OVERLEDEN. HIJ WERD: Soldier N. Gooseman died. He was found dead in his hammock. He had only reported sick the day before, with a tight chest. He apparently suffocated.
SOLDAAT NICOLAAS BEL LOVEN VAN DUIJNKERK: Soldier Nicolaas Bel Loven of Duijnkerke died.
SOLDAAT NO.29, JAN LEUSEKENS UIT AMSTERD: Soldier No. 29, Jan Leusekens of Amsterdam, died.
SOLDAAT OF GECHANGEERDE MATROOS NICOLAAS: Soldier or transferred sailor Nicolaas Kot of Duinkerke jumped overboard and refused to grab the ropes that were thrown to him.
SOLDAAT P. SCHOFTEN OVERBOORD EN GEZONKE: Soldier P. Schoften overboard and sunk.
SOLDAAT PIERRE GODJE VAN DONGE OVERLEDEN: Soldier Pierre Godje from Donge died
SOLDAAT PIETER DAELMAN OVERLEDEN AAN EEN: Soldier Pieter Daelman died of a malignant fever.
SOLDAAT PIETER HOOFMAN VAN DOORNIK OVERL: Soldier Pieter Hoofman from Doornik died
SOLDAAT PIETER JACOB VAN RONSELE VAN OOS: Soldier Pieter Jacob van Ronsele from Oostcamp died
SOLDAAT PIETER JAQUES VANGE? VAN GENEVE: Soldier Pieter Jaques Vange [?] from Geneva died
SOLDAAT REMIE BIGNON VAN BRUGGE OVERLEDE: Soldier Remie Bignon from Bruges died
SOLDAAT S. VAN DUIN UIT DE BOEIEN ONTSLA: Soldier S. van Duin released from irons and punished.
SOLDAAT TOBIAS SCHEIJG VAN KEMNIS OVERLE: Soldier Tobias Scheijg from Kemnis died
SOLDAAT WENSEL BAND OVERLEDEN, WELKER LI: Soldier Wensel Band died; his body, he having died of dysentery, to be put overboard immediately.
SOLDAAT WILLEM CLAASEBAAS VAN VRELANT OV: Soldier Willem Claasebaas from Vrelant died
Soldier Zeeman of the 3rd Regiment, 1st Battalion, died. The body was put overboard during the day watch.
SOLDAAT, JAN DE ROO, OVERLEDEN. TROKKEN: Soldier Jan de Roo died. Hauled the ventilator daily and this month read the articles of war.
SOLDATEN ANTHONIJ ABRIK VAN FREDEWIJLLES: Soldiers Anthonij Abrik from Fredewijlles and Philip Merret from Lausanne died
SOLDATEN EN MATROZEN OEFENEN MET HET HAN: Soldiers and sailors drill with small arms
SOLDATEN EN ROEIERS OEFENEN MET HANDGEWE: Soldiers and rowers drill with small arms and grenades.
Soldiers and rowers drill with small arms
SOLDATEN EXERCEREN EN VUREN. MAKEN TUSSE: Soldiers drill and fire. Clean the between-decks, burn [?], then sprinkle with vinegar. Skipper Jan Scholk died
SOLDATEN EXERCEREN MET HANDGEWEER. ZOND: Soldiers drill with small arms. Sent a sloop to a merchant ship to fetch collected rainwater.
SOLDATEN F. NICKEL EN F. DE VOS OVERLEDE: Soldiers F. Nickel and F. de Vos died
SOLDATEN JAN SPECT VAN HASLINGEN EN ADAM: Soldiers Jan Spect from Haslingen and Adam Lijber from Oosthum
SOLDATEN JOHANNIS GRAAFF VAN VERINGE EN: Soldiers Johannis Graaff from Veringe and Jan Francois Louwrens from Hestens died
SOLDATEN OEFENEN MET HANDGEWEER EN GRANA: Soldiers drill with small arms and grenades. The sailors with the guns
SOMS GEEN STUUR IN HET SCHIP: At times no steerage in the ship
SOMS HEEL DONKER VAN MIST: At times very dark with mist
SOMS STAAT ER EEN X BIJ DE WINDKRACHT: At times there is an X next to the wind force
SOMS STORMVLAGEN EN AANHOUDENDE REGEN: At times storm gusts and continuous rain
SON ABORDADOS PERO LUEGO LES DEJAN SEGUI: They are boarded but then allowed to continue their voyage
SONDAN A LAS 6:00 Y NO SE HALLO FONDO. L: Sounded at 6:00 and found no bottom. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SONDAN A LAS 9:00 SIN HALLAR FONDO. LOS: Sounded at 9:00 without finding bottom. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SONDAN A MEDIODIA Y HALLAN 15 BRAZAS DE: Sounded at noon and found 15 fathoms of sand and shells. Hove to. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SONDAN SIN HALLAR FONDO EN 60 BRAZAS. LO: Sounded without finding bottom at 60 fathoms. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation
SONDAN Y CON 150 BRAZAS NO HALLAN FONDO: Sounded and with 150 fathoms found no bottom
SONDAN Y ENCUENTRAN 52 BRAZAS CON ARENA: Sounded and found 52 fathoms with brown sand and fine gravel
SONDAN Y ENCUENTRAN 59 BRAZAS CON ARENA: Sounded and found 59 fathoms with sand and small shells. At 17:00 sighted land. The labours and hardships on the ship continue
SONDAN Y HALLAN SOLO 36 BRAZAS DE FONDO: Sounded and found only 36 fathoms of fine black and brown sand, which surprises them since according to the dead reckoning they should have 70 to 80 fathoms
SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO. NO PUEDE OBSER: Sounded and found no bottom. Cannot observe "for lack of horizon"
SONDAN Y NO HALLAN FONDO. VEN VARIOS PAJ: Sounded and found no bottom. See several birds in the afternoon; besides the one resembling the thrush, see another like a sparrow but with red legs, and in the morning some called tablas because the pattern of their wings makes little white and black squares; shearwaters are still in sight and sargassum has passed. The conjunction of the moon has occurred with a good appearance
SONDAN. A LA VISTA LA ISLA DE LOBOS Y DE: Sounded. In sight the island of Lobos and afterwards that of Flores and the English Bank
SONDARON CON 108 BRAZAS SIN ENCONTRAR FO: Sounded with 108 fathoms without finding bottom. At 6:30 saw land, which seemed to them a small island 7 to 8 leagues distant, whose middle bore N 34° E. At 8:45 saw another land further east than the first, which seemed to be another island. According to the noon bearing the southernmost and easternmost island is at 46° 30' latitude and 46° 56' longitude. It seemed to them that one island was 4 to 5 leagues from the other, on the line NW 1/4 W–SE 1/4 E
SONDARON Y ENCONTRARON EL AGUA DE COLOR: Sounded and found the water of a somewhat broken colour
SONDÉ PAR 15, 16, 18,20 ET 22 BRASSES, E: Sounded at 15, 16, 18, 20 and 22 fathoms, approaching the middle of the Channel of Tartary
SONDÉ PAR 18, 16, 15, 14, 13 ET 12 BRASS: Sounded at 18, 16, 15, 14, 13 and 12 fathoms. Anchored in the Bay of Castries, in [?] fathoms (19:30)
SONDÉ PAR 36 ET 25 BRASSES, FOND DE SABL: Sounded at 36 and 25 fathoms, sandy bottom. At half past 2 in the morning, anchored in 25 fathoms. At 10 o'clock, weighed anchor at noon,
SONDÉ PAR 45 BRASSES, FOND DE VASE. MOUI: Sounded at 45 fathoms, muddy bottom. Anchored in 5 O fathoms, muddy bottom (14:00)
Sounded at 45 to 50 fathoms, muddy bottom. Anchored in 42 fathoms, muddy bottom (19:00)
SONDÉ PAR 55 ET 45 BRASSES, FOND DE VASE: Sounded at 55 and 45 fathoms, muddy bottom. Anchored in 45 fathoms, muddy bottom (18:00).
SONDÉ PAR 55 ET 50 BRASSES, FOND DE SABL: Sounded at 55 and 50 fathoms, sandy bottom.
SONDÉ PAR 80 BRASSES, FOND DE SABLE VASE: Sounded at 80 fathoms, muddy sandy bottom.
SONDÉ À CETTE DISTANCE, PAR 120 BRASSES,: Sounded at this distance, at 120 fathoms, muddy bottom.
SPELEN ZO MET DE ZEILEN DAT \"DE KOTTER\: Play with the sails so that "the Kotter" (= the ruff) sails past the Havick!
SPRAKE EEN VISSER SCHUIJT DIE ONS ZEIJDE: Spoke a fishing boat which told us that we had the Goeree [?] and SSE on the compass 6 miles from us, end of journal
SPRENGEN MET LEMONSAP TUSSENDEKS EN IN D: Sprinkle with lemon juice between decks and in the quarterdeck
SPRENGEN MET LIMOENSAP TUSSENDEKS EN IN: Sprinkle with lime juice between decks and in the quarterdeck
SPRINGEN MET LEMONSAP TUSSENDEKS EN IN D: Sprinkle with lemon juice between decks and in the quarterdeck
ST ANTHONY OBSERVATIE ZON EN MAAN: ZZO N: St Anthony observation of sun and moon: SSE N/S, 17,25
ST MICHAEL LIGT VOLGENS KAART VAN KAPITE: According to the chart of Captain W. F. Owen, St Michael lies at 25°55' NW, so the chronometers are perfect.
ST. ANNA IS 1 DER VLAAMSE EILANDEN, OOK: St. Anna is one of the Flemish Islands, also called by the Spaniards the Acc..se Islands, or in Latin Insula Accipitaum (?).
ST. ANTHONY IS ÉÉN VAN DE ZOUTE EILANDEN: St. Anthony is one of the Salt Islands
STAAN MET HET BESTEK OP EILAND SAXENBURG: By the dead reckoning we are at Saxenburg island, but saw nothing
STAAN VLGS HET BESTEK BEOOSTEN KAAP DE L: By the dead reckoning east of Cape de la Hague, 16 miles off the shore
There is something strange about the symbols.
STAAT VOOR WARE BEKOMEN BREEDTE 'WAAR GE: Stands for true latitude obtained, 'where taken, sketch'. Meridian west of the Lizard, 95 miles.
STAKEN DE REVEN UIT DE MARSZEILEN: Shook the reefs out of the topsails
STAMPTEN ZWAAR. POMPTEN LENS VAN 15 OP 1: Pitched heavily. Pumped the bilge from 15 to 10 inches
STAMPTEN ZWAAR/GEWELDIG, KREGEN VEEL WAT: Pitched heavily/violently, took in much water over the deck. In the evening could no longer see the forward part of the ship.
STEEDS ZWAAR STAMPEN KREGEN EEN ZEE OVER: Continually pitching heavily, took a sea over the whole ship
STELDE ONS KOERS NA T VADERLAND GOD VERL: Set our course for the fatherland; God grant us a safe voyage
STELDE ONSE KOERS NA HET VADERLAND: Set our course for the fatherland
STELDE ONZE KOERS NAAR HET VADERLAND: Set our course for the fatherland
STELDE OP ZIJN VERZOEK DEN BOOTSMANSMAAT: At his request appointed the boatswain's mate as quartermaster and the quartermaster Arij Guijten as boatswain's mate.
STELDEN EEN MATROOS AAN ALS BOTTELIER VO: Appointed a sailor as steward at 14 guilders per month, named Andries Roselet.
STELDEN HIEROP ONS BESTEK, KOMT ZB 34°40: Set our dead reckoning accordingly, comes to N latitude 34°40 and longitude 34°26
STELDEN NIEUWE KWARTIERMEESTER, DE MATRO: Appointed new quartermaster, the sailor Jan Maurits
STELDEN ONS BESTEK EN WAREN VOLGENS DIEN: Set our dead reckoning and according to it were on the Mercator chart at north latitude 49 degrees 25 minutes and longitude 11 degrees, where our dead reckoning begins
Set our course for the fatherland.
STELENDE MATROOS WILLEM VIJNCK VAN HAARL: Thieving sailor Willem Vijnck from Haarlem is tried
STELLEN DE BOS?MANSMAAT FRANS V/D RIET V: Appoint the boatswain's mate Frans v/d Riet from Rosendaal as steward.
STELLEN DE LENGTE BIJ OP 14G30MIN, OMDAT: Adjust the longitude to 14°30', because they do not see Jan Mayen
STELLEN DE SCHIPPER M. JURRIAANS IN ZIJN: Reinstate the skipper M. Jurriaans in his previous rank
STELLEN MATROOS JACOB GOESEN VAN ROTTERD: Appoint sailor Jacob Goesen from Rotterdam as steward's mate and the soldier Peter Streffer from Langerweer as provost..
STERK ONWEER, ZEER STIL TOT 3 GLAZEN, TO: Strong thunderstorm, very calm until 3 glasses, then suddenly a very strong wind from the west
STERKE NOORDERLICHT AAN DE LUCHT: Strong northern lights in the sky
STERKE RAFELING VAN STROOM.TIMMERLIEDEN: Strong ripples of current. Carpenters caulk
STERKE RAVELING BIJ HET SCHIP (MEN DENKT: Strong ripples near the ship (thought to be due to the current. Deviation for the [?] 8.5 miles. Changed longitude 34'. The compasses vary 7° 30' N/W
STERKE RAVELING TREKKENDE OM DE ONO: Strong ripples, running towards the ENE
STERKE RAVELING VAN STROOM ALSOF MEN DOO: Strong ripples of current as if sailing through surf. Current runs towards the SW. At night lightning in the SE and E.
STERKE RAVELING VAN STROOM OM DE NW. SNE: Strong ripples of current towards the NW. Fastest speed in the 24 hours 9.5 miles
STERKE RAVELING VAN STROOM, AL(S)OF MEN: Strong ripples of current, as if sailing in surf. Ripples probably run towards the N.
STERKE STROMING OM DE ZUID 14 A 15 MIJL: Strong current towards the south, 14 to 15 miles per day
STERKE STROOM IN HET WATER: \"ALSOF HET: Strong current in the water: "as if it is boiling".
STERKE VUERING IN HET WATER. ZAGEN EEN M: Strong phosphorescence in the water. Saw a mallegaas.
STERKE VUERING IN HET WATER. ZIEN VEEL V: Strong phosphorescence in the water. See many flying fish
Strong phosphorescence in the water. See many birds and flying fish.
STERKE VURING IN 'T WATER. VEEL VIS BIJ: Strong phosphorescence in the water. Much fish near the ship
STERKE VURING RAAVELING VAN STROOM VEEL: Strong phosphorescence, ripples from the current, many small fish.
STERKE VUURRING IN HET WATER. ZIEN KOKSH: Strong phosphorescence in the water. See [?] and various [?] and tropicbirds. See much vegetation drifting
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN AANNEMENDE KOE: Stiff topgallant breeze and increasing breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEMENDE KOEL: Stiff topgallant breeze and decreasing breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Stiff topgallant breeze and topgallant breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN GEREEFDE MARSZ: Stiff topgallant breeze and reefed topsail breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MARSZEILSKOELT: Stiff topgallant breeze and topsail breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MEERDERE KOELT: Stiff topgallant breeze and stronger breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN MINDERE KOELTE: Stiff topgallant breeze and lighter breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE EN ONGESTADIGE KO: Stiff topgallant breeze and unsteady breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE TOT GEREEFDE MARS: Stiff topgallant breeze to reefed topsail breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE TOT MARSZEILSKOEL: Stiff topgallant breeze to topsail breeze
STIJVE BRAMZEILSKOELTE-GEREEFDE MARSZEIL: Stiff topgallant breeze, reefed topsail breeze
STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN AFNEM: Stiff reefed topsail breeze and decreasing breeze
STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZ: Stiff reefed topsail breeze and topgallant breeze
STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN ONDER: Stiff reefed topsail breeze and lower-sail breeze
STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN ONGES: Stiff reefed topsail breeze and unsteady breeze
STIJVE GEREEFDE MARSZEILSKOELTE-ONDERZEI: Stiff reefed topsail breeze, lower-sail breeze
STIJVE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN BRAMZEILSKOELT: Stiff topsail breeze and topgallant breeze
STIJVE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN GEREEFDE MARSZ: Stiff topsail breeze and reefed topsail breeze
STIJVE MARSZEILSKOELTE EN ONGESTADIGE KO: Stiff topsail breeze and unsteady breeze
STIL, SOMS EEN LUCHTJE: Calm, sometimes a breath of air
STOKVIS AAN DE SLAVEN GEGEVEN TERWIJL ZI: Stockfish given to the slaves while it was spoiling from the leak that had been there
STONDEN 'SMIDDAGS MET HET BESTEK OP ASCE: At noon stood with the reckoning on Ascension, but noticed nothing, although at times they have 8 miles visibility
STONDEN MET HET BESTEK REEDS LANDWAARTS: Stood with the reckoning already inland. Sounded several times, no bottom. Also no change seen in the water yet. (This should be the case according to experts.)
STONDEN MET ONS BESTEK OP T EILAND TRINI: Stood with our reckoning on the island Trinidad, guessed to be one degree more westerly, as one thought?
STONDEN VLGS HET BESTEK 77,5 MIJL WEST E: According to the reckoning stood 77,5 miles west and 36 miles south on the coast of Guiana
STONDEN VOLGENS .. TEGEN EN OP HET LAND,: According to .. against and on the land, without being able to see anything
STONDEN VOLGENS DIEN MET ONS BESTEK OP ': According to that, stood with our reckoning on the land
STONDEN VOLGENS HET NEVEN GEMETEN AAN LA: According to the fog measured to land, but could not perceive the least of it.
STOOMENDE EN ZEILENDE LATER ENKEL ZEILEN: Steaming and sailing, later only sailing, from Paramaribo to Curaçao
The tide stopped to the west.
STORMVLAGEN IN DE MIDDAG, LATER 'EEN BUI: Storm gusts at midday, later 'a squall but being mostly rain & no wind'
STRAFFEN MATROOS C. STOON WGNS STELEN VA: Punished sailor C. Stoon for stealing liquor and drunkenness, committed by him several times
Punished sailor Severing for theft. Supplies from the pharmacy are spoiled, also the sick-bread is too hard to eat
STRAFTEN WEGENS LIEDERLIJKHEID DE MATROZ: Punished for dissoluteness the third-class sailors J.W. Petersen and J.D. Kas.
STRANDMEEUWEN, KOKSHENNEN EN NOORDKAPERS: Gulls, [?] and right whales. Strong phosphorescence
STROOM BRENGT IEDERE DAG 1° MISGISSING I: Current causes 1° error in latitude every day
STROOM HAD HET SCHIP 39'22\" OM DE WEST: Current had set the ship 39'22" to the west and 22' to the south.
STROOM HEEFT HET SCHIP SEDERT HAAR VERTR: Current has set the ship 20,5 miles toward NE 1/4 E since her departure from Havana
STROOM OF MISGISSING 2 ETMALEN NTO 9 MIJ: Current or error 2 days NTO 9 miles
STROOM OF MISREKENING NOTO, 1/4 OOST,? M: Current or miscalculation NOTO, 1/4 East, ? miles. Unsteady force ??
STUREN (NET ALS) HET SCHIP DE LIEFDE NOT: Steering (just like) the ship De Liefde NOTO.
STUREN O BIJ TOELATING VAN GODS WIND EN: Steering E with God's permission of wind and weather.
STUREN OM DE N EN NO OM DE BREEDTE VAN D: Steering N and NE to run the latitude of the Cape
STUREN ONO OM CORVUS (CORVO) EN FLORES M: Steering ENE to miss Corvus (Corvo) and Flores. Remark about the position of the islands (Corvo and Flores) on various charts
STUREN TUSSEN JAVA EN PRINSEN EILAND: Steering between Java and Prinsen Island
Steering southeast because of the difficult sea.
STUREN ZUID OM DE BREEDTE VAN MADERA AF: Steering south to run down the latitude of Madeira.
STUREN ZWTW OMDAT MEN ZOVEEL ZUID HAD OM: Steering southwest by west because they had so much south, in order to reach their position (35 miles??).
STUREN ZWTZ OMDAT ZE 'VEEL ZUID HEBBEN O: Steering southwest by south because they 'have much south during the day'.
STUURDE ZO AAN, VERLEGGEN DE COMPAS VAN: Steered southeast, shifting the compass by 2.5 degrees N: easterly until correct.
STUURDE ZUID AAN OM DE BREEDTE VAN DE EI: Steered south to run down the latitude of the islands.
STUURDEN 'S NACHTS VAN WTN GAANDEWEG NOO: At night steered gradually more northerly from west by north to northwest, around the Cape of Good Hope.
STUURDEN LANGS DE STREKKING VAN DE WAL O: Steered along the line of the shore at a suitable distance.
STUURDEN OP DE ZUID HOEK VAN DWARS IN DE: Steered on the south point from abeam under way, anchored in 24 [?], land in coral. Brabandshoedster NE. Peak of Krakatau west. East L. abeam under way NNE 1/4 E.
STUURDEN WEST BIJ 'T NOORDEN AAN OM OP D: Steering west by north to reach the latitude of Antigua.
STUURDEN WTZ AAN OM OP DE BREEDTE VAN DE: Steering west-southwest to reach the latitude of the southeast point of Antigua.
STUURDEN ZW R/W HOEWEL DEZE COMP GEEN SC: Steering southwest R/W, although these compasses having no sliding [?] cards, always M/W lay [?].
STUURDEN ZZO BIJ DE TOELATING DER WIND: Steering south-southeast as the wind allowed.
Mate Jan Coenraat Knol in service.
STUURMAN PETERSON WEGENS PLICHTSVERZUIM: Mate Peterson in irons for neglect of duty.
STUURMAN SIMON BOT VAN DE 'OUDECASPEL' K: Mate Simon Bot of the 'Oudecaspel' comes to speak about a disagreement.
STUURMANSLEERING J.C. KLEIN IN DE BOEIEN: Mate's apprentice J.C. Klein confined in irons for neglecting his watch.
SUKKELDE VOORT. DIEPTE VAN 46 A 47 VADEM: Dawdled onward. Depth of 46 to 47 fathoms, black mud and sand and some brown shells beneath.
SUPONGO QUE HA CAMBIADO EL REFERENTE PAR: I suppose the reference for measuring longitude has changed, but it indicates nothing.
SUSPENDIMOS EL ANCLA DE ESTRIBOR (...) Q: We weighed the starboard anchor (...) we were left with the anchor straight up and down...
SUSSANNA HAD GISTEREN OOK LAND GEZIEN. Z: Sussanna also sighted land yesterday. Their S latitude 34° 50'. Estimate of the Johanna: S latitude 35° 0' and longitude 42°8'. Had also sighted the land in the NNW. AE: sounded with 100 fathoms, gray sand. With 100 fathoms of line, no bottom.
SWARE HOOS IN NOTO DOCH VERDWEEN HEEL SC: Heavy waterspout in northeast by east, but it vanished very suddenly.
SYMPISIOMETER: 290809. ANKER OP (SCHIP L: Sympisiometer: 290809. Anchor up (ship lay in the roads of Deal)
SYMPISIOMETER: 297600. LENGTEPOSITIE VAN: Sympisiometer: 297600. Longitude position of 3 other ships: Doggersbank 8°46'. Prins van Oranje 8°52'. Sumatra 8°43'
SYMPISIOMETER: 299300. LENGTE VAN DOGGER: Sympisiometer: 299300. Longitude of Doggersbank 9°59'. Prins van Oranje 9°47'
SYMPISIOMETER: 299600. PASSEREN BARBADOS: Sympisiometer: 299600. Passing Barbados in the forenoon
SYMPISIOMETER: 300000. LENGTE POSITIE VA: Sympisiometer: 300000. Longitude position of the 3 other ships: Doggersbank 5°49'. Prins van Oranje 5°50'. Sumatra 5°53'
SYMPISIOMETER: 300400. LENGTEPOSITIE VAN: Sympisiometer: 300400. Longitude position of 3 other ships that are sailing along with the [?]: Doggersbank 4°36'. Prins van Oranje 4°37'. Sumatra 4°39'
SYMPISIOMETER: 302200. ANKER OP. VERTREK: Sympisiometer: 302200. Anchor up. Departure from Cadir
SYMPISIOMETER: 308600. LENGTE VAN 3 ANDE: Sympisiometer: 308600. Longitude of 3 other ships: Doggersbank 9°43'. Prins van Oranje 9°43'. Sumatra 9°39'
TAMBIÉN UNA URCA SUECA QUE NAVEGABA DE E: Also a Swedish cargo ship that was sailing from Stockholm to Liorna with a cargo of iron. "Latitude by the land"
TAMBOER J. WOLFS WEGENS DRONKENSCHAP EN: Drummer J. Wolfs locked in irons for drunkenness and unruly violence.
TAMBOUR DER TROEPEN OVERLEDEN (6 OVERLED: Drummer of the troops died (6 deaths in total)
TAN FUERTE COMO LA DEL CANAL DE BAHAMA O: As strong as that of the Bahama Channel usually is
TAPTEN 9 DUIM WATER IN HET SCHIP: Drew off 9 inches of water in the ship
TE 1 UUR IN DE HONDENWACHT SCHOOT DE WIN: At 1 o'clock in the dog watch the wind suddenly shot round to the SSW, lost an upper and an inner lee studding sail.
TE 15:00 SCHOOT DE WIND MET EEN ZWARE BU: At 15:00 the wind shifted with a heavy squall to the south.
TE ANKER HET WEER IS TE SLECHT OM VERDER: At anchor, the weather is too bad to sail further
TE VIJER UUREN PEILDEN DE ZUIDHOEK VAN C: At four o'clock took a bearing of the south point of Canaria [?], by estimate 4 miles away; took our reckoning from here and steered SSW.
TE VOORLIJK MET HET BESTEK 1°44' OF 21,2: Too far ahead by the reckoning, 1°44' or 21.25 miles
TEGEN 5 UUR WAS DE BEKOMEN LENGTE VAN DE: Towards 5 o'clock the longitude obtained for the Poursuivante was 1 degree 30 minutes. (Presumably also concerns a ship from the same convoy)
TEGEN DE AVOND OP DE UITKIJK NAAR EEN ON: Towards evening on the lookout for an uninhabited island. It was plotted in the reckoning at 21:10 south latitude and 87 longitude; saw nothing.
TEGEN DE MIDDAG HAALDE DE LUCHT ZWAAR OP: Towards noon the sky clouded over heavily.
TEGEN DE MIDDAG WERD HET DOODSTIL: Towards noon it became dead calm
TEGEN MIDDAG ZAGEN TAMELIJK HOOGLAND, HE: Towards noon saw fairly high land, recognised it as Palo Nyas from [?] to ENE, unfavourable, 8 miles distance, probably the land near Gannoo Point.
TEKEN (VIERKANTJE MET HORIZONTALE STREEP: Symbol (small square with a horizontal line through the middle) in the wind direction column.
TEKENING VAN VLAGGENMAST MET DRIE SEINVL: Drawing of a flagpole with three signal flags.
TELEGRAFISCH SEIN VD ADMIRAAL OM ZICH ON: Telegraphic signal from the admiral to place themselves under the command of the Jason. Telegraphing with Jason (art. 7) "For how many days do you have water on board?" True longitude obtained according to chronometer
TELKENS IS DE DROOGE THERMOMETER OVERGEN: Each time the dry thermometer was taken over
TEMPERATUUR EN BAROMETERSTAND ZIJN AFKOM: Temperature and barometer reading come from the day watch. Entered the Suriname River.
TEMPERATUUR EN LUCHTDRUK DIT KEER VERMEL: Temperature and air pressure this time stated at the forenoon watch, further weather at the afternoon watch.
TEMPERATUUR EN LUCHTDRUK VANAF HIER BIJ: Temperature and air pressure from here at the forenoon watch.
TEMPERATUUR VAN REGENWATER VAN EEN REGEN: Temperature of rainwater from a rain squall with calm was 74 degrees
At 1 o'clock the sun was eclipsed.
TEN 1/2 8 UREN OVERLEED EEN MATROOS GENA: At half past 7 o'clock a sailor named Conelis van Campen, native of Maaslandsluis, died. He left nothing behind. His wage was 9 guilders per month. He has a transfer to the Company of 150 guilders, 2 months' wages and a chest.
TEN 10 URE HUN EDELE MET HET VAARTUIG VA: At 10 o'clock Their Honours came on the current with the vessel of Mr Rolandus and went aboard the state's cutter De Windhoop, the flagship giving a salute of 17 shots. At 2 o'clock (afternoon watch) Their High Mightinesses left the cutter. Again a salute of 17 shots. The ship Schiedam paraded.
TEN 10 UUR ANKERDEN TER REEDE TEXEL 49 D: At 10 o'clock anchored in Texel roads, 49 days and 102 from Sunda Strait and 104 from Batavia.
TEN 10 UUR VERSCHEEN NEPTUNES MET ZIJNE: At 10 o'clock Neptune appeared with his consorts [?]. The crew held the usual baptism ceremony for crossing the line, which lasted until 12 o'clock.
TEN 10:00 U SUMATRA'S WESTKUST. LAND 6/0: At 10:00 Sumatra's west coast. Land 6/0 [?]. At 4 o'clock Krakatau E 1/2 N
TEN 10H30 OVERLEED DE FUSELIER JAN WILLE: At 10:30 the fusilier Jan Willem Robijns died.
TEN 11H30 OVERLEED DE MATROOS 3E KLAS DI: At 11:30 the sailor 3rd class Diedericks died.
TEN 12 U. WENDEN OM DE NNO: At 12 o'clock tacked about to the NNE
TEN 12 UREN HEES DEN ADMIRAAL BRAAK BENE: At 12 o'clock the admiral Braak, together with all the [?] ships, hoisted the Batavian flag and pennant in honour of the first session of the National Convention, and asked the ship's company whether they were prepared, according to their sworn oath, to protect the One and Indivisible Republic, which was answered by all with yes, whereupon the entire crew cheered three times; gave the people an extra drink.

TEN P.L.V. VERSTOPTE LUCHT, AANNEMENDE W: At P.L.V. clogged air, the wind increasing from NE by E with a rapidly rising sea. First watch storm weather. Dog watch squally weather and a terribly high running sea. Lost the longboat and the jib, turned away downwind under the reefed barque sail. Day watch it blew a hurricane. The sea ran terribly high, but was flattened by the force of the wind. The ship lay smothered under the water. The lee side could no longer be seen. Furled sails blew to shreds on the yards. The main mast threatened to fall overboard. Biting rain and hail prevented us from looking up, or scoured the skin from our faces. Towards eight o'clock resolved to cut the topmasts and yards overboard, as sea and wind were still increasing in fury and the mercury of the barometer kept falling steadily. This difficult operation succeeded by half past eight. In the forenoon watch the main and fore topmasts and yards, and the topgallant masts and yards, were overboard and clear of the ship. The ship felt noticeable relief, so that from time to time the lee rail became visible again. The bulwarks were entirely gone and the sea rolled and washed over the ship as over a reef. The wind varied between NNE and NW with continuous sharp hail. It was impossible to look up or to understand one another. It was not possible to get to the lee pump. Pumped steadily with the weather pump, which at times seemed to run dry. Barometer falling.

From St Eustacius the ship sails to St. Maarten and from there again to Curaçao.
VAN ST. EUSTATIUS NAAR SABA. VAN SABA NA: From St. Eustatius to Saba. From Saba to St. Eustatius.
VAN TOP LAND TE ZIEN IN NWTW: Land seen from the masthead at northwest by west
VAN TOP NIETS TE ZIEN: Nothing to be seen from the masthead
VAN TOP NOG NIETS GEZIEN, VERDUBBELEN DE: Still nothing seen from the masthead, the lookouts are doubled.
VAN YA 10 ENFERMOS Y CREEN QUE ES DEL PA: There are already 10 sick and they believe it is from the bread from Havana.
VAN YA 6 ENFERMOS DE CALENTURA Y 2 MAS D: There are already 6 sick with fever and 2 more with tumors.
VAN ZZW TOT WEST LAGEN HET KOMPAS OP 22°: From SSW to west the compass lay at 22° N/W
VANAF DEZE DATUM ZIJN DE MISWIJZINGEN VA: From this date the compass variations are recorded. These are the variations used.
VANAF HEDEN RANTSOEN VAN WATER AAN HET V: From now on begin giving the crew a ration of water.
VANAF HEDEN STAAT ER BIJ DE BAROMETERSTA: From now on the barometer reading shows +3 mm. This is probably a value found after the barometer was calibrated.
VANAF HIER ALLEEN BEVONDEN BREEDTE EN LE: From here only the latitude and longitude found are recorded. Remarks about the reckoning.
From here the ship still sails to St. Maarten and then to Curaçao.
VANAF HIER VAART HET SCHIP OP DE KUST VA: From here the ship sails along the coast of Guiana and there is no good data in the text.
VANAF HIER WORDEN DE GEGEVENS VAN DE LUC: From here the air pressure and temperature data are recorded at the AMW; I add these to the NMW before it.
VANAF HIER WORDT TIJDMETER 18° INGEVOERD: From here chronometer 18° is entered at 'true obtained longitude'.
VANAF NU NEEM IK HET WEER EN DE WIND OP: From now on I record the weather and wind from the AMW, PVW and EW when these are not given for the VMW.
VANAF NU STAAT ER REGELMATIG GCOP (GEKOP: From now on 'GCOP' (dead reckoned) regularly appears next to the course.
VANAF VERTREK UIT HAVANA WAREN ER 111 PE: Since departure from Havana 111 people have been under the doctor's treatment, of whom 20 had died. On arrival 25 were still under treatment.
VANGEN 'S NACHTS 1,5 LEGGER WATER: Catch 1,5 casks of water during the night
VANGEN DAGELIJKS NOG VEEL VIS: Still catch a lot of fish daily
VANGEN DE EERSTE VIS GENAAMD STATUS: Catch the first fish, called Status
Catch a pike of 5 feet 6 inches long.
VANGEN EEN VIS ALBIDROE EN EEN HAAI: Catch a fish [?] and a shark
VANGEN NOG VEEL VIS: Still catch a lot of fish
Catch a lot of mackerel again.
VANUIT CURACAO ONDERNEEMT HET SCHIP NOG: From Curaçao the ship undertakes another voyage to the Caribbean Sea (little coordinate data), to arrive back at Curaçao on 15 March, when the journal is closed.
VANUIT HET SCHIP WORDT AAN ANDERE MEEVAR: From the ship, signals are made to the other ships sailing along to report their positions. The ships sailing along are Revolutie, De Brave, De Bellona, De Havick and De Sirene.
VANWEGE DE OPGELOPEN SCHADE TIJDENS DE S: Because of the damage sustained during the storm, it is decided to sail to the Cape of Good Hope
VAREN HIERNA LANGS DE KUST VAN AFRIKA NA: Afterwards sail down along the coast of Africa.
Sail in the river of Suriname.
VAREN NAAR RIO CAMMEROEN, TERUG NAAR RIO: Sail to Rio Cammeroen, back to Rio de Gabon, then over to Sint Thome, where they come to anchor.
VAREN RICHTING BENGALEN: Sail in the direction of Bengal
VAREN UIT OP 20 AUGUSTUS RICHTING NEDERL: Set sail on 20 August in the direction of the Netherlands
VAREN VAN KAAP DE GOEDE HOOP NAAR CEYLON: Sail from the Cape of Good Hope to Ceylon through the Madagascar strait.
VAREN VOOR DE KUST LANGS OP 5 TOT 9 VAAM: Sail along the coast in 5 to 9 fathoms of water. Sand and mud bottom. The ship is 55° 22' further east than the reckoning, so 80,5 miles. So Cape Orange lies at 328° according to the chart.
VARENDE IN 'T GEZICHT DER KUST VAN AFRIK: Sailing in sight of the coast of Africa
VARIABLE Y FRESQUITO: Variable and a gentle fresh breeze
VARIACIÓN 18º NO. MERIDIANA DEL SOL: 52º: Variation 18º NW. Meridian altitude of the sun: 52º S
VARIAN EL RUMBO PARA IR EN DEMANDA DE RI: They change course to head for Rio de Janeiro
VARIAS NEVADAS, UNA DURÓ 9 HORAS (...) L: Several snowfalls, one lasted 9 hours (...) The horizons and skies have been squally with snow and freezing drizzle as it fell;
VARIAS TURBONADAS SIN MALICIA EN EL HORI: Several squalls without menace on the horizon, but at 6 in the morning one came that brought us a lot of rain and wind, which then continued with variation.
VARIETÉ DE VENTS,FIXÉS ON A' NNE, A MIDI: Variable winds, fixed at NNE; at noon it was established; at six o'clock the wind calmed and shifted to SE; during the night the wind jumped to NNW.
VE 9 EMBARCACIONES JUNTAS DE LAS CUALES: Sees 9 vessels together, of which 4 looked like frigates, 4 packet boats and 1 brigantine, which were following on the westward tack
VE DOS EMBARCACIONES A LARGA DISTANCIA N: Sees two vessels at a long distance, cannot make out their movements
VE UNA EMBARCACION POR SU BARLOVENTO REC: Sees a vessel to windward, recognizes it as a packet boat that is on the northward tack
VEEL ALBATROSSEN EN STORMVOGELS BIJ HET: Many albatrosses and storm petrels near the ship
VEEL DORADES EN DOLFIJNEN BIJ HET SCHIP,: Many dorados and dolphins near the ship, catch a dorado.
VEEL GEDRAAI VAN WEST NAAR OOST T/M 26/1: Much shifting from west to east until 26/1
VEEL GEVOGELTE BIJ HET SCHIP WAARONDER S: Many birds near the ship, including small shore gulls. Strong phosphorescence in the water.
VEEL GEVOGELTE BIJ HET SCHIP: KAAPSE DUI: Many birds near the ship: Cape pigeons and southern birds
VEEL KAAPSE DUIVEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Many Cape pigeons near the ship
VEEL KAAPSE DUIVEN EN Z VOGELS: Many Cape pigeons and southern birds
VEEL KAAPSE DUIVEN, MALEVIETEN EN MEEUWE: Many Cape pigeons, mollymawks and gulls
VEEL KAAPSE DUIVEN. 1 N.= GROOTE DRAIJP: Many Cape pigeons. 1 N. = large [?] (perhaps a right whale)
VEEL KROOS EN DORADES ? BIJ HET SCHIP, Z: Much duckweed and dorados [?] near the ship, see fish for the first time
VEEL MEEUWEN EN BOSKOPPEN BIJ HET SCHIP: Many gulls and [?] near the ship
VEEL MEEUWEN EN DRIE KURKRINGVOGELS BIJ: Many gulls and three [?] near the ship.
VEEL MEEUWEN EN EEN ZWALUW. ZE VINDEN HE: Many gulls and a swallow. They find the water greatly changed in color.
VEEL PORTUGESE MAI OF WAIS, ZAGEN VERSCH: Many Portuguese man-of-war, saw several pieces of seaweed.
VEEL SCHAARVOGELS EN VIS, RODE BEZAANTJE: Many shearwaters and fish, red by-the-wind sailors, phosphorescence in the water.
VEEL SCHAARVOGELS, PIJLSTAARTEN, EXTRA V: Many shearwaters, tropicbirds, extra many fish. At night phosphorescence and current.
VEEL SLIJTAGE AAN ZEILEN EN TUIG: Much wear on sails and rigging.
VEEL SLIJTAGE AAN ZEILEN EN TUIG. KOMPAS: Much wear on sails and rigging. Compasses adjusted, 1.5 points north westerly variation.
VEEL VAN 'T VOLK LOOPT BLOOTVOETS: Many of the crew go barefoot.
VEEL VERSCHILLENDE SOORTEN VOGELS EN VIS: Many different kinds of birds and fish.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP ZIEN EEN SCHAARVO: Many fish near the ship, saw a shearwater.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP. ZIEN EEN SCHAARV: Many fish near the ship. Saw a shearwater.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP. ZIEN TWEE GRAUWE: Many fish near the ship. Saw two grey gulls. Saw two black birds.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP.BEVONDEN EEN TEER: Many fish near the ship. Found a tar barrel in the hold leaked empty to within 10 cans. Ship's council, found 3 invalids. Caught half a corde (fish) of 90 lb. Strong ripples from current. The water seen very pale. Sounded with 120 fathoms of line, no bottom. Turned the gunpowder.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP.VANGEN EEN HAAI M: Many fish near the ship. Caught a shark with 8 young in it, 13 or 14 inches long. Cleaned the between-decks. Fumigated with gunpowder and juniper berries and sprinkled with vinegar.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP.ZIEN 2 GRAUWE MEE: Many fish near the ship. Saw 2 grey gulls.
VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP.ZIEN GROENTEN DRI: Many fish near the ship. Saw vegetables floating and a piece of wood.
VEEL VIS EN EEN ENKELE ZWARTE MEEUW. ZIE: Many fish and a single black gull. Saw northern right whales.
VEEL VIS EN SCHAAR EN ANDERE VOGELS: Many fish and shearwaters and other birds.
VEEL VIS EN VUURRING IN HET WATER: Many fish and phosphorescence in the water.
VEEL VIS EN ZEEVOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP: Many fish and seabirds near the ship.
VEEL VIS GEVANGEN, ZODAT HET HELE SCHEEP: Caught much fish, so that the whole ship's company could eat.
VEEL VIS, OOK ENKELE SCHAARVOGELS EN STR: Many fish, also a few shearwaters and beach gulls, saw many white and 2 grey gulls.
VEEL VIS, OOK GROTE VLIEGENDE VISSEN EN: Many fish, also large flying fish and phosphorescence in the water.
VEEL VIS, RODE BEZAANTJES EN EEN ENKELE: Many fish, red by-the-wind sailors and a single shearwater.
VEEL VIS, SCHAARVOGELS EN PIJLSTAARTEN E: Many fish, shearwaters and tropicbirds and flying fish [?] on the deck.
VEEL VIS, VEEL VLIEGENDE VIS, ENKELE VOG: Many fish, many flying fish, a few birds.
VEEL VIS, ZIEN EEN PIJLSTAART EN VERSCHE: Many fish, saw a tropicbird and several red by-the-wind sailors floating.
VEEL VIS, ZIEN EEN SCHAARVOGEL, EN EEN P: Many fish, saw a shearwater and a tropicbird.
VEEL VIS. STROOM EN VURING IN 'T WATER: Many fish. Current and phosphorescence in the water.
VEEL VISSEN BIJ HET SCHIP:ALSKAER ?, TON: Many fish near the ship: [?], tunas, northern right whales.
VEEL VISSEN GEZIEN ( PIJLSTAART, EN VLIE: Many fish seen (tropicbird and flying fish).
VEEL VLIEGENDE VISSEN EN ANDERE VISSEN B: Many flying fish and other fish near the ship.
VEEL VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP, WAARONDER VEE: Many birds near the ship, including many shorebirds, also a [?].
VEEL VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP. VINGEN EEN JA: Many birds near the ship. Caught a gannet (or albatross).
VEEL VOGELS EN E XTRA VEEL VIS: Many birds and extra many fish.
VEEL VOGELS EN KAAPSE DUIVEN. VLIEGENDE: Many birds and Cape pigeons. Flying fish and other fish.
VEEL VOGELS EN VIS BIJ SCHIP CALLEVAATEN: Many birds and fish near the ship Callevaaten.
VEEL VOGELS EN VIS, WITTE BEZAANTJES: Many birds and fish, white by-the-wind sailors.
VEEL VOGELS EN VIS. ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE GR: Many birds and fish. Saw several large round white [?] floating, shaped like pigs, blowing and [?] eggs [?]. Phosphorescence in the water.
Many birds and fish near the ship.
VEEL VOGELS, IN DE NACHT STERKE VURING: Many birds, strong phosphorescence in the night.
VEEL ZEE KRIJGEN VEEL WATER OVER: Shipping much sea, much water coming over.
VEEL ZWARTE MEEUWEN EN EEN STRANDMEEUW: Many black gulls and a beach gull.
VEERMAN ALS LUITENANT TER ZEE EERSTE KLA: Veerman placed as lieutenant at sea first class on His Majesty's ship Zeeland.
VEERMAN VERBLIJFT VAN 26 JUNI TOT 23 JUL: Veerman stays in the city from 26 June to 23 July, with Rear Admiral Buijskes and with Governor R. Darling.
Many flying fish on the deck.
VEN 1 PARDELA Y 1 MARTIN PLACA. CIELOS Y: They see 1 shearwater and 1 martín placa. Skies and horizons covered with light cloudiness. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
VEN 2 EMBARCACIONES A LAS 0:00 CON LUZ A: They see 2 vessels at 0:00 with a light astern.
VEN 2 RABIAHORCADOS Y BOLADORES. CIELOS: They see 2 frigatebirds and flying fish. Skies and horizons with cloudiness. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
VEN 2 RABIJUNCOS Y 2 PAJAROS SEMEJANTES: They see 2 tropicbirds and 2 birds similar to doves, white and black.
VEN 3 MATAS DE SARGAZO, TONINAS BLANCAS: They see 3 clumps of sargassum, white porpoises and a quantity of birds and a large gull. Skies and horizons hazy. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
VEN CHILE CONDOR A LAS 15:00: They see a Chile condor at 15:00.
VEN EL ISLOTE CANBRIDG (CAMBRIDGE) EN LA: They see the islet Canbridg (Cambridge) in the early morning.
They see some whales in the afternoon.
VEN ESTE DIA PAJAROS NEGROS: They see black birds this day.
VEN HILEROS DE CORRIENTES DEL N CON FUER: They see lines of strong current from the N. The wind calm before night and they anchor WNW of the low island that is opposite Cabo de Matas. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
VEN LA ISLA DE HIERRO: They see the island of Hierro.
VEN LA ISLA DE LA MADERA. ANOCHECEN EN E: They see the island of Madeira. At nightfall they are on the meridian of Puerto Santo, 6 leagues distant.
VEN MARTINPLACAS, PARDELAS Y OTROS PAJAR: They see martinplacas, shearwaters and other birds (from this it appears the martinplacas are birds and not dolphins).
VEN MUCHAS BANDADAS DE AVES Y ALGUNAS MA: They see many flocks of birds and some swarms of [?]. They also see whales, sea lions and a multitude of shore birds.
VEN MULTITUD DE PARDELAS Y DE OTROS PAJA: They see a multitude of shearwaters and other small black birds similar to martins, which show themselves when there is a storm. The data are usually from dawn and the noon observation.
VEN PULO TIMON POR LA TARDE: They see Pulo Timon in the afternoon.
VEN TONINAS TRANSITANDO DEL O PARA EL E: They see porpoises passing from W to E and a young whale, and the martinplaca birds have stayed with them since leaving port.
VEN UN RABIJUNCO POR LA TARDE: They see a tropicbird in the afternoon.
VEN UNA BALLENA MUERTA A LAS 8:00: They see a dead whale at 8:00.
VEN UNA ESTRELLA CON UNA COLA MUY LARGA: They see a star with a very long tail towards the SW, rising in the E 1/4 SE at 00:00.
VENDU VAN NALATENSCHAP VAN VERDRONKEN OF: Sold from the estate of the drowned young officer T. Lorie.
VENÍA DE LA COSTA DE GUINEA (SEGÚN PAREC: She came from the coast of Guinea (as it seemed, loaded with Black people).
VERAND. LENGTE 1° 27'. MET DE DAG DE KOE: Changed longitude 1° 27'. The breeze decreasing during the day.
Changed meridian distance to the east 12 miles.
VERANDERD MERIDIAAN OM DE MAST 13,75 MIJ: Changed meridian [?] 13,75 miles. West of Lezard 77 miles.

VERANDERDE LENGTE 15'. WACHTEN HET SCHIP: Change of longitude 15'. Waited for the ship.

Mallebaardschen coast between NE 1/2 [?] and [?] 1/2 [?] (it looked like a ship), not identified because of the great distance. Sounded 115 fathoms, no bottom.

VERANDERDE LENGTE 1°22. (GIS, PLAT) HEIJ: Change of longitude 1°22. (Estimate, flat) [?] sand ENE 34 miles.

Jager: north latitude 41 degrees 23 minutes, longitude 333 degrees 58 minutes.

VERANDERDE LENGTE 9'. GEBETERDE KOERS EN: Change of longitude 9'. Corrected course and distance [?] 7/8 W, 13,25 miles.

VERANDERDE LENGTE OM DE? 38'. AW: \"HIER: Change of longitude to the [?] 38'. AW: "Here we have had winds like this for some days." (quotation)
VERANDERDE LENGTE, 1° 28. ZW HOEK VAN PO: Change of longitude, 1° 28. SW point of Porto Sancto NW and the NE point NE of us. Observation (also of other seafarers) that Porto Sancto lies at 359° 30' longitude and latitude 33°, thus 4° and 30' to the east and in latitude 0° 30' too far north. According to our calculations the roads of Fonsyael (Funchal) lie at a latitude of 32° 29'.
VERANDERDE LENGTE? ° EN 15. (CHIRURGIJN: Change of longitude [?]° and 15. (Surgeon comes aboard)

VERANDEREN KOERS OM NIET BIJ DE EILENDEN: Changing course so as not to get hemmed in by the islands.
VERANDERING EN VERMINDERING VAN RANTSOEN: Change and reduction of rations: cheese, butter, vinegar, gin, salt meat, bacon, pearl barley, bread, grey peas and green peas. All this in connection with the southeast wind that began to settle in ever more steadily
VERBEELDEN ONS MADERA TE ZIEN IN HET? TE: Imagine ourselves seeing Madeira in the [?] to the S, which however was not yet visible at noon. The commander gave a signal to come round astern; sails saw at the same time the island Porto Santo in the WSW 1/2 W, whereupon the commander [?] gave a signal to take measurements.
VERBEETERDE ONS BESTEK 2 GR. IN LENGTE O: Corrected our reckoning 2 degrees in longitude to the east because we have almost 3 points of compass error

VERBETERDE KOERS IS VERMELD EN BIJ BEHOU: Corrected course is noted and entered alongside the course and distance kept. The general course through the day is WNW 1/3 W, the distance 25,75 miles. I mention this last one only because I find the differences in distance so large.

VERBETERDE KOERS ZOTZ 2 MIJL: Corrected course SE by S 2 miles

VERBETEREN HET BESTEK 6 GRADEN OOSTELIJK: Correct the reckoning 6 degrees more easterly,
VERBETEREN HET BESTEK MET 10 MIJL RECHT: Correct the reckoning by 10 miles due east
VERBETEREN HET BESTEK. BLEVEN BIJ DE RON: Correct the reckoning. Stayed with the round chart
VERBETEREN HET BESTEK. ZIJN TROPICUS CAP: Correct the reckoning. Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn.
VERDEELDEN SPULLEN VAN HET SCHIP VAN DE: Divided the items from the ship of the previous day among the crew and the embarked troops
VERDER IN BOEK MOOIE HELDERE TEKENINGEN: Further in the book are fine clear drawings and a description of Diego Garcia.
VERDER ZEILENDE IN HET KANAAL. LOODDEN E: Sailing on in the Channel. Sounded and found a depth of 50 to 60 fathoms.
VERDRONKEN: SCHEEPSJONGEN ADAM VAN DE VE: Drowned: ship's boy Adam van de Velde of Vlissingen
VERGELIJKEN HET BESTEK MET ANDERE SCHEPE: Compare the reckoning with other ships of the convoy
VERGELIJKEN HET BESTEK MET DE COMMANDANT: Compare the reckoning with the commander and the Kenau Hasselaar and the Hippomenes
VERHAAL OVER DE VERHOUDING MET HET SCHIP: Account of the relationship with the ship of Reul
VERHAALTJE OVER BINNENKOMST KONING GOAH: Short tale about the arrival of King Goah
VERHANDELING OVER DE LIGGING VD ZUIDELIJ: Treatise on the position of the southernmost Serter on the chart. Course and distance since departure from the roadstead where we lay, according to the ordinary [?], at 0° 0' longitude and 32° 46' N yesterday evening at 8 o'clock
VERHEID 7 MIJL NIET ZEKER. WEST MERIDIAA: Distance 7 miles not certain. West meridian 258,75 miles. Changed 4,75 miles W. Obtained 250 miles (not certain).
VERHEID NIET VERMELD: EW T/M VW IS 24 MI: Distance not stated: EW to VW is 24 miles toward WSW
VERJAARDAG VAN DE ERFPRINS VAN ORANJE WO: Birthday of the hereditary prince of Orange is celebrated
VERKENDE DE KUST IN HET NO VOLGENS BESTE: Sighted the coast in the NE, according to the reckoning Grand Bassa
VERKOCHT ENIGE NAGELATEN ROMMELING VAN D: Sold some left-behind junk of the deserted sailor Josep Armenie
VERKOCHTEN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE OVERLEDEN: Sold the goods of the deceased Dokus de Vos
Sold the goods of the deceased mate
VERKOCHTEN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE OVERLEDENE: Sold the goods of the deceased
Sold the goods of the deceased Jan van Houten
VERKOCHTEN DE GOEDEREN VAN DE VERDRONKEN: Sold the goods of the drowned sailor Roelof Sijbranste
VERKOCHTEN DE SCHEEPSKLEREN AAN 'T VOLK: Sold the ship's clothes to the crew
VERKOCHTEN GOEDEREN VAN OVERLEDENE + BED: Sold goods of the deceased + amount
VERKOPEN ACHTERGEBLEVEN GOEDEREN VAN TWE: Selling the belongings left behind by two deserters who stayed behind in Cape Town (A. Datterd and I. Boldermans)
VERKOPEN DE GOEDEREN VD VERMISTE KOK: Selling the goods of the missing cook
VERKOPEN GOEDEREN VAN OVERLEDEN LUIT. 2E: Selling goods of the deceased lieutenant 2nd class C. Scholl
VERKOPEN HET GOED VAN DE OVERLEDENE. GEB: Selling the belongings of the deceased. Using the air pumps twice a day.
VERKOPEN KLEREN AAN 'T SCHEEPSVOLK. MAKE: Selling clothes to the ship's crew. Cleaning the between decks.
VERLAAT EERSTE INTENTIE OM DE CARIBISCHE: Abandons his first intention of entering the Caribbean Sea at Guadeloupe, but because of the description by Capt. Andr Livingston to John Pivedy 1824 that in August and September there are many calms and southerly winds there, accompanied by hurricanes, and also because the crew is very inexperienced, he (Capt. vd Panter) decides to sail into the Caribbean Sea between Tobago and Granada
VERLAGEN DE COMPASSEN OP 11 GRADEN NOORD: Adjusting the compasses to 11 degrees northwest variation
VERLATEN CURAÇAO EN ZETTEN KOERS IN DE R: Left Curaçao and set course in the direction of the Mona Passage
Left Havana and are going to Trunillo.
VERLEDEN CORPORAAL JOHAN GODLIEB EGGERS: Deceased corporal Johan Godlieb Eggers of Straalsond
VERLEGDE COMPASSEN VAN 12 OP 10 NOORDWES: Adjusted compasses from 12 to 10 northwest variation
VERLEGDEN DE KOMPASSEN OP 22° 30\" NOORD: Adjusted the compasses to 22° 30" northwest variation
VERLEGDEN KOMPAS VAN 35 OP 30 GRADEN NOO: Adjusted compass from 35 to 30 degrees northwest variation

VERLEGGENDE COMPASSEN VAN 5/ TOT OP 21/2: Adjusting the compasses from 5 to 2 1/2 degrees northwesterly variation.
VERLEIDEN DE KOMP. VAN 7° 30' OP 10° 00: Adjusting the compasses from 7° 30' to 10° 00 NW
VERLEIDEN DE KOMPASSEN VAN 0° 0' TOT OP: Adjusting the compasses from 0° 0' to 2° 30' NW. Hailed the Three Brothers: its latitude was 10° 53' and longitude 95° 10'.
VERLEIJDEN DE COMPASSEN OP 6 GRADEN BEOO: Adjusting the compasses to 6 degrees east of the needle
VERLEIJDEN DE COMPASSEN VAN 15° OP 12°30: Adjusting the compasses from 15° to 12°30' NW
VERLIETEN ST. HELENA. DIT IS EEN EXTRACT: Left St. Helena. This is an extract from the journal of the ship Valentine, which was part of a convoy of 14 ships.
VERLIJDEN DE KOMPASSEN OP? GRADEN. GEBET: Adjusting the compasses to [?] degrees. Corrected course and [?] 7/8 W, 20.25 miles. Changed longitude 0° 13'.

VERLIJDEN ONZE KOMPASSEN VAN 10 GRADEN N: Adjusting our compasses from 10 degrees to 5 degrees westerly variation
VERMIST DE MATROOS GENAAMD J. JOSTAPEL D: Missing the sailor named J. Jostapel, who lay sick in the bow. Presumably jumped into the sea. More sick aboard.
VERMIST MATROOS GERRIT ABBENHUYSEN DIE W: Missing sailor Gerrit Abbenhuysen, who probably went overboard and drowned
VERMIST SOLDAAT ANTONIJ REIJNES VAN FRAN: Missing soldier Antonij Reijnes of Frankfort.
VERMIST SOLDAAT HERMANUS WOLFF VAN FREMO: Missing soldier Hermanus Wolff of Fremondsdorf
VERMIST SOLDAAT JENRATN POULUS ZUIJDERLA: Missing soldier Jenratn Poulus Zuijderlandt of Leijden.
VERMIST SOLDAAT VAN 'T REGT VAN WURTEMBU: Missing soldier of the Wurtemburg regiment
VERMIST: MATROOS DE WIT. OVERLEDEN MATRO: Missing: sailor de Wit. Deceased: sailor Raadje Kaassen
VERMISTE SCHEPEN ZIJN WEER BIJ HET KONVO: The missing ships are back with the convoy.
VERMOEDELIJK OP DE BANK VAN ANGULAS GEKO: Presumably came onto the Angulas bank
Suspect seeing land in the SSE.
VERNAMEN STERKE STROOM. IN DE NAMIDDAG V: Noticed a strong current. In the afternoon altered course to E by S. With this one cannot comply with Order No. 14 written on folio 10. Explanation about this. Believe that S.E.Comp has the best interest at heart with her dear ship and crew.
VERONDERSTELDEN BIJ HET LAND VAN MATARAM: Supposed to be near the land of Mataram [?] and stony red land
VERONDERSTELLEN EEN STERKE STROOM OM DE: Suppose a strong current to the N.
VERONDERSTELLEN LAND TE ZIEN DOCH KONDEN: Suppose we see land but could not be sure of it because of the hazy mist. According to the reckoning we are at the land.
VERONGELUKT MATROOS ANTHONIE JUDOKUS LEE: Accident: sailor Anthonie Judokus Leezand killed
VERONGELUKT: DE TWEEDE TIMMERMAN JOHAN D: Accident: the second carpenter Johan Diderick Schroider of Hamburgerberg killed
VEROVEREN EEN ENGELSE KOOPVAARDER, GELAD: Captured an English merchantman, loaded with provisions, brandy and wine, from Levenport to Terra Neuffe; an officer and some men from the Jager go over to the English ship.
VERSCHEIDENE HEREN AAN BOORD, PARADEERDE: Several gentlemen aboard, paraded with the crew in the rigging
VERSCHEIDENE HEREN VAN DE REGERING VAN D: Several gentlemen of the government of the shore aboard. On departure 9 shots.
VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP, WAARO: Several birds near the ship, including the so-called Cape pigeons
VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS. ZIEN ENIGE VUERING: Several birds. See some phosphorescence in the water.
VERSCHEIDENE WITTE MEEUWEN EN SCHAARVOGE: Several white gulls and scissor-birds near the ship

Found that, because we saw no land, the reckoning was too far east; set our reckoning to the average latitude and longitude of the Jager, Vliegende Visch and ourselves.

VERSCHIL DER LENGTE 3 GRADEN 21 MINUTEN: Difference of longitude 3 degrees 21 minutes east.

VERSCHIL DER LENGTE 4 GRADEN 54 MINUTEN: Difference of longitude 4 degrees 54 minutes east.
VERSCHILLENDE KANO'S AAN BOORD. STROOM G: Several canoes aboard. During the night the current had set the ship more than 6 miles to the east, so that they were below Settra Krou
VERSCHILLENDE SCHEPEN WISSELEN LENGTEN E: Several ships exchange longitudes and latitudes
VERSCHILLENDE TIJDMETERS WORDEN MET ELKA: Several chronometers are compared with each other
VERSCHILLENDE VOGELS. STERKE VURING IN ': Several birds. Strong phosphorescence in the water
VERSTREKKEN VOOR 14 DAGEN RANTZOEN VOOR: Issued 14 days' ration for the crew. Held ship's council about the sick. Found 6 invalids, of whom 5 with tertian fever and 1 suffering from scurvy
VERSTREKTE DE SLAVEN 2 KEER IN DE WEEK S: Gave the slaves bacon and meat twice a week and 2 small drams of spirits, pipe and tobacco a week
VERSTREKTE DE SLAVEN ALLE 8 DAGEN PIJPEN: Gave the slaves pipes and tobacco every 8 days
VERSTREKTE VOOR EEN MAAND RANTSOEN NAMEN: Issued a month's ration, namely butter, oil and vinegar
VERSTREKTEN 1/2 MAAND RANTSOEN. MAKEN SC: Issued a half month's ration. Cleaning the between decks.
VERSTREKTEN ALLEEN BIER A DE SCHEEPELING: Issued only beer to the crew. Rolled tremendously.
VERSTREKTEN HALF MAANDRANTSOE. HIELDEN S: Issued a half month's ration. Held ship's council, found 5 invalids, mostly on the mend.
VERSTREKTEN ZUURKOOL, OLIE, EN AZIJN AAN: Issued sauerkraut, oil, and vinegar to the crew
VERTREK VAN REEDE VAN SANTA CRUZ. AFGEVA: Departure from the roadstead of Santa Cruz. Departure reckoning from the roadstead of Santa Cruz: north latitude 28°28', longitude west of Greenwich 16°16'
Departed for the roadstead of Batavia.
VERTREKKEN UIT GALLE. OM 3 UUR NEMEN ZE: Departed from Galle. At 3 o'clock they take the dead reckoning position with the given longitude and latitude. The captain is given a letter to carry from the Company ship De Patriot, Captain M. Bosma.
VERTREKKEN UIT KDGH MET DE GOUVERNEUR GE: Departed from KDGH with the Gouverneur Generaal, Casteel van Tilburg and the Nieuwvijvervreugd.
Departs from there again the next day.
VERTROKKEN UIT BATAVIA, RICHTING HELLEVO: Departed from Batavia, heading for Hellevoetsluis.
VERTROKKEN UIT ST. GEORGE D'ELMINA. POSI: Departed from St. George d'Elmina. Positions begin in the crossing to the 'Bight'.
VERTROKKEN UIT SURINAME, ZEILENDE NAAR C: Departed from Suriname, sailing to Curaçao.
Departed from the roads of Batavia.
VERTROKKEN VAN ST. MAARTEN NAAR SURINAME: Departed from St. Maarten for Suriname. Dead reckoning since 8 o'clock in the morning.
VERTROKKEN VANUIT DE REDE VAN CORMANTIJN: Departed from the roads of Cormantijn.
VERVERSINGEN EN EXTRA WIJN VOOR 'T VOLK: Fresh provisions and extra wine for the crew.
Continuation of the earlier leg Suriname/Curaçao. Saw Little Tobago straight ahead.
VERVOLG MET DE OFFICIEREN EN BEMANNING V: Continuation with the officers and crew of the Admiraal Evertsen. From here on with the Cadmus.
VERVOLG VAN HET JOURNAAL OVERGENOMEN DOO: Continuation of the journal, taken over by the first officer after the death of the captain.
VERZETTE HET BESTEK 1°18' WESTELIJKER: Shifted the dead reckoning 1°18' further west.
VERZETTE HET BESTEK 5 GRADEN WESTELIJK D: Shifted the dead reckoning 5 degrees west, thus 119gr24min.
VERZOND 8 APRIL MET DE NEDERLANDSE BRIK: Sent on 8 April with the Dutch brig Ocomaze, Captain Evers, the report of the ship and crew, the statement of the defects discovered in the bottom, of the broken yards, and the covering letter.
VESTREKKEN 1/2 MAAND RANTSOEN.HIELDEN SC: Issued a half-month ration. Held ship's council. Found 6 invalids, of whom 1 very weak.
VICTUALIEMEESTER A VAN NIEUWLAND OVERLED: Victualling master A van Nieuwland died.
VIENTO DE LA MAÑANA O TARDE / TIEMPO GEN: Wind of the morning or afternoon / general weather.
VIENTO FRESQUITO PARA EL E ANOCHECIÓ HOR: Light fresh wind toward the E. At nightfall horizons and skies [?], the sea moderate with the same wind.
VIENTO MEDIODÍA / REFERENCIA DE MAR DE T: Midday wind / sea reference for the whole day.
VIENTO MEDIODÍA / REFERENCIA DEL MAR DE: Midday wind / sea reference for the whole day.
