WESTELIJKSTE VAN GROOT CANARIËN ZTO 11 A: Westernmost point of Groot Canariën S by E 11 to 12 miles.
WIERDE BESLOTEN, IN STILLIGHEID OM DE ME: It was decided, quietly, to destroy the [?] papers and signals given along...
WIJ ... WAARE OM 1/2 8 UURE MET HET CONV: We ... were at sea with the convoy at 7:30.
WIJ EISEN BETALING VOOR DE SCHOTEN, MAAR: We demand payment for the shots, but he says he has no money. We were allowed to pick a gold watch as payment. Many apologies from his side, and that it was only the 2nd voyage he made in these regions and that they had frightened him beforehand. He also did not know that the land had [?] and so had not taken us for a warship. He had no wish at all to show contempt for the flag of the State. All on the Hoop are very remorseful, also a passenger, Mr. Zegers. In the end the skipper does not have to pay for the bullets.
WIJ KORTE OP DE HAVE EN WIERDEN AFGEDANK: We [?] in the harbour and were discharged, so God be praised and thanked for the safe voyage, signed ad vand Gon.
WIJ WAREN OOSTELIJKER ALS ONSE GISSING W: We were further east than our estimate was.
WIJ ZULLE OOSTELIJKER ZIJN WANT MEN HEEF: We should be further east, because visibility is good but no land can be seen yet. Taking that for now, 17:30.
WILDE MADERA IN 'T ZICHT LOPEN OM ONZE T: Wilde Madera in sight, ran to check our chronometer, which ran irregularly, having gone at Cadiz from a lag of 1,03 seconds to a gain of 0,97 seconds.
WILLEN BEZUIDEN DE KLIP NEGRUS BLIJVEN D: Want to stay south of the Negrus rock, which on the chart of the Atlantic Ocean by Heather 1825 lies at 48º 5'' N. Remarks on the position of the islet Maijda and the chart by Heel 1811 and Heather 1825.
WILLEN ST. JAGO AANDOEN VOOR VERVERSINGE: Want to call at St. Jago for fresh supplies for the sick, whose number grows daily.
WINDKRACHT EN VORM BEWOLKING VAN DE PVW: Wind force and cloud form from the PVW.
WISSELEN SEINEN UIT MET FORT NIEUW AMSTE: Exchange signals with Fort Nieuw Amsterdam and Fort Zeelandia. Under sail: 05.00 h. Anchored: 14:30 h.
WISSELEN VAN SALUUT SCHOTEN MET PRINCES: Exchange salute shots with Princes Carolina.
WITTE STRANDMEEUWEN EN KAAPSE DUIVEN: White shore gulls and Cape pigeons.
WOLKDRIJVENDE LUCHT MOOI WEER: Sky with drifting clouds, fine weather.
WORDEN BRANDING GEWAAR DAT MEN VOOR ISLA: Noticed breakers, so we were off Isla de Sal.
WORDEN DOOR DE HOGE DEINING STERK OM DE: Were set strongly to the north by the high swell, drifted mostly without steering.
WORDEN OM DE OOST GEZET, OOK VLGS TIJDME: Were set to the east, also according to the chronometer.
WORDEN TOT 2 KEER ACHTERNAGEZETEN DOOR E: Were chased from astern up to 2 times by English ships.
WORDT IETS VERMELD OVER EEN ZEILORDER OM: Something is mentioned about a sailing order to sail with the Iris, Jager, Vliegende Visch, Piet Heijn and the Pollux.
WORDT OVERLEG GEVOERD OVER DE AANHOUDEND: Discussion is held about the persistent southwesterly winds that considerably delayed the voyage to New-York.
Y SIGUIENDO EN DEMANDA DE LA TIERRA Y HA: And continuing in search of land and finding myself 8 leagues from it...
YA NO LE QUEDAN COCINEROS SANOS: He has no healthy cooks left.
YA SON 6 PULGADAS. VEN PARDELAS Y MARTIN: Now it is 6 inches. They see shearwaters and [?].
Saw the south coast of Java in the morning.
ZAGEN 3 SCHEPEN WELKE MET DEN DAG OM DE: Saw 3 ships which during the day lay to the NE but later tacked with us.
ZAGEN 4 KANO'S MET IN ELK 2 NEGERS. RUIL: Saw 4 canoes with 2 Black men in each. Traded fish for gin.
ZAGEN 4 SCHEPEN VEN TE LOEFWAARD EN EEN: Saw 4 ships to windward and one close by ahead to leeward. EW.: They give the signal of reconnaissance to the ship to leeward. The ship answered this with a counter signal. They reduce sail to stay with it.
ZAGEN 5 SCHEPEN AAN LIJ, ZIJ GEVEN HET S: Saw 5 ships to leeward, they give the signal of reconnaissance: lower the fore topsail and 2 shots. They could not see whether (those other ships) gave the counter signal.
ZAGEN BEZAANTIES DRIJVEN. PASSEREN DE TR: Saw by-the-wind sailors floating. Passed the Tropic of Cancer.
Saw an exceptional number of flying fish.
ZAGEN BOSJES GROENTE DRIJVEN, ZAGEN EEN: Saw tufts of greens floating, saw a cook's hen.
ZAGEN BRANDING AAN STUURBOORD, LEEK GRON: Saw breakers to starboard, looked like ground breakers, but could not sound any bottom.
ZAGEN CAGALOTTEN IN MENIGTE RONDOM HET S: Saw sperm whales in great numbers around the ship.
ZAGEN DAT HUN KOOPVAARDER VAN HEN AFGERA: Saw that their merchantman had drifted away from them. Then sailed under small sail.
ZAGEN DE BOER MET ZIJN VARKES EN VEEL VL: Saw the Farmer with his pigs and many flying fish.
ZAGEN DE COMMANDANT, MAAR DE MERCUUR ABS: Saw the commander, but the Mercuur absent, afterwards could no longer see the Thetis.
ZAGEN DE EERSTE ALBATROSSEN EN ANDERE KA: Saw the first albatrosses and other Cape birds.
ZAGEN DE GEHELE DAG VEEL GROTE VISSEN, W: Saw many large fish all day, including a sperm whale, and caught a shark.
ZAGEN DE JOHANNA MARIA CHRISTINA NAHMENS: Saw the Johanna Maria Christina Nahmens.
ZAGEN DE KOMPASAFW OP 18° N/W: Saw the compass variation at 18° NW.
ZAGEN DE KOMPASAFW OP 24° N/W: Saw the compass variation at 24° NW.
ZAGEN DE KUST VAN ANGOLA, DIEPTE 32 VADE: Saw the coast of Angola, depth 32 fathoms.
ZAGEN DE MAAN DOOR DE ECLIPS ZEER STERK: Saw the moon diminish very strongly through the eclipse.
ZAGEN DE TOP DER PIEK MET WOLKEN BEZET E: Saw the top of the peak shrouded in clouds and covered with snow.
ZAGEN DES S'NACHTS WIT WATER EEN UUR LAN: Saw white water at night for one hour.
ZAGEN DOOR DE DAG ALBATROSSEN EN ZWARTE: Saw albatrosses and black storm petrels during the day.
ZAGEN DOOR DE DIKKE REGENACHTIGE LUCHT G: Because of the thick, rainy sky, saw no land.
ZAGEN DOOR HEIIGHEID VAN DE LUCHT GEEN L: Because of the haziness of the sky, saw no land (should have seen the Salt Islands).
ZAGEN DUIZENDEN BEZAANTIES DRIJVEN: Saw thousands of mizzen-sail jellyfish floating.
ZAGEN EEN BRUINE VIS EN EEN VOGEL BIJ HE: Saw a brown fish and a bird near the ship.
ZAGEN EEN BUITENGEWONE GROTE HOEVEELHEID: Saw an extraordinarily large number of birds.
ZAGEN EEN DODE WALVIS. VINGEN EEN VOGEL: Saw a dead whale. Caught a bird.
ZAGEN EEN DOODE NOORDCAPER EN EEN MENIGT: Saw a dead right whale and a multitude of birds [?]. It was white above the water.
ZAGEN EEN EILAND LAAG BEGROEID MET KREUP: Saw a low island overgrown with scrub, which was not shown on any of the charts, at 10 deg. 6' S and 152 deg. 12' W, and named it Frederiksoord.
ZAGEN EEN FREGATVOGEL EN VERSCHEIDENE BO: Saw a frigatebird and several spotted dolphins.
ZAGEN EEN GROOT AANTAL BRUINVISSEN EN VO: Saw a large number of porpoises and birds.
ZAGEN EEN GROTE MENIGTE VOGELS: Saw a great multitude of birds.
Saw a shark and many birds.
ZAGEN EEN KAAPSE DUIF BIJ HET SCHIP: Saw a Cape pigeon near the ship.
ZAGEN EEN KAAPSE DUIF EN VERSCHEIDENE HA: Saw a Cape pigeon and several sharks.
ZAGEN EEN KAAPSE DUIF. ZAGEN EEN TAKJE D: Saw a Cape pigeon. Saw a twig floating.
ZAGEN EEN KOMEET IN HET WNW MET DE STAAR: Saw a comet in the WNW with its tail turned toward the zenith.
ZAGEN EEN KOMEET OF STAART-STAR. HET JOU: Saw a comet or tailed star. The log gives 10 degrees more as latitude.
ZAGEN EEN LANDVOGEL EN EEN SCHILDPAD: Saw a land bird and a turtle.
ZAGEN EEN LANDVOGEL EN VERSCHEIDENE ZEEM: Saw a land bird and several seagulls.
ZAGEN EEN MAANECLIPS, DE VERDUISTERING B: Saw a lunar eclipse; the eclipse began at 8 o'clock in the evening and was finished at 9 o'clock in the evening.
ZAGEN EEN MALLEGAAS, ENG. ALBATROS CAAPS: Saw a mallemuck, in English albatross, and Cape pigeons.
ZAGEN EEN MALLEVIET EN VERSCHEIDENE ANDE: Saw a [?] and several other birds.
ZAGEN EEN MEENIGTE ZEEKROOST LANGS HET S: Saw a multitude of sea spawn floating along the ship.
ZAGEN EEN MENIGTE BUIKEN VAN ZEEKATTEN D: Saw a multitude of cuttlefish bellies floating.
ZAGEN EEN MENIGTE KREEFTEN DRIJVEN: Saw a multitude of lobsters floating.
ZAGEN EEN MENIGTE NOORDKAPERS: Saw a multitude of right whales.
ZAGEN EEN MENIGTE VOGELS EN GROEN KROOST: Saw a multitude of birds and green spawn near the ship.
Saw a multitude of birds and whales.
ZAGEN EEN NOORDKAPER EN EEN MEEUW: Saw a right whale and a gull.
ZAGEN EEN NOORDKAPER, ZO GROOT ALS HET H: Saw a right whale as big as half the ship.
ZAGEN EEN REGENBOOG AAN DE MAAN OM 7 UUR: Saw a rainbow around the moon at 7 o'clock in the evening. By our reckoning we should be at the latitude of Porto Santo.
Saw a rainbow around the moon.
ZAGEN EEN STRANDMEEUW, PIJLSTAARTEN EN S: Saw a gull, pintails and [?] birds.
ZAGEN EEN STUK HOUT DRIJVEN WAAR VOGELS: Saw a piece of wood floating with birds sitting on it.
ZAGEN EEN TROPIAVOGEL, ENIGE LANGE EBBE: Saw a tropicbird, some long-winged gulls and many flying fish.
ZAGEN EEN UIL BIJ 'T SCHIP: Saw an owl near the ship.
ZAGEN EEN VUUR, PRESUMEERDEN DAT WE BEZU: Saw a fire; presumed that we were south of the [?].
ZAGEN EEN WALVIS BUITEN DE BAAI: Saw a whale outside the bay.
ZAGEN EEN WALVIS, MEN GING ER MET TWEE S: Saw a whale; two boats went after it, together with Commander Snel. Our boat came within shooting range but the whale became aware of it, as did the boat of Snel, which was close behind it.
ZAGEN EEN WALVIS. VERKLEURDE ZEE, VUILGR: Saw a whale. Discolored sea, dirty green.
ZAGEN EEN WATERHOOS DICHT BIJ HET SCHIP: Saw a waterspout close to the ship.
ZAGEN EEN WATERSLANG EN EEN GROTE HAAI B: Saw a sea snake and a large shark near the ship.
ZAGEN EEN ZEER GROTE VOGEL BIJ HET SCHIP: Saw a very large bird near the ship.
ZAGEN EEN ZEER MOOIE REGENBOOG VAN DE MA: Saw a very beautiful rainbow from the moon.
ZAGEN EEN ZON ECLIPS EN NIEUWE MAAN STAN: Saw a solar eclipse and the position of the new moon.
ZAGEN ENIGE BEZAANTJES BIJ HET SCHIP: Saw some mizzen-sail jellyfish near the ship.
ZAGEN ENIGE MALLEMUKEN VOGELS BIJ 'T SCH: Saw some mallemuck birds near the ship.
Saw some pintails near the ship.
ZAGEN ENIGE VERANDERINGEN AAN 'T WATER: Saw some changes in the water.
ZAGEN ENIGE VOGELEN EN VEEL VLIEGENDE VI: Saw some birds and many flying fish near the ship.
ZAGEN ENIGE ZUIDVOGELS OF ZWARTE MEEUWEN: Saw some southern birds or black gulls.
ZAGEN ENKELE SCHOTSEN IJS. KOMEN VEEL BA: Saw a few ice floes. Met a lot of bay ice, and at 20.00 hours they sailed into a pack of ice.
ZAGEN GALE OM 4 UUR PASSEERDEN DE GROTE: Saw a gale. At 4 o'clock passed the Great Whale, a rock. The pilots Jan van Drijschel and Joost Schraders came aboard.
ZAGEN GEEN LAND. IS TE HEIIG: Saw no land. It is too hazy.
ZAGEN GROOT AANTAL BRUINVISSEN EN CACHEL: Saw a large number of porpoises and sperm whales.
ZAGEN GROTE VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP: Saw large birds near the ship.
ZAGEN HELE TROEPEN ZEEVOGELS EN OOK VLIE: Saw whole flocks of seabirds and also flying fish.
ZAGEN HET EILAND DE SAL NIET: Did not see the island of Sal.
ZAGEN HET NOORDERLICHT VAN NO-WNW: Saw the northern lights from NE to WNW.
ZAGEN HET VUUR VAN KAAP OTMAY NNW, 7 MIJ: Saw the light of Cape Otmay NNW, 7 miles.
ZAGEN HOOGLAND IN HET ZO , DAT VOOR HET: Saw high land in the SE, which was taken for the island of Palma. Corrected course and distance, SW by S 1/8 W 20 miles, change of longitude 0° 39'. The island of Ferro? in sight, running.
ZAGEN IN DE ACHTERMIDDAG DE ENGELSE BARK: In the afternoon saw the English bark Mandarin from Sydney to China.
ZAGEN IN DE ACHTERMIDDAG EEN SCHIP IN HE: In the afternoon saw a ship in the S lying with us. By day the ship was still astern.
ZAGEN IN DE AMW BERMUDA EN RAAKTEN ALDAA: Saw Bermuda in the [?] and struck the rocks there with the rudder. Entered the harbor of Bermuda on 1 June. Set out again on 8 August for the Netherlands.
ZAGEN IN PVW DE LOODSBOOT DIE EEN AANSCH: Saw in the [?] the pilot boat, which gave a written order from the captain at sea, Twent, to sail with the Komeet to Texel.
ZAGEN KROOST DRIJVEN EN VLIEGENDE VISCH: Saw spawn floating and flying fish.
Saw land, think it is Great Fish Point.
ZAGEN LAND. COERS EN VERHEID TOT 4 UUREN: Saw land. Course and distance up to 4 hours SE 5 miles, Table Mountain bears W by N 3 miles, and took a bearing of the same at E by N 1/2 N 3.5 miles, thus by reckoning coming 6.5 miles to the east.
ZAGEN MENIGTE BONTE MEEUWEN, VEEL VIS, E: Saw a multitude of spotted gulls, much fish, a few turtles and many so-called Portuguese men-of-war. Saw them as long as we were east of the Salvages; when we were west of them they disappeared, except for the last-mentioned.
ZAGEN MENIGTE ZEEWIER DRIJVEN: Saw a multitude of seaweed floating.
ZAGEN MET DE DAG DE HOEK VAN POORTLAND I: During the day saw the point of Portland in the NNE 1/2 E, and in the evening Bolt Head (near Plymouth) in the NW by W.
ZAGEN MET DEN DAG LAND IN ZTO, HET GEHAK: During the day saw land in the SE, the jagged mountains SW by W.
ZAGEN MET ZONSONDERGANG NIETS VAN DE STR: At sunset saw nothing of the [?].
Saw another number of flying fish.
ZAGEN NOG EEN WEINIG KROOS DRIJVEN, DOCH: Saw a little more duckweed floating, but not since.
ZAGEN NU EN DAN WRAK HOUT DRIJVEND, HIEL: Saw wreckage wood floating now and then, kept a good lookout.
ZAGEN OM 1 UUR DE VLAG OP OEDJONG PANKA: At 1 o'clock saw the flag flying on Oedjong Panka. At about 5 o'clock took the pilot O.D. Dirksen aboard.
ZAGEN OM 14.00 UUR DE TOREN VAN SCHRAVEZ: At 14.00 hours saw the tower of Schravezand. At 21.00 hours came to anchor in Hellevoetsluis.
ZAGEN OM 17.00 UUR DE NOORDZEEKUST: Sighted the North Sea coast at 17.00 hours.
ZAGEN OM 6 UUR TWEE EILANDEN EN HIELDEN: Sighted two islands at 6 o'clock and took them for Klapper and Trouwers. Not very sure of the said landmark identification. In the night at 6.30, steady squalls of wind, rain with thunder and lightning, and a high, uncomfortable sea until 4.00 in the morning.
ZAGEN OOK VRIJ WAT FEUN HAAIJE MET 5 BIJ: Also saw quite a few [?] sharks, 5 together.
ZAGEN OP DE MIDDAG ST HELENA N 1/3 O 10: Saw St Helena at noon, N 1/3 E, 10 miles.
ZAGEN PALMA TEN 8EN IN 'T OZO, 4 MIJL: Saw Palma at 8 o'clock in the ESE, 4 miles.
ZAGEN REEDS EEN MENIGTE VLIEGENDE VISSEN: Already saw a multitude of flying fish.
Saw snow on the peaks of the island of Palma.
ZAGEN STRUIK BAMBOE DRIJVEN. ZIEN PIJLST: Saw a clump of bamboo floating. Saw a tropicbird. Some shore gulls. Ring of fire in the water.
ZAGEN TEN 6 UREN DE EILANDEN PALMA EN TE: Saw the islands of Palma and Tenerife at 6 o'clock.
ZAGEN TOEN VERSCHEIJDEN SCHOTSE IJS, SCH: Then saw several ice floes, shot lines into the boats.
ZAGEN TROMPETTEN DRIJVEN . VUURRING IN H: Saw trumpeters floating. Ring of fire in the water.
ZAGEN TWEE ROOFVOGELS VAN LAND EN EEN GL: Saw two birds of prey from land and a [?] settle in the rigging.
ZAGEN TWEE STUKKEN WIER OF GROENTE DRIJV: Saw two pieces of seaweed or greenery floating, probably from the islands of St. Paul and Amsterdam.
ZAGEN TWEE TOT 3 LANDVOGELTJES EN VERAND: Saw two to 3 little land birds and a change in the water.
ZAGEN VAN TIJD TOT TIJD VERSCHILLENDE SO: From time to time saw various kinds of fish.
ZAGEN VEEL ALBATROSSEN EN ZOGENAAMDE ZOT: Saw many albatrosses and so-called silly birds.
ZAGEN VEEL BEZAANTIES EN TAKJE KROOS DRI: Saw many by-the-wind sailors and a sprig of duckweed floating.
ZAGEN VEEL GAFFELAARS EN HET LAND VAN SC: Saw many gaff-rigged vessels and the land of Schouw.
ZAGEN VEEL GROENTE EN VUILNIS DRIJVEN: Saw much greenery and rubbish floating.
ZAGEN VEEL GROTE VISSEN EN VERSCHEIDENE: Saw many large fish and several birds.
ZAGEN VEEL HAAIEN EN EEN GROTE VOGEL: Saw many sharks and a large bird.
ZAGEN VEEL KROOS DRIJVEN EN VLIEGENDE VI: Saw much duckweed floating and flying fish.
ZAGEN VEEL MEEUWEN EN VLIEGENDE VISSEN: Saw many gulls and flying fish.
ZAGEN VEEL ROBBEN, VOGELS EN KAAPSE TROM: Saw many seals, birds and Cape trumpeters.
ZAGEN VEEL ROTJES HETWELK VOGELS ZIJN DI: Saw many little auks, which are birds one usually sees near the ice.
ZAGEN VEEL VIS BIJ 'T SCHIP: Saw many fish near the ship.
ZAGEN VEEL VOGELS EN VISSEN ALS CRETTE E: Saw many birds and fish such as [?] and dolphins.
ZAGEN VEEL VOGELS ONDER ANDERE CAAPSCHE: Saw many birds, among others Cape pigeons, near the ship.
ZAGEN VEEL VOGELS VLIEGEN. VINGEN EEN KL: Saw many birds flying. Caught a small turtle of 17 pounds.
ZAGEN VELE VISSEN ALS NOORDKAPERS EN WAL: Saw many fish such as northern right whales and whales; one of the latter kind came close along the ship; by estimate the tail was 16 to 18 feet wide (…)
ZAGEN VELE VISSEN WAARONDER NOORDKAPERS: Saw many fish, among them northern right whales that followed the ship, the largest of them by estimate 30-40 feet.
ZAGEN VERANDERING IN 'T WATER: Saw a change in the water.
ZAGEN VERANDERING IN 'T WATER. ZEER HOGE: Saw a change in the water. Very high swell from the NW [?].
ZAGEN VERANDERING IN HET WATER: Saw a change in the water.
ZAGEN VERANDERING VAN WATER WAARVAN DE R: Saw a change of water, the direction of which was WTN - OTZ.
ZAGEN VERHANDERINGH IN 'T WATER. TEN ANK: Saw a change in the water. At anchor in 15 fathoms, sandy bottom.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDE SCHOOSE, ZAGEN PAKIJS: Saw several ice floes, saw pack ice.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE BLAADJES EN TAKJES VA: Saw several leaves and twigs of trees floating.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE BOSJES KROOS DRIJVEN: Saw several clumps of duckweed floating.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE BOSKOPPEN EN VUURRING: Saw several [?] and a ring of fire in the water.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE MEEUWEN OF KAAPSE DUI: Saw several gulls or Cape pigeons.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE PIJLSTAARTEN, SCHAARV: Saw several tropicbirds, [?] birds, fulmars and a [?].
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS EN GROENTE DRI: Saw several birds and greenery floating.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE ZUIDVOGELS, KAAPSE DU: Saw several southern birds, Cape pigeons and 2 [?].
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE ZWARTE EN RODE ROOFVO: Saw several black and red birds of prey.
ZAGEN VERSCHEIDENE ZWARTE MEEUWEN EN EEN: Saw several black gulls and a tropicbird.
ZAGEN VERSCHILLENDE VOGELS WAARONDER OOK: Saw several birds, among them some shore gulls.
ZAGEN VERSCHILLENDE WALVISSEN EN GAAN ME: Saw several whales and go out with a boat on [?] rope.
ZAGEN VOOR HET EERST PARTIJ JONG IJS: Saw a quantity of young ice for the first time.
Saw flying fish for the first time.
ZAGEN ZEEGEWAS DRIJVEN EN KAAPSE DUIVEN: Saw seaweed floating and Cape pigeons.
ZAGEN ZWARE BRANDING, WAARSCHIJNLIJK VAN: Saw heavy surf, probably from the reef of Bonnevista. Could see nothing ahead of us because of the hazy air.
ZATEN PRECIES OP BESTEK: Were exactly on the reckoned position.
ZE BEVINDEN ZICH 646,5 MIJL TEN OOSTEN V: They are 646,5 miles east of Baaij Falso and 34,5 miles west of Amsterdam.
ZE DACHTEN OOSTELIJKSTE TE ZIJN DAT MEN: They thought they were the most easterly of what was estimated.
ZE GEVEN HET SEIN OM DE COMMANDEUR TE SP: They give the signal to speak to the commodore.
ZE GISSEN DAT ZE TUSSEN HET MAIDE-EILAND: They guess that they are sailing between the Maide island and the 5 rocks.
ZE HEBBEN DE TIJDMETER STIL LATEN STAAN: They let the chronometer stand still.
ZE HOUDEN AF NAAR LISSABON WEGENS ZIEKTE: They bear away toward Lisbon because of the illness of the wife of the ambassador Bangeman Huygens.
ZE VERGELIJKEN HET BESTEK MET DE COMMAND: They compare the reckoning with the commander and the Kenau Hasselaar.
ZE ZATEN VOLGENS HET LOGBOEK HELEMAAL FO: According to the logbook they were completely wrong and did not know well where they were; the current had set them even further west than thought.
ZE ZITTEN NIET MIS MET HET BESTEK: They are not far wrong with the reckoning.
ZE ZOUDEN VLGS HET BESTEK LAND MOETEN ZI: According to the reckoning they should see land, but they see no land.
ZEE BUIIG BEVONDEN 7 MINUTEN NOORD STROO: Squally sea, found a current of 7 minutes north.
ZEE GING HEEL RUIG MET DE LAMPOLIE OM, Z: The sea went very rough and upset the lamp oil, so that we had to make do with the light of the sky.
ZEE LIEP HOOG WAARDOOR HET SCHIP SLINGER: The sea ran high so that the ship rolled; toward noon a lee sail spar broke; steered NE. The ship sprang a leak because of the high level of the sea, which made her roll.
ZEER MOOIE ILLUSTRATIE VAN EEN VERSTERKI: Very fine illustration of a reinforcement on the bowsprit.
ZEER NEVELIG, KUNNEN GEEN 3 MIJL ZIEN. D: Very foggy, cannot see 3 miles. Depth 75-55 fathoms, gray fine sand with pieces of small shells and some green. Concluded from this that the bottom was that of the [?] treatise on depth, bottom and approach of [?] (=position).
ZEER SCHOON NOORDERLICHT, VLAMMENDE VAN: Very fine northern lights, flaming from the N-NNE toward the east and west.
ZEER SUBIET OVERLEDEN SOLDAAT JOHANNIS S: Very suddenly died soldier Johannis Schoenewal of Koningsberg
ZEER VEEL BROOD BESCHIMMELD. HOUDEN SCHE: A great deal of bread moldy. Held a ship's council over the crew, 4 invalids, only half a month's rations left
ZEER VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: Very many fish near the ship
ZEER VEEL VIS BIJ HET SCHIP EN SCHAARVOG: Very many fish near the ship and skuas.
ZEER WEINIG ZIEKEN. DE GEHEEL EQUIPAGE V: Very few sick. The entire crew of 87 heads is still complete, a blessing of the highest order, all the more as they must make do with the ship's galley stores, and stockfish and bacon are spoiled by the heat.
ZEESTAAT ZEER HOOG, MEN VERMOEDT VEROORZ: Sea state very high, thought to be caused by the Amazon river.
ZEEWATERTEMPERATUUR OP DE MIDDAG. TEMPER: Sea water temperature at noon. Temperature in the shade at noon was 73 degrees
ZEI ONS OVER DE VLOOT HEEL SLECHT MET DE: Told us across the fleet that the fishery is going very badly
ZEIJLDEN AL LANGS DE KUST OP 2 A 3 MIJLE: Sailed all along the coast at 2 to 3 miles distance, with 2 glasses, saw the flag of Hesen… saw the tower which stands on the hill of Tressinda... at 4 o'clock anchored in the roads of Ponne Cayl
ZEILDE 6 A 7 MIJLEN PER WACHT. SNELLE VO: Sailed 6 to 7 miles per watch. Fast progress. Set everything that could be of use.
Sailed close along the coast of Africa.
ZEILDE ONDER DE KANT HEEN VAN T IJS WEST: Sailed under the edge of the ice westward and took leave of my uncle Pieter Mooij, went SWbyS, having the wish for the fatherland
ZEILDEN GEDURENDE HET ETMAAL IN HET GEZI: Sailed during the day in sight of the coast.
ZEILDEN LANGS DE LOOP VAN DE KUST VAN GU: Sailed along the course of the coast of Guyana
ZEILDEN TUSSEN PALMA, GOMERA EN TENERIFE: Sailed between Palma, Gomera and Tenerife and east of Ferro through.
ZEILDEN VOLGENS STREKKING DER ENGELSE KU: Sailed following the trend of the English coast
ZEILDEN WEER NAAR DE MADDELENE BAAI: Sailed again to the Maddelene bay
ZEILEN BENOORDEN MIDDELBURG EN AMSTERDAM: Sailing north of Middelburg and Amsterdam, and between Haarlem and Rotterdam and via Hoorn to Batavia.
ZEILEN DE 10E DE RIVIER VAN SIERRA LEONE: On the 10th sailed up the river of Sierra Leone
ZEILEN DE MADDELENE BAAIJ UIT, LANGS DE: Sail out of the Maddelene bay, along the shore southward
Sailing out of the Sunda Strait.
Sailing in the northeast trade wind.
ZEILEN IN DE PVW LANGS CURAÇAO HEEN: Sailing in the PVW along Curaçao
ZEILEN IN HET ZICHT VAN JAVA, GEEN WAARN: Sailing in sight of Java, no more observations. Arrived on 7 September 1787 in the roads of Batavia.
Sailing along the coast of Guyana.
ZEILEN NU UIT PATRIA NAAR KAAP DE GOEDE: Now sailing from Patria to the Cape of Good Hope. Could not give the latitude found, because they report no sun.
ZEILEN OP DE GRONDEN. NA DEZE DAG GEEN G: Sailing on the shoals. After this day no more good data. Anchored on 30 September in Mounts Bay. The journal ends on 16 October in Mounts Bay.
ZEILEN TUSSEN DE LINIE EN KAAP DE BONA E: Sailing between the Line and Cape of Good Hope.
ZEILEN VANAF NU IN DE SPAANSE ZEE: Sailing from now on in the Spanish sea
ZEILENDE DOOR STRAAT MALAKKA, GEEN LENGT: Sailing through the Strait of Malacca, no more longitude. Arrived on 14 May in the roads of Malacca. No more good data after that. Arrived on 27 July in the roads of Batavia.
ZEILENDE IN DE NOORDELIJKE ATLANTISCHE O: Sailing in the northern Atlantic Ocean. Longitude obtained is chronometer longitude. Two chronometers, No. 28 and No. 3. In case of difference I keep to No. 28. Barometer reading six digits, it reads 29_1 1/2. Further on it reads 28_11.
ZEILENDE IN HET GEZICHT VAN FAGO EN BRAV: Sailing in sight of Fogo and Brava.
ZEILENDE LANGS DE KUST VAN VENEZUELA VAN: Sailing along the coast of Venezuela from La Guaira to Porto Cabello. Departed on 16 November.
ZEILENDE UIT DE BAAI FALS NAAR CEIJLON: Sailing out of False Bay to Ceylon
ZEILENDE VAN CURAÇAO NAAR DE MONA PASSAG: Sailing from Curaçao to the Mona Passage.
ZEILENDE VAN CURAÇAO NAAR LAGUAYRE. 8 NO: Sailing from Curaçao to Laguayre. Departed 8 November.
ZEILENDE VAN DE MONA PASSAGE NAAR SINT T: Sailing from the Mona Passage to Saint Thomas.
Sailing from Fruxillo to Vera Cruz.
Sailing from Havana to the Netherlands.
ZEILENDE VAN NEDERLAND NAAR DE KUST VAN: Sailing from the Netherlands to the coast of Guinea.
Sailing from Popo to the Camarones.
Sailing from Port Mahon to Holland.
Sailing from Port Mahon to Malta.
ZEILENDE VAN ST EUSTATIUS NAAR ST MARTIN: Sailing from St Eustatius to St Martin, anchored there.
Sailing from St. Maarten to Suriname.
ZEILENDE VAN SURINAME NAAR ST. EUSTATIUS: Sailing from Suriname to St. Eustatius. Reckoning measured since 5:30 from the topgallant point.
Sailing from Vera Cruz to Havana.
ZEILENDE VOLGENS STREKKING DE KUST: Sailing following the trend of the coast
ZEND DE SLOEP MET LUITENANT BONNEMA NAAR: Sent the sloop with Lieutenant Bonnema to Fort Nieuw Amsterdam (to prepare the salute). Sent Lieutenant Pichot with the launch to the government in Paramaribo.
ZENDEN DE CHALOUP AAN LAND OM OLIE TE KO: Sent the shallop ashore to boil oil.
ZENDEN EEN OFFICIER MET DE CHALOUP VAN B: Sent an officer with the shallop from on board with (the message) that the sheets had been cut away. This one positioned itself at the point of the reef of Ontong Java, in 5 fathoms.
ZENDEN ONZE TIMMERLIEDEN NAAR DE 'ADMIRA: Sent our carpenters to the 'Admiraal de Ruyter' to repair the bowsprit. The ship Langewijk also supplies carpenters.
ZETTEN 'T BESTEK IN DE RONDE KAART. HET: Put the reckoning on the plain chart. It seems that the days run from one day watch to the next day watch, so when 'HW' or 'at night' is mentioned, it actually concerns the following day, but in the records and in the journal it is counted under this day (so not the following day). Furthermore, the distinction between the letters L and S is hard to make in the journal writer's hand, so it will sometimes happen that instead of luchtje [light breeze] it should read zuchtje [sigh of wind] (then written with an S) and vice versa
ZETTEN BESTEK IN DE KAART: Put the reckoning on the chart
ZETTEN BESTEK OP 71°30' EN 12°2' VERBETE: Put the reckoning at 71°30' and 12°2', corrected our reckoning 2 degrees to the west
ZETTEN DE GEWEERKISTEN OMLAAG IN HET ACH: Put the musket chests down in the after hatch, exercised with the guns and small arms
ZETTEN DUBBELE UITKIJKEN VOOR 'T EILAND: Set double lookouts for the island of Monij. Lightning in the N.
ZETTEN DUBBELE UITKIJKEN VOOR DE COCUS E: Set double lookouts for the Cocos Islands
ZETTEN DUBBELE UITKIJKEN VOOR DE EILANDE: Set double lookouts for the islands of St. Paul and Amsterdam
ZETTEN HET BESTEK 19 MINUTEN OOSTELIJKER: Put the reckoning 19 minutes more easterly
ZETTEN HET BESTEK 30 MIJLEN OM DE WEST O: Put the reckoning 30 miles to the west at the longitude of 33° 40' and at the latitude found.
ZETTEN HET BESTEK AF OP DE OVERZEILDER N: Marked the reckoning off on the over-sailer according to the position of the islands at 97 deg. 4'.
ZETTEN HET BESTEK IN DE RONDE CAART. WAN: Put the reckoning on the plain chart. When 'at night' or dog watch (HW) is mentioned, it concerns the night and the dog watch of the following day, because the journal days run from day watch to day watch
ZETTEN HET BESTEK IN DE WASGRADIGE PASKA: Put the reckoning on the Mercator chart
ZETTEN HET BESTEK OP 13° LENGTE W VAN GR: Put the reckoning at 13° longitude W of Greenwich
ZETTEN HET BESTEK OVER IN DE KAART VAN C: Put the reckoning over onto the chart from Cape Verde to the Cape of Good Hope.
ZETTEN HET BESTEK OVER IN DE NIEUWE OVER: Put the reckoning over onto the new over-sailer. Signal from the commander art. 10 PKZ with 1 shot
ZETTEN HET BESTEK PROVISIONEEL 8° WESTWA: Put the reckoning provisionally 8° westward, this is on this latitude N approx. 78.5 miles
ZETTEN HET BESTEK TWEE GRADEN WESTELIJKE: Put the reckoning two degrees more westerly (without seeing land)
ZETTEN HET LIJK OVERBOORD. MATROOS, NEUE: Put the corpse overboard. Sailor Neuenboom died.
ZETTEN HET LIJK VAN DE SCHOOLMEESTER OVE: Put the corpse of the schoolmaster overboard
ZETTEN HET RAD EN NACHTHUIS OP DE KAJUIT: Put the wheel and binnacle on the cabin
ZETTEN IN DE MORGENSTOND HET LIJK OVERBO: Put the corpse overboard at daybreak.
ZETTEN KOERS OM DE OOST OM LAND IN HET G: Set course to the east to run into sight of land
ZETTEN KOERS RICHTING VADERLAND EN GINGE: Set course toward the fatherland and went SWbyS on the compass
ZETTEN KRACHT VAN ZEILEN, OMDAT DE SURSE: Set full sail, because the Surseance is no longer in sight, and with the thick sky may well have been passed.
ZETTEN LIJK OVERBOORD. MATROOS, HENDRIK: Put the corpses overboard. Sailor Hendrik Stoop died. Sailor Franc Flanand died. In the evening the corpses were put overboard.
ZETTEN ONS BESTEK 24' ZUIDELIJKER EN KWA: Put our reckoning 24' more southerly and came to the latitude N of 17° 9'.
ZETTEN ONS BESTEK IN DE WASSENDE GRAAD C: Put our reckoning on the Mercator chart. The journal days run from day watch to day watch, so with 'at night' or with the dog watch (HW) is meant that night or dog watch of the following day
ZETTEN ONS BESTEK OP 97G50M ZIJNDE 10 MI: Put our reckoning at 97G50M, being 10 miles off the shore
ZETTEN ONS BESTEK OP DE LENGTE VAN DE VL: Put our reckoning at the longitude of the Flying Fish of the 25th of May, being 15 degrees 8 minutes, and since that time changed to the east 2 degrees 44 minutes. Difference of longitude 3 degrees 18 minutes east.
ZETTEN ONZE KOERS EEN STREEK UIT DE WAL: Set our course one point off the shore because the wind was scant.
ZETTEN WEER KLEINE ZEILTJES BIJ NA DE ST: Set small sails again after the storm of the previous night
ZETTEN WEGEN BRUTALITEIT SOLDAAT S. VAN: Put soldier S. van Duin in irons because of brutality.
ZEYLENDE LANGS DE GREYNKUST NA DÉLMINA: Sailing along the Grain Coast to Elmina
ZIE VOOR DE TERUGREIS NAAR NEDERLAND VAS: For the return voyage to the Netherlands see Vasco da Gama_1826, FAM_22253_17.
ZIEKEN AAN BOORD VOLGENS DE DOCTOR: 51 M: Sick on board according to the doctor: 51 men crew, 83 men transport.
ZIEKENTROOSTER A. KUIPER IN DE BOEIEN WG: Sick-comforter A. Kuiper in irons for drunkenness
Illnesses among the people improving greatly.
ZIEKTEN VERMINDEREN ONDER 'T VOLK, HEBBE: Illnesses decreasing among the people, still have 45 sick in the bunks.
ZIEN 'S AVONDS EEN MOMENT EEN KOMEET IN: Saw a comet for a moment in the evening in the NNW, the tail in the south
ZIEN 'S NACHTS EEN KOMEET STER IN 'T OOS: Saw a comet star in the east at night.
ZIEN 'S NACHTS EEN MAANECCLIPS: OM 11 UU: Saw a lunar eclipse at night: at 11 o'clock the moon is completely darkened until about 2 o'clock.
ZIEN 'S NACHTS EEN VUUR VAN DE WAL: Saw a fire on shore at night
ZIEN 'S NACHTS OM CA. 3:00 EEN LICHTGEVE: Saw at night at about 3:00 a luminous glow in the water. It turns out to be a collection of luminous insects (in the water), which light up when touched. The insects are described as 'whitish, having a hard point and slimy skin, hollow inside with an opening at the thickest end
ZIEN 'S NACHTS UIT NAAR EILAND FERDENAND: Looked out at night for the island of Ferdenando.
ZIEN 'T LAND VAN MONTIGO. VERANDERDE MER: See the land of Montigo. Changed meridian to the E 10.75.
ZIEN 1 GROTE KWAL VOORBIJ DRIJVEN EN HET: See 1 large jellyfish drifting past and the water changes.
ZIEN 1 PEYLSTAART, 1 LANDVOGELTJE EN 1 S: See 1 tropicbird, 1 land bird and 1 small gull.
ZIEN 17 SCHEPEN. ZIEN EEN STUK VAN EEN L: See 17 ships. See a piece of a railing drifting. See the root of a tree drifting. Senior merchant and former warehouse master of Samarang, Carel Godeijn, died.
ZIEN 2 BAMBOSSE DRIJVEN EN ENIGE GROENTE: See 2 bamboos drifting and some weed.
ZIEN 2 WITTE VLAGGEN WAAIEN OP MONA EN E: See 2 white flags waving on Mona and a man with a dog on the beach who seems to need help; put out a jolly boat, which returns with 2 adventurers.
ZIEN 3 WITTE PIJLSTAARTEN EN 2 WITTE MEE: See 3 white tropicbirds and 2 white gulls.
ZIEN 3 WITTE PIJLSTAARTEN EN EEN KLEIN B: See 3 white tropicbirds and a small clump of duckweed; fished it up. It had small round bobbles, and on them something slightly larger, like a peppercorn, yellow.
ZIEN 4 KOKSHENNEN EN GROENTE, KAAPSE DUI: See 4 kokshen birds and weed, Cape pigeons near the ship.
ZIEN 4 SCHAARVOGELS EN EEN WIT STRAND ME: See 4 shearwaters and a white small gull.
ZIEN AANTAL VOGELS BIJ HET SCHIP: See a number of birds near the ship.
ZIEN ALLEEN PIJLSTAARTEN, MEEUWEN EN SCH: See only tropicbirds, gulls and shearwaters.
ZIEN BAMBOES EN EEN BEZANTIE, ZIEN VOGEL: See bamboos and a jellyfish, see birds.
ZIEN BAMBOEZEN EN STUKKEN HOUT DRIJVEN: See bamboos and pieces of wood drifting.
ZIEN BASTAARD MALLIGAZEN, SCHAARVOGELS E: See bastard petrels, shearwaters and many fish, several large red jellyfish.
ZIEN BASTER MALLEGAASE, GELE PEILSTAARTE: See bastard petrels, yellow tropicbirds, shearwater and other birds, see [?].
See jellyfish with oar-like fins drifting.
ZIEN BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN EN ZIEN EEN PIJL: See jellyfish drifting and see a tropicbird.
ZIEN BLAUWE MEEUWEN, MALFIETEN EN CAAPSE: See blue gulls, petrels and Cape pigeons.
ZIEN BOS GROENTE DRIJVEN: See a bunch of weed drifting.
ZIEN BOSJES GROENTE DRIJVEN EN ZEEHONDE: See bunches of weed drifting and seals, also right whales. See much seaweed drifting all day, in small patches and in bunches. The color of the water near the islands is also darker than west of the islands, where the water was a very bluish light green. And now at a much shorter distance it is a much darker green and not so clear. This is surely caused by the abundant drifting weed washing off the island.
ZIEN CAAPSE DUIVEN, ZIJN IETS GROTER DAN: See Cape pigeons, they are somewhat larger than a pigeon, short flight and very beautiful wings. Also see a kokshen.
ZIEN CATIS HENNEN EN EEN SCHILPAD: See catis hens [?] and a turtle.
ZIEN CIRCA 11H45 HET BEGIN VAN DE ZONSVE: See around 11h45 the beginning of the solar eclipse; since we had no good telescopes, our observations could only be very inaccurate.
ZIEN DAT HET WATER HEEL DONKERGROEN GEWO: See that the water has turned very dark green, see a piece of wood or a plank drifting, see large southern birds and small black birds.
See the English barquentine in the southeast.
ZIEN DE FLUIT DE FORTUIJN OPLEVEN, DENKE: See the fluyt Fortuijn coming up, think a man has fallen overboard.
ZIEN DE KOMEETSTAR HEEL KLAAR IN HET ZO: See the comet very clearly in the southeast at 8 o'clock. It was at its highest 25 degrees above the horizon, and when it was first in the southeast its tail stood like this (star upper right, tail toward lower left), and through the south toward the southwest (star lower right, tail toward upper left) 9 or 10 feet long, and the star appeared very fiery, going thus below the southwest. Note: we saw this comet before our departure from Suriname, there, in the morning at 3 or 4 o'clock in the east with its tail pointing upward.
ZIEN DE KRUIN VAN DE PIEK BOVEN DE WOLKE: See the summit of the peak above the clouds. Come to anchor at the northernmost fort.
ZIEN DE TWEE EILANDEN LE COIN DE MIRE EN: See the two islands Le Coin de Mire and Isle Platte, between which they sail.
ZIEN DOMINICA ZO. PEILEN ZO PUNT MONTSER: See Dominica to the southeast. Bearings: southeast point of Montserrat NTW 1/4 W and north point of Guadeloupe E 1/2 N. Took bearings of Antiqua NOTN. Took bearings of Montserrat NWTW.
ZIEN EEN ALBATROS. HEBBEN WEERLICHT EN O: See an albatross. Have lightning and thunderstorm in the northeast, which made a strange sound, like cannon shots.
ZIEN EEN BAMBOESTOK EN ANDERE VUILIGHEDE: See a bamboo stick and other filth drifting and the water changed.
ZIEN EEN BARK, LADEN DE BATTERIJ MET SCH: See a bark, load the battery with live shot.
ZIEN EEN BASTAARD MALLEGAAS EN ENIGE MEE: See a bastard petrel and some gulls.
See a bunch of weed drifting.
ZIEN EEN COKSHEN(?) EN EEN TROMPET DRIJV: See a kokshen (?) and a trumpet drifting.
ZIEN EEN DONDERSLAG IN HET WATER SLAAN I: See a thunderclap strike the water in the east, the seawater flew up from it like a small cloud. The number of sick still increases daily. They now have 54 sick with high fevers. Some are falling ill for the 2nd time.
ZIEN EEN ENKEL BOSJE GROENTE DRIJVEN, EE: See a single bunch of weed drifting, a tropicbird and sea foam.
ZIEN EEN GRAUW STRANDMEEUWTJE EN 2 KAAPS: See a grey small gull and 2 Cape pigeons.
ZIEN EEN GRAUWE VOGEL VEEL VIS BIJ HET S: See a grey bird, much fish near the ship.
ZIEN EEN GROTE KOMEET (PVW), DEZELFDE KM: See a large comet (PVW), the same comet that was first seen on 2 March.
ZIEN EEN GROTE WITTE STRANDVOGEL: See a large white shore bird.
See a waterspout in the west-southwest.
ZIEN EEN KLOMP VUUR UIT DE LUCHT VALLEN,: See a lump of fire fall from the sky, which gave much light.
See a kokshen and 2 right whales.
ZIEN EEN KOKS HEN, EEN WITTE KAAPSE DUIF: See a kokshen, a white Cape pigeon, silver gull, white petrel and other birds.
ZIEN EEN KOKSHEN (ZONSOPGANG), ZIEN VERS: See a kokshen (sunrise), see several small gulls, had strong phosphorescence in the water (EW).
ZIEN EEN KOKSHEN EN MALAGAASEN VLIEGEN (: See a kokshen and petrels flying (white with black wingtips). The water changes.
ZIEN EEN KOKSHEN, ANDERE VOGELS EN CASEL: See a kokshen, other birds and sperm whales and a single bunch of weed drifting. At night whole clumps of phosphorescence.
ZIEN EEN KRING DRIJVEN WAAR VEEL VIS BIJ: See a ring drifting where there was much fish.
ZIEN EEN LANDVOGEL EN HADDEN EEN ZEEDUIV: See a land bird and had devilfish near the ship.
ZIEN EEN LANDVOGEL STERK LIJKEND OP EEN: See a land bird strongly resembling a plover or woodcock.
ZIEN EEN LANDVOGEL. STERKE VUURRING IN H: See a land bird. Strong phosphorescent ring in the water.
ZIEN EEN MALLE???, VERSCHEIDENE PIJLSTAA: See a petrel [?], several tropicbirds and shearwaters, also see some pieces of bamboo drifting. See a length of plank drifting. Phosphorescent ring in the water.
ZIEN EEN MALLEMOK EN EEN SCHAARVOGEL, VE: See a fulmar and a shearwater, many birds.
ZIEN EEN MALLIG, ZIEN EEN TROMPET DRIJVE: See a petrel, see a trumpet drifting.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE BEZANTJES DRIJVEN: See a multitude of jellyfish drifting.
See a multitude of grey gulls.
See a multitude of grey birds.
See a multitude of weed drifting.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE GROTE VISSEN, ALS VINVI: See a multitude of large fish, like fin whales, which stuck their fins out of the water and seemed to be as much as 15 or 20 feet long, which from afar look like a small lateen sail. Sperm whales and right whales.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE MALLEGASEN. VANGEN 4 MA: See a multitude of petrels. Catch 4 mackerel.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE STRANDMEEUWTJES. ZIEN E: See a multitude of small gulls. See a petrel in the [?].
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE VAN GROENTE DRIJVEN PRE: See a multitude of weed drifting; presumed, after checking many journals, to be at a longitude of 95 degrees, and that the weed came from the islands of Saint Paul and Amsterdam.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE VAN VOGELS EN VLIEGENDE: See a multitude of birds and flying fish, much fish near the ship.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE WITTE EN GRAUWE MALLEMO: See a multitude of white and grey fulmars sitting on the water.
ZIEN EEN MENIGTE ZEESLANGEN: See a multitude of sea snakes.
ZIEN EEN NOORDKAPER EN 2 MALLEFIJTEN. (Z: See a right whale and 2 petrels. (See fish and birds.)
ZIEN EEN NOORDKAPER EN ENKELE GRAUWE STR: See a right whale and a few grey gulls.
ZIEN EEN NOORDKAPER. ZIEN VOOR DE EERSTE: See a right whale. See the northern lights for the first time.
ZIEN EEN OOS IN HET ZZW. OVERBOORD GESPR: See a waterspout in the south-southwest. Jumped overboard and perished, soldier Christoffel Oostwall of Mergelsteede.
ZIEN EEN PEIJLSTAARDT EN VEEL KROOS DRIJ: See a tropicbird and much duckweed drifting.
ZIEN EEN PEIJLSTAART. ZIEN NOG EEN WITTE: See a tropicbird. See another white tropicbird.
ZIEN EEN PIJLSTAART EN ENIGE WITTE MEEUW: See a tropicbird and some white gulls.
ZIEN EEN PIJLSTAART EN VLIEGENDE VISSEN: See a tropicbird and flying fish.
ZIEN EEN PIJLSTAART, ZIEN VEEL VOGELS. S: See a tropicbird, see many birds. Ship's prayer. Squally with thunder and lightning and rain. Therefore made little sail.
ZIEN EEN RODE LUCHT ZOALS HET NOORDERLIC: See a red sky like the northern lights.
ZIEN EEN ROG BIJ HET SCHIP: See a ray near the ship.
ZIEN EEN SCHILDPAD DRIJVEN (OCHTEND). ID: Saw a turtle drifting (morning). Same turtle in the afternoon
ZIEN EEN SCHILDPAD EN KROOS DRIJVEN: Saw a turtle and duckweed drifting
ZIEN EEN SCHILDPAD EN LATER EEN ZEESLANG: Saw a turtle and later a sea snake swimming close to the ship.
ZIEN EEN SCHILDPAD EN VERSCHEIDENE VOGEL: Saw a turtle and several birds
ZIEN EEN SCHIP, MAKEN DE BATTERIJ IN ORD: Saw a ship, got the battery in order
ZIEN EEN SCHIP, OOK EEN STUK ROND EN EEN: Saw a ship, also a round piece and a flat piece of wood drifting
Saw a cuttlebone from a cuttlefish drifting. Saw Portuguese men-of-war. Saw a small land bird
ZIEN EEN STRANDMEEUW, EEN GRAUWE STRANDM: Saw a shore gull, a grey shore gull
ZIEN EEN STUK HOUT DRIJVEN: Saw a piece of wood drifting
Saw a piece of wood drifting.
Saw a piece of a tree drifting.
ZIEN EEN TROMPET DRIJVEN EN VERSCHEIDENE: Saw a trumpet drifting and several small gulls
ZIEN EEN TROMPET DRIJVEN ZIJNDE EEN ZEEG: Saw a trumpet drifting, being a sea plant so named for its resemblance to a musical instrument. It is a sign of approaching some island or lowering shore.
ZIEN EEN VLIEGENDE VIS. ZIEN TWEE NOORDK: Saw a flying fish. Saw two right whales
ZIEN EEN VREEMDE VOGEL. EEN KARKAS VAN E: Saw a strange bird. The carcass of an enormous cuttlefish (14 feet) is hauled on board. A large shark (8 feet) comes at it and keeps biting a piece off. The captain fires a harpoon at the shark several times in vain, because the harpoon did not penetrate the hide. The shark is caught with an iron hook on the lead line, with a piece of the cuttlefish as bait. NMW: Saw a right whale. Fired at it with small shot. Also a multitude of dorado (sea bream) near the ship
Saw a fire from the ships.
ZIEN EEN WILDE DUIF BIJ HET SCHIP EN ROD: Saw a wild pigeon near the ship and red jellyfish
ZIEN EEN WITTE MEEUW.HADDEN VEEL MALLEWE: Saw a white gull. Had many fulmars [?] and flying fish near the ship
Saw the root of a tree drifting.
ZIEN EEN WORTEL VAN EEN BOOM DRIJVEN. ZI: Saw the root of a tree drifting. Saw a strange ship.
ZIEN EEN ZEEROB, KAAPSE DUIVEN EN MEEUWE: Saw a seal, Cape pigeons and gulls
ZIEN EEN ZUIDVOGEL EN KAAPSE DUIVEN: Saw a southern bird and Cape pigeons
ZIEN EEN ZUIDVOGEL EN VERSCHEIDENE MEEUW: Saw a southern bird and several gulls
ZIEN EEN ZUIDVOGEL. TONIJNEN BIJ 'T SCHI: Saw a southern bird. Tuna near the ship [?]. Saw a multitude of birds
ZIEN EERSTE KAAPSE TROMPET EN EEN BOS GR: Saw the first Cape trumpet and a bunch of weed in the water
ZIEN EERSTE KOKSHEN VLIEGEN: Saw the first cook hens flying
ZIEN ENGELSE OORLOGSSCHEPEN OP DE REDE V: Saw English warships on the roads of Basseterre, think this is a troop transport from England to North America. Saw among others the Vulture, the Greyhound, the Yarmouth
ZIEN ENIGE BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN EN PIJLSTA: Saw some Portuguese men-of-war drifting and tropicbirds
ZIEN ENIGE BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN. NOG VEEL: Saw some Portuguese men-of-war drifting. Still many large fish near the ship
ZIEN ENIGE BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN. VEEL VOGE: Saw some Portuguese men-of-war drifting. Many birds and fish near the ship
ZIEN ENIGE BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN. VUURRING: Saw some Portuguese men-of-war drifting. Phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN ENIGE CHASELOTTEN EN VERSCHEIDENE V: Saw some sperm whales and several birds
ZIEN ENIGE MEEUWEN. ZIEN TWEE NOORDKAPER: Saw some gulls. Saw two right whales
ZIEN ENIGE PIJLSTAARTEN EN BEZAANTJES DR: Saw some tropicbirds and Portuguese men-of-war drifting. Phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN ENIGE PIJLSTAARTEN EN VEEL KROOS: Saw some tropicbirds and much duckweed
ZIEN ENIGE PIJLSTAARTEN EN VEEL KWALLEN: Saw some tropicbirds and many jellyfish and Portuguese men-of-war
ZIEN ENIGE SCHAARVOGELS EN EEN STRANDMEE: Saw some frigatebirds and a small shore gull.
ZIEN ENKELE SCHAARVOGELS. STERKE VUURRIN: Saw a few frigatebirds. Strong phosphorescence and many fish in the water
ZIEN GEEN GROENTE MEER, WEL 2 KOKSHENNEN: Saw no more weed, but 2 cook hens.
ZIEN GEEN LAND OP DEZE LENGTE EN BREEDTE: Saw no land at this longitude and latitude. Set the position on the round chart 4 ("four") degrees east. West meridian 188,25 miles. Changed 14 miles W. Obtain 202,25 miles. (Estimate, no chart.) Terceira W 1/2 N, 4 miles [?]
ZIEN GEEN LANDTEKENS, LODEN MAAR GEEN GR: Saw no signs of land, sounded but found no bottom
ZIEN GEEN LANDTEKENS. IN DE AVOND DENK M: Saw no signs of land. In the evening it was thought land was seen in the [?].
ZIEN GEEN VOGELS, ALLEEN BESAANTIES DRIJ: Saw no birds, only Portuguese men-of-war drifting.
ZIEN GEEN VOGELS, VINGEN EEN VLIEGENDE V: Saw no birds, caught a flying fish of 17,5 inches with tail.
ZIEN GEEN WALVIS ENKEL VINNEVIS: Saw no whale, only finback whales
ZIEN GOMERA (DAAR ZIJN ZE NIET ZEKER VAN: Saw Gomera (they are not sure of it there, "very far away")
ZIEN GRAUWE STRANDMEEUWTJES EN KAAPSE DU: Saw small grey shore gulls and Cape pigeons
ZIEN GROENTE DRIJVEN EN EEN STUK ZEESCHU: Saw weed drifting and a piece of sea foam
ZIEN GROENTE DRIJVEN, EN GRAUWE STRANDME: Saw weed drifting, and grey shore gulls. At sunset 2 cook hens and many fields of weed.
ZIEN GROENTE DRIJVEN, ZIEN EEN KOKS HEN: Saw weed drifting, saw a cook hen
ZIEN GROENTE EN WITTE PIJLSTAARTEN EN SC: Saw weed and white tropicbirds and frigatebirds
ZIEN GROENTEN DRIJVEN. VEEL VUURRING IN: Saw weed drifting. Much phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN GROENTEN EN NISTELINGEN DRIJVEN. ZI: Saw weed and [?] drifting. Also saw a cook hen.
ZIEN GROTE BESAANTIES MET ROEIVINNEN DRI: Saw large Portuguese men-of-war with oar-fins drifting.
ZIEN GROTE BOOM DRIJVEN EN EEN SCHILDPAD: Saw a large tree drifting and a turtle
ZIEN GROTE GRAUWE VOGELS, VANGEN DAGELIJ: Saw large grey birds, catch much fish daily
ZIEN GROTE ROODACHTIGE VLAMMEN IN HET WA: Saw large reddish flames in the water.
ZIEN GROTE SCHILDPAD, EEN MENIGTE BONIJT: Saw a large turtle, a multitude of bonito, dorado and sharks near the ship. NMW: A great multitude of birds like small gulls.
ZIEN GROTE VELDEN KROOST DRIJVEN FRIS VA: Saw large fields of duckweed drifting, fresh in color.
ZIEN GROTE VOGELS EN ZWARTE MEEUWEN: Saw large birds and black gulls
ZIEN GROTE WATERVOGELS, ZUIDVOGELS: Saw large water birds, southern birds
Saw the comet very clearly at night.
ZIEN HELE SCHORREN MET SCHARDIJN. 'S NAC: Saw whole shoals of sardines. Heavy dew at night.
ZIEN HELE TROEPEN GRAUWE VOGELTJES ALS S: Saw whole flocks of small grey birds like shore gulls. Saw the comet star at night in the [?] E with the tail to the west.
ZIEN HELE TROEPEN KLEINE VIS DRIJVEN: Saw whole flocks of small fish drifting
ZIEN HET SCHEIDEN KOK HENNEN ,ZIE MEDE E: Saw the cook hens parting, also saw a small shore gull
ZIEN IN DE MIDDAG DE KUST VAN AFRIKA: Saw the coast of Africa in the afternoon
ZIEN IN DE VOORMIDDAG OP EEN AFSTAND VAN: Saw in the forenoon at a distance of 0,5 mile a pinewood beam drifting in the water
Saw Cape pigeons and storm petrels.
ZIEN KLEINE BEZAANTIES DRIJVEN, ZIEN OOK: Saw small Portuguese men-of-war drifting, also saw 3 white tropicbirds, a frigatebird and a bastard fulmar
ZIEN KLEINE EN GROTE BESAANTIES MET ROEI: Saw small and large Portuguese men-of-war with oar-fins. Saw small pieces of sea foam drifting.
ZIEN KLEINE QUALTIES (KWALLETJES?) EN BE: Saw small jellyfish (little jellyfish?) and Portuguese men-of-war drifting.
ZIEN KLEINE STRANDMEEUWEN. ZIEN EEN WITT: Saw small shore gulls. Saw a white gull
ZIEN KLEINE STUKJES GROENTE DRIJVEN EN K: Saw small pieces of weed drifting and [?] and butterflies.
ZIEN KOCKS HEN EN EENIGE LOMME: Saw cook hens and some guillemots
ZIEN KOKSHENNEN, CAAPSE DUIVEN, PIJLSTAA: Saw cook hens, Cape pigeons, tropicbirds, southern birds and a single leaf of weed
ZIEN KROOS DRIJVEN, MAAR MINDER DAN OP A: Saw duckweed drifting, but less than on other voyages, saw seagulls
ZIEN KROOS EN STUKKEN HOUT DRIJVEN: Saw duckweed and pieces of wood drifting
ZIEN KROOST DRIJVEN IN ZEE. LEVENDIG VAN: Saw duckweed drifting in the sea. Lively in color.
ZIEN KWALLEN EN GROTE BESAANTIES DRIJVEN: Saw jellyfish and large Portuguese men-of-war drifting. Saw a frigatebird.
ZIEN LAND EN DOEN DAARVOOR SEIN, ART. 69: Saw land and made a signal for it, art. 69, no. 6, [?] signals. Made signal art. 372 from the large signal book. Signalled 28° 44' latitude and 2° 42' longitude
ZIEN LAND, MAAR KUNNEN DOOR DE DIKKE LUC: Saw land, but could not make it out because of the thick air.
Saw only 1 frigatebird and nothing more.
ZIEN MALLEGASEN, KOKSHENNEN EN ANDERE VO: See fulmars, kokshens and other birds
ZIEN MALLEGASEN. DENKEN DAT HET WATER IE: See fulmars. Think the water has changed somewhat.
ZIEN MALVIETEN, STERKE VURING IN 'T WATE: See fulmars, strong phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN MENIGTE SPARTEVOGELS: See a multitude of sparrow birds
ZIEN MENIGTE VAN VIS EN VOGELS: See a multitude of fish and birds
ZIEN MENIGTE VISSEN BIJ HET SCHIP: See a multitude of fish near the ship
ZIEN MET DE DAG DE KUST VANNW TOT NO: See the coast by day from NW to NE
ZIEN MET DEN DAG ST BARTHOLOMEUS, ST EUS: See by day St Bartholomeus, St Eustacius, St Kitts, Nevis and Rodondo
Still see the small grey birds.
ZIEN NOG EEN BOSJE KROOS DRIJVEN, VINGEN: Still see a clump of weed drifting, caught a young frigatebird
ZIEN NOG ENIGE BOSSEN GROENTEN DRIJVEN: Still see some clumps of seaweed drifting
Still see no signs of land.
ZIEN NOG GROENTEN DRIJVEN . ZIEN VERSCHE: Still see seaweed drifting. See several tropicbirds and fish near the ship. At night phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN NOG MEEUWEN, MAAR MINDER DAN 3 DAGE: Still see gulls, but fewer than 3 days earlier.
ZIEN NOG VEEL BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN: Still see many by-the-wind sailors drifting
ZIEN NOG VEEL KLIP GROENTEN DRIJVEN: Still see much rock seaweed drifting
ZIEN NOGAL VEEL STRANTMEUWEN: Still see quite a lot of shore gulls
ZIEN NOORDCAPERS EN VINVISSEN: See right whales and fin whales
ZIEN NOORDKAPER BIJ SCHIP: See a right whale near the ship
ZIEN NOORDKAPER EN 1 BOS ZEEGRAAN (?): See a right whale and 1 clump of [?]
ZIEN NOORDKAPERS EN EEN GROOTE ZUIDVOGEL: See right whales and a large southern bird
ZIEN NOORDKAPERS EN VLIEGENDE VISSEN: See right whales and flying fish
ZIEN OM 8 UUR 'S AVONDS EEN KOMEET IN HE: See at 8 o'clock in the evening a comet in the WSW 3/4 W that ends at the constellation Orion and runs along Pegasus.
ZIEN OOK ENKELE SCHOTS: Also see a few ice floes
ZIEN OPEENS ALLE LANDTEKENS TEGELIJKERTI: Suddenly see all the signs of land at the same time: trumpets, fulmars, seals, the water seems changed.
See a tropicbird and a frigatebird.
See tropicbirds, frigatebirds and fish. Phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN RONDHOUT, BOSJES GROENTE EN EEN ROB: See a spar, clumps of seaweed and a seal or sea dog drifting.
ZIEN SCHAARVOGEL EN STERKE VURING IN HET: See a frigatebird and strong phosphorescence in the water
See a frigatebird and a small white gull.
ZIEN SCHAARVOGELS EN PEILSTAARTEN, VEEL: See frigatebirds and tropicbirds, many birds, see something like a coconut drifting with a tree leaf
ZIEN SCHAARVOGELS, STRANDMEEUWEN EN ROEI: See frigatebirds, shore gulls and large [?] by-the-wind sailors (but fewer than yesterday).
ZIEN SCHAARVOGELS. HADDEN VEEL VIS BIJ H: See frigatebirds. Had many fish near the ship
ZIEN SCHOTSEN IJS BEWESTEN ONS: See ice floes to the west of us
See strong phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN STERKE VURINGEN IN HET WATER: See strong phosphorescence in the water
See strong phosphorescence in the water.
See shore gulls and by-the-wind sailors.
ZIEN STRANTMEEUTJES EN MALLEMAKKEN: See small shore gulls and fulmars
ZIEN STUK VAN EEN IJKEN PLANK DRIJVEN: See a piece of an oak plank drifting
ZIEN TROMPETTEN DRIJVEN, DIT ZIJN GROENT: See trumpets (kelp) drifting, this is seaweed that washes off the rocks. When dried you can make sound on it. See 3 divers flying
ZIEN TWEE WITTE MEEUWEN. ZIEN EEN GRAUWE: See two white gulls. See a grey and a white gull
ZIEN VAN DE VUREN VAN LEZARD DOET ONS ON: Sight of the lights of Lezard shows us that the chronometer indicates about 4,75 miles or 29 minutes of longitude too far west
See no more land from the topmast.
ZIEN VEEL BEZAANTJES EN QUALLEN DRIJVEN: See many by-the-wind sailors and jellyfish drifting
ZIEN VEEL GEVOGELTE EN VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: See many fowl and fish near the ship
ZIEN VEEL GRAUWE MEEUWEN ALS STRANDMEEUW: See many grey gulls and shore gulls, also small Cape pigeons.
ZIEN VEEL GRAUWE OF VALE MEEUWEN, OOK PI: See many grey or pale gulls, also tropicbirds and white small shore gulls
ZIEN VEEL GROENTE DRIJVEN. ZIEN EEN KOKS: See much seaweed drifting. See a kokshen.
ZIEN VEEL GROENTEN DRIJVEN EN VEEL VIS B: See much seaweed drifting and many fish near the ship. Strong phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN VEEL GROTE CASELOTTEN EN 'S NACHT G: See many large sperm whales and at night large clumps of phosphorescence
ZIEN VEEL KAAPSE DUIVEN EN GROTE ZUIDVOG: See many Cape pigeons and large southern birds, also grey shore gulls.
ZIEN VEEL KLEINE BOSJES GROENTE DRIJVEN,: See many small clumps of seaweed drifting, see a tropicbird, flying fish
ZIEN VEEL KLEINE GRAUWE MEEUWEN.'ZIEN EN: See many small grey gulls. See a piece of wood drifting that was overgrown with shells
ZIEN VEEL KLEINE KWALLETJES DRIJVEN EN B: See many small jellyfish drifting and by-the-wind sailors. At night strong phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN VEEL KLEINE VIS VOORBIJDRIJVEN: See many small fish drifting past
ZIEN VEEL KLIJNE ZEEKWALLETJES EN BEZAAN: See many small sea jellyfish and by-the-wind sailors and at night strong phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN VEEL KROOS DRIJVEN EN EEN COKSHEN P: See much weed drifting and a kokshen, tropicbirds and gulls, also fulmars
ZIEN VEEL KROOS DRIJVEN, ZIEN PIJLSTAART: See much weed drifting, see tropicbirds
See much weed and flying fish.
See much weed drifting, fresh color.
ZIEN VEEL LANDVOGELS EN EEN NOORDKAPER: See many land birds and a right whale
ZIEN VEEL LANDVOGELS EN VIS BIJ HET SCHI: See many land birds and fish near the ship. See a rose
See many fulmars and Cape pigeons.
See many gulls and other birds.
ZIEN VEEL MEEUWEN, CAAPSE DUIVEN EN ZUID: See many gulls, Cape pigeons and southern birds. Phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN VEEL PIJLSTAARTEN . ZIEN EEN GROOT: See many tropicbirds. See a large bamboo drifting. Strong phosphorescence in the water
ZIEN VEEL QUALLEN EN BEZAANTJES DRIJVEN: See many jellyfish and by-the-wind sailors drifting
ZIEN VEEL ROGGEN EN KROOST DRIJVEN: See many rays and weed drifting
ZIEN VEEL SCHAARVOGELS, PIJLSTAARTEN EN: See many frigatebirds, tropicbirds and fulmars
See many shore gulls and sea gulls.
ZIEN VEEL STRANDMEEUWEN EN EEN MALLEGAAS: See many shore gulls and a fulmar and a kokshen and tropicbirds
ZIEN VEEL STRANDMEEUWEN, VERANDERING VAN: See many shore gulls, change of water and a right whale
ZIEN VEEL TONIJNEN DRIJVEN EN MALLEGASEN: We see many tuna floating and fulmars flying, strong phosphorescence in the water.
We see much filth in the water.
We see many fish near the ship.
ZIEN VEEL VLIEGENDE VIS. VEEL ANDERE VIS: We see many flying fish. Many other fish near the ship. Give sea coral to the crew. Tarred the barge and the boat.
ZIEN VEEL VOGELS EN GROENTE DRIJVEN. ZIE: We see many birds and greenery floating. See no change of water.
We see many birds and gulls.
ZIEN VEEL VOGELS EN QUALLEN: We see many birds and jellyfish.
We see many birds and fish.
ZIEN VEEL VOGELS WAARONDER 2 WITTE STRAN: We see many birds, among them 2 white small shore gulls and some shearwaters.
ZIEN VEEL VOGELS, W.O. MALLEMAKKE: We see many birds, among them fulmars.
ZIEN VEEL VOGELS, ZIEN VEEL GRAUWE MEEUW: We see many birds, we see many grey gulls.
ZIEN VEEL WITTE BEZAANTJES: We see many white by-the-wind sailors.
ZIEN VEEL WITTE STRANDMEEUWEN EN SCHAARV: We see many white shore gulls and shearwaters.
We see many white shore gulls.
ZIEN VEEL ZWARTE MEEUWEN EN ANDERE VOGEL: We see many black gulls and other birds, see a cook hen and a small shore gull.
ZIEN VEEL ZWARTE VOGELS EN EEN MALLE VIE: We see many black birds and a [?].
ZIEN VEEL ZWARTE ZUIDVOGELS EN EEN WIT S: We see many black southern birds and a white small shore gull.
ZIEN VELE WITTE MEEUWEN EN SCHAARVOGELS: We see many white gulls and shearwaters.
ZIEN VERANDERING IN 'T WATER. ZIEN VEEL: We see a change in the water. We see many birds.
ZIEN VERANDERING IN HET WATER: We see a change in the water.
ZIEN VERANDERING IN HET WATER, METEN DIE: We see a change in the water, measure depth 42 feet, coarse sand with shells.
We see a change in the water.
ZIEN VERANDERING VAN 'T WATER: We see a change in the water.
ZIEN VERANDERING VAN WATER: We see a change in the water.
ZIEN VERANDERING VAN WATER DAT BLEEK WAS: We see a change in the water, which was pale.
ZIEN VERANDERING VAN WATER. BESHRIJVING: We see a change in the water. Description of the land. They sail within 2 miles of the nearest shore. See heavy surf. Think it is the blunt point that is in the chart book as 'Klijpige Hoek', which lies between the point of the bay of Dirk de Vrijs and the Wijn Coops Bergen. Later it turns out to have been the point lying between Dirk de Vrijs Bay and Mniwrijs Bay.
ZIEN VERANDERINGEN IN 'T WATER: We see changes in the water.
We see discolouration in the water.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE BEZAANTJES EN RODE ZEE: We see several by-the-wind sailors and red sea [?] floating. Strong phosphorescence.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE BOSJES GROENTE DRIJVEN: We see several bunches of greenery floating, see birds, see cook hens.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE BOSKOPPEN. ZIEN BEZAAN: We see several [?]. See by-the-wind sailors drifting past.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE BOSSEN GROENTEN. STERK: We see several bunches of greenery. Strong phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE HOZEN ???.VEEL VIS BIJ: We see several [?]. Many fish near the ship.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE KAAPSE DUIVEN EN KOKSH: We see several Cape pigeons and cook hens.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE KLEINE VIS DRIJVEN: We see several small fish floating.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE MALLEGASEN EN EEN KOKS: We see several fulmars and a cook hen.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE MALLEGASEN, OOK KOKSHE: We see several fulmars, also cook hens and other birds.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE RODE KWALLETJES DRIJVE: We see several small red jellyfish floating, we thought they must come from the islands, also saw by-the-wind sailors.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE SCHAARVOGELS, VEEL VIS: We see several shearwaters, many fish and [?].
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE SCHAARVOGELS. VUURRING: We see several shearwaters. Phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE SCHEPEN OP DE REDE VAN: We see several ships in the roads of Basseterre.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE SOORTEN VOGELS: We see several kinds of birds.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS EN HEEL VEEL VI: We see several birds and very many fish near the ship.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS EN VEEL VIS BIJ: We see several birds and many fish near the ship.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE VOGELS EN VLIEGENDE VI: We see several birds and flying fish.
ZIEN VERSCHEIDENE WITTE MEEUWEN EN HADDE: We see several white gulls and had fish near the ship.
ZIEN VERSCHIJDEN GROENE BOOMBLADEREN EN: We see several green tree leaves and thorn branches drifting past, and the water changing even more.
ZIEN VERSCHILLENDE VOGELS OM DE ZO TREKK: We see various birds migrating toward the southeast.
ZIEN VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: We see fish near the ship.
ZIEN VLIEGENDE VIS BIJ HET SCHIP: We see flying fish near the ship.
ZIEN VLIEGENDE VIS EN EEM PIJLSTRAAT: We see flying fish and a tropicbird.
ZIEN VLIEGENDE VISJES, 2 NACHTUILEN. STE: We see small flying fish, 2 owls. Strong phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN VLIEGENDE VISSEN EN MEEUWEN: We see flying fish and gulls.
ZIEN VOGELS EN VLIEGENDE VIS: We see birds and flying fish.
ZIEN VOGELS EN VLIEGENDE VISSEN: We see birds and flying fish.
ZIEN VOGELS. WATER VUURT STERK MET GROTE: We see birds. Water glows strongly with large flames. This is a sign that one is nearing the coast.
ZIEN VOGELS: 2 WILDE EENDEN, EEN KRAANVO: We see birds: 2 wild ducks, a crane and a grey heron.
We see duckweed floating for the first time.
We see flying fish for the first time.
We see duckweed floating for the last time.
ZIEN VOOR HET EERST IJS: We see ice for the first time.
ZIEN VOOR HET EERST SCHOTSEN IJS: We see Scottish ice for the first time.
ZIEN VREEMD SCHIP, COMMANDANT HIJST ENGE: See a strange ship, commander hoists English flag, strange ship also, commander later hoists the Batavian flag and pennant. Braave chases the hostile ship, which must be brought to the commander.
ZIEN VURING IN HET WATER (EERSTE WACHT): We see phosphorescence in the water (first watch).
ZIEN VURING IN HET WATER (EW): We see phosphorescence in the water (first watch).
We see another piece of wood floating.
ZIEN WEER KAAPSE DUIVEN EN STRANDMEEUWEN: We see Cape pigeons and shore gulls again.
ZIEN WEER VEEL PIJLSTAARTEN EN KROOS: We see many tropicbirds and duckweed again.
ZIEN WEER VEEL WITTE STRANDMEEUWEN EN SC: We see many white shore gulls and shearwaters again.
ZIEN WEINIG OF GEEN KROOS MEER DRIJVEN E: We see little or no more duckweed floating and several tropicbirds.
ZIEN WEINIG SCHAARVOGELS EN STRANDMEEUWE: We see few shearwaters and shore gulls.
ZIEN WIT STRANDMEEUWTJE, EN 2 KAAPSE DUI: We see a white small shore gull and 2 small Cape pigeons.
ZIEN WITTE EN ZWARTE STRANDMEEUWTJES: We see white and black small shore gulls.
ZIEN WITTE VOGEL EN VLIEGENDE VISSEN: We see a white bird and flying fish.
ZIEN ZEESCHUIM DRIJVEN EN ZIEN CA. 4 MAL: We see sea foam floating and see about 4 fulmars. The water has changed.
ZIEN ZEESCHUIM EN VEEL RODE BEZAANTJRES: We see sea foam and many red by-the-wind sailors floating. Phosphorescence in the water.
ZIEN ZEEVOGELS OP HET WATER TER GROTE VA: We see seabirds on the water the size of a wild goose.
ZIEN ZWARE HOOS IN ZO EN KREGEN EEN WIND: We see a heavy waterspout in the southeast and got a gust of wind from it, and it dispersed.
ZIEN ZWARE SCHEPEN EN MAKEN KLAAR VOOR B: We see heavy ships and make ready for battle.
ZIEN ZWARTE VOGEL EN VLIEGENDE VIS: We see a black bird and flying fish.
They see very many land birds this day.
ZIJN - DOOR DES HEEREN ZEGEN - DE DROOGT: By the Lord's blessing, have passed the shoals of the Ambrollos. Set double lookouts for the islands of Trinidad and Ascension.
ZIJN ALLE ZIEKTEN UIT HET ZIEKENHUIS OPG: All the sick have been fetched from the hospital, ready to depart.
ZIJN CA RECHT BOVEN DE ZON: Are about directly beneath the sun.
ZIJN DE . TROPICUS CAPRICORNI GEPASSEERD: Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn. Pitching heavily.
ZIJN DE ACHTSTE VANUIT ST MARTIN NAAR ST: On the 8th departed from St Martin for St Thomas.
ZIJN DE HAVEN VAN CURACAO UITGEVAREN EN: Have sailed out of the harbour of Curacao and are now in the Caribbean Sea.
ZIJN DE HELE DAG BEZIG MET WATER HALEN,: Busy the whole day fetching water, [?], [?], mending sails, etc.
ZIJN DE KAAP VERDISCHE EILANDEN GEPASSEE: Have passed the Cape Verde Islands.
ZIJN DE KEERKRING GEPASSEERD, BRENGEN DE: Have passed the tropic, spend the afternoon in fitting merriment, extra dram.
ZIJN DE TROPICUS CANCER PEGASSEERD. GEVE: Have passed the Tropic of Cancer. Give the crew 1.5 can of drinking water. Had always given the crew this and also 10 ounces of beer daily.
Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn.
ZIJN DE TROPICUS CAPRICORNICUS GEPASSEER: Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn.
Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn. Cast the lead but found no bottom.
ZIJN DE ZON GEPASSEERD: GEEN VOORWERP GA: Have passed the sun: no object cast a shadow to the side.
ZIJN EILANDEN TRINIDAD EN ASCENSION GEPA: Have passed the islands of Trinidad and Ascension.
ZIJN IN HET KANAAL, MAAR HEBBEN NIETS GE: Are in the Channel, but took no bearings. Came on 25 October to the roads of Vlissingen.
ZIJN NA LANG ZWERVEN EN OMZIKKELEN WAARS: After long wandering and circling, are probably in the east trade wind.
ZIJN TROPICUS CAPERNIJ GEPASSEERD. KEREN: Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn. Turn the gunpowder and cartridges.
ZIJN TROPICUS CAPRI CORNI GEREEFDE PASSE: Pass the Tropic of Capricorn under reefed sails.
ZIJN TROPICUS CAPRICORNI GEPASSEERD: Have passed the Tropic of Capricorn.
ZIJN VAN VOORNEMEN OM DE REIJS NA T VADE: Intend to continue the voyage to the fatherland, as usual at night take meals every third watch.
By estimate have passed the sun.
ZIJN'T EILAND FERDINANDO DE NORONHA GEPA: Have passed the island of Fernando de Noronha.
ZITTEN MET HET BESTEK 60 MIJL LANDINWAAR: By dead reckoning are 60 miles inland. Midday: depth of 20 fathoms.
ZO HOEK GUNNERS EILAND, ZW 1/4 Z. DUIVEN: Southeast point of Gunners Island, southwest by south. Duiventoren, [?] 1/4 west. Southwest point of Flat Island, north-northwest 1/2 west.
ZODAT WIJ 7 GRADEN 8 MIN WESTELIJKER WAA: So that we were 7 degrees 8 minutes further west than our dead reckoning had it.
ZODAT WIJ ONS WEER 23 MINUTEN NOORDELIJK: So that we found ourselves again 23 minutes further north.
ZOEKEN EILAND FRIALS ROCKS. KONDEN NIETS: Searching for the island Frials Rocks. Could discover nothing.
ZOMTIJDS NOG EEN ENKELDE SCHOTS, IN DE E: In summer still an occasional squall; in the east one runs into the ice, probably from the west coast.
ZON EN MAAN: 115GR 1 MIN LENGTE: Sun and moon: 115 degrees 1 minute longitude.
ZON EN MAAN: 143GR 56 MIN LENGTE: Sun and moon: 143 degrees 56 minutes longitude.
ZON OP 2° RECHT BOVEN ONS HOOFD, MOETEN: Sun at 2° directly above our heads, we must be enduring unbearable heat.
ZON OP OM 5 UUR EN ONDER OM 7 UUR: Sun up at 5 o'clock and down at 7 o'clock.
ZOND 1E LUITENANT VAN DE VELDE MET DE JO: Sent 1st Lieutenant Van de Velde with the jolly boat to the shore, etc.
ZOND DEN LUIJTENANT PICHOT EN DEN SCHRIJ: Sent Lieutenant Pichot and the clerk Ilksen aboard the merchant ship De Vrouwe Clara Magdalena to appoint first mate Govert Mulder as captain in place of its deceased captain Elias van Houtten.
ZONDEN 3 MAN NAAR SCHIPPER REUL, DIE EEN: Sent 3 men to Captain Reul, who had a leaking ship and many sick.
ZONDEN 4 ZIEKEN NAAR HET HOSPITAAL, KRIJ: Sent 4 sick men to the hospital, received wool and poultry aboard.
ZONDEN 5 ZIEKEN (IMPERTINENTEN) NAAR HET: Sent 5 sick men (troublemakers) to the hospital. Took 4 gunners into service. Received rice and katjang (peanuts) aboard, and weapons and sails, also coffee, tea and sugar. Received 16 native soldiers aboard.
ZONDEN 7 HELE EN 5 HALVE VARKENS NAAR LA: Sent 7 whole and 5 half pigs ashore.
ZONDEN EEN ONDEROFFICIER MET 13 MATROZEN: Sent a petty officer with 13 sailors to the ship of Captain Abraham Siwirs to help get it ready to sail along with us.
ZONDEN ENIGE ZIEKEN MET DE CHALOUP AAN L: Sent some sick men ashore with the launch to stretch their legs.
Solar eclipse, but not visible here.
ZONSONDERGANG NO HOEK VAN PUNTO DE NAGO: Sunset: the NE corner of Punto de Nago bearing northwest by west and the southernmost corner of Gran Canaria south half east, 4.5 miles. Bearing the S corner of the Canaries ESE.
ZONSONDERGANG PEILEN HET WESTELIJKSTE VA: Sunset: bearing the westernmost part of Rontan southeast by east, W/Z [?] easterly, and Utila south.
ZONSONDERGANG PEILEN ZUIDELIJKST ZICHTBA: Sunset: bearing the southernmost visible land south.
ZONSONDERGANG W HOEK RONTAN ZO 0,5 MIJL: Sunset: W corner of Rontan SE 0.5 mile and Utila southwest by west half west and the Hog Island southeast by south half south. Compared the English and Spanish charts; the writer finds the Spanish chart better.
ZONSOPGANG: ZIEN GEEN LAND. VERBETERDEN: Sunrise: see no land. Corrected the dead reckoning. They are 1° 10' or 17 miles too far east. Bearing the corner of Wijn Coops Bergen ESE half south and the westernmost land that could be seen north by west half west, estimating we are 4 to 5 miles from the nearest shore. In the afternoon saw Rouwen Island west by north. Bearing then, when we had the corner in the south, SE, 21 fathoms of grey sand with clay, mixed with specks and little shells. De Liefde also comes to anchor here.
ZOUDEN DUS 4 MINUTEN MET DE ZEE OM DE Z: Would thus have drifted 4 minutes to the south with the sea.
ZOUDEN VOLGENS HET BESTEK LAND MOETEN ZI: According to the dead reckoning we should see land.
ZUCHTJES EN STIL: Light breaths of wind and calm.
ZUIDERBREEDTE, DOPEN DOOR NEPTUNIS KON A: South latitude, the baptism by Neptune could be bought off.
ZUIDVOGELS EN HET WATER NOG HEEL VERANDE: Southern birds and the water still very changeable.
ZULLEN ONS BESTEK ZETTE OP 16GR 30 M LEN: Will set our reckoning at 16 degrees 30 minutes longitude, because we cannot see Hitland.
ZUURKOOL EN APPELS ZIJN BEDORVEN, BEMANN: Sauerkraut and apples are spoiled, the crew now receives [?] in the drinking water on doctor's orders, the crew is regularly ordered to wash their clothes.
SW point of island Nieves 31° [?] the W.
ZWAAR STAMPEN VAN SCHIP DOOR ZEE VAN VOR: Heavy pitching of the ship in a head sea.
ZWAAR VERLOOP VAN DONDER, BLIXEM EN REGE: Heavy bout of thunder, lightning and rain in the PV.
ZWAAR WEERLICHT IN HET ZZW IN DE HONDENW: Heavy lightning in the SSW during the dog watch.
ZWARE BUIEN MET DONDER EN WEERLICHT: Heavy squalls with thunder and lightning.
ZWARE STORM IN DE AW, PV EN EW: Heavy storm in the AW, PV and EW.
ZWARE STORM VAN ZW EN NW MET AANHOUDENDE: Heavy storm from SW and NW with continuous rain.
ZWARE STROOMRAFELING UIT N, DIE ONS IN E: Heavy ripple of current from the N, which approached us in a moment. Conclude from it a change in the water. It becomes as thick and muddy as in the rivers in Holland on a winter day. The water was somewhat blackish, now becomes greenish. Grey sandy bottom at 55 fathoms.
ZWARE ZEEBEVING OM 7.45H IN DE OCHTEND,: Heavy earthquake at 7.45h in the morning, 1.5 minutes long, were then at 22 south latitude and 75 west longitude.
À MIDI, RELEVÉ LE FORT À L' E7S À 5 LIEU: At noon, the fort bore E7S at a distance of 5 leagues.
À QUATRE HEURES DU MATIN, APPAREILLÉ. MO: At four o'clock in the morning, got under way. Anchored in 30 fathoms, muddy bottom: the fort bore S27E at 2 leagues. At 13:00 hours, got under way.
Last day of the log. Arrival at Cádiz.
…OM 1 U KREGEN EEN HEVIGE RUKWIND UIT 'T: …At 1 o'clock got a violent gust of wind from the SW, within half an hour the weather was over…
